and contemplate the flourishing of the restoration.
Since Your Majesty has entrusted me with the nation's heavy burden,
and expects me to bring peace and prosperity,
if my memorial is found acceptable,
please hand it over for implementation."
Thereupon, the 'land survey' was implemented according to regional boundaries.
Only the three prefectures of Xú, Yǎn, and Qīng residing in Jìnlíng
were exempt from this regulation.
Many sojourning commanderies and counties
were merged and abolished.
Gōng was appointed General Who Guards the West and Governor of Yùzhōu.
Gōng firmly declined the titles of Grand Tutor, Shepherd of the Province, and the swordsmen,
and returned the yellow *yuè* (axe).
In the seventh month,
Zhū Língshí pacified Shǔ,
beheaded the false Shǔ King Qiáo Zòng,
and sent his head to the capital.
In the ninth month,
Gōng's second son, Yìzhēn, was enfeoffed as Duke of Guìyáng County,
as a reward for pacifying Qí and subduing Lú Xún.
The Son of Heaven reiterated his previous decree,
bestowing upon Gōng the titles of Grand Tutor and Shepherd of Yángzhōu,
with the addition of feathered parasols, drums and pipes, and twenty swordsmen.
More than a hundred generals and officials earnestly urged him,
and so he accepted the feathered parasols, drums and pipes, and swordsmen,
but firmly declined the rest.
In the tenth year (414 CE),
the people were allowed to rest and labor was simplified.
The Eastern Residence was built,
and its offices constructed.
Sīmǎ Xiūzhī, General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jīngzhōu,
was a prominent member of the imperial clan
and had the support of the people of Jiānghàn.
Gōng suspected him of having rebellious intentions.
Xiūzhī's nephew, Qiáo Wáng Wénsī, was in the capital,
recruiting light-hearted chivalrous men.
Gōng seized Wénsī and sent him back to Xiūzhī,
ordering him to deal with him as he saw fit.
Xiūzhī memorialized to have Wénsī deposed,
and also wrote a letter to Gōng expressing his apologies.
In the first month of the eleventh year (415 CE),
Gōng arrested Xiūzhī's son Wénbǎo and nephew Wénzǔ,
and both were granted death in prison.
He then led his armies west to campaign.
He was again granted the yellow *yuè*,
and appointed Governor of Jīngzhōu.
On the *xīnsì* day,
he departed from the capital,
with Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn Dào Lián overseeing the affairs of the remaining residence.
Xiūzhī submitted a memorial stating his case: "I have heard that fortune does not always remain constant;
order and disorder alternate.
Once the calamities of the 'yang nine' have passed,
from ruin comes prosperity.
Formerly, usurping ministers acted contrary to righteousness,
and the imperial order was broken.
The predestined generations had not yet
change,
the imperial destiny would again flourish.
Grand Commandant chén Yù, with his martial prowess and clear judgment,
raised the banner of righteousness,
eliminated the prime culprit,
and restored the imperial residence to its proper state.
As a commoner, a mere individual,
he helped
restore the imperial altars of soil and grain.
He suppressed Lú Xún in the south
and pacified Guǎnggù in the north.
Over a thousand years,
no one's achievements can compare to his.
Consequently, the four seas praised his excellence,
and the court and populace revered him.
Having reached
the highest position of Grand Minister,
with power overshadowing the sovereign,
he failed to manage his achievements with propriety,
and indulged in arrogance due to imperial favor.
Believing that his rewards had reached their peak,
his ambition turned towards the supreme position.
Executions and punishments became wantonly abusive,
and governance became tyrannical and harsh.
Signs of his ambition for the imperial throne became more evident day by day,
and the etiquette of a subject was completely neglected.
Your Majesty's daily meals
often lacked provisions for various occasions.
Supplies for the palace,
were not even
one-tenth of what they should be.
During the Empress's illness,
medicine was not adequately provided.
She wrote many personal letters
to make various requests.
All these things were heard and seen by court officials,
and none were not saddened
and exasperated,
yet dared not speak.
Yuán Xiǎn's fifth son, Fǎxīng, former Inspector of Yángzhōu,
during Huán Xuán's rebellion,
fled far away.
Once the royal road was open,
he was able
to return to his origins.
The lineage of the Grand Tutor,
which had been extinguished, was revived.
Among all those with feelings,
who would not feel joy and celebration?
Yù, with his predatory ambition,
showed no regard for consequences,
seeing Fǎxīng as intelligent
and discerning,
and bound to become the hope of the people.
As the fragrant orchid flourished,
he harbored inward hatred,
and so he wantonly incited false rumors,
executing him without cause.
Grand Marshal chén Déwén
and the Queen and princesses,
were in dire straits and greatly pressed,
and together desperately pleaded for their lives.
But the traitor wantonly inflicted harm,
vowing not to grant clemency,
and the anguish of their injustice
moved passers-by.
As
his own status was humble but his position exalted,
and he had received great imperial favor,
he married his illegitimate daughter to Déwén,
resulting in an unsuitable match,
which was truly due to coercion.
Former General of the Guards Liú Yì,
Right General Liú Fān, Former General Zhūgě Chángmín, Minister of Personnel Xiè Hùn, and Southern Barbarian Commandant Xī Sēngshī,
some with great achievements and virtuous descendants,
held high reputations
themselves.
All were pillars of the state,
entrusted with aiding and assisting,
yet without any crime or fault,
they were suddenly annihilated.
Such a suspicious and cruel nature
is rarely seen throughout history.
I, your subject, reflecting on my family's decline,
relied on him to survive.
The imperial favor I received
is unmatched throughout history.
Therefore, both publicly and privately, I submitted to him,
complying with all matters.
When I was again
appointed to Jīngzhōu,
I repeatedly made earnest pleas,
believing that my talent was weak but my position high,
and that I should not long hold responsibility for a divided region.
I repeatedly requested to resign,
but he absolutely would not listen.
Previously, I brought my elderly
mother,
and half my family west,
while all my sons and nephews
remained in the capital.
My elder brother's son, the Prince of Qiáo, Wénsī,
though young and an ordinary person,
was largely free from fault or regret.
By nature he enjoyed socializing,
and did not know how to guard against danger from afar.
A group of villains conspired against him,
creating rumors.
Yù then executed scholars and officials,
and sent Wénsī far away.
I complied with his wishes,
memorialized
a request,
asking for Wénsī to be deposed,
and for the main lineage to be succeeded otherwise.
I sent my son Wénbǎo to escort my daughter back east.
I thought I had shown utmost sincerity and obedience,
and that this was as far as it could go.
How could I have known that Yù harbored
malicious intent,
and would launch an attack,
adding evil to Wénsī,
fabricating crimes and grievances?
The words of the petty men
spread as rumors far and wide,
yet I, in my pure foolishness,
ignorantly believed it could not
be true.
Soon, my Administrator of the Household, Zhāng Màodù, frantically returned east.
Tán Fànzhī, the Administrator of Nánpíng, also abandoned his command and rebelled on the third day of this month.
Soon there was confirmation
that the eastern army had already advanced.
Yù's current action
is not due to any grievance or hatred.
It is simply because I am a pillar of the royal house,
holding a high position as a regional commander.
With all the worthy men gone,
only I
remain.
His plan is to eliminate me
to achieve his usurpation and regicide.
General who Guards the North chén Zōngzhī and Inspector of Qīngzhōu chén Jìngxūan
are both deeply feared by Yù,
and he intends
to eliminate them in sequence,
and then overthrow the celestial authority,
making the matter easier.
Now, the righteous troops of Jīng and Yōng,
have gathered without being summoned.
The multitude of volunteers
has assembled like a forest.
This is not something I, lacking virtue, could have brought about.
It is the spiritual power of the seven imperial ancestral temples
that pervades both the seen and unseen realms.
I have immediately appointed Wénsī as General who Shakes Martial Power and Administrator of Nánjùn.
Zōngzhī's son, Lǔ Guǐ, Administrator of Jìnglíng, has been promoted to General who Assists the State.
I, your subject,
along with Zōngzhī, am personally leading the main army,
taking up positions at Jiāngjīn,
arraying our forces and asserting our might,
responding as circumstances require.
Now, the scarlet banner points only
at Yù and his brothers, fathers, and sons.
Once the rebellious bandits are crushed,
I will immediately send further reports.
Due to my weakness,
Yù has been able to act with arrogance.
I am deeply ashamed and mortified,
unable to show my face.
Hán Yánzhī, Registrar and Adjutant to Xiūzhī's headquarters,
was a former subordinate
who possessed administrative skill and talent.
Before the Duke reached Jiānglíng,
he secretly sent someone to write a letter to him, saying:
“Wénsī's actions,
are known far and wide.
Last autumn, when Kāngzhī was sent to escort Sīmǎ Jūn back,
it was the ultimate act of public duty.
Yet he showed no humility or shame at all,
nor did he submit any memorial.
Wénsī's rebellion against the rightful authority
is something that Heaven and Earth will not tolerate.
I received the imperial command to campaign west,
to stop only his father and son.
The old settlers in that region,
who were driven and compelled by him,
I will not question any of them.
In previous years, Xī Sēngshī, Xiè Shào, Rèn Jízhī, and others,
conspired for years,
and solely served as strategists for Liú Yì.
That is why they came to this pass.
You and others,
who were temporarily forced,
originally had no slightest grievance.
My intentions towards others
have always been thus.
Now I am on a nearby path,
and it is precisely the day for all of you to surrender.
If the main army sets out,
and weapons clash,
I truly will not distinguish between orchids and mugwort.
Therefore, I fully explain my intentions,
and show them to all those who share my feelings.”
Hán Yánzhī replied: “I understand that you are personally leading your cavalry
and have advanced far into the western borders.
All the literati and common people in the region
are not without fear and terror.
Why is that?
Because no one knows the declared reason for your military expedition.
Now I have received your esteemed
letter,
and only now do I know it is due to the former actions of the Prince of Qiáo,
which truly makes me sigh with regret.
Sīmǎ Píngxī is loyal and devoted to the state,
and manifests love towards people.
He should be sought among the ancients.
Considering
that the Emperor had the merit of restoring order,
and the state relied on him,
he promoted virtue and entrusted sincerity,
and consulted and looked up to him in every matter.
The Prince of Qiáo was impeached for a minor matter in the past,
and yet he still memorialized to resign his position;
how much more so should he have remained silent with such a great transgression?
But Kāngzhī's previous words did not fully express his meaning,
therefore, he again sent Hú Dào to convey his thoughts.
Before Hú Dào could return,
you had already
memorialized to depose him.
What was not fully expressed was his fate.
The trust and intimacy between us,
should it be like this?
What was wrong,
that you immediately raised arms?
Since the righteous banner took
power,
the regional governors in all four directions,
who dared not first consult with each other,
and directly memorialize the Son of Heaven?
The Prince of Qiáo was reprimanded by the Chancellor,
and then a memorial was submitted to depose him.
What has become of rightful
authority?
On what grounds was the memorial submitted?
It can be said:
“To impose a crime,
surely there is no lack of pretexts?”
Your Excellency, Liú Yù,
among the people within the four seas,
who does not see this intention of yours,
and yet you still wish to deceive the nation's elite!
What Heaven and Earth will not tolerate,
is with them, not with
us.
Your letter says:
“My intentions towards others
have always been thus.”
Now you attack another's lord,
and tempt people with profit.
This truly can be called:
“My intentions towards others
have
always been
thus.”
Liú Fán died within the Chānghé Gate,
Zhūgě perished by the hands of your attendants.
You used sweet words to deceive the regional governors,
and attacked them with light forces,
thus
causing there to be no loyal officials in the court,
and no trustworthy lords outside the palace.
To consider this a successful strategy
is truly shameful.
The generals and assistants in your headquarters and the virtuous members of the court
live day by day entrusting their lives to fate,
and have long yearned for peace.
I am truly base and inferior,
but I have often heard the Way from noble men.
With the supreme virtue of the General Who Pacifies the West,
how could he be without
ministers who would serve him with their lives?
I cannot throw myself into the tiger's mouth.
It is clear that I follow the path of Xī and Rèn.
Even if chaos were to continue endlessly,
and the nine streams were in turmoil,
I would rather wander in the underworld with Zāng Hóng,
and
speak no more.”
The Duke read the letter and sighed.
He showed it to his aides and said:
“This is how one should serve a lord.”
In the third month,
the army reached Jiānglíng.
Initially, Lǔ Zōngzhī, Governor of Yōngzhōu, had always feared that the Duke would not tolerate him,
and allied himself with Xiūzhī.
At this point, he led his son, Guǐ, Prefect of Jìnglíng, to meet at Jiānglíng.
Liú Qiánzhī, Prefect of Jiāngxià, intercepted them;
his army was defeated, and he was killed.
The Duke ordered Xú Kuízhī, Grand Administrator of Péngchéng, and Wáng Yǔnzhī, Adjutant, to go out to Jiāngxiàkǒu,
but they were again defeated by Guǐ,
and both perished.
At this time, the Duke's army was anchored at Mǎtóu.
That very day, he led his forces to cross the Jiāng River.
He personally supervised his generals as they landed.
All of them eagerly struggled to be first.
Xiūzhī's forces collapsed.
He and Guǐ fled to Xiāngyáng.
Jiānglíng was pacified.
He was additionally appointed Colonel Protector of the Southern Barbarians.
When he was about to be officially installed,
it happened to be a "Four Waste Days".
His aides Zhèng Xiānzhī, Chǔ Shūdù, Wáng Hóng, and Fù Liàng advised changing the day.
He did not permit it.
He issued an order saying:
“This province has accumulated many ills,
and incidents have followed one after another.
The people are exhausted, fields are overgrown,
and looms are empty.
Furthermore, the old regulations are obscure and contradictory,
and conscripted labor is frequent and arduous.
Children and the elderly are deprived of care,
the old and young are forced into military service,
families with no able-bodied men are conscripted,
or even those in mourning are called to service.
I constantly ponder the suffering of the people,
forgetting sleep even in the middle of the night.
It is truly fitting to abolish harsh policies,
and to promote leniency and benevolence.
So that the decadent customs and corrupt governance
may be renewed with affairs,
and the transformation to peace and unity
be achieved within a month.
In Jīngzhōu and Yōngzhōu,
the Western Office, Southern Barbarian Bureau officials, and soldiers aged twelve and under,
and sixty and above,
as well as those supporting orphans and young children,
and single able-bodied men facing great hardship,
are all to be sent home.
Those who are destitute and cannot survive,
shall be provided with long-term relief.
Officials and officers who have served diligently for a long time in the prefecture and province
shall be evaluated and ranked according to their efforts.
And this year's land tax shall also be abolished.”
In the fourth month,
the Duke again led his forces to advance and campaign,
reaching Xiāngyáng.
Xiūzhī fled to the Qiāng.
The Son of Heaven again reiterated the previous decree,
appointing him Grand Tutor and Governor of Yáng Province,
permitting him to wear his sword and shoes when entering the imperial hall,
to walk leisurely in court,
and to be announced without stating his name.
Additionally granting him feathered canopies in front of his carriage and a military band,
and he was to appoint Left and Right Chief Clerks, Marshals, and four Attachés.
His third son, Yìlóng, was enfeoffed as Duke of North Péngchéng County.
Liú Dàolián, General of the Central Army, was appointed Governor of Jīng Province.
On the jiǎzǐ day of the eighth month,
the Duke arrived from Jiānglíng.
He respectfully returned the yellow battle-axe,
and firmly declined the titles of Grand Tutor, Governor of the Province, feathered canopies, and military band.
He accepted the rest of the appointments.
The court deliberated that the Duke's virtue and merits were lofty and weighty,
and it was no longer appropriate to address him as Protector-General.
Since he had already been granted special courtesies,
when submitting memorials, his name would no longer be stated.
His heir apparent was appointed Governor of Yǎn Province.
In the twelfth year, first month,
an edict was issued for Gōng to reappoint officials as before.
He was additionally appointed Grand Administrator of the North (Píngběi Jiāngjūn) and Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
He was further made Dūdū of Southern Qín,
overseeing a total of twenty-two zhōu.
Gōng, believing that the staff of the Píngběi Jiāngjūn were few in both civil and military personnel,
deemed it unsuitable to establish a separate office.
Thus, the Píngběi office was abolished
and merged with the main office.
His heir apparent was made Inspector of Yùzhōu.
In the third month,
Gōng was additionally appointed Grand Dūdū of internal and external affairs (Zhōngwài Dàdūdū).
When Gōng first pacified Qí,
he still had the intention of settling Guān and Luò,
but as Lú Xún invaded and pressed on,
his plans did not come to fruition.
With Jīng and Yōng now pacified,
he planned an external campaign.
Coincidentally, the Qiāng ruler Yáo Xìng died,
and his son Hóng succeeded him.
Brothers began to kill each other,
causing turmoil in Guānzhōng.
Gōng then ordered a strict alert and prepared for a northern expedition.
He was additionally appointed General Exterminating the West (Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn) and Inspector of Sī and Yù zhōu.
His heir apparent was made Inspector of Xú and Yǎn zhōu.
A decree stated:
"I initiated the great righteousness
starting from my home zhōu,
recovered the imperial throne,
and established glorious achievements.
I expelled external powerful enemies
and cleansed internal traitors;
these are all the results of the sincere efforts of the people of the state and the zhōu.
Our sentiments are like wind and frost,
our righteousness penetrates metal and stone.
Now I am about to take leave and march west,
to campaign in Guān and Hé.
My weak successor has undeservedly received
this current appointment,
such deep affection and circumstances
can be called profound.
Recently, state affairs have been busy,
and punishments have not ceased.
Reflecting on this,
how can I not sigh deeply?
For those who have committed crimes and been imprisoned for five years or less,
they may be pardoned and released.
Civil and military officials who have completed their service but have not yet received honorable promotions
shall be rewarded according to their ranks."
Gōng accepted the position of Zhōngwài Dūdū and Sīzhōu Inspector,
and also declined the ceremonial respects due to Dàsīmǎ, the Prince of Lángyá.
The court agreed.
Gōng wished to inspire distant regions with his righteous reputation and
lead the Prince of Lángyá on a northern expedition.
In the fifth month,
Yǐn Chōng, the faux Grand Master of the Imperial Household (Huángmén Shìláng) of Qiāng, led his brothers to submit.
Gōng was further appointed Inspector of North Yōngzhōu,
granted a front feathered canopy (yǔbǎo) and a drum and pipe band (gǔchuī),
and the number of guards with ceremonial swords (bānjiàn) was increased to forty.
He was relieved of the position of Director of the Secretariat (Zhōngshū Jiān).
On the Dīngsì day of the eighth month,
he led the main army from the capital.
His heir apparent was made General of the Central Army (Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn)
and superintendent of the affairs of the Grand Commandant's (Tàiwèi) residence.
Liú Mùzhī, the Right Director of the Palace Secretariat (Shàngshū Yòu Púyè), was made Left Director of the Palace Secretariat,
overseeing the military affairs of the Supervisor of the Army (Jiānjūn) and Central Army (Zhōngjūn) offices.
He resided in the Eastern Residence (Dōngfǔ),
managing all internal and external affairs.
In the ninth month,
Gōng arrived at Péngchéng and
was additionally appointed Inspector of Xúzhōu.
Previously, he had dispatched General of the Champions (Guànjūn Jiāngjūn) Tán Dàojì and General Dragon Aspect (Lóngxiáng Jiāngjūn) Wáng Zhèn'è to march on Xǔ and Luò.
The Qiāng who were stationed along the route
all submitted at the mere sight of them.
Wéi Huá, the faux Inspector of Yǎnzhōu, who had occupied Cāngyuán,
also led his forces to surrender.
Gōng also sent Wáng Zhòngdé, the Inspector of North Yǎnzhōu, ahead with a naval force to enter the Hé River.
Zhòngdé defeated the Suǒlǔ at Liángchéng in Dōngjùn
and advanced to pacify Huátái.
In the tenth month,
the combined armies reached Luòyáng and
besieged Jīnyǒng.
Hóng's brother, Guāng, the faux General Pacifying the South (Píngnán Jiāngjūn), requested to surrender
and was sent to the capital.
The five imperial tombs of Jìn were repaired
and guards were stationed.
The Emperor's edict stated: "When Sōng and Dài match the utmost,

Therefore, Xià and Yīn relied on the lords of Kūn and Péng,
and the
Zhōu dynasty depended on the assistance of Qí and Jìn.

Therefore, he is advanced to Prime Minister (Xiàngguó),

He is enfeoffed with ten commanderies as Duke of Sòng,
granted the full nine bestowments,

Obey this command with respect,

carefully attend to the various
states,
and reverently display your eminent virtue,
to fulfill the auspicious mandate of my great ancestor.
Appoint a Sòng State Shìzhōng, Huángmén Shìláng, Shàngshū Zuǒchéng, and Láng (Láng),
who shall follow the imperial envoy to welcome you.
〔一三〕
Chífú Chìpán (Qífú Chìpán), the barbarian from Bāohǎn (Bāohǎn), sent an envoy to your excellency to request to serve in suppressing the Qiāng (Qiāng).
He was appointed Píngxī Jiāngjūn and Hénángōng.
In the first month of the thirteenth year,
your excellency advanced with the navy for punitive action,
leaving Péngchénggōng Yìlóng (Yìlóng) to guard Péngchéng.
When the army reached Liúchéng,
passing by Zhāng Liáng's (Zhāng Liáng's) temple,
he issued an order saying:
"Great virtue does not perish;
it is fitting for the sacrificial canon.
The lament of Wēiguǎn (Wēiguǎn) deepens with every reflection on these matters.
Zhāng Zǐfáng's (Zhāng Zǐfáng's) Dao (Dào) was second only to Huángzhōng (Huángzhōng),
and his illumination was almost divine.
His mysterious connection to the wind and clouds,
〔一四〕made him an imperial mentor,
greatly saving the world from chaos,
subduing Xiàng (Xiàng) and stabilizing Hàn (Hàn).
He can indeed be compared to Yī (Yī) and Wàng (Wàng)
in virtue, like benevolent rulers.
As for his spiritual communion on the bridge
and his profound agreement with the Dao (Dào) at Shāngluò (Shāngluò),
the interval between his fame and obscurity
is mysteriously difficult to fathom.
The source and flow are vast and deep,
one cannot fathom their beginning.
Passing through the old Pèi (Pèi) territory,
and pausing at Liúchéng,
the spiritual temple is dilapidated and ruined,
the remaining statues are dim and obscure.
Tracing his footsteps, I think of the man,
and sigh with deep emotion.
Those who pass by Dàliáng (Dàliáng) sometimes linger in thought at Yímén (Yímén);
those who visit Jiǔyuán (Jiǔyuán) also linger at Suíhuì (Suíhuì).
The rafters can be rebuilt,
and the red and blue paintings repaired.
Mugwort and pondweed can be offered
seasonally,
to relieve the feeling of reminiscing about the past,
and to preserve his unblemished achievements."
The Son of Heaven posthumously conferred on his excellency's grandfather the title of Tàicháng,
and on his father that of Zuǒguānglù Dàfū,
but he declined to accept them.
In the second month,
General Guànjūn Tán Dàojì and others reached Tóngguān.
In the third month, on the day Gēngchén,
the grand army entered the Yellow River.
The Suǒlǔ cavalry and infantry, numbering 100,000,
encamped at Hójīn.
The Duke ordered the various armies to cross the river and defeat them.
The Duke arrived at Luòyáng.
In the seventh month,
he reached Shǎnchéng.
General Lóngxiáng Wáng Zhèn'è cut down trees to make boats,
and floated down the Yellow River into the Wèi River.
In the eighth month,
Prefect of Fúfēng Shěn Tiánzǐ decisively defeated Yáo Hóng at Lántián.
Wáng Zhèn'è captured Cháng'ān,
and personally seized Hóng.
In the ninth month,
the Duke arrived at Cháng'ān.
Cháng'ān was abundant and complete,
with treasures and storages overflowing.
The Duke first collected its ritual vessels, armillary sphere, and gnomon,
and presented them to the capital;
the rest of the rare treasures and precious jades
were bestowed upon the generals and commanders.
Yáo Hóng was sent in custody
and beheaded in the market of Jiànkāng.
He paid respects at the mausoleum of Emperor Gāodì of Hàn,
and held a grand assembly of civil and military officials at Wèiyāng Diàn.
In the tenth month,
the Son of Heaven issued an edict saying: "I have heard that when ancient kings governed the world,
they honored virtue with grand treasures above,
and established feudal lords to commend meritorious deeds below.
Thus, when achievements were completed,
Wénmìng
was granted a black jade,
and when all within the four seas came to acknowledge sovereignty,
Jī Dàn enjoyed the enfeoffment of Guī and Méng.
Indeed, to assist the sagely and proclaim achievements,
to aid virtue and expand grand plans,
rewards should be pushed to the extreme,
and favor should be renowned in rare
ages.
How much more so for one who guides the young and ignorant,
uniquely wielding the power of creation and transformation!
Due to my unworthiness,
I encountered many difficulties in my family,
with chaos rising like thunder and clouds,
and Yi and Houyi usurping the mandate,
losing my position in the capital.
I was then dispersed to Mánjīng,
facing hardship and humility,
and my destiny was controlled by
malevolent villains.
The Chancellor, Duke of Sòng,
endowed by Heaven with sagely wisdom,
was born in his generation to meet the opportune moment.
His sincerity penetrates the three spiritual realms,
and his grand principles are broadly displayed.
He rescued my person from the precariousness of a bird's nest,
and restored the spiritual mandate
from its collapse.
He has truly reached the extreme of submitting to authority,
his brilliance shining across the eight directions.
Furthermore, he has accumulated the merit of unifying the nation externally,
and internally amassed the achievements of suppressing the common people's rebellion,
eliminating the root of strong evil
at its inception,
fostering the source of hidden villainy,
embodying the way of outward benevolence and hidden usefulness,
and achieving the great repair of the six offices.
There is nothing that he has not accomplished like clouds moving and rain falling,
completing every task.
He has indeed marched in line
with the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors,
and is worthy of being recorded in annals and documents.
Since the loss of the army during Yǒngjiā,
more than ten jǐ (cycles) have passed.
The five capitals have been divided and fallen,
yet the orthodox calendar has continued to reach us;
only Sān Qín has been suspended
and separated,
not having submitted for a moment.
To this day, the Qiānglǔ have repeatedly caused chaos,
indulging in tyranny for three generations,
relying on the hundred-and-two passes that are easy to defend,
and trusting in the Hángǔ Pass which can be closed.
Strategic calculations and military plans
have not
been made against them for a long time.
The Duke, destined by Heaven to govern the age,
has revealed and displayed his mighty spiritual power.
Internally, he has pondered the concerns of the feudal lords,
and externally, he has brought about the punishment of Heaven.
Thus, when the war chariots were merely trained,
Xǔ and Zhèng submitted to his influence;
when the gongs and axes were not yet pointed,
Chán and Luò were cleared of their mist.
He enabled the southern side of the old palace gate
to once again gather the axle-caps of myriad states,
and the elders of Dōngjīng
to again behold
the glory of the Sīlì.
He allowed me to sit facing the screen and fold my hands in respectful ease,
and to preserve the grand and glorious achievements.
Therefore, looking far back at ancient precedents,
and consulting with the multitude of strategists,
I respectfully bestow a unique honor,
to brightly open up the
territory.
The system for riding carriages
is inferior to old regulations;
the beauty of his honorific title
has not yet reached the highest rank.
How can this be sufficient to manifestly reward his magnificent achievements,
and truly fulfill the hopes of the people;
to be a bulwark for the royal
domain,
and to hold the long reins of the six directions?
In reality, the Duke always upholds a humble virtue,
so modest that none can surpass him;
he considers the path of advancement difficult,
and regards favor as a cause for distress.
For this reason, I have reduced and diminished the grand
system,
and there will be further decrees later.
From then until now,
his grand achievements have grown ever greater,
his awe-inspiring power has reached the Jiǔhé,
and Wèi and Zhào have submitted.
He turned his chariots at Xiáo and Tóng,
and the continuous cities crumbled like ice.
Then he drove straight to Bà and Chǎn,
hung his banner at Lóngmén,
and the rebellious bandit Yáo Hóng
was captured with a rope around his neck.
A hundred years of defilement
were cleansed in a single morning;
the resentment of our ancestors
was avenged in
a single day.
He has followed the footsteps of Yǔ,
his influence extending throughout the world,
even overseas,
with none failing to submit.
His merit is truly for ten thousand generations,
and his peace will be eternal.
This is not something that can be praised by musical instruments and odes of gold and stone,
but rather something that can be announced to the gods,
and engraved on Sōng and Dài mountains.
I have also heard that
when the Way of Zhōu was far-reaching, the Yuèzhuó sang at Qí;
when the virtues of Èrnán were spread,
the Qílín-chariot appeared as a good omen.
Since the Duke's grand decree was first issued,
until
its completion,
spiritual auspicious signs have shone brilliantly,
too numerous to count.
How could it be merely white pheasants arriving from afar,
and auspicious grains returning nearby?
I constantly look up to the mysterious responses,
and look down to examine human
plans.
Considering his Taoist achievements when advancing,
and national precedents when retreating,
how can I simply follow the Duke's humility and modesty,
and long suppress this grand plan?
It is fitting to respectfully perform the grand ceremony,
to truly fulfill the hopes of both the unseen and the seen.
Therefore, promote the Duke of Sòng's rank to King,
with the ten commanderies of Hǎilíng, Dōng'ān, Běilángyé, Běidōngguǎn, Běidōnghǎi, Běiqiáo, Běiliáng of Xúzhōu, and Rúnán, Běiyǐngchuān, Nándùn of Yùzhōu,
to augment the State of Sòng.
His positions as Chancellor, Governor of Yángzhōu, acting General Zhēngxī, and Inspector of the four provinces of Yǒng, Yù, Běixú, and Yōng remain as before."
In the eleventh month,
Former General Liú Mùzhī died.
Xu Xiànzhī, the Left Sīmǎ, was appointed to temporarily manage the retained duties.
All important matters previously decided by Mùzhī
were now consulted with him.
The Duke wanted to rest his carriage in Cháng'ān
and strategize against Zhào and Wèi,
but upon Mùzhī's death,
he returned.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
he departed from Cháng'ān.
He appointed Guìyánggōng Yìzhēn as General Ānxī and Inspector of Yōngzhōu,
leaving trusted generals and aides to assist him.
In the intercalary month,
the Duke entered the Yellow River from Luò,
opened the Biànqú Canal, and returned home.
In the first month of the fourteenth year, on the day Rénxū,
Gōng arrived at Péngchéng,
and lifted the martial law, putting away the armor.
He appointed Fǔguó Jiāngjūn Liú Zūnkǎo as the Cìshǐ of Bìngzhōu,
concurrently the Tàishǒu of Hédōng,
to guard Púbǎn.
Gōng resigned from Sīzhōu,
and concurrently held the Cìshǐ positions of Xú and Jì two zhōu,
firmly declining the advancement of his peerage.
In the sixth month,
he received the nine bestown honors from Xiàngguó Sònggōng.
The order stated:
"I, with my meager virtue,
bear an exceptionally heavy burden;
guarding my position and serving the vassalage,
I fear exceeding my bounds.
The imperial grace is grand and abundant,
attributing merits and offering praises,
thus making me equal to Qí and Jìn,
and considering the national rites.
Although I have sincerely maintained my duty
for ten years now,
the imperial decree has not been rescinded,
and all officials, both within and outside the court,
have diligently encouraged me.
Relying on the achievements brought by fate,
participating in these glorious deeds,
with my humble capabilities,
I share in the matters of great virtue.
I ponder deeply,
unsure of where to entrust my fate.
At the beginning of this grand fortune,
I wish to extend this joyous occasion.
Therefore, within the state, all crimes from 'death penalty with mitigating circumstances' downwards,
committed before dawn on the twenty-third day of this month,
shall all be pardoned.
For the widowed, orphaned, and solitary who cannot sustain themselves,
each person shall be granted five hú of grain.
Criminal cases in the government and prefectures
shall also be completely cleared.
Other matters shall strictly follow the old regulations."
An imperial edict honored Yùzhāng Gōng Tàifūren as Sònggōng Tàifēi,
and the Heir Apparent, Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn,
as the second in command of the Xiàngguó Fǔ.
Tàiwèi Jūnzī Jìjiǔ Kǒng Jìgōng was appointed as Sòngguó Shàngshūlìng,
Qīngzhōu Cìshǐ Tán Zhǐ as Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn,
and Xiàngguó Zuǒ Chángshǐ Wáng Hóng as Shàngshū Púyè.
All other hundred officials were to follow the system of the imperial court.
Another edict also stipulated that beyond the ten commanderies enfeoffed to Sòngguó,
he was free to make appointments.
Before this, Ānxī Zhōngbīng Cānjūn Shěn Tiánzǐ had killed Ānxī Sīmǎ Wáng Zhèn'è,
and the various generals then killed Ānxī Zhǎngshǐ Wáng Xiū.
Guānzhōng fell into chaos.
In the tenth month,
Gōng dispatched Yòujiāngjūn Zhū Língshí to replace Ānxī Jiāngjūn Guìyáng Gōng Yìzhēn as Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ.
After Yìzhēn's return,
he was pursued by the Fófó captives,
suffered a great defeat,
and barely escaped with his life.
The various generals and Zhū Língshí were all lost.
Lǐngjūn Tán Zhǐ died,
and Zhōngjūn Sīmǎ Tán Dàojì was appointed as Zhōnglǐngjūn.
In the twelfth month,
the Son of Heaven passed away,
and Dàsīmǎ Lángxié Wáng ascended the throne.
In the first month of Yuánxī first year,
an imperial edict was issued, dispatching an envoy to summon Gōng to assist the government.
It also reiterated the previous command,
advancing Gōng's peerage to Wáng.
The ten commanderies of Hǎilíng, North Dōnghǎi, North Qiáo, and North Liáng of Xúzhōu, Xīncài of Yùzhōu, North Chénliú of Yǎnzhōu, and Chénjùn, Rǔnán, Yǐngchuān, and Xíngyáng of Sīzhōu,
were added to Sòngguó.
〔一五〕In the seventh month,
he accepted the command,
and pardoned crimes punishable by five years of imprisonment or less within the state.
The capital was moved to Shòuyáng.
Shàngshū Liú Huáishèn was appointed as Běixúzhōu Cìshǐ,
to guard Péngchéng.
In the ninth month,
he resigned from Yángzhōu.
In the twelfth month,
the Son of Heaven commanded that Wáng's crown should have twelve tassels,
that he should erect the Son of Heaven's banner and flag,
that a clear path be made for him when he went out and entered,
that he ride in a golden chariot,
drawn by six horses,
that five seasonal auxiliary chariots be prepared,
that a máotóu and yúnhǎn be placed,
that there be a dance of eight rows,
and that bells and chime stands be set up.
Wáng Tàifēi was promoted to Tàihòu,
Wángfēi to Wánghòu,
the Heir Apparent to Tàizǐ,
and the titles and peerage of the Wángzǐ and Wángsūn,
all followed the old rites.
In the fourth month of the second year,
Wáng was summoned to assist the government.
In the sixth month,
he arrived at Jīngshī.
Emperor Jìn abdicated in favor of Wáng,
and the imperial edict stated: "When Heaven created the primeval chaos,
it established overseers,
thereby shaping the three realms and governing and transforming all under heaven.
Therefore, when the Great Dao prevails,
the worthy and capable are selected.
Rise and fall
have no fixed period,
and succession is not confined to one clan;
this has spanned a hundred kings
and has been so since ancient times.
The way of Jìn has declined,
with many troubles through successive generations;
since Yuánxīng,
calamities have piled up.
Until the three lights shifted positions,
and the crown and shoes swapped places,
Ānhuáng was exiled,
and the ancestral sacrifices were abandoned and extinguished,
then the fortune of our Xuān and Yuán
was forever cast to the ground.
Looking around the realm,
it was already utterly collapsing.
Xiàngguó Sòngwáng,
endowed by Heaven with sacred virtue,
his divine martial prowess outstanding in his generation,
rectified the decaying fortune
and re-established the Central Plains.
He has indeed revived the extinguished and continued the severed,
acting as a boat for those who were sinking.
As for
looking up to the celestial spheres,
and observing the seven luminaries,
he chastised the disobedient
and restored the lost territories.
Thus, he captured three false rulers,
cleansed the five
capitals,
and even the lands of tattooed faces and grass garments,
and the chiefs of the dragon wastes and northern deserts,
all turned their heads towards the rising sun
and bathed in his profound grace.
Therefore, the four spirits displayed auspicious omens,
and rivers and mountains revealed propitious diagrams;
auspicious signs mingled,
and glorious responses shone brightly.
The celestial phenomena indicated the time for revolution,
and both Chinese and barbarians expressed their desire to peacefully endorse.
The omens for the transfer of virtue
are manifest in both the visible and invisible.
The crow perched
where it was meant to,
truly gathering the enlightened and wise.
How could it be merely that Yánkāng has a home,
and Xiánxī announces its end?
Formerly, when the virtue of fire was weak,
the ancestor of Wèi achieved his功;
when the Yellow Dragon's fortune was not competing,
the three later empresses diligently served.
Therefore, Heaven's calendar count
truly has its fixed place.
Although I am dull
and ignorant of the Great Dao,
my perpetual observation of rise and fall
has been for a long time.
Considering the noble righteousness of the four dynasties,
and consulting the ultimate hopes of Heaven and man,
I shall abdicate my throne to another palace,
and yield
the throne to Sòng,
all in accordance with the precedents of Táng, Yú, Hàn, and Wèi."
After the draft of the edict was completed,
it was sent to the Son of Heaven for him to personally write it.
The Son of Heaven immediately took up his brush
and said to his attendants:
"During Huán Xuán's time,
Heaven's mandate had already changed,
but it was prolonged again by Liú Gōng,
for nearly twenty years.
Today's matter
is what I have long been content with."
On the day Jiǎzǐ,
the decree stated: "I inform you, Sòngwáng: When the primeval antiquity began,
it was vast and distant,
and its details cannot be heard.
From the time of written characters,
down to the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors,
all
were sagely rulers of the four seas,
who halted warfare and established great enterprises.
Thus, emperors and kings
are the universal instruments for governing all things;
the way of the ruler
is the utmost impartiality under Heaven.
In the past,
葉,
deeply understood this Way.
Therefore, when Heaven's mandate finally ceased,
Táng and Yú did not manage to pass on their lineage;
when the heavenly signs arrived and concurred,
Shùn and Yǔ could not maintain their humility.
Thus,
to govern the three cosmic powers,
to clarify and order the eternal transformations,
to set a model for antiquity,
and to leave a legacy for myriad generations,
nothing surpasses this.
From that time onward,
through successive dynasties, this grew ever more splendid.
The Hàn dynasty inherited the virtue
of Fàngxūn,
and Wèi also walked the path of Chónghuá.
It is truly because they worked in concert with both men and spirits,
and took the welfare of the people as their heart.
Formerly, our ancestors were reverent and enlightened,
residing at the apex of power,
but the succession of brightness and darkness,
and the waxing and waning, have their appointed times.
The fall of Shāng foreshadowed disaster,
not just for one generation;
if even that
could not be overcome,
how much more so now?
That which Heaven abandons,
has its reasons from antiquity.
However, Your Majesty embodies the disposition of a supreme sage,
encompassing the virtues of the two cosmic forces.
Your brilliance matches the sun and moon;
Your Way accords with the four
seasons.
When the altars of earth and grain were overturned,
Your Majesty rescued and preserved them.
When the Central Plains were overgrown and chaotic,
You again brought aid and restored them.
From those who stubbornly refused to submit,
transgressed the laws, and defied mandates,
to those who committed
crimes reaching to the heavens,
and usurped territory for ten thousand *lǐ* –
none were not moistened by Your winds and rains,
nor shaken by Your thunder and lightning.
The Way of the Nine Punishments has been thoroughly applied,
and the transformation of the Eight Laws has naturally brought order.
How could it be merely to bestow generosity upon the people,
and save the common folk?
It is truly that Your righteousness pervades the four seas,
and Your Way overawes the eight wildernesses.
As for Heaven displaying its signs,
and the Four Numinous Beasts manifesting their portents,
the texts of *túchèn* are already clear,
and the hopes of gods and men have changed.
The hundred officials sing in the court,
the common people chant in the wilds,
the myriad masses clap and dance,
eagerly awaiting a new era.
If it were not
that the people gladly support this,
and Heaven's mandate is gathered here,
how could I,
be able to exclusively possess it?
Therefore, I reverently look up to the imperial spirits,
and humbly comply with the public consensus.
I respectfully abdicate the divine implements,
and bestow the imperial
throne upon your person.
The great fortune has ended,
and Heaven's mandate is forever concluded.
Alas!
May Your Majesty indeed hold fast to the Mean,
reverently follow the established principles,
fulfill the noble wishes of all within the four seas,
and expand
this grand enterprise without end.
May You constantly receive blessings and good fortune,
to respond to the earnest expectations of the three spiritual powers.
Moreover, the imperial decree states: I have heard that Heaven gives birth to the myriad people,
and establishes rulers over them.
Emperors, as they appear in the world,
are truly for the public good of the four seas.
Rise and fall depend on merit and virtue;
advancement and decline rest with the individual.
Thus, every state that exists must perish;
the years of its reign are recorded in divination.
Succession is not constant;
sages and enlightened ones grasp its token.
In ancient times,
the three sages followed this path;
they consulted the Four Chiefs,
to
magnanimously practice abdication.
The achievements of the former kings
forever set a model for endless generations.
When the Liú clan abdicated,
they truly emulated Yáo.
When Wèi announced its end,
it also followed this
precedent.
It is how our founding ancestor grasped the changing fortune and complied with human affairs,
seized the opportune moment and secured Heaven's blessing.
But the Way is not always stable;
barbarians brought chaos to Huá,
causing us to lose
our Lo-eating lands,
and forcing the state south of the Jiāng.
Then we encountered unfortunate destiny,
and suffered continuous decline and ruin.
Up to Yuánxīng,
the imperial sacrifices were finally overthrown.
Fortunately, thanks to divine military prowess illuminating Heaven,
and great principles
being grandly initiated,
our altars of earth and grain were restored,
and our nation was rebuilt.
Your Majesty's sagely virtue is reverent and enlightened,
emulating Heaven's brilliance and greatness.
Responding to the appointed time, You were born,
and clearly protected the royal house.
Internally, You
alleviated national difficulties;
externally, You spread grand strategies.
You executed the arch-villains at Hànyáng,
and banished the usurping thieves to Yízhǔ.
You cleared the disorder in Xīmín,
and pacified Nányuè.
You twice calmed Jiāng and Xiāng,
and expanded
and secured Fán and Miǎn.
As for harboring the ambition to unify the realm,
and desiring to bring all under one culture and teaching,
when the royal army set out,
the Yī and Luò rivers flowed clear;
when its formidable power reached Xiáo and Tóng,
Huàshān dispelled
its mists.
The false chieftain offered his jade disk in surrender,
and Xiányáng was immediately brought to order.
Though inscribed on bronze vessels,
and sung in odes and histories,
the greatness of Your achievements
has no equal.
Thus, You laid down arms and cultivated
culture,
grandly extending virtuous governance.
With the Eight Regulations, You governed the myriad people;
with the Nine Offices, You administered the states.
You sought to encompass the Three Kings,
and implement the Four Affairs.
Therefore, You are trusted by both the visible and invisible worlds,
and Your righteousness
moves distant lands.
From those who have been subject through generations,
to where boats and chariots can reach,
none fail to sing praises of Your benevolence and virtue,
and dance in welcome at Your court.
I always respectfully ponder the Way's achievements,
and continually observe the cycle of mandates.
Heaven's tally of destiny
truly rests with Your person.
Therefore, the five planets ascend to their positions,
repeatedly showing signs of removing the old;
the three luminaries align their numbers,
certainly manifesting omens of inaugurating the new.
*Túchèn* and auspicious portents
are clearly present.
Moreover, Your dragon-like countenance is exceptional,
a unique appearance bestowed by Heaven.
Your majestic
bearing as a ruler
shines like the sun and moon.
Tradition states,
"Only Heaven is great,
and Yáo emulated it."
The *Shī* says,
"There is a mandate from Heaven,
mandating this Wénwáng."
Indeed,
"one who leaps in
the abyss"
will ultimately
enjoy the position of the ninth-five line;
"one whose achievements reach Heaven and Earth"
will certainly
receive the great enterprise of the throne.
Formerly, when the virtue of Earth announced its end,
the succession was passed to our Jìn.
Now,
the cycle of destiny has changed its oracle,
and will forever end here,
also passing from the virtue of Metal to Sòng.
Looking up to the splendid righteousness of the four previous dynasties,
and observing the regular pattern of clarity and obscurity,
I consulted the various dukes,
Thus, when it came to all the various ministers,
they all said, "How auspicious!"
None opposed My will.
Now, I dispatch Dàn, holding the imperial staff, concurrently Grand Protector (Tài Bǎo), Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary (Sàn Qí Cháng Shì), and Grand Master of Remonstrance (Guāng Lù Dà Fū),
and Xuān Fàn, concurrently Grand Commandant (Tài
Wèi) and President of the Department of State Affairs (Shàng Shū), to present the emperor's imperial seals and ribbons.
The ceremony of accepting the abdication
shall be entirely in accordance with the precedents of Táng, Yú, Hàn, and Wèi.
May the King truly respond to humanity and the gods,
reign over all nations,
and at this opportune time, receive divine blessings,
thereby fulfilling the mandate of Heaven's favor.
The King presented a memorial declining the offer,
but the Jìn emperor had already abdicated to the residence of the Prince of Lángxié,
so the memorial could not be delivered.
Thereupon, Chénliú Wáng Qiánsì and two hundred seventy others,
along with the officials of the Sòng court,
all submitted memorials urging him to ascend the throne.
Still, the King did not consent.
The Grand Astrologer (Tài Shǐ Lìng) Luò Dá presented dozens of celestial portents and auspicious omens,
and the multitude of officials again earnestly requested him,
whereupon the King complied.
Collation Notes
Basic Annals (Běn Jì) Volume Three, Emperor Wǔ, Part Two
In the summer, the sixth month, on the Dīng Mǎo day of Yǒngchū first year [420 CE],
an altar was erected in the southern suburbs,
and he ascended the imperial throne,
offering a burnt sacrifice to Heaven.
The pronouncement read: "I, the Emperor's subject, Yù,
dare to use a dark bull
to solemnly announce to August Heaven and Empress Earth.
The Jìn emperor, having announced the exhaustion of his dynastic fate,
with the Mandate of Heaven now returned,
reverently accepts this grand destiny,
and entrusts
it to Me, Yù.
Indeed, the establishment of a ruler to govern the world
is for the public good of all under Heaven.
When virtue fills an emperor or king,
the people gladly gather to support him.
From the beginning of Táng and Yú,
down to Hàn and Wèi,
there was none
who did not, by supreme wisdom, connect with the cultured ancestors,
and by primal merit, ascend the imperial throne.
Thus, they were able to greatly save the common people
and leave teachings for endless generations.
Since the Jìn moved eastward,
the four cardinal virtues have not been upheld,
and where the grand ministers
relied,
it has been so for a long time.
The difficulties of Lóng'ān and
the disaster of Yuánxīng
led to the emperor's displacement
and the extinction of ancestral sacrifices.
Although I, Yù, am not from Qí or Jìn in terms of territory,
nor do I have
even one company of troops,
I looked up in indignation at the difficulties of the time
and looked down in sorrow at the widespread suffering.
I threw up my sleeves and gave a single command,
and the imperial sacrifices were restored.
And when in peril, I was able to sustain;
when fallen, I was able to uphold.
The traitors and evildoers
were all exterminated,
and the usurpers and pretenders were certainly destroyed.
Truly, the rise and fall have their appointed time;
misfortune ending has its definite number.
As for greatly restoring the Jìn imperial house,
quelling chaos and aiding the people,
I relied on the opportune moment
and indeed bore
this heavy responsibility.
Furthermore, people of different customs admire righteousness,
and translators from distant lands come to court.
Wherever the imperial calendar extends,
all submit to its prestige and teachings.
Even the three spiritual powers manifested auspicious signs,
mountains and rivers announced good omens,
and human
and divine blessings converged,
becoming increasingly evident with each passing year.
Therefore, the multitude of dukes, ministers, and officials,
and the countless common people,
all said that the imperial spirits descended to inspect from above,
and the Jìn court sincerely offered from below,
that Heaven's
mandate cannot be long delayed,
and the imperial throne cannot be left vacant for a moment.
Thus, compelled by the unanimous opinion,
I respectfully undertake this great ceremony.
Humbly, with my meager virtue,
I am entrusted above the myriad people.
Although I look up in awe of Heaven's majesty,
and disregard these minor formalities,
I deeply harbor eternal thoughts
and am fearful as if falling.
Respectfully choosing
an auspicious day,
I ascend the altar and accept the abdication,
announcing and sacrificing to the Supreme Emperor,
thereby responding to the sentiments of all nations.
May Heaven's protection be greatly enhanced,
and forever bless the Sòng dynasty.
May the bright spirits accept this sacrifice."
After the ceremony,
he proceeded with the imperial carriage to Jiànkāng Palace,
and held court in the Tàijí Front Hall.
An imperial edict stated:
"Indeed, generations succeed each other,
receiving Heaven's mandate to rule.
Although the encounters differ
and the changes in affairs vary,
if one's achievements benefit the realm
and one's Way shakes the living people,
the path of rise and fall
is one and the same across different ages.
I, being of meager virtue,
found Myself in a time of great difficulty,
relying on the end of misfortune
and the strength of the scholars and common people.
Thus, I was able to save those drowning,
rectify the world, quell chaos,
and bring peace to the nation and its people.
My achievements are not half of those of antiquity,
but My merit parallels the great deeds of the past.
The Jìn clan, having repeatedly encountered many difficulties,
its dynastic fortune already shifted,
reverently observed the former kings
and followed the established rules,
thereby bestowing the great mandate upon My person.
My virtue being insufficient,
I could not decline,
and so I reverently obeyed the three spiritual powers
and accepted this grand blessing.
I performed the burnt sacrifice in the southern suburbs
and accepted the abdication in the ancestral temple.
Humbly, in this time of shared ability,
the destiny of popular acclaim has gathered.
Auspicious blessings have begun,
and grand joy is just starting.
I wish to bestow felicitous grace
upon these myriad common people.
Therefore, a general amnesty is granted to all under Heaven.
Jìn Yuánxī Second Year is changed to Yǒngchū First Year.
The people are granted two ranks of nobility.
For the widowed, orphaned, solitary, and those unable to support themselves,
each person shall receive five *hú* of grain.
Outstanding rents and old debts shall no longer be collected.
Those who have violated local public opinion and pure discourse, or committed bribery, lewdness, or theft,
shall all be cleansed and purified,
and granted a fresh start.
Those serving long sentences
shall all be specially pardoned and released.
Those who lost official positions, were deprived of titles,
imprisoned, or stripped of their labors
shall all follow the old regulations."
The Jìn emperor was enfeoffed as Línglíng Wáng,
with a full county as his domain.
He was allowed to carry the emperor's banners and pennants,
ride in the vice-carriages of the five seasons,
use the Jìn calendar,
and the ceremonial music and rituals for the suburban sacrifices to Heaven and Earth
were all to follow Jìn precedents.
His memorials were not to be called *biǎo* (memorials to the throne),
and responses to his memorials were not to be called *zhào* (imperial edicts).
His deceased father was posthumously honored as Xiàomù Huángdì,
and his deceased mother as Mù Huánghòu.
The Queen Mother Wáng was honored as Huáng Tàihòu.
An imperial edict stated:
"Indeed, the lamentation for the absence of Yǔ's influence
is deeply felt by later generations.
Great virtue must be commemorated with sacrifices,
and the Way, when grand, extends for a hundred generations.
The Jìn clan's enfeoffments and titles
all changed with the shift in destiny.
However, regarding those whose virtue paralleled Wēi and Guǎn,
and whose meritorious deeds aided the common people,
who were loved by the people and had trees planted in their memory,
these should not be cut down.
Even across different eras,
their significance should not be obliterated.
The appropriate reduction in status
shall entirely follow previous precedents.
Shǐxīng Gōng may be demoted to Shǐxīng Xiàn Gōng,
Lúlíng Gōng to Cháisāng Xiàn Gōng,
each with a thousand households;
Shǐ'ān Gōng to Lìpǔ Xiàn Hóu,
Chángshā Gōng to Lǐlíng Xiàn Hóu,
Kānglè Gōng may be directly enfeoffed as a Xiàn Hóu,

each with five hundred households: to maintain the sacrifices for the former Jìn Chancellor (chéngxiàng) Wáng Dǎo, Grand Tutor (tài fù) Xiè Ān, Grand General (dà jiāngjūn) Wēn Jiào, Grand Commander (dà sīmǎ) Táo Kǎn, and Cavalry General (chē qí jiāngjūn) Xiè Xuán.
As for those who exerted their strength in Yìxī [405-418 CE]
and shared in the difficulties,
their original ranks shall all be retained,
without any reduction."
Jìn Línchuān Wáng Sīmǎ Bǎo was enfeoffed as Xīfēng Xiàn Hóu,
with an estate of a thousand households.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Sīkōng Dào-lián was appointed Tàiwèi,
and enfeoffed as the King of Chángshā.
Sītú Dào-guī was posthumously enfeoffed as the King of Línchuān.
Shàngshū Púshè Xú Xiàn-zhī was promoted to Zhèn-jūn Jiāngjūn,
Yòu-wèi Jiāngjūn Xiè Huì to Zhōng-lǐng-jūn,
Sòng-guó Lǐng-jūn Tán Dào-jì to Hù-jūn Jiāngjūn,
and Zhōng-lǐng-jūn Liú Yì-xīn to Qīngzhōu Cìshǐ.
Nánjùn Gōng Yì-qìng was established as the King of Línchuān.
An imperial edict also stated:
"To record merits and commemorate efforts
is a vital canon for a state,
and to be diligent in the end and remember the old
is what is highly esteemed in the heart.
Since the great enterprise was founded
seventeen years ago,
the world has been in turmoil,
and military chariots have moved annually.
From east to west,
there has been no day of peace.
It truly relied on the generals and commanders exhausting their hearts,
and the civil and military officials giving their utmost performance,
to pacify internally and expand externally,
finally achieving success.
Our awe-inspiring majesty has spread far and wide,
rebels and traitors have been eliminated,
and thus the ritual of abdication was performed,
and the imperial mandate was bestowed upon us.
Remembering merits and recalling efforts,
we never forget them even in sleep.
All those who showed sincerity and diligence
should share in the national celebration.
Let the regulations for rewards, commendations, and exemptions
be deliberated and implemented in due time.
For those who died in battle,
generous posthumous grants and gifts shall be bestowed."
On the day Yǐhài,
Guìyáng Gōng Yì-zhēn was established as the King of Lúlíng,
Péngchéng Gōng Yì-lóng as the King of Yídū,
and the fourth imperial son Yì-kāng as the King of Péngchéng.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
an imperial edict stated:
"Ancient kings,
in their inspection tours of the regions,
personally observed the people and things,
sought out and promoted the hidden talents,
relieved disasters and cared for the suffering,
thus enabling their benevolent influence to spread far,
bringing peace to the distant and near.
We, being of limited understanding,
fall short of the former sagacious rulers.
By virtue of receiving the mandate of heaven,
we are entrusted with the leadership of the myriad people.
Day and night, our thoughts are preoccupied
with seeking to understand the people's ailments.
Our abilities are weak, and matters are difficult,
as if without a ford to cross.
We are vigilant even at night, with perpetual thoughts,
our heart racing to distant regions.
Therefore, special envoys shall be dispatched to travel to the four directions,
to commend the worthy and promote the good,
and to inquire about the people's sufferings.
Should there be any cases of unjust or excessive lawsuits,
or policies and punishments that are divergent and erroneous,
harming the transformation and disturbing governance,
and not complying with the people's sentiments,
all such matters must be fully reported.
All matters should be handled appropriately,
without deviating from the mean,
to articulate the imperial court's benevolent concern
and convey the suppressed feelings of the common people."
On the day Wùyín,
an imperial edict stated:
"The hundred officials are burdened with heavy duties but receive meager salaries,
their stipends not enough to substitute for farming.
Although the national reserves are not yet abundant,
it is essential to ensure sufficiency for both public and private needs.
All provisions that were previously halved
shall be fully restored to their original amount.
The current salaries of the six armies are generally acceptable and
are not subject to this rule.
As for other officials,
if their basic salaries have always been low,
they shall also be proportionally increased."
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the Jìn Tàishǐ Calendar was revised to the Yǒngchū Calendar.
In autumn, on the day Dīnghài of the seventh month,
the remaining individuals who were accomplices in robberies and confiscated to the imperial offices were pardoned and released.
All households that had been displaced were permitted to return to their native lands.
Furthermore, the transport of timber and transport ships
shall no longer be exacted from various commanderies,
but entirely entrusted to the Duh-shuǐ office for separate assessment.
Whatever the imperial offices require
shall be separately handled by dispatching chief officers to purchase goods from the people at fair prices,
compensating them immediately,
and no longer demanding rent or requiring the people to procure them.
Moreover, the use of carts and oxen seized from captives was abolished,
and they are not to be commandeered under official authority.
Additionally, due to the burdensome nature of market taxes,
they shall be generously reduced.
For those who joined the expedition to Guān and Luò,
perished on the battlefield,
or went missing and did not return,
their families shall be given relief and grants.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the King of Chénliú, Cáo Qián-sì, passed away.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the offices of the five garrisons and three generals were reinstated,
and the number of Diànzhōng Jiāngjūn was increased by twenty,
with others remaining outside the official quota.
On the day Wùxū,
Hòu-jiāngjūn and Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Zhào Lún-zhī was promoted to Ān-běi Jiāngjūn,
Zhēnglǔ Jiāngjūn and Běi-xúzhōu Cìshǐ Liú Huái-shèn was promoted to Běi-píng Jiāngjūn,
and Zhēng-xī Dàjiāngjūn and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī Yáng Shèng was promoted to Chēqí Dàjiāngjūn.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Zhèn-xī Jiāngjūn Lǐ Xīn was promoted to Zhēng-xī Jiāngjūn,
Píng-xī Jiāngjūn Qǐfú Chì-pán was promoted to Ān-xī Dàjiāngjūn,
Zhēng-dōng Jiāngjūn and King of Gāogōulí Gāo Lián was promoted to Zhēng-dōng Dàjiāngjūn,
and Zhèn-dōng Jiāngjūn and King of Bǎijì Fúyú Yìng was promoted to Zhèn-dōng Dàjiāngjūn.
The offices of Dōnggōng Rǒngcóng Púshè and Lǚbēn Zhōnglángjiāng were established.
On the day Wùshēn,
the spirit tablets were moved to the Tàimiào,
with the imperial carriage personally attending.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an imperial edict stated:
"In the past, military and state affairs were pressing,
requiring expedient measures;
the laws against robbery were severe,
implemented for a specific period.
Now that the benevolent rule is renewed,
and governance is harmonious and laws are simplified,
these laws can be entirely abolished
and the old regulations reinstated.
Regarding rebels, traitors, and those guilty of three offenses of illicit sexual activity or theft being conscripted as artisans,
it originally referred to committing the same offense three times,
implying no reform.
However, those in charge recently often combined multiple offenses,
counting them as three,
which greatly violates the spirit of the original enactment;
this shall be broadly re-clarified."
In the eighth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Xī-zhōnglángjiāng and Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ, the King of Yídū, Yì-lóng, was promoted to Zhèn-xī Jiāngjūn.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
a pardon for defectors and rebels was issued:
those who surrendered within the specified period
were exempted from rent and cloth taxes for two years.
Those who previously had property deeds and household registers still preserved
were permitted to restore their original registrations.
All old commanderies and prefectures named 'North' (Běi) were
all abolished;
those established temporarily in the south
were permitted to be named 'South' (Nán).
Furthermore, the regulation that those who deliberately self-mutilated for no reason should be conscripted as artisans
was truly due to harsh and troublesome policies and punishments,
which the people could not endure;
this clause shall be abolished.
Qīngzhōu was abolished and merged with Yǎnzhōu.
On the day Wùchén,
an imperial edict stated:
"The three commanderies of Péng, Pèi, and Xiàpī
were where the enterprise began,
with deep affection and loyalty.
Accomplishments are spurred by affection,
a truth common to ancient and modern times.
Péngchéng, as our ancestral home,
holds a place of special honor.
Its preferential exemption regulations
should be the same as Fēng and Pèi.
Therefore, Pèi-jùn and Xiàpī shall be granted rent and cloth tax exemptions for thirty years."
On the *xīnwèi* day,
the Emperor posthumously bestowed the title of Jìng Huánghòu (敬皇后) upon Consort Zāng (臧氏).
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
the royal heir apparent was established as the Crown Prince.
On the *yǐhài* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"We have received the mandate of Heaven and the succession of the calendar,
and have been entrusted with the heavenly decree.
We are blessed with the good fortune accumulated through virtuous deeds,
and rely on the strength of Our officials and people.
The seven ancestral temples are complete with rituals,
following the excellent precedents.
The former empress and empress mother are reverently honored,
and their instructions are duly followed.
Sacrifices for the ancestors have been duly established,
with sincere reverence.
Furthermore, with the Crown Prince's palace fully equipped with rites,
the imperial foundation is increasingly secure.
National celebrations and family rituals
have occurred one after another in recent days.
How can We, alone,
bear this joy?
Therefore, all those currently undergoing criminal punishment, regardless of severity,
are to be pardoned.
This is limited to one hundred days,
starting from today.
Slaves and servants previously conscripted for military affairs
shall each return to their original masters.
If any have died, or earned merits leading to their freedom or release,
their value shall be repaid within the same time limit."
On the *rénwǔ* day, the first day of the intercalary month,
an imperial edict stated:
"Regarding the guards for the imperial tombs of the Jìn (晉) dynasty and the various princely mausoleums,
appropriate regulations should be immediately established.
As for the tombs of prominent worthies and ancient sages
who were highly esteemed in previous eras,
who either established virtue and displayed integrity
or pacified chaos and protected the people,
and whose graves are not far,
they should all be swept and maintained.
The responsible officials shall present a detailed report."
On the *dīngyǒu* day, Kǒng Jìgōng (孔季恭), *Tèjìn* (特進) and *Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū* (左光祿大夫), was additionally granted the title of *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī* (開府儀同三司).
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Although officials in charge of cases often consult extensively,
when officials are ordered to deliberate,
they should do so with clarity and thoroughness.
Recently, some have merely used the general term 'consultation' (*cānxiáng*, 參詳),
which is vague in official documents.
From now on, anyone who has a specific opinion
must explicitly name the person.
If opinions differ,
the old practice of submitting separate reports shall be followed."
Another edict stated:
"Regarding the dispatch of winter envoys (*dōngshǐ*, 冬使) to various places,
some are sent and some are not.
Such duties should be curtailed,
and all are now to be stopped.
Only during the great celebrations of the New Year's Day (*yuánzhēng*, 元正)
are they not subject to this rule.
The dispatch of winter envoys from commanderies and counties to the provincial capital and the *Dūdūfǔ* (都督府)
is also to be stopped."
On the *rénzǐ* day, the first day of the ninth month,
ten *Dōnggōng Diànzhōng Jiāngjūn* (東宮殿中將軍) were established for the Eastern Palace,
along with twenty supernumerary officials (*yuánwài*, 員外).
On the *rénshēn* day,
the office of *Dūguān Shàngshū* (都官尚書) was established.
In winter, on the *xīnmǎo* day of the tenth month,
the Jìn (晉) dynasty's ritual period of twenty-six months for *wángsùxiángtǎn* (王肅祥禫) was changed,
to follow Zhèng Xuán's (鄭玄) twenty-seven months before ending mourning.
On the *xīnsì* day, the first day of the twelfth month,
the imperial carriage went to Yánxián Táng (延賢堂) to hear lawsuits.
In the second year, on the *xīnyǒu* day of the first month of spring,
the imperial carriage offered sacrifices at the southern suburbs,
and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
the use of gold and silver plating was prohibited.
Lúlíng Wáng Yìzhēn (廬陵王義真), Governor of Yángzhōu (揚州), was appointed *Sītú* (司徒).
Xú Xiànzhī (徐羨之), *Shàngshū Púyè* (尚書僕射) and *Zhèn Jūn Jiāngjūn* (鎮軍將軍), was appointed *Shàngshū Lìng* (尚書令) and Governor of Yángzhōu.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
the Mán (蠻) tribes in Nánkāng Jiēyáng (南康揭陽) rebelled,
and the commanderies and counties attacked and defeated them.
On the *jǐmǎo* day,
the use of bronze nails in funerals was prohibited.
The administration of Kuàijī Commandery (會稽郡) was abolished.
In the second month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
the imperial carriage visited Yánxián Táng to examine and test *xiùcái* (秀才) and *xiàolián* (孝廉) from various provinces and commanderies.
Gù Liàn (顧練), a *xiùcái* from Yángzhōu, and Yīn Lǎng (殷朗), a *xiùcái* from Yùzhōu (豫州), whose answers accorded with the imperial will,
were both appointed *Zhùzuò Zuǒláng* (著作佐郎).
On the *wùshēn* day,
it was decreed that officials holding the rank of *Zhōng Èrqiān Shí* (中二千石) should receive an additional one hundred *qǐng* of public land.
In the third month, on the *yǐchǒu* day,
for the first time, limits were set for the staff of the Jīngzhōu (荊州) administration: the number of generals was not to exceed two thousand,
and the number of civil officials was not to exceed ten thousand.
For other provincial administrations, the number of generals was not to exceed five hundred,
and the number of civil officials was not to exceed five thousand.
Soldiers were not included in these limits.
In summer, on the *jǐmǎo* day, the first day of the fourth month,
an imperial edict stated:
"Excessive sacrifices (*yíncí*, 淫祠) that mislead the people and waste resources,
which were prohibited by previous regulations,
shall all be ordered to be removed by the local authorities, along with their various temples.
However, shrines established for ancient worthies or based on meritorious deeds
are not subject to this rule."
On the *wùshēn* day,
the imperial carriage heard lawsuits in Huálín Yuán (華林園).
On the *jǐhài* day,
Wáng Zhòngdé (王仲德), *Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn* (左衞將軍), was appointed Governor of Jìzhōu (冀州).
In the fifth month, on the *jǐyǒu* day,
the offices of three commandants (*xiàowèi*, 校尉) for the Eastern Palace's cavalry (*túnqí*, 屯騎), infantry (*bùbīng*, 步兵), and elite guards (*yìjūn*, 翊軍) were established.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the imperial carriage again visited Huálín Yuán to hear lawsuits.
In the sixth month, on the *rénzhōng* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Although corporal punishment by rod (*zhàngfá*, 杖罰) has old regulations,
due to the numerous and fragmented duties,
investigations and punishments follow one after another.
If all were truly guilty,
their bodies could not withstand it;
if it is merely a formality,
it defeats the purpose of establishing punishment.
Therefore, a rough standard for moderate and light punishments should be deliberated upon."
The imperial carriage again heard lawsuits in Huálín Yuán.
On the *jiǎchén* day,
it was decreed that officials from the fourth rank downwards in various government offices,
as well as those punished by various administrative offices,
were permitted to receive forty strokes of the rod administered by the central government offices.
In autumn, on the *jǐsì* day of the seventh month,
there was an earthquake.
In the eighth month, on the *rénchén* day,
the imperial carriage again heard lawsuits in Huálín Yuán.
In the ninth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Línglíng Wáng (零陵王) passed away.
The imperial carriage, for three mornings, led all officials in mourning in the court hall,
following the precedent of Emperor Míng of Wèi (魏明帝) mourning for Shānyáng Gōng (山陽公).
The *Tàiwèi* (太尉), bearing the imperial credential, supervised
the funeral according to Jìn (晉) rituals.
In winter, on the *dīngyǒu* day of the tenth month,
an imperial edict stated:
"Military regulations are severe and strict,
but suitability is paramount.
When a conscript dies or deserts,
their collateral relatives are immediately investigated,
leading to widespread displacement,
with no apparent end.
This results in people of rank and status
being wrongly implicated.
Therefore, it is fitting to reform this with magnanimity,
and remove these harsh laws.
From now on, if a criminal is to serve in the military and their entire household is to be conscripted,
they shall be handed over to the camp for supervision.
If the household head or only one person is punished,
[一０]no relatives shall be implicated
or suffer guilt by association."
On the *jǐhài* day, Dà Jǔqú Méngxùn (大沮渠蒙遜), the Hú (胡) chieftain of Liángzhōu (涼州), was appointed *Zhèn Jūn Dà Jiāngjūn* (鎮軍大將軍), *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī* (開府儀同三司), and Governor of Liángzhōu.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
the imperial carriage heard lawsuits in Yánxián Táng,
and Yīng Xí (應襲), *Yuánwài Sànqí Chángshì* (員外散騎常侍), was appointed Governor of Níngzhōu (寧州).
In the third year, in spring, the first month, on the *jiǎchén* (甲辰) day,
an edict was issued that all punishments, regardless of their severity,
were to be pardoned and commuted.
On the *rénzǐ* (壬子) day,
Wáng Zhòngdé (王仲德), formerly the Inspector of Jìzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Xúzhōu.
On the *guǐchǒu* (癸丑) day,
Xú Xiànzhī (徐羨之), Administrator of the Department of State Affairs and Inspector of Yángzhōu, was appointed *Sīkōng* (司空) and Supervisor of the Department of State Affairs (錄尚書事),
retaining his inspectorate as before.
Wáng Hóng (王弘), General of the Garrison and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, was promoted to General of the Guards (衞將軍) and granted the title of *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī* (開府儀同三司).
Fù Liàng (傅亮), Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince, was appointed Administrator of the Left (尚書僕射).
Xiè Huì (謝晦), Central Leader of the Army, was appointed Leader of the Army (領軍將軍).
On the *yǐmǎo* (乙卯) day,
Máo Dézǔ (毛德祖), General of the Garrison, was appointed Inspector of Sīzhōu.
〔一一〕On the *yǐchǒu* (乙丑) day,
an imperial edict stated:
“In ancient times, when states were established,
education was considered paramount.
To promote customs and instruct the world,
nothing is more important than this.
To enlighten the ignorant and stimulate the dull,
all must depend on it.
Therefore, from the time of prosperous kings
down to recent ages,
none failed to honor learning and arts
and establish schools and academies.
Since ancient times, there have been many troubles,
with warhorses at the city gates,
banners unfurled and furled,
allowing no leisure in a day.
This has led to the decay of schools,
the neglect of reading and recitation,
the daily deployment of armies,
and the storage of sacrificial vessels,
causing the spirit of education and guidance
to almost fall to the ground.
The younger generation greatly fears being ignorant,
and the old secretly sigh at the lack of scholars.
This is why the ‘Airs of the States’ (國風) are forever contemplated,
and the ‘Minor Odes’ (小雅) recall the past.
Now, the King’s dominion extends far and wide,
and the Chinese territories are again peaceful.
Scholars who aspire to virtue
hope for this day by day.
It is fitting to widely recruit imperial descendants,
cultivate and encourage the young,
select and equip Confucian officials,
and greatly revitalize the national academy.
Let the responsible officials examine old statutes
and implement them in due course.”
In the second month, on the *dīngchǒu* (丁丑) day,
an imperial edict stated:
“Yùzhōu borders the Jiānghǔ (江滸) to the south
and connects to the Hé (河) and Luò (洛) to the north.
Its people are scattered and its territory vast,
making transportation difficult and distant.
It is appropriate for its administration
to have its own conveniences.
The various commanderies west of the Huái (淮)
can be established as Yùzhōu;
those east of the Huái
will be Nányùzhōu.”
Yīkāng (義康), the Prince of Péngchéng and Inspector of Yùzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Nányùzhōu.
Liú Cuì (劉粹), General Who Quells Barbarians, was appointed Inspector of Yùzhōu.
Furthermore, ten commanderies of Jīngzhōu were separated to re-establish Xiāngzhōu.
Zhāng Shào (張邵), General of the Left Guards, was appointed Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
〔一二〕On the *wùyín* (戊寅) day,
Liáng (梁) commandery of Xúzhōu
was returned to Yùzhōu.
In the third month,
the Emperor became unwell.

DàoLián (道憐), the Grand Commandant and Prince of Chángshā, Xú Xiànzhī (徐羨之), the *Sīkōng*, Fù Liàng (傅亮), Administrator of the Left, Xiè Huì (謝晦), Leader of the Army, and Tán Dàojì (檀道濟), General of the Household, all attended with medicine.
The officials requested prayers to the deities,
but the Emperor refused,
only allowing *Shìzhōng* (侍中) Xiè Fāngmíng (謝方明) to report his illness to the ancestral temple.
On the *dīngwèi* (丁未) day,
Yìzhēn (義真), the *Sītú* (司徒) and Prince of Lúlín, was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry (車騎將軍), granted the title of *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*, and appointed Inspector of Nányùzhōu.
The Emperor’s illness recovered.
On the *jǐwèi* (己未) day,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
At this time, scattered households from Qín (秦) and Yōng (雍) all moved south into Liángzhōu.
On the *gēngshēn* (庚申) day,
ten thousand bolts of plain silk and damask were sent,
〔一三〕and rice was transported from Jīng (荊) and Yōng (雍) provinces.
The inspectors of the provinces were entrusted with distributing them as appropriate.
On the *xīnyǒu* (辛酉) day,
the fugitive Diāo Mí (刁彌) attacked the capital city
and managed to enter.
Lù Zhòngyuán (陸仲元), Grand Commandant’s Provost of the Left, pursued and executed him.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *yǐhài* (乙亥) day,
Yáng Shèng (楊盛), Duke of Qiúchí, was enfeoffed as King of Wǔdū.
Yáng Fǔ (楊撫), General Who Pacifies the South, was promoted to General Who Annalizes the South (安南將軍).
On the *dīnghài* (丁亥) day,
Xú Yǎn (徐琰), Provost of Chariots and Cavalry, was appointed Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
On the *gēngyín* (庚寅) day,
Kǒng Jìgōng (孔季恭), Grand Master of Remonstrance with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon and *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*, passed away.
In the fifth month,
the Emperor’s illness worsened.
He summoned the Crown Prince and admonished him, saying:
“Tán Dàojì (檀道濟), though capable and strategic,
has no grand ambitions,
unlike his elder brother Sháo (韶) who has an untameable spirit.
Xú Xiànzhī (徐羨之) and Fù Liàng (傅亮) should have no other schemes.
Xiè Huì (謝晦) has participated in many campaigns
and is quite familiar with stratagems and changes.
If there is any dissent or betrayal,
it will surely be this man.
After a slight recovery,
he can be placed in Kuàijī (會稽) or Jiāngzhōu.”
He also wrote a personal edict stating:
“The imperial court need not have separate administrations.
The Chancellor, when holding the inspectorship of Yángzhōu,
can be provided with a thousand armed guards.
If an important minister is required
to have protectors against ill-doers,
they can be assigned from the imperial guard.
