For any military campaigns, they are to be fully supplied with imperial troops,
and returned to their former duties upon completion.
Should there be a young ruler in future generations,
all court affairs are to be entrusted to the Chancellor,
and the Empress Dowager need not attend court.
Since guards are not permitted to enter the palace gates,
important individuals may be granted the privilege of carrying swords.”
On the *guǐhài* (癸亥) day,
the Emperor passed away in the Western Palace
at the age of sixty.
〔一四〕In autumn, the seventh month, on the *jǐyǒu* (己酉) day,
he was buried at Chūnínglíng (初寧陵) on Jiǎngshān (蔣山), Jiànkāng (建康) county, Dānyáng (丹陽).
The Emperor was pure, simple, and had few desires.
He was strict and orderly in his conduct.
He never looked upon the adornments of pearls, jade, carriages, or horses.
In his rear chambers, there was no sound of fine silk or music.
Níngzhōu once presented an amber pillow,
whose luster and color were exceedingly beautiful.
At that time, he was about to campaign north,
and amber was used to treat metal wounds.
The Emperor was greatly pleased,
and ordered it crushed and distributed among his generals.
When Guānzhōng was pacified,
he acquired Yáo Xīng’s (姚興) niece.
She was greatly favored,
and because of her, he neglected his duties.
Xiè Huì (謝晦) remonstrated,
and she was immediately sent away.
All his wealth and silk were kept in the outer treasury,
with no private hoard inside.
When the Sòng (宋) capital was established,
officials proposed that the East and West Halls be furnished with folding-legged beds and silver-plated nails.
The Emperor refused,
insisting on straight-legged beds
and iron nails.
When his daughters married,
their dowries did not exceed 200,000,
with no brocade, embroidery, gold, or jade.
Both internally and externally, the prohibitions were observed,
and everyone was frugal.
His nature was especially simple and easygoing.
He often wore clogs with interconnected teeth
and liked to wander outside the Shénhǔ Gate (神虎門),
accompanied by no more than ten attendants.
At that time, Xú Xiànzhī (徐羨之) resided in Xīzhōu (西州).
The Emperor once visited Xiànzhī,
walking out of the Xīyè Gate (西掖門).
His imperial retinue rushed to follow,
having already left the Xīmíng Gate (西明門).
When his sons greeted him in the morning,
he would enter his chambers, take off his official robes,
and only wear a skirt and hat,
like a common household member.
During Xiàowǔ’s (孝武) Dàmíng (大明) era,
the Emperor’s former private chamber was demolished,
and the Yùzhú Hall (玉燭殿) was built in its place.
He viewed it with his officials.
At the head of the bed was an earthen screen,
and on the wall hung a hemp lantern and a hemp rope whisk.
〔一五〕*Shìzhōng* Yuán Yǐ (袁顗) greatly praised the Emperor’s virtue of frugality and simplicity.
Xiàowǔ (孝武) did not reply,
but only said:
“If a country bumpkin had this,
he would consider it excessive.”
Thus, he was able to rule the entire empire
and achieve great accomplishments.
The historian says: The Hàn dynasty reigned for four hundred years.
Its longevity rivaled that of the prosperous Zhōu dynasty.
Although the four seas were in turmoil,
the people remained loyal to the Liú clan.
The common people, though apprehensive,
had no intention of transferring their allegiance.
Wèi Wǔ (Cáo Cāo) merely subdued the masses with military might,
and thus was able to usurp the mandate of heaven.
Although the dynastic reign changed,
the people had not forgotten Hàn.
When the Wèi house became weak and isolated,
resentment accumulated among the populace.
The Jìn family leveraged their position as prime ministers,
and took advantage of the weakness of the imperial clan.
For generations, they wielded great power,
establishing the foundation of their royal enterprise.
When Sòng Zǔ (Liú Yù) received the mandate,
his righteousness surpassed previous models.
From the time the Jìn court moved south,
emoluments departed from the royal house.
Court power and national destiny
successively fell to the prime ministers.
Though the monarch's position existed,
his authority had long vanished.
Huán Wēn possessed a heroic talent that overshadowed his generation,
and his achievements were unmatched for a time.
The enterprise of transferring the imperial tripod was already complete,
and the hopes of heaven and man were about to change.
From this point onward,
the Jìn path became increasingly obscured.
Dàozi initiated the calamities,
and Yuánxiǎn brought about the final conflict.
Huán Xuán seized the opportunity and rode the tide,
in addition to his father's achievements,
he founded a new dynasty.
The people had no dissenting hearts.
Gāozǔ (Liú Yù) was not like Huán (Huán Wēn) or Wén (Sīmǎ Yì),
he had no army of a single division.
Yet, in less than ten days,
he eliminated the wicked and suppressed the violent,
worshiped Jìn at the altars to heaven and earth,
preserving the old customs,
purged internally and cleared externally,
his achievements filled the realm.
By the time the bells and chimes changed their sound,
and sacrifices to heaven marked a new era,
the people had already abandoned Jìn,
which was different from the beginning of Yánkāng (Cáo Pī's reign).
His accomplishments in pacifying the chaos
were also distinct from the end of Xiánxī (Sīmǎ Yán's reign).
Thus, Gōng Huáng's (Sīmǎ Déwén) humble abdication
was almost like being relieved of a burden.
As for where the people gladly shifted their allegiance,
and where their songs of praise gathered,
Wèi and Jìn took the name,
while Gāozǔ reaped the reality.
How grand!
Collation Notes
Annals IV: The Young Emperor
The Young Emperor's personal name was Yìfú,
his childhood name was Chēbīng,
he was Emperor Wǔ's eldest son.
His mother was Lady Zhāng.
He was born in Jīngkǒu in the 2nd year of Yìxī of Jìn (406 CE).
Emperor Wǔ had no sons late in life,
and when the Emperor was born,
he was greatly pleased.
At the age of ten,
he was appointed Hereditary Prince of Yùzhāng.
The Emperor possessed physical strength,
was skilled in horsemanship and archery,
and understood music.
When the Sòng state was established,
he was appointed Hereditary Prince of Sòng.
In the 1st year of Yuánxī (419 CE),
he was promoted to Crown Prince of Sòng.
When Emperor Wǔ accepted the abdication,
he was established as Crown Prince.
On Guǐhài day in the 5th month of the 3rd year of Yǒngchū (422 CE),
Emperor Wǔ died.
On that very day,
the Crown Prince ascended the imperial throne.
A general amnesty was proclaimed.
The Empress Dowager was honored as Grand Empress Dowager.
On Rénshēn day in the 6th month,
Fù Liàng, Minister of the Secretariat, was appointed Supervisor of the Central Secretariat.
Sīkōng Xú Xiànzhī, General of the Guards Xiè Huì, and Liàng were appointed to assist in governance.
On Wùzǐ day,
Grand Commandant, Prince Dàolián of Chángshā, died.
On Dīngwèi day in the 9th month of autumn,
the officials proposed that Emperor Wǔ be worshipped at the southern suburb,
and Empress Wǔjìng at the northern suburb.
In the 11th month of winter, on Wùwǔ day,
a comet appeared in Yíngshì (constellation).
In the 12th month, on Gēngxū day,
Wèi troops captured Huátái.
In the 1st month of spring the following year, on Jǐhài day (the first day of the month),
a general amnesty was proclaimed,
and the era name was changed to Jǐngpíng 1st year.
Civil and military officials were promoted two ranks.
On Xīnchǒu day,
sacrifices were offered at the southern suburb.
The barbarian general Dáxī Āng broke through Jīnyǒng,
and advanced to besiege Hǔláo.
Máo Dézǔ attacked the barbarians and defeated them.
The barbarians retreated but then regrouped.
Tuòbá Mùmò also sent Prince Ānpíng Shèguī to raid Qīngzhōu.
On Guǐmǎo day,
Hénán Commandery fell.
On Yǐmǎo day,
a comet appeared in Dōngbì (constellation).
On Dīngchǒu day in the 2nd month,
the Grand Empress Dowager died.
Jǔqú Méngxùn and Tǔyùhún Āchái both sent envoys to pay tribute.
On Gēngchén day,
Méngxùn was granted the title of General of Agile Cavalry,
and enfeoffed as King of Héxī.
Āchái was appointed General Anxi, Governor of Shāzhōu,
and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiāohé.
On Xīnwèi day,
Sūn Fǎguāng of Fùyáng rebelled,
and attacked Shānyīn.
Chǔ Dànzhī, Grand Administrator of Kuàijī, dispatched Lù Shào, Magistrate of Shānyīn, to suppress and defeat him.
On Rénzǐ day in the 3rd month,
Empress Xiàoyì was interred in Xīngníng Líng.
In this month,
the Gāolì kingdom sent envoys to pay tribute.
On Jiǎzǐ day,
Liú Cuì, Governor of Yùzhōu, sent troops to attack Xǔchāng,
and killed Yǔ Lóng, the barbarian Administrator of Yǐngchuān.
[一０] On Yǐchǒu day,
barbarian cavalry raided Gāopíng.
Initially, after their defeat north of the Yellow River, the barbarians
requested a renewal of peace and alliance;
but upon hearing of Gāozǔ's death,
they resumed their invasions and disturbances.
The lands of Hé and Luò were thrown into turmoil.
In the 4th month of summer,
Tán Dàojì marched north,
arriving at Línqú,
where he burned the barbarians' siege equipment.
On Yǐwèi day,
Wèi troops captured Hǔláo,
seizing Máo Dézǔ, Governor of Sīzhōu, and returning with him.
In the 7th month of autumn, on Guǐyǒu day,
Lady Zhāng, his birth mother, was honored as Empress Dowager.
On Dīngchǒu day,
due to drought,
an imperial edict pardoned criminals sentenced to five years imprisonment or less.
[一一]
In the 10th month of winter, on Jǐwèi day,
a comet appeared in Dǐ (constellation),
pointing to Wěi (constellation),
traversing Shè tí (Boötes),
heading towards Dàjiǎo (Arcturus).
In the middle month, it was in Wēi (constellation),
and in the last month, it swept Tiāncāng before disappearing.
In this year,
Wèi ruler Tuòbá Sì died,
and his son Táo ascended the throne.
In the 12th month, on Bǐngyín day,
[一二] the three commanderies of Jiāngyáng, Jiānwéi, and Ānshàng in Níngzhōu were abolished,
and merged into Sòngchāng Commandery.
On Guǐsì day, the first day of the 2nd month of spring in the 2nd year,
there was a solar eclipse.
[一三] Liú Yìzhēn, Prince of Lúlín and Governor of Nányùzhōu, was demoted to commoner,
and exiled to Xīn'ān Commandery.
On Yǐwèi day,
his imperial younger brother Yìgōng was appointed General of the Champions,
and Governor of Nányùzhōu.
On Yǐsì day,
there was a great wind,
[一四] and five-colored clouds in the sky.
Soothsayers predicted war.
The Gāolì kingdom sent envoys with tribute.
The regents sent an envoy to execute Yìzhēn in Xīn'ān.
In the 5th month of summer,
Wáng Hóng, Governor of Jiāngzhōu, and Tán Dàojì, Governor of Nányǎnzhōu, came to court.
[一五] The Emperor's conduct and actions contained many errors.
On Yǐyǒu day,
the Empress Dowager issued an edict saying: The royal house is in disarray,
and the heavens' misfortune has not yet abated.
The late emperor's founding of the dynasty was not long-lasting,
and he departed the world and ascended to heaven.
Yìfú, as the eldest successor,
was entrusted with the heavenly position.
Unexpectedly, he indulged in extreme wickedness
and utter depravity,
reaching this extent.
While the great deceased was in his coffin,
and the realm was sorrowful and terrified,
he rejoiced in misfortune and uttered perverse words,
expressing joy on his face while supposedly in grief.
He even summoned musicians and
the palace.
He gathered entertainers and officials,
and had actors perform with pipes and strings.
There was nothing that was not fully played.
Rare delicacies and sweet dishes
were more plentiful than on ordinary days.
He selected consorts and concubines,
and had children born in the palace,
shamelessly
without compunction.
His scandalous reputation spread far and wide.
When Empress Yìhòu passed away,
a severe heavenly punishment was added.
He personally, with his attendants, pulled the ropes, singing and shouting,
pushing and jostling the imperial coffin,
clapping his hands and laughing,
which was heard throughout
the palace and government offices.
Furthermore, day and night he indulged in debauchery,
and his petty associates engaged in wanton play.
He initiated countless construction projects,
and expenses were innumerable.
The imperial treasury became empty,
and the people's strength was exhausted.
Punishments were cruel
and abusive,
and the number of prisoners increased daily.
Holding the position of an emperor,
he enjoyed the tasks of a menial servant;
occupying the supreme dignity of "ten thousand chariots,"
he delighted in the duties of a menial.
He personally wielded whips and cudgels,
beating
the innocent,
taking pleasure in it.
He dug ponds and built towers,
finished in the morning and destroyed in the evening.
He conscripted artisans and laborers,
exhausting the myriad people.
Near and far, there were sighs and laments;
both gods and men were filled with resentment and anger.
The altars of the land
and grain were about to fall.
How could he possibly continue to inherit and guard this great enterprise,
and rule over all nations?
Now he is deposed as Yíngyáng Wáng,
following precisely the precedents of Chāngyì Wáng of Hàn and Hǎixī Wáng of Jìn.
Zhènxī Jiāngjūn, Yídū Wáng,
is benevolent, intelligent, filial, and fraternal,
manifesting these virtues from his youth.
His moral character is pure and refined,
and his discernment is clear and fair.
He is fit to inherit the great succession
and brightly rule over
the myriad people.
The responsible officials should carefully follow precedents
and promptly escort him to the throne.
I, the deceased's wife, enduring these hundred misfortunes,
though living, feel as if I have perished.
I forever grieve these circumstances,
my heart broken
and choked with sorrow.
Initially, Xú Xiànzhī and Fù Liàng intended to depose the emperor.
They prompted Wáng Hóng and Tán Dàojì to seek to attend the national mourning.
Hóng and others came to court.
They sent the Palace Secretariats Xíng Āntài and Pān Shèng to be their internal contacts.
That morning,
Tán Dàojì and Xiè Huì led troops in the front,
while Xú Xiànzhī and others followed.
Taking advantage of the opening of the Dōngyè Mén,
they entered through the Yúnlóng Mén.
Pān Shèng and others had already warned the palace guards,
so no one resisted.
At that time, the emperor was setting up shops in Huálín Yuán,
personally selling goods.
He also dug canals and piled up earth
to resemble the Pògāng Dài,
and with his attendants, he pulled boats and sang and shouted,
taking joy in it.
In the evening, he toured the Tiānyuān Chí,
and slept on the dragon boat.
He had not yet risen that morning when
soldiers advanced
and killed two attendants beside the emperor,
wounding the emperor's finger.
He then came out of the Dōnggé
and had the imperial seal and cords seized.
The officials bowed their farewells,
and he was sent to the Dōnggōng,
then confined in Wú Jùn.
That day,
an amnesty was issued for all crimes below capital punishment.
The empress dowager ordered the return of the imperial seal and cords.
Tán Dàojì entered and guarded the court hall.
On the *guǐchǒu* day of the sixth month,
Xú Xiànzhī and others sent the Palace Secretariat Xíng Āntài to assassinate the emperor at Jīnchāng Tíng.
The emperor possessed great strength
and did not immediately submit to control.
He burst out and ran towards the Chāngmén.
He was pursued and tripped by a gate bar,
leading to his death.
He was nineteen years old at the time.
(The above is missing) For a founder of an enterprise,
it is a revelation from heaven;
for a ruler who preserves traditions,
how difficult it is!
(18) Collation Notes
Basic Annals No. 5, Emperor Wén
Tàizǔ Wén Huángdì, personal name Yìlóng,
childhood name Chē'ér,
was the third son of Wǔdì.
In the third year of Yìxī of Emperor Ān of Jìn (407 CE),
he was born in Jīngkǒu.
During the rebellion of Lú Xún,
he was four years old.
Gāozǔ sent the Cīyì Cānjūn Liú Cuì to assist him in garrisoning Jīngchéng.
In the eleventh year (415 CE),
he was enfeoffed as Péngchéng Xiàn Gōng.
When Gāozǔ marched against the Qiāng people and reached Péngchéng,
he was about to advance further,
and appointed him Xing Guànjūn Jiāngjūn to remain behind.
The Jìn court further conferred upon him the title of Shǐchíjié, Jiān Xú Yǎn Qīng Jì Sì Zhōu Zhū Jūnfāng, Xúzhōu Cìshǐ,
with his general title remaining as before.
When Guānzhōng was pacified,
Gāozǔ returned to Péngchéng,
and further conferred upon him the titles of Jiān Sī Zhōu Yù Zhōu zhī Huáixī Yǎn Zhōu zhī Chénliú Zhū Jūnfāng, Qián Jiāngjūn, Sīzhōu Cìshǐ,
with Shǐchíjié remaining as before,
and he was to garrison Luòyáng.
He was then re-appointed as Dūdū Jīng Yì Níng Yōng Liáng Qín Liù Zhōu Yù Zhōu zhī Hénán Guǎngpíng Yáng Zhōu zhī Yìchéng Sōngzī Sì Jùn Zhū Jūnfāng, Xī Zhōngláng Jiāng, Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ,
with Shǐchíjié remaining as before.
In the first year of Yǒngchū (420 CE),
he was enfeoffed as Yídū Wáng,
with a fief of three thousand households.
He was advanced to oversee Běiqín,
in addition to the previous seven prefectures.
He was promoted to the title of Zhènxī Jiāngjūn,
and given one set of drums and pipes.
He was also advanced to oversee Xiāngzhōu.
That year he came to court.
He was fourteen years old at the time.
He was seven *chǐ* and five *cùn* tall,
widely read in classics and history,
and skilled in *lìshū* calligraphy.
In the seventh month of the second year of Jǐngpíng
, Shǎodì was deposed.
All officials, with the ceremonial carriage, reverently welcomed
him to assume the imperial succession.
The travelling palace arrived at Jiānglíng,
and the imperial seals and sashes were presented.

Shìzhōng chén Xiù, Sànqí Chángshì chén Nízhī, Zhōngshū Jiān Shàngshū Lìng Hùjūn Jiāngjūn Jiànchéng Xiàn Gōng chén Liàng, Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn chén Jǐngrén, Jǐshìzhōng Yóujī Jiāngjūn Lóngxiāng Xiàn Hóu chén Lóng, Yuèqí Xiàowèi Dūtíng Hóu chén Gāng, Jǐshì Huángmén Shìláng chén Kǒng Qúzhī, Sànqí Shìláng chén Liú Sīkǎo, Yuánwài Sànqí Shìláng chén Pān Shèng, Zhōngshū Shìláng chén Hé Shàngzhī, Yǔlín Jiān Fēngyáng Xiàn Kāiguó Hóu chén Xiāo Sīhuà, Chángjiān Shàngshū Zuǒchéng Déyáng Xiàn Hóu chén Sūn Kāng, Lìbù Lángzhōng Qídūwèi chén Zhāng Màodù, Yícáo Lángzhōng chén Xú Chánglín, Cāngbù Lángzhōng chén Yǔ Jùnzhī, Dūguān Lángzhōng chén Yuán Xún and others submitted a memorial, stating:
"We humbly understand that prosperity and decline succeed each other,
and when things reach their limit, they change.
This is why the Way of Heaven does not flatter
and why the divined generations are long and auspicious.
Recently, the imperial fortune faced decline,
and the royal house was in a difficult and obscure state.
The mandate of the nine regions
had nowhere to return,
and Gāozǔ's foundation
was about to fall to the ground.
Thanks to the profound and deep virtue of the foundation,
which both men and gods aided,
the altars of soil and grain were pacified,
and all living beings obtained peace.
We respectfully believe that Your Majesty's imperial virtue is natural,
and Your sagely wisdom is in command.
Filial piety and fraternity are manifest throughout the family and state,
and Your elegant conduct is proclaimed among the tributary regions.
Therefore, auspicious omens accumulated,
and propitious signs illuminated [the realm].
The spirits of the ancestral temple
looked to the west,
and the myriad nations and common people
looked to Your radiance to find life.
We, Your servants, are honored to be among the court ranks,
participating in carrying out Your commands.
Again we meet a glorious and bright era,
and once more we witness the enterprise of great peace.
The traveling palace has arrived;
looking up at the city walls and gates,
we cannot contain our joy and delight like that of the duckweed.
We respectfully go to the gate to present this memorial."
The Emperor replied:
"The imperial fortune has been difficult and exhausted,
and often encounters hardship and decline.
Looking up at the grand foundation,
I recall the nation's past,
and forever yearn for his person,
filled with sorrow and regret.
Fortunately, the seven hundred years of the dynasty's longevity endured,
and the loyal and virtuous ministers supported it,
thus able to transform decline into prosperity,
and bring order to both heaven and humanity.
Unworthily, with my lack of virtue,
I have mistakenly received this great mandate.
Reflecting on myself, I am anxious and fearful;
how can I possibly bear it?
I shall temporarily return to the court
to express my grief at the imperial tombs,
and also to share my thoughts with the wise and eminent.
I hope you understand my feelings,
and do not offer superfluous words."
The officials and scribes of the various prefectures and provinces all declared themselves servants,
requesting to put up signs on all gates,
exactly like those in the palace.
The Emperor did not permit it.
On the day of Jiǎxū,
he departed from Jiānglíng.
On the day of Bǐngshēn in the eighth month,
the imperial carriage arrived at the capital city.
On the day of Dīngyǒu,
he paid respects at the Chūníng Líng,
then returned to the central hall and ascended the imperial throne.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day of Dīngyǒu of the first year of Yuánjiā,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
The second year of Jǐngpíng was changed to the first year of Yuánjiā.
Civil and military officials were promoted two ranks.
Unpaid taxes and old debts were not to be collected again.
On the day of Gēngzǐ,
the acting Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn and Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ, Xiè Huì, was made Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn and Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day of Guǐmǎo,
Sīkōng Lù Shàngshū Shì and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ, Xú Xiànzhī, was promoted to Sītú;
Wèi Jiāngjūn and Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ, Wáng Hóng, was promoted to Sīkōng;
Zhōngshū Jiān and Hùjūn Jiāngjūn, Fù Liàng, was granted the additional title of Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī;
Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn and Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ, Xiè Huì, was granted the title of Wèi Jiāngjūn;
Zhènběi Jiāngjūn and Nányǎnzhōu Cìshǐ, Tán Dàojì, was granted the title of Zhēngběi Jiāngjūn.
On the day of Jiǎchén,
his birth mother, Hú Jiéyú, was posthumously honored as Huáng Tàihòu,
with the posthumous name Zhāng Hòu.
Wèi Jiāngjūn and Nánxúzhōu Cìshǐ, Péngchéng Wáng Yìkāng, was granted the title of Piàojí Jiāngjūn;
Guānjūn Jiāngjūn and Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ, Yìgōng, was granted the title of Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn
and enfeoffed as Jiāngxià Wáng.
His sixth imperial younger brother, Yìxuān, was made Jìnglíng Wáng.
His seventh imperial younger brother, Yìjì, was made Héngyáng Wáng.
On the day of Wùshēn,
Yùzhōu Cìshǐ Liú Cuì was made Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ;
Xiāoqí Jiāngjūn Guǎn Yìzhī was made Yùzhōu Cìshǐ;
Nánmán Xiàowèi Dào Yànzhī was made Zhōnglǐngjūn.
On the day of Jǐyǒu,
the tax on cloth for the current year in Jīng and Xiāng provinces was halved.
On the day of Bǐngzǐ in the ninth month,
Consort Yuán was established as Empress.
In the spring, first month, on the day of Bǐngyín in the second year,
Sītú Xú Xiànzhī and Shàngshū Lìng Fù Liàng submitted memorials to return governmental authority,
and the Emperor began to personally attend to affairs.
On the day of Xīnwèi,
the imperial carriage offered sacrifices in the southern suburbs,
and a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
In the third month, on the day of Yǐchǒu,
Zuǒ Jiāngjūn and Xúzhōu Cìshǐ Wáng Zhòngdé was granted the title of Ānběi Jiāngjūn.
In the summer, fifth month, on the day of Wùyín,
Tèjìn Xiè Dàn passed away.
In the autumn, eighth month, on the day of Jiǎshēn,
due to the refugee population from Guānzhōng moving into Hànchuān,
Jīngzhào, Fúfēng, Féngyì, and other commanderies were established.
On the day of Yǐyǒu,
Piàojí Jiāngjūn and Nánxúzhōu Cìshǐ Péngchéng Wáng Yìkāng was made Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī;
the newly appointed Sīkōng Wáng Hóng was made Chējì Dàjiāngjūn and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī;
Ròujūn Chángshǐ Jiāng was made Guǎngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the winter, eleventh month, on the day of Guǐyǒu,
former Jiāngjūn Yáng Xuán was made Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn and Běiqínzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the spring, first month, on the day of Bǐngyín in the third year,
Sītú Lù Shàngshū Shì and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ Xú Xiànzhī,
Shàngshū Lìng Hùjūn Jiāngjūn and Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū Fù Liàng,
having committed crimes, were executed.
Zhōnglǐngjūn Dào Yànzhī and Zhēngběi Jiāngjūn Tán Dàojì were dispatched to attack Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Xiè Huì,
and the Emperor personally led the six armies on a western expedition.
A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the day of Dīngmǎo,
Chējì Dàjiāngjūn and Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ Wáng Hóng was made Sītú Lù Shàngshū Shì and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ;
Piàojí Jiāngjūn and Nánxúzhōu Cìshǐ Péngchéng Wáng Yìkāng was transferred to Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ;
Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn and Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ Jiāngxià Wáng Yìgōng was transferred to Nánxúzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day of Jǐsì,
former Hùjūn Jiāngjūn Zhào Lúnzhī was made Zhènjūn Jiāngjūn.
In the intercalary month, on the day of Bǐngxū,
the imperial prince Shào was born.
In the second month, on the day of Yǐmǎo,
all prisoners and convicts
were pardoned.
On the day of Wùwǔ,
Jīnzǐ Guānglù Dàfū Wáng Jìnghóng was made Shàngshū Zuǒ Púshè;
Yùzhāng Tàishǒu Zhèng Xiānzhī was made Shàngshū Yòu Púshè.
Jiàn'ān Tàishǒu Pān Shèng, having committed a crime, was executed.
On the day of Gēngshēn,
Tèjìn Fàn Tài was granted the additional title of Guānglù Dàfū.
On this day,
the imperial carriage departed from the capital.
On the day of Wùchén,
Dào Yànzhī and Tán Dàojì thoroughly defeated Xiè Huì at Yǐnjī.
On the day of Bǐngzǐ,
the imperial carriage returned from Wúhú.
On the day of Jǐmǎo,
Huì was captured at Yántóu
and sent to the capital for execution.
In the third month, on the day of Xīnsì,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In summer, the fifth month, on the day Yǐwèi,
Tán Dàojì, General Who Conquers the North and Inspector of Nányànzhōu, was appointed Grand General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu.
Dào Yànzhī, Central Leader of the Army, was appointed Inspector of Nányùzhōu.
On the day Wùxū,
Yǐ Xīn, Prince of Chángshā and General of the Rear, was appointed Inspector of Nányànzhōu.
On the day Yǐsì,
Dà Jǔqú Méngxùn, Grand General of Cavalry and Protector of Liángzhōu, was changed to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry.
An imperial edict stated:
"When a sagacious king rules the world,
he widely extends his four ears (attention),
like patrolling mountains and observing regions,
collecting customs and observing governance.
This is why true and false are surely discerned,
the remote are not overlooked,
the king's beneficence is unimpeded,
and even the nine marshes are heard from.
I, being of meager virtue,
have unworthily succeeded to this great enterprise.
Although I constantly ponder the way of governance,
and my will is set on it from dawn till dusk,
wishing for Fùyán,
and thinking of it even in my sleep,
yet the outstanding talents of the countryside
remain hidden and not yet brought forth,
and the feelings of the people and their hidden grievances
are still beyond my sight and hearing.
Therefore, I constantly reflect on the realm,
forsaking sleep and forgetting food.
Now that malevolent influences have been swept away,
and the world within the four seas is peaceful and tranquil,
honoring the worthy and spreading transformation
begins herewith.
Envoys shall be dispatched to tour the four directions.
Regarding the excellent officials and administrators who fulfill their duties,
and the good people of even humble households,
they should be thoroughly and completely listed in memorials,
without any omissions.
If judicial cases are not cared for,
or governance is perverse and erroneous,
harming the people and corrupting instruction,
these matters should be fully reported.
The elderly, the widowed and lonely, the young orphans, and those with the six infirmities who cannot support themselves
should be generously provided for and relieved by the commanderies and counties.
Widely gather public opinion,
and broadly accept good counsel,
striving to fully implement the purpose of this mission,
so that it is as if I personally observe it."
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the imperial carriage attended a hearing of lawsuits at Yánxiántáng.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Zhào Lúnzhī, General Who Guards the Army, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left and Leader of the Army.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the imperial carriage again attended a hearing of lawsuits at Yánxiántáng.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
another hearing of lawsuits took place.
Wáng Huá, General of the Right Guard, was appointed Central Protector of the Army.
In winter, the eleventh month, on the day Wùyín,
Jí Hàn, Inspector of Liángzhōu and Nánqínzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Yìzhōu.
Liú Dàochǎn, Army Advisor to the General of Cavalry, was appointed Inspector of Liángzhōu and Nánqínzhōu.
On the day Jǐhài,
Liú Zūnkǎo, Colonel of the Southern Man, was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
Xiāo Sīhuà, Palace Assistant Secretary, was appointed Inspector of Qīngzhōu.
On the day Rénxū,
Xú Peìzhī, former Administrator of Wújùn, plotted rebellion,
and he and his accomplices were all executed.
The fourth year, in spring, the first month, on the day Yǐhài, which was the first day of the lunar month,
a partial amnesty was granted within a hundred li of the capital.
On the day Xīnsì,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices in the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
the emperor traveled to Dāntú
to visit Jīnglíng.
In the third month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
an imperial edict stated:
"Dāntú, my hometown, is deeply cherished,
where the great enterprise began.
Setting foot in this land, I am filled with endless emotion.
In ancient times, Emperor Zhāng of Hàn, on his southern tour,
bestowed grace upon the Yuán clan.
How much more so now, when the bonds of affection and righteousness are even greater than in those past days.
I wish to spread my remaining benevolence
to comfort and recompense the gentry and common people.
Therefore, the rent and cloth tax of this county for this year shall be remitted,
and all those sentenced to five years of punishment or less shall be pardoned and released;
families of those who scaled the city walls in three battles and those of grand generals
shall be provided for as appropriate."
On the day Dīnghài,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Zhèng Xiānzhī, Right Director of the Imperial Secretariat, passed away.
On the day Rényín,
the practice of wearing five-colored threads and 'life-threads' on the Summer Solstice was prohibited,
a proposal by Zhūgě Chǎnnzhī, Magistrate of Fùyáng.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Wáng Huīzhī, Grand Judge, was appointed Inspector of Jiāozhōu.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Wáng Huá, Central Protector of the Army, passed away.
There was a plague in the capital.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
envoys were dispatched to inquire after the people
and provide medicine;
if the deceased had no family,
coffins were granted.
In the sixth month, on the day Guǐmǎo, which was the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Gēngshēn,
Yīn Mù, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Gold and Purple, was appointed General Protector of the Army.
The fifth year, in spring, the first month, on the day Yǐhài,
an imperial edict stated:
"I respectfully undertake this grand enterprise,
governing the four seas,
but moral transformation has not spread widely,
and the way of governance is often obscure.
Seeking the cause in human affairs,
I reflect with worry, whether awake or asleep.
Moreover, recently yin and yang have been out of order,
and drought and plague have become a calamity.
Looking up at these warnings of disaster,
the blame deeply rests with me.
I contemplate how to humble myself and diligently reflect,
deliberate on legal cases and examine punishments in detail,
to respond to the wrath of Heaven above
and relieve the suffering of the people below.
All ministers and officials,
each should present honest words,
pointing out successes and failures,
without any concealment."
On the day Jiǎshēn,
the imperial carriage reviewed military exercises at Xuánwǔguǎn.
On the day Wùzǐ,
there was a great fire in the capital,
and envoys were dispatched to comfort and distribute relief.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Jǐhài,
Xiāo Mózī, Colonel of the Southern Man, was appointed Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Xú Huò, Administrator of Shǐxīng, was appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Zhāng Shào, Inspector of Xiāngzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngxū,
Wáng Hóng, Grand Minister of Education, was demoted to General Who Guards the Army, with the privilege of establishing a staff of three high officials.
There was a great flood in the capital.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
envoys were dispatched to inspect and distribute relief.
Chéng Dàohuì, Grand Administrator of Jiāngxià, was appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
In autumn, the eighth month, on the day Rénxū,
Fàn Tài, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left with Special Advancement, passed away.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
the imperial carriage attended a hearing of lawsuits at Yánxiántáng.
In the intercalary month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Liú Déwǔ, Army Major of the Right Army, was appointed Inspector of Yùzhōu.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zhōu Jízhī, Chancellor to the Duke of Ānlù, was appointed Inspector of Níngzhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the day Gēngyín,
Zhào Lúnzhī, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left and Leader of the Army, passed away.
In this year,
the kingdom of Tiānzhú sent envoys to offer local products.
The sixth year, in spring, the first month, on the day Xīnchǒu,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices in the southern suburbs.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
Péngchéng Wáng Yìkāng, General of Cavalry and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was appointed Grand Minister of Education and Director of the Imperial Secretariat,
also concurrently serving as General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Nánxúzhōu.
In the third month, on the day Dīngsì,
the imperial son Shào was established as Crown Prince.
On the day Wùwǔ,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and civil and military officials were promoted one rank.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Yīn Jǐngrén, General of the Left Guard, was appointed Central Leader of the Army.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Wáng Jìnghóng, Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed President of the Imperial Secretariat.
Línchuān Wáng Yìqìng, Governor of Dānyáng, was appointed Left Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
Jiāng Yí, Minister of Personnel, was appointed Right Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénchén, which was the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Guǐsì,
Wáng Jìnghóng, newly appointed President of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left with Special Advancement.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Liú Dàojì, Army Major to the General Who Guards the Army, was appointed Inspector of Yìzhōu.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Féngyì Jùn was established within Yōngzhōu.
In the seventh month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Kǒng Mòzhī, Left Supervising Secretary of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
In this month,
the King of Bǎijì sent envoys to offer local products.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùwǔ,
Lǒngxī and Sòngkāng Commanderies were established within Qínzhōu.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Rénshēn,
Yīn Jǐngrén, Central Leader of the Army, resigned due to mourning.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐchǒu, which was the first day of the lunar month,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīnghài,
the Kingdom of Hénán and the King of Héxī sent envoys to offer local products.
The seventh year, in spring, the first month, on the day Guǐsì,
Tǔyùhún Mùróng Guī was appointed General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Shāzhōu.
In this month,
the King of Wō sent envoys to offer local products.
In the third month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Right General Dào Yànzhī was dispatched for a northern expedition.
The naval forces entered the Yellow River.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Yǐn Chōng, formerly the Sīmǎ of the General Who Conquers Barbarians, was made Inspector of Sīzhōu.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Yīn Jǐngrén, formerly the Central Leader of the Army, was made General Leading the Army.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the country of Hēluōdān sent envoys to offer local products.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Yáng Nándāng of the Dī people, General Who Captures the Gentry, was made Inspector of Qínzhōu.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Sǔo barbarians abandoned Qíao'áo garrison and fled.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Zhēn Fǎhù, Adviser to the General Who Pacifies the North, was made Inspector of Liángzhōu and Nánqínzhōu.
On the day Wùxū,
the Sǔo barbarians abandoned Huátái garrison and fled.
On the day Jiǎyín,
the countries of Línyì, Hēluó, and Shīzǐ sent envoys to offer local products.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Nányùzhōu was abolished and merged with Yùzhōu.
Yìxuān, Prince of Jìnglíng and Left General, was made Inspector of Xúzhōu.
On the day Wùwǔ,
a mint was established,
and four-zhū coins were cast.
On the day Wùyín,
Jīnyǒng City was captured by the Sǔo barbarians.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐwèi,
Hǔláo City was again captured by the Sǔo barbarians.
On the day Rénchén,
Tán Dàojì, General Who Conquers the South, was dispatched for a northern punitive expedition.
Dào Yànzhī, Right General, retreated from Huátái.
In the twelfth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Yìxīn, Prince of Chángshā and Inspector of Nányànzhōu, was made Inspector of Yùzhōu;
Sīmǎ Jíhàn, Minister of Works, was made Inspector of Sīzhōu.
On the day Yǐhài,
there was a fire in Jīngyì,
which spread and burned the north wall of the Grand Altar of the Soil and Grain.
Zhú Língxiù, Inspector of Yànzhōu, was found guilty and executed.
In the eighth year, spring, first month, on the day Gēngyín,
Zhūyá Commandery was re-established in Jiāozhōu.
On the day Guǐsì,
Shēn Xuān, General of the Left Army, was made Inspector of Yànzhōu.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Tán Dàojì, General Who Conquers the South, defeated the Sǔo barbarians at Dōngpíng Shòuzhāng.
In the second month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Wéi Lǎng, Sīmǎ of the General Who Pacifies the North, was made Inspector of Qīngzhōu.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Jiāng Yí, Right Grand Master of Remonstrance, was made Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Huátái was captured by the Sǔo barbarians.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Tán Dàojì, General Who Conquers the South, withdrew his army and returned.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Xiāo Sīhuà, Inspector of Qīngzhōu, abandoned the city and fled.
Liú Zūnkǎo, Right Commandant of the Palace Guard of the Heir Apparent, was made Inspector of Nányànzhōu.
In the third month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the Imperial carriage heard lawsuits in the Yánxiántáng.
On the day Wùshēn,
an edict stated:
"Recently, military operations have been frequent,
and national expenditures have greatly increased.
Resources and stores are insufficient,
and all institutions are still too numerous.
It is advisable to uphold simplicity and economy
to adapt to the actual situation.
Internal and external officials should consult broadly
to ensure frugality."
In summer, fourth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Yuán Wànlíng, Prince of Héngyáng and Imperial Tutor, was made Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
Xú Zūnzhī, Adviser to the Rear Army, was made Inspector of Yànzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
the area south of the Yangtze River and Jìnlíng Commandery of Yángzhōu were assigned to Nánxúzhōu,
and the area north of the Yangtze River to Yànzhōu.
Yìxuān, Prince of Jìnglíng and Inspector of Xúzhōu, was made Inspector of Nányànzhōu;
Sīmǎ Jíhàn, Minister of Works, was made Inspector of Xúzhōu.
In the intercalary month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
an edict stated:
"Recently, agriculture and sericulture have been neglected,
and those who wander and eat are numerous.
Wild lands are not cultivated,
and supervision and taxation are unheard of.
When there is a flood or drought,
there is immediately a shortage.
If the fundamental task is not deeply pursued,
abundance will have no source.
Commandery administrators govern within the imperial domain,
and county magistrates are the rulers who are close to the people.
They should encourage and instruct,
and guide with good regulations.
All should exert their strength,
leaving no land unproductive.
Farming, sericulture, and cultivation
should each be done to the utmost.
If there are those who excel in farming,
their names should be listed and reported at the end of the year."
There was a drought in Yángzhōu.

The offices of General of Accumulated Archers and General of Strong Crossbows were established.

In the tenth year, spring, first month, on the day Jiǎyín,

The country of Hēluōdān in Zhépózhōu sent envoys to offer local products.

In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
On the day Bǐngchén,
an imperial edict stated:
"The tranquility of the Zhōu dynasty
truly came from its many worthy men,
and the prosperity of the Hàn dynasty
also depended on finding the right people.
For a long time,
I have longed for worthy men in my waking and sleeping hours,
but finding wisdom is difficult,
and bringing forth the brilliant has not been effective.
This has resulted in overlooked talents remaining in the wilderness,
and the court being empty of officials.
Reflecting on previous records,
my shame for my lack of virtue is profound.
'Recommend those you know'
was the earnest instruction of Xuānní (Confucius),
and 'contributing scholars for official positions'
was an established standard of previous generations.
Therefore, a decree should be announced both inside and outside the court,
that each should make recommendations.
They will be selected according to their abilities
to observe their usefulness."
That night,

Péngchéng Wáng Yìkāng (彭城王義康), General-in-chief, concurrent Grand Minister of Works, Administrator of the Affairs of the Department of State, and Governor of Yángzhōu (揚州), was appointed Governor of Jiāngzhōu (江州),
retaining his title of General-in-chief.
Jiāngxià Wáng Yìgōng (江夏王義恭), Minister of Works and Governor of Southern Yànzhōu (南兗州), was appointed Grand Minister of Works and Administrator of the Affairs of the Department of State.
On the *wùyín* day,
Línchuān Wáng Yìqìng (臨川王義慶), General of the Guards, was appointed Governor of Southern Yànzhōu (南兗州) with his existing title,
and Yīn Jǐngrén (殷景仁), Director of the Department of State Affairs and General of the Guards, was appointed Governor of Yángzhōu (揚州),
retaining his position as Director.
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Liú Yìróng (劉義融), a State Councilor, was appointed General of the Palace Guard,
and Xú Zhànzhī (徐湛之), Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed Protector-General.
On the *dīnghài* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The previously supplied fields, grain, and seeds for the common people of Yáng (揚) and Southern Xú (南徐) prefectures,
and the rent and grain taxes that were previously excused for several years in Yǎn (兗), the two Yù (豫), Qīng (青), and Xú (徐) prefectures, which are now due,
are all halved.
For this year, if there are areas with no harvest,
〔二一〕they are to be fully excused.
All outstanding debts
are to be generously assessed and reduced.
Furthermore, local and prefectural assessments and taxes,
and market levies in various places,
are often burdensome and severe.
The benefits from mountains and wetlands
are sometimes prohibited;
and the categories of people called for labor service
even include the young and weak.
All such instances
harm governance and injure the people.
From now on, all must comply with laws and regulations,
striving to be fair and equitable.
If there are any inconveniences,
they should be reported separately according to the specifics,
without merely seeking temporary expediency
and thus departing from the spirit of compassion and relief.
The responsible officials are to clearly proclaim and disseminate this,
in accordance with Our intent.”
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
Yīn Jǐngrén (殷景仁), Director of the Department of State Affairs and Governor of Yángzhōu (揚州), passed away.
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Wáng Qiú (王球), Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs.
〔二二〕On the *wùchén* day,
Shǐxīng Wáng Jùn (始興王濬), Governor of Southern Yùzhōu (南豫州), was appointed Governor of Yángzhōu (揚州);
Wǔlíng Wáng Jùn (武陵王駿), Governor of Xiāngzhōu (湘州), was appointed Governor of Southern Yùzhōu (南豫州);
and Nánpíng Wáng Shuò (南平王鑠) was appointed Governor of Xiāngzhōu (湘州).
In this year,
the King of Wǔdū (武都), the King of Hénán (河南), and the State of Báijì (百濟) sent envoys to present local products.

In summer, in the fifth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,

〔二三〕Línchuān Wáng Yìqìng (臨川王義慶), General of the Guards and Governor of Southern Yànzhōu (南兗州), and Nánqiáo Wáng Yìxuān (南譙王義宣), General Who Conquers the North and Governor of Southern Xúzhōu (南徐州), were both granted the privilege of establishing a *fǔ* (府) and the honors of the Three Ducal Ministers.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Sòngxī Commandery (宋熙郡) was established in Jiāozhōu (交州).
In this month,
the Miǎn River (沔水) overflowed.
In the sixth month, on the *wùchén* day,
envoys were dispatched to tour and provide relief.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Liú Yìróng (劉義融), General of the Palace Guard, passed away.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *wùxū* day,
Zhào Bófú (趙伯符), Governor of Xú (徐) and Yǎn (兗) prefectures, was appointed General of the Palace Guard.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Zāng Zhì (臧質), Administrator of Bādōng (巴東) and Jiànpíng (建平) commanderies, was appointed Governor of Xú (徐) and Yǎn (兗) prefectures.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Nányàn (南燕), Púyáng (濮陽), and Nánguǎngpíng (南廣平) commanderies of Southern Xúzhōu (南徐州) were abolished.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
Wáng Qiú (王球), Director of the Department of State Affairs, passed away.
〔二四〕On the *jǐhài* day,
Mèng Yǐ (孟顗), Governor of Dānyáng (丹陽), was appointed Director of the Department of State Affairs.
The Dī (氐) chieftain Yáng Nándāng (楊難當) again raided Hànchuān (漢川).
In the twelfth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
Péi Fāngmíng (裴方明), General of Dragon Valor, was dispatched with Liú Zhēndào (劉真道), Governor of Liáng (梁) and Qín (秦) prefectures, to suppress him.
In this month,
〔二五〕Cuàn Sōngzǐ (爨松子), Administrator of Jìnnìng (晉寧), rebelled,
and Xú Xún (徐循), Governor of Níngzhōu (寧州), suppressed him.
In this year,
the State of Sùtè (肅特), the State of Gāolí (高麗), the State of Sūmílí (蘇靡黎), and the State of Línyì (林邑) all sent envoys to present local products.
In the nineteenth year, in the first month, on the *yǐsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The foundation from which all things originate is the profound teaching of the sagacious and enlightened;
when the foundation is established, transformation is achieved, and learning is therefore highly valued.
Thus, edicts are issued based on the Three Virtues,
and promoted through the Four Arts,
so that people can be guided by righteous principles
and brought into order and decorum.
In the flourishing and sagacious eras of great kings,
〔二六〕this was always followed.
When the Yǒngchū (永初) era received the Mandate,
its institutions and principles were grand and far-reaching,
intending to harmonize all people
and unify diverse customs.
An imperial edict instructed the officials
to greatly establish schools;
however, due to frequent encountering of difficulties and adversities,
these were not yet built.
Looking back at previous achievements,
We desire to spread great accomplishments.
Now that the four quarters are pacified
and both Rong (戎) and Huá (華) admire and yearn for us,
widely instructing the sons of nobles
is truly a task of the present time.
Therefore, we should follow established regulations
and promote this grand undertaking.”
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
as Our long illness had recovered,
We first offered the *yuè* (礿) sacrifice,
〔二七〕and a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
In the fifth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Liú Zhēndào (劉真道), Governor of Liáng (梁) and Qín (秦) prefectures, and Péi Fāngmíng (裴方míng), General of Dragon Valor, defeated the Dī (氐) chieftain Yáng Nándāng (楊難當),
and Qiúchí (仇池) was pacified.
In the intercalary month,
there was heavy rainfall in the capital region;
on the *dīngsì* day,
envoys were dispatched to tour and provide relief.
In the sixth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Dà Jùqú Wúhuì (大沮渠無諱) was appointed General-in-chief Who Conquers the West and Governor of Liángzhōu (涼州).
In autumn, in the seventh month,
Liú Zhēndào (劉真道), Governor of Liáng (梁) and Qín (秦) prefectures, was appointed Governor of Yōngzhōu (雍州),
and Péi Fāngmíng (裴方míng), General of Dragon Valor, was appointed Governor of Liáng (梁) and Southern Qín (南秦) prefectures.
On the *jiǎxū* day of the month's end,
there was a solar eclipse.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
the State of Ruìruì (芮芮) sent envoys to present local products.
On the *jǐhài* day,
Zhōu Wànsuì (周萬歲), Administrator of Jìnnìng (晉寧), was appointed Governor of Níngzhōu (寧州).
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The sons of nobles have just gathered,
and their studies are beginning to flourish.
Since the subtle words of the sages faded,
nearly a thousand years have passed;
reflecting on these matters and people,
We feel a sense of melancholy.
The descendants of the sages
should quickly be discussed for succession.
At the site of the former temple,
a special construction is to be undertaken,
and according to old regulations, officials are to be appointed to oversee the sacrifices,
with offerings made in the four seasons.
Qùelǐ (闕里) previously suffered from banditry and chaos,
and the school buildings were ruined.
The commandery of Lǔ (魯) is to repair the school buildings
and recruit students.
In the past, even for worthy sages and those with a single good deed,
their burial mounds were protected
and grazing forbidden;
how much more so for the Ni Fù (尼父) [Confucius], whose virtue is manifest among the people
and whose merits span a hundred generations,
yet his grave mound is overgrown
and thorns are not cut.
A few households near the tomb are to be excused from their duties
to manage the sweeping and cleaning.”
Five households from Lǔ (魯) Commandery, including Kǒng Jǐng (孔景), who resided near the tomb of Kǒngzǐ (孔子),
were excused from their levies and services,
provided for sweeping and cleaning,
and also planted six hundred pine and cypress trees.
In this year,
the State of Póhuáng (婆皇) sent envoys to present local products.
In the twentieth year, in spring, in the first month,
the Wànchūn (萬春) and Qiānqiū (千秋) gates were opened to the east and west of Táichéng (臺城).
In the second month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Yǔ Dēngzhī (庾登之), Governor of Jiāngzhōu (江州), was appointed Protector-General.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
〔二八〕Lúlíng Wáng Shào (廬陵王紹) was appointed Governor of Jiāngzhōu (江州).
Qiúchí (仇池) was overrun by the Suǒ Lǔ (索虜).
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the imperial carriage reviewed troops at Báixià (白下).
In the third month, on the *xīnhài* day,
Héngyáng Wáng Yìjì (衡陽王義季), General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Jīngzhōu (荊州), was promoted to General-in-chief Who Conquers the West.
Shēn Tǎn (申坦), Administrator of Bāxī (巴西) and Zǐtóng (梓潼) commanderies, was appointed Governor of Liáng (梁) and Southern Qín (南秦) prefectures.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the *jiǎwǔ* day,
the sixth imperial son, Dàn (誕), was enfeoffed as Guǎnglíng Wáng (廣陵王).
In the fifth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Yǔ Dēngzhī (庾登之), Protector-General, passed away.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Yáng Wéndé (楊文德) was appointed General Who Conquers the West and Governor of Northern Qínzhōu (北秦州),
and enfeoffed as King of Wǔdū (武都).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Xiāo Sīhuà (蕭思話), Commander of the Southern Barbarians, was appointed Governor of Yōngzhōu (雍zhōu).
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Liú Zhēndào (劉真道), former Governor of Yōngzhōu (雍zhōu), and Péi Fāngmíng (裴方míng), Governor of Liáng (梁) and Southern Qín (南秦) prefectures, were found guilty
and died in prison.
In the eighth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Táo Mǐnzǔ (陶愍祖), Grand Judge, was appointed Governor of Guǎngzhōu (廣zhōu).
In the twelfth month of winter, on the day *gēngwǔ*,
Tán Hézhī, Grand Administrator of Shǐxīng, was made Administrator of Jiāozhōu.
On the day *rénwǔ*,
an imperial edict stated:
"The state takes its people as its foundation,
and the people take food as their heaven.
Thus, if one man ceases farming,
hunger will surely follow.
When granaries are full,
rituals and propriety flourish.
Recently, however, wherever one looks, there is poverty and destitution;
families have no overnight stores.
Should taxes and labor be temporarily uneven,
people harbor sorrow and distress;
if the year is not abundant,
then illness and want spread from house to house.
This is truly because governmental virtue has not been sincere,
leading to these弊 (problems);
or perhaps because cultivation and sericulture are not widespread,
and much of the land's benefit is left unused.
Governors lack methods of transformation and guidance,
and the populace forgets the duty of diligent effort.
Reflecting on the great relief (needed),
my thoughts are fixed on it day and night.
Although decrees are frequently issued,
they ultimately fail to punish or encourage,
and merely wishing for greater prosperity
how can it be achieved?
The relevant officials should promulgate the old regulations,
and ensure the diligent enforcement of duties.
Those who wander without employment
should all be ordered to attach themselves to an occupation.
Investigate and assess diligence and idleness,
and apply rewards and punishments accordingly.
Observe competence and deficiency,
and strictly carry out demotions and promotions.
In ancient times, the emperor personally plowed the imperial fields,
reverently providing sacrificial grains.
Looking up to the former kings,
I wish to follow their excellent precedents.
Therefore, an area of a thousand *mǔ* should be measured and designated,
and an auspicious day for divination chosen.
I shall personally lead all officials
to perform rites in the suburban fields,
hoping that our sincerity
will extend to these people."
In this year,
Héxī Guó, Gāolì Guó, Bǎijì Guó, and Wō Guó all sent envoys to present local products.
In this year,
various commanderies and prefectures suffered damage to their crops from floods and droughts,
and the people faced severe famine.
Envoys were dispatched to open granaries for relief,
and to provide grain and seeds.
In the spring of the twenty-first year, in the first month, on the day *jǐhài*,
the areas of Nánxú, Nányùzhōu, and west of the Zhèjiāng in Yángzhōu
〔二九〕all had alcohol prohibited.
A general amnesty was declared throughout the empire.
All debts incurred before the nineteenth year
were entirely forgiven and abolished.
For those who suffered harvest failures last year,
their burdens were assessed and reduced.
In particularly distressed areas,
envoys were sent to the commanderies and prefectures to provide relief as appropriate.
All who wished to engage in farming,
but lacked seeds and provisions,
were granted supplies and loans.
The laborers overseen by the various departments managing the thousand *mǔ* cultivation project
were each given cloth according to rank.
On the day *wǔwǔ*,
Yìqìng, Prince of Línchuān and Wèijiāngjūn, passed away.
On the day *xīnyǒu*,
Liú Yìzōng, Tàizǐ Zhānshì, was made Administrator of Nányǎnzhōu.
In the second month, on the day *gēngwǔ*,
Zhào Bófú, Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn, was made Administrator of Yùzhōu.
On the day *jǐchǒu*,
Yìgōng, Prince of Jiāngxià, Sītú and Lù Shàngshū Shì, was promoted to Tàiwèi,
and concurrently held the position of Sītú.
On the day *gēngyín*,
Shěn Yǎnzhī, Yòuwèijiāngjūn, was made Zhōnglǐngjūn.
On the day *xīnmǎo*,
the seventh imperial son, Hóng, was enfeoffed as Prince of Jiànpíng.
On the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Dàn, Prince of Guǎnglíng, was made Administrator of Nányǎnzhōu.
In the fourth month of summer,
Xú Gēng, a commoner from Jìnlíng and Yánlíng, contributed a thousand *hú* of rice to aid the famine-stricken people.
In the fifth month, on the day *rénxū*,
Hé Shàngzhī, Shàngshū, was made Zhōnghùjūn;
Liú Dàoxī, Zīyì Cānjūn, was made Administrator of Guǎngzhōu.
In the sixth month,
there were continuous rains and floods.
On the day *dīnghài*,
an imperial edict stated:
"Persistent rains have lasted for days,
and floods are causing distress.
The people's accumulated savings are depleted,
making them prone to scarcity and want.
Officials of the two counties and all heads of the various offices and departments
should each inspect the actual situation within their jurisdiction,
provide them with firewood and rice,
and ensure thoroughness."
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day *dīngyǒu*,
Jùn, Prince of Shǐxīng and Administrator of Yángzhōu, was promoted to Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn;
Jùn, Prince of Wǔlíng and Administrator of Nányùzhōu, was promoted to Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn.
〔三０〕On the day *yǐsì*,
an imperial edict stated:
"In recent years, grain harvests have been damaged,
and excessive droughts or floods have become disasters.
This is also due to the fact that suitable cultivation methods
have not yet been fully utilized.
From now on, all commanderies belonging to Nánxú, Yǎn, Yù, and west of the Zhèjiāng in Yángzhōu,
shall all be instructed to plant wheat
to supplement their deficiencies.
Immediately transport existing seeds from Péngchéng and Xiàpī Jùn,
and entrust the Administrators with their distribution as loans.
The land in Xú and Yù has many paddy fields,
but the common people exclusively focus on dry-land farming.
The two military commanders should be informed
to inspect the old dikes,
lead the people in repairing and building them,
and also mandate the reclamation of wasteland,
to be completed by next year.
All various commanderies and prefectures
should be ordered to exert their utmost in utilizing land resources,
encouraging and guiding cultivation,
and ensuring that sericulture, hemp, and ramie cultivation
are each carried out to their fullest extent,
and not merely comply with official documents."
In the eighth month, on the day *wùchén*,
Yìjì, Prince of Héngyáng, Zhēngxī Dàjiāngjūn and Administrator of Jīngzhōu, was transferred to Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and Administrator of Nányǎnzhōu;
Yìxuān, Prince of Nánqiáo, Zhēngběi Jiāngjūn and Administrator of Nánxúzhōu, was made Chēqí Jiāngjūn and Administrator of Jīngzhōu.
〔三一〕Dàn, Prince of Guǎnglíng and Administrator of Nányǎnzhōu, was made Administrator of Nánxúzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the day *jiǎchén*,
Dàjùqú Ānzhōu was made Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn and Administrator of Liángzhōu,
and enfeoffed as Prince of Héxī.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day *jǐmǎo*,
Xú Qióng, Zuǒjūn Jiāngjūn, was made Administrator of Yǎnzhōu;
Shēn Tián, Dàjiāngjūn Cānjūn, was made Administrator of Jìzhōu.
In the spring of the twenty-second year, in the first month, on the day *xīnmǎo*, which was the first day of the month,
the new Yuánjiā Xīnlì calendar of Hé Chéngtiān, Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng, was adopted.
On the day *rénchén*,
Jùn, Prince of Wǔlíng, Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn and Administrator of Nányùzhōu, was reassigned as Administrator of Yōngzhōu;
Shuò, Prince of Nánpíng and Administrator of Xiāngzhōu, was made Administrator of Nányùzhōu.
In the second month, on the day *xīnsì*,
Wáng Sēnglǎng, Shìzhōng, was made Administrator of Xiāngzhōu.
On the day *jiǎxū*,
the eighth imperial son, Huī, was enfeoffed as Prince of Dōnghǎi;
the ninth imperial son, Chǎng, was enfeoffed as Prince of Yìyáng.
In the sixth month of summer, on the day *xīnhài*,
Shuò, Prince of Nánpíng and Administrator of Nányùzhōu, was made Administrator of Yùzhōu.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day *jǐwèi*,
Mèng Yǐ, Shàngshū Púyè, was made Shàngshū Zuǒpúyè;
Hé Shàngzhī, Zhōnghùjūn, was made Shàngshū Yòupúyè.
Jùn, Prince of Wǔlíng and Administrator of Yōngzhōu, attacked the Miǎn barbarians along the Miǎn River,
and relocated over fourteen thousand people to the capital.
On the day *yǐyǒu*,
Yìjì, Prince of Héngyáng, Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn and Administrator of Nányǎnzhōu, was reassigned as Administrator of Xúzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the day *jǐwèi*,
〔三二〕the prohibition on alcohol was lifted.
In the tenth month of winter,
a thousand *qǐng* of abandoned fields at Húshú were reclaimed.
In the twelfth month, on the day *yǐwèi*,
Fàn Yè, Tàizǐ Zhānshì, plotted rebellion,
and he and his confederates were all executed.
On the day *dīngyǒu*,
Yìkāng, Prince of Péngchéng and Dàjiāngjūn, was dismissed and reduced to commoner status.
On the day *gēngxū*,
Zhào Bófú, former Administrator of Yùzhōu, was made Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
In the spring of the twenty-third year, in the first month, on the day *dīngsì*,
Lù Huī, Grand Administrator of Chángshā, was made Administrator of Yìzhōu.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
Mèng Yǐ, Shàngshū Zuǒpúyè, left office.
Displaced people from Hànchuān were relocated to the Miǎn River area.
〔三三〕
In the second month, on the day *guǐmǎo*,
Liú Yìbīn, Zuǒwèijiāngjūn, was made Administrator of Nányǎnzhōu.
In the third month,
the Suǒ barbarians raided Yǎn and Yù.
Shēn Tián, Administrator of Qīng and Jì, defeated them.
In the fourth month of summer, on the day *dīngwèi*,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the empire.
In the sixth month, on the day *guǐwèi*, which was the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
Tán Hézhī, Administrator of Jiāozhōu, campaigned against Línyì Guó,
and conquered it.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the day *xīnwèi*,
Dù Tǎn, Sǎnqí Chángshì, was made Administrator of Qīngzhōu.
In the eighth month, on the day *guǐmǎo*,
red-turbaned bandits from Jiēyáng attacked Jiàn'ān Jùn,
burning its city and government offices.
In the ninth month, on the day *jǐmǎo*,
the Emperor's carriage visited the Guózǐxué,
and administered examinations to the students.
Fifty-nine people responded to the questions.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *wùzǐ*,
an edict stated:
"The *xiángxù* (schools) have been established for several years,
and the sons of noble families have achieved success in their studies.
Recently, I personally tested them,
and witnessed their excellent talent.
I fondly recall Zhū and Sì,
and forever cherish the past.
The students' answers and questions
were largely commendable.
The officials in charge of teaching
should all be rewarded."
Silk was bestowed, with varying amounts.
In the twelfth month, on the day *dīngyǒu*,
Xiāo Jǐngxiàn, the *Lóngxiáng Sīmǎ*, was appointed *Jiāozhōu Cìshǐ*.
This year,
there was a great harvest.
The northern dike was built,
Xuánwǔ Hú was established,
and Jǐngyáng Shān was built in Huálín Yuán.
In the twenty-fourth year, spring, first month, on the day *jiǎxū*,
a general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire,
and civil and military officials were promoted one rank.
Prisoners were pardoned or had their sentences reduced,
and various debts were宽减 with varying degrees.
Orphans, the elderly, and those with the six disabilities who could not support themselves
were each granted five *hú* of grain.
Half of this year's land tax for Jiànkāng and Mòlíng counties was remitted.
In the third month, on the day *rénshēn*,
Hùjūn Jiāngjūn Zhào Bófú was transferred.
In the summer, fifth month, on the day *jiǎxū*,
Dù Tǎn, the *Qīngzhōu Cìshǐ*, was additionally appointed *Jìzhōu Cìshǐ*.
In the sixth month,
the capital suffered from an epidemic.
On the day *bǐngxū*,
envoys were sent to all commanderies, counties, garrisons, and departments
to thoroughly inspect them
and provide medicine.
In this month,
due to the high price of goods,
a large coin was decreed to be worth two [regular coins].
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *yǐmǎo*,
the gold, silver, and treasures obtained from Línyì
were distributed as rewards, with varying amounts.
In the eighth month, on the day *yǐwèi*,
Héngyáng Wáng Yìjì, the *Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn* and *Xúzhōu Cìshǐ*, passed away.
On the day *kuǐmǎo*,
Liú Yìbīn, the *Nányánzhōu Cìshǐ*, was appointed *Xúzhōu Cìshǐ*.
In the ninth month, on the day *jǐwèi*,
Shěn Yǎnzhī, the *Zhōnglǐngjūn*, was appointed *Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn*.
On the day *xīnwèi*,
Xú Zhànzhī, the *Tàizǐ Zhànshì*, was appointed *Nányánzhōu Cìshǐ*.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day *rénwǔ*,
Hú Dànshì of Yùzhāng rebelled,
killing the *Tàishǒu* Huán Lóngzhī.
Tán Hézhī, the former *Jiāozhōu Cìshǐ*, returned south to Yùzhāng
and suppressed the rebellion.
On the day *rénchén*,
Jiànpíng Wáng Hóng was appointed *Zhōnghùjūn*.
In the eleventh month, on the day *jiǎyín*,
the tenth imperial son, Hún, was enfeoffed as Rǔyīn Wáng.
In the twenty-fifth year, spring, first month, on the day *wùchén*,
an edict stated:
"Recently, ice and snow have lasted for ten days,
and firewood and grain have become expensive.
Many poor families
are in distress and lacking.
Let officials inspect the two counties of the capital and the garrisons
and bestow firewood and rice upon them."
In the second month, on the day *gēngyín*,
an edict stated:
"Not forgetting danger in times of peace
is a common principle for managing the world;
training troops and teaching warfare
is a state institution.
Therefore, by establishing discipline and clarifying what is shameful,
the young and old will know what is forbidden.
Although military administration has been improved recently,
the orders have not been clearly understood.
Now that Xuānwǔ Chǎng has just been completed,
a date should be set for a grand drill of all armies.
We shall take advantage of a hunting expedition
to practice military arts and discuss matters."
In the intercalary month, on the day *jǐyǒu*,
a grand military parade was held at Xuānwǔ Chǎng.
In the third month, on the day *gēngchén*,
the imperial carriage conducted a hunting expedition.
In the summer, fourth month, on the day *yǐsì*,
two new gates, Chānghé and Guǎngmò, were built.
The former Guǎngmò Mén was renamed Chéngmíng,
and Kāiyáng was renamed Jīnyáng.
On the day *yǐmǎo*,
Wǔlíng Wáng Jùn, the *Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn* and *Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ*, was promoted to *Ānběi Jiāngjūn* and *Xúzhōu Cìshǐ*.
On the day *kuǐhài*,
Xiāo Sīhuà, the *Yòuwèi Jiāngjūn*, was appointed *Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ*.
In the fifth month, on the day *jǐmǎo*,
the decree for large coins to be worth two [regular coins] was abolished.
In the sixth month, on the day *gēngxū*,
Línglíng Wáng Sīmǎ Yuán yú passed away.
On the day *gēngshēn*,
Wǔlíng Wáng Jùn, the *Ānběi Jiāngjūn* and *Xúzhōu Cìshǐ*, was additionally appointed *Yánzhōu Cìshǐ*.
On the day *bǐngyín*,
Nánqiáo Wáng Yìxuān, the *Chējì Jiāngjūn* and *Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ*, was promoted to *Sīkōng*.
In the autumn, seventh month, on the day *rénwǔ*,
Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū Wáng Jìnghóng passed away.
In the eighth month, on the day *jǐyǒu*,
Liú Xiùzhī, the *Fǔjūn Cānjūn*, was appointed *Liáng* and *Nánqín* two *Zhōu Cìshǐ*.
On the day *jiǎzǐ*,
the eleventh imperial son, Yù, was enfeoffed as Huáiyáng Wáng.
In the ninth month, on the day *xīnwèi*,
Hé Shàngzhī, the *Shàngshū Yòupúyè*, was appointed *Shàngshū Zuǒpúyè*;
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn Shěn Yǎnzhī was transferred;
Liú Zūnkǎo, the *Wúxīng Tàishǒu*, was appointed *Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn*.
In the twenty-sixth year, spring, first month, on the day *xīnsì*,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the southern suburbs.
In the second month, on the day *jǐhài*,
the imperial carriage traveled by land to Dāntú
to visit the imperial tombs.
In the third month, on the day *dīngsì*,
[三四]an edict stated:
"I have been away from the northern capital
for over twenty years.
Though it is said to be near,
there was no path to see it.
Now, as there is peace within the four seas,
the weather is harmonious, and the year is bountiful,
I am again able to pay homage to the old ancestral graves,
expressing my boundless thoughts,
and feast the old people,
conveying my longing for the distant past.
This emotion surpasses that for my hometown (*sāngzǐ*)
and is deeper than my passing through Pèi.
I speak with eternal passion,
and my gratitude and comfort are indeed profound.
It is fitting to widely proclaim benevolence and kindness,
extending it to all under heaven.
A general amnesty is hereby proclaimed throughout the empire.
Half of this year's rent and tax for the *qiáo* and old households of Dāntú County shall be remitted.
For the counties through which I have traveled,
half of the land tax shall be remitted.
Officials of the two-thousand-*shí* rank have all worked diligently in royal affairs
and should be rewarded.
Families whose members died or perished in the three battles of climbing the city walls and in major battles,
and those who are old, sick, single, or weak,
shall all receive widespread support and relief.
Envoys shall be dispatched to tour among the common people
and inquire about their hardships.
Orphans, widows and widowers, and those with the six disabilities who cannot support themselves
shall each be granted five *hú* of grain."
Envoys were dispatched to offer sacrifices at the tomb of Hē Wújì, the late *Jìn Gù Sīkōng Zhōngsù Gōng*.
On the day *yǐchǒu*,
the three commanderies of Nánpèi, Běipèi, and Xiàpī were re-established.
Another edict stated:
"Jīngkǒu has been auspicious since ancient times,
with its significance manifest in recent history.
Embracing rivers and mountains,
it forms a vital screen for the heartland.
Its roads extend in four directions,
its benefits reach the Huái and the sea.
Its cities are high and bright,
its customs pure and unified.
It encompasses strategic advantages,
truly a renowned capital.
Thus, it could illuminate the imperial spirit
and prosper the imperial enterprise.
In recent years, governors and officials have moved,
and military personnel and civilians have scattered.
The markets and residences
are not as they were in the past.

he posthumously changed the posthumous and temple names.
The historian remarks: Tàizǔ showed exceptional talent in his youth.
Though he lacked the strict guidance of tutors,
Heaven endowed him with a harmonious and keen disposition,
and he naturally possessed the virtues of a ruler.
When he assumed the imperial position,
his reign was long.
The framework of governance was fully established,
and regulations were clear and strict.
Punishments were categorized,
and noble ranks were not granted indiscriminately.
Thus, he could achieve internal clarity and external peace,
and the four seas were tranquil.
In the past, the Eastern Hàn dynasty often referred to the precedents of Jiànwǔ and Yǒngpíng.
From that time onward,
Yuánjiā was also frequently mentioned,
which indeed signifies its prosperity.
However, in assigning generals and dispatching commanders,
he deviated from the principle of entrusting authority.
His talent fell short of Guāngwǔ,
yet he remotely controlled military strategies,
even down to the days of attack and hours of battle.
All had to await his final instructions.
Although the loss of armies and the destruction of forces
might not be due to generals like Hán or Bái,
the prolonged invasion of the border regions
was also a result of this.
Moreover, when words leaked from his private chambers,
it became difficult to bind the palace attendants,
though calamity arose unexpectedly,
there was indeed a reason for it.
Alas!

Annals, Chapter 6: Emperor Xiàowǔ
Emperor Shìzǔ Xiàowǔ, personal name Jùn,
courtesy name Xiūlóng, milk name Dàomín,
was the third son of Emperor Wén.
He was born in the seventh year of Yuánjiā, autumn, the eighth month, on the *gēngwǔ* day.
In the twelfth year,
he was made Prince of Wǔlíng,
with a fief of two thousand households.
In the sixteenth year,
he was appointed Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Xiāngzhōu, General Who Conquers the Barbarians, and Inspector of Xiāngzhōu,
also commanding the garrison at Shítou.
In the seventeenth year,
he was promoted to Holder of a Tally, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Nányù, Yù, Sī, Yōng, and Bìng five provinces, and Inspector of Nányùzhōu,
with his general title remaining as before,
still garrisoning Shítou.
In the twenty-first year,
he was additionally made Supervisor of Qínzhōu,
and promoted to General Who Comforts the Army.
The following year,
he was transferred to Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Yōng, Liáng, the four Qín provinces (North and South), Xiāngyáng, Jìnglíng, Nányáng, Shùnyáng, Xīnyě, and Suí six commanderies of Jīngzhōu,
Pacifying Barbarians Colonel, and Inspector of Yōngzhōu,
with his tally and general title remaining as before.
Since the Jìn dynasty's move to the south,
Xiāngyáng had not had an imperial prince as a major governor.
At that time, Tàizǔ wished to campaign in Guān and Hé,
hence this appointment.
Soon after, he was granted a set of drums and pipes.
In the twenty-fifth year,
he was restyled Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Nányǎn, Xú, Yǎn, Qīng, Jì, and Yōu six provinces, and Liángjùn of Yùzhōu, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Xúzhōu,
with his tally remaining as before,
garrisoning Péngchéng in the north.
Soon after, he concurrently served as Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
When Jùn, Prince of Shǐxīng, became Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu,
the Emperor relieved him of the supervision of Nányǎn.
In the twenty-seventh year,
due to the defeat at Rǔyáng,
his title was demoted to General Who Guards the Army.
Moreover, due to the southern invasion by the Suǒ barbarians,
he was demoted to Northern Central-Army General.
In the twenty-eighth year,
he was promoted to Supervisor of Nányǎnzhōu and Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu,

Soon after, he was transferred to Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Jiāngzhōu, Jiāngxià of Jīngzhōu, Xīyáng, Jìnxī, and Xīncài four commanderies of Yùzhōu, Southern Central-Army General, and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu,

At that time, the barbarians along the Yangtze River were raiding,

For the first time, troops were stationed at the palace gates and in the upper galleries.
Zhū Xiūzhī, the Administrator of Jiāngxià, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Yōngzhōu.
Wáng Tánshēng, the Censor-in-Chief, was appointed Governor of Guǎngzhōu.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Liǔ Yuánjǐng, the newly appointed Governor of Yōngzhōu, was appointed General of the Palace Guard.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Lǔ Shuǎng, the Governor of Sīzhōu, was appointed Governor of Yùzhōu.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Liú Xiùzhī, the Governor of Liángzhōu and Nánqínzhōu, was appointed Governor of Yìzhōu.
Páng Xiùzhī, the Grand Commandant’s Chief Clerk, was appointed Governor of Liángzhōu and Nánqínzhōu.
Xú Yíbǎo, the Army Commander of the General of the Household, was appointed Governor of Yǎanzhōu.
Wáng Xuánmó, the General Who Pacifies Barbarians, was appointed Governor of Xúzhōu.
Suíwáng Dàn, the General of the Household, was promoted to General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry.
Wáng Sēngdá, the Right Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to another post.
Chǔ Zhànzhī, the Administrator of Dānyáng, was appointed Right Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
Huī, the Heir Apparent of Nánqiáowáng, the Grandee Remonstrant, was appointed Governor of Xiāngzhōu.
On the *dīngsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The founding kings established teachings,
striving to promote governance.
Supporting ministers assisted the era,
diligently offering important policies.
Looking up to the sagely rules,
this path has always been preserved.
I, with my humble person,
am connected to the inherited grand enterprise.
To propagate the inherited benevolence
is my unwavering intention.
Indeed, to base expenditure on income
is a state ordinance,
yet the appropriateness of provision
often deviates from normal standards.
Military service consumes resources,
and treasuries are depleted.
Public and private expenditures,
have not yet been reduced.
This is not how to follow the former edicts,
and respectfully uphold the legacy.
From now on, all matters that can diminish oneself and benefit the people, or move from complexity to simplicity,
should be implemented,
to match my intentions.”
On the *gēngshēn* day,
an edict ordered the responsible officials to deliberate on merits and award according to their different grades.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,

Tǔyùhún Shíyín, the General Who Pacifies the West and Governor of Xīqínzhōu and Hézhōu, was promoted to General-in-Chief Who Guards the West, and granted the privilege of opening a *fǔ* and having the same official rank as the Three Ducal Ministers.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Nánxúzhōu was again divided to establish Nányǎanzhōu.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Nánqiáowáng Yìxuān was enfeoffed as Nánjùnwáng.
Suíwáng Dàn was enfeoffed as Jìnglíngwáng.
Kǎi, the second son of Yìxuān and Marquis of Yíyáng, was enfeoffed as Yíyángxiànwáng.
In the intercalary month, on the *rénshēn* day,
Shěn Qìngzhī, the General of the Palace Guard, was appointed General Who Guards the Army and Governor of Nányǎanzhōu.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Liǔ Yuánjǐng, the General of the Palace Guard, was appointed General of the Palace Guard.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Lè Xún and fifteen others, serving concurrently as Grandee Remonstrants and Regular Palace Attendants, were dispatched to inspect the customs of the regions.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the rent and taxes for Xúnyáng and Xīyáng Commanderies were remitted for three years.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Nánjùnwáng Yìxuān, the Chancellor, was changed to Governor of Jīngzhōu and Xiāngzhōu.
Jìnglíngwáng Dàn, the General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Governor of Jīngzhōu, was changed to Governor of Yángzhōu.
Wáng Sēngdá, the Colonel Who Quells the Southern Barbarians, was appointed General of the Palace Guard.
In this month,
the office of Minister of the Guard was established.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *xīnchǒu* day, the first day of the month,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The world’s path is not yet peaceful,
and the only worry is the state.
Indeed, to gather all good deeds
is certainly not something to be discussed by a single talent.
Especially with my meager virtue,
facing a period of decline and weakness,
I ponder day and night,
ever awaiting the dawn.
Princes, dukes, ministers, and gentlemen,
anyone with excellent counsel or good governance
that can uphold integrity and guide customs,
should all express their sincerity,
without any concealment.”
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The common people are exhausted and suffering,
and corvée labor and taxes are still numerous.
Reflecting on this,
it is appropriate to promote frugality and reduction.
All expenditures not for military or state affairs
should be completely halted.
Minor crafts and the Imperial Workshop should be reduced.
Carved patterns and elaborate skills,
gold and silver decorations,
things not related to practicality,
are strictly forbidden.
Imperial food and clothing
should be reduced, eliminating extravagance.
Hunting and gathering by land and water
should follow the seasons and months.
Official and private markets
must ensure fairness.
Regarding public enclosures of rivers, seas, fields, and ponds,
the extent of their opening or closing should be thoroughly considered.
Competition for profit by noble relatives
is strictly prohibited.”
On the *wùxū* day,
Zōng Quān, the General of the Right Palace Guard, was appointed Governor of Guǎngzhōu.
On the *jǐsì* day,
Nánpíngwáng Shuò, the Minister of Works, passed away.
In the eighth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
all former military servants of Emperor Wǔ,
who had once been in the imperial residence,
and whose persons were still alive,
were universally granted freedom from servitude.
On the *yǐhài* day,
Jiànpíngwáng Hóng, the Left Senior Director of the Department of State Affairs, was additionally appointed Supervisor of the Central Secretariat and General of the Central Army.
On the *dīnghài* day,
