Yuán Hóng, the Administrator of Pèijùn, was appointed Governor of Níngzhōu.
Fèi Shěn, the Army Commander of the General of the Garrison, was appointed Governor of Liángzhōu and Nánqínzhōu.
On the *jiǎwǔ* day,
Wáng Sēngdá, the General of the Palace Guard, was transferred to another post.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīngsì,
the former Shàngshū, Liú Yìqí, was made Zhōnghùjūn.
On the day Rénxū,
those who died in battle at Xīntíng
were again granted the same treatment as those in the capital.
Xiāo Jiǎn, the Nánhǎi Tàishǒu and a member of Shào's faction, rebelled, holding Guǎngzhōu.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Fǔguó Jiāngjūn Dèng Wǎn suppressed and pacified him.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the imperial carriage listened to lawsuits at Yuèwǔtáng.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Zuǒjūn Jiāngjūn Lǔ Xiù was made Sīzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Bǐngchén,
the Sàiměng (朔望問訊) greetings of all officials in the imperial secretariat and bureaus were suspended.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the Kingdom of Gāolí sent envoys to offer local products.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jiǎxū,
the Dūshuǐtái was abolished,
the office of Dūshuǐ Shǐzhě was eliminated,
and the office of Shuǐhéng Lìng was established.
On the day Guǐwèi,
in preparation for establishing the Eastern Palace,
the offices of Tàizǐ Shuàigēnglìng, Bùbīng, Yìjūn Xiàowèi, Lǚfēn Zhōnglángjiàng, Rǒngcóng Púshè, and Zuǒyòu Jīnú Jiāngjūn were eliminated.
The Zhōngshùzǐ, Zhōngshèrén, Shùzǐ, Shèrén, and Xǐmǎ
each had their former numbers reduced by half.
In the first year of Xiàojiàn, spring, in the first month, on the day Jǐhài, the new moon,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices in the Southern Suburbs,
changed the era name,
and granted a general amnesty to the empire.
On the day Rényín,
Dānyáng Yǐn Xiāo Sīhuà was made Ānběi Jiāngjūn and Xúzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Hùjūn Jiāngjūn Liú Yìqí was transferred from his post,
and Shàngshūlìng Hé Shàngzhī was made Zuǒguānglù Dàfū and Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
On the day Wùshēn,
an imperial edict stated:
"To primarily value agriculture for sustenance
is the fundamental task of governing the state.
To select scholars and observe their conduct
is to govern the court correctly.
The internal difficulties have just eased,
and political education has not yet been fully disseminated.
There is still the drawback of wasted clothing and food,
and the selection system lacks the excellence of 'observing the state' (觀國).
In the past, Wèi Wén (衛文) diligently served the people,
and Gāozōng respectfully observed silence;
they were eventually able to recruit worthy men from reclusion,
leading to the flourishing of the latter years of the great Yīn dynasty.
I am often uneasy and anxious,
never forgetting to reflect on this day and night.
All officials who administer and serve the people
should carefully re-examine the old regulations
and diligently maximize the land's benefits.
Those who diligently farm and accumulate well
should have their names reported by their respective localities.
The regulations for commendation and selection
should be carefully established.
From the four quarters, those outstanding in filial piety and integrity,
if without talent, should not be nominated.
Those who respond to the call and are truly worthy
should be immediately appointed and promoted.
If there is nothing worthy of note,
they should still be granted an official position.
If there are those who are not fit to serve
and have falsely obtained honorable recommendation,
they should be sent back to their hometowns
and further subjected to a ban from official service.
The Shàngshū (Ministry of Personnel) is the root of all officials,
the pivot of all governmental achievements.
The Chéngláng (Secretaries) and various departments
each have their responsibilities.
However, recently, matters, whether great or small,
all fall to the Lìng (Director) and Pú (Attendant).
This is not how various talents should be utilized to build,
nor how many abilities should accomplish undertakings.
The system should be clarified again,
and all should be held responsible for their accomplishments,
diligence and idleness should be investigated,
and rewards and punishments strictly enforced."
On the day Rényín,
four-zhū coins were re-minted.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Imperial Prince Zǐyè was established as Crown Prince.
A promotion of one rank was granted to all in the empire who had lost their fathers.
Filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives were granted grain and silk according to different grades.
In this month,
the Zhèngguāng Diàn was begun.
In the second month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Yùzhōu Cìshǐ Lǔ Shuǎng, Chējì Jiāngjūn and Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ Zāng Zhì, Chéngxiàng and Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ Nánjùn Wáng Yìxuān, and Yǎnzhōu Cìshǐ Xú Yíbǎo raised troops and rebelled.
On the day Yǐhài,
Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn Dōnghǎi Wáng Huī was transferred from his post.
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn Liǔ Yuánjǐng was promoted to Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn.
On the day Rénwǔ,
a partial amnesty was granted to Yùzhōu.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn Wáng Xuánmó was made Yùzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Guǐsì,
Xuánmó advanced and occupied Liángshān.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Ānběi Sīmǎ Xiàhóu Zǔhuān was made Yǎnzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the third month, on the day Guǐhài,
internal and external garrisons were put on high alert.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Ānběi Jiāngjūn and Xúzhōu Cìshǐ Xiāo Sīhuà was made Ānnán Jiāngjūn and Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ,
and Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn Liǔ Yuánjǐng was made Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ with his original title.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Tàizǐ Zuǒwèi Shuài Páng Xiùzhī was made Xúzhōu Cìshǐ.
Xú Yíbǎo was defeated by Xiàhóu Zǔhuān,
abandoned his troops, and fled.
On the day Bǐngyín,
Fǔguó Zhǎngshǐ Míng Yìn was made Jìzhōu Cìshǐ.
In summer, in the fourth month, on the day Wùchén,
Hòujiāngjūn Liú Yìqí was made Xiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Píngxī Jiāngjūn and Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Zhū Xiūzhī was made Ānxī Jiāngjūn and Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Zhènjūn Jiāngjūn and Nányǎnzhōu Cìshǐ Shěn Qìngzhī heavily defeated Lǔ Shuǎng at Xiǎoxiàn in Lìyáng,
and beheaded Shuǎng.
On the day Guǐsì,
Qìngzhī was promoted to Zhènběi Dàjiāngjūn.
The sixteenth imperial brother, Xiūqiàn, was enfeoffed as Dōngpíng Wáng.
Before he could be formally appointed,
he passed away.
In the fifth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Yìxuān and others attacked Liángshān,
and Wáng Xuánmó heavily defeated them.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the state of emergency was lifted.
On the day Guǐhài,
Wúxīng Tàishǒu Liú Yánsūn was made Shàngshū Yòupúshè.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùchén,
Zāng Zhì fled to Wǔchāng,
where he was beheaded by someone,
and his head was sent to the capital.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn Liǔ Yuánjǐng was promoted to Fǔjūn Dàjiāngjūn,
and Zhènběi Dàjiāngjūn Shěn Qìngzhī was also granted Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn and Wǔchāng Wáng Hún was made Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Guǐwèi,
Yángzhōu was divided to establish Dōngyángzhōu.
Jīng, Xiāng, Jiāng, and Yùzhōu were divided to establish Yǐngzhōu.
The Nánmán Xiàowèi was abolished.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the office of Lùshàngshūshì was abolished.
On the day Gēngyín,
Yìxuān was granted death in Jiānglíng.
In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day Bǐngshēn, the new moon,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Bǐngchén,
a general amnesty was granted to the empire.
Civil and military officials were granted one rank of爵.
Overdue taxes and old debts were not to be collected again.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
Jiànchāng Jùn was established in Yōngzhōu.
Huìjī Tàishǒu Yìyáng Wáng Chǎng was made Dōngyángzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Fǔjūn Dàjiāngjūn Liǔ Yuánjǐng was reinstated as Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn,
retaining his original title.
On the day Rényín,
Yóujī Jiāngjūn Yuán Hùzhī was made Xúzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Rénchén,
Ānxī Sīmǎ Liáng Tǎn was made Cìshǐ of Liáng and Nánqín prefectures.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Qiángnú Jiāngjūn Yǐn Huáishùn was made Níngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Zuǒguānglù Dàfū Hé Shàngzhī resigned as Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Shàngzhī was granted the title of Tèjìn.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Ānnán Jiāngjūn and Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ Xiāo Sīhuà was made Zhènxī Jiāngjūn and Yǐngzhōu Cìshǐ.
In winter, in the tenth month, on the day Wùyín,
an imperial edict stated:
"Kǒng Ní (Confucius) embodied Heaven and descended virtue,
like the flourishing of Zhōu and the rise of Hàn,
he governed the three realms (heaven, earth, man)
and crowned a hundred kings.
From previous generations,
he has been universally praised and extolled.
Due to the wrong person in charge of rites,
the ancestral sacrifices were neglected.
The former court had long preserved his legacy,
and an edict was issued to build a shrine,
but worldly affairs obstructed the effort,
and the matter could not be accomplished.
With frequent and profound national difficulties,
loyal and brave individuals have risen up,
truly relying on sacred righteousness,
which the great teaching encourages.
I forever bear this in mind,
never forgetting it even as I await the dawn.
Therefore, a temple system should be established,
following the rites of the feudal lords.
A bright and auspicious site should be carefully chosen,
and ample sacrificial offerings should be provided."
On the day Dīnghài,
Mìshūjiān Dōnghǎi Wáng Huī was made Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn and Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.
Ānlù Jùn was established in Yǐngzhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
the Dūshuǐ Tái (Directorate of Waterways) was re-established,
and the office of Dūshuǐ Shǐzhě (Commissioner of Waterways) was instituted.
In this year,
taxes were first levied on Qiaomin (immigrants) in Nánxúzhōu.
In the second year, first month, on the day Rén Yín,
Yù, Prince of Xiāngdōng, General of Champion Cavalry, was appointed Zhōnghùjūn (Central Protector of the Army).
In the second month, on the day Jǐ Chǒu,
the state of Pólóu sent envoys to present local products.
On the day Bǐng Yín,

Shěn Qìngzhī, General-in-Chief Who Guards the North and Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, was appointed Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū (Grandee of the Left, Grand Master of Bright Happiness) and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī (Chancellor with Ceremonial Privileges Equal to the Three Dukes).
On the day Xīn Sì,
Liú Yánsūn, Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu.
In the third month, on the day Xīn Hài,
Liú Zūnkǎo, Grand Administrator of Wúxīng, was appointed Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
On the day Rén Zǐ,
Yáng Wénzhì, acting General Who Conquers the West, was appointed General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Běiqínzhōu.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Rén Shēn,
the state of Hénán sent envoys to present local products.
On the day Rén Wǔ,
Tán Hézhī, Grand Administrator of Yùzhāng, was appointed Inspector of Yùzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the day Wù Xū,
Liú Zūnkǎo, Inspector of Xiāngzhōu, was appointed Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs;
Yuán Hóng, formerly Sīmǎ of the Vanguard Army, was appointed Inspector of Jiāozhōu.
On the day Gēng Zǐ,
Shēn Tǎn, General of Aid to the State, was appointed Inspector of Xú and Yǎn prefectures.
On the day Guǐ Mǎo,
Gù Jìzhī, General of the Right Guard, was appointed Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
On the day Dīng Wèi,
Wáng Yǎn, Jīnzǐ Guānglù Dàfū (Grandee of Golden Purple, Grand Master of Bright Happiness), was appointed Yòu Guānglù Dàfū (Grandee of the Right, Grand Master of Bright Happiness).
In the sixth month, on the day Jiǎ Zǐ,
due to the lifting of national mourning,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
On the day Gēng Chén,
Wáng Xuánmó, Marquis of Qǔjiāng County, was appointed Inspector of Yùzhōu.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Guǐ Sì,
the thirteenth imperial younger brother, Xiūyòu, was enfeoffed as Prince of Shānyáng;
the fourteenth imperial younger brother, Xiūmào, was enfeoffed as Prince of Hǎilíng;
the fifteenth imperial younger brother, Xiūyè, was enfeoffed as Prince of Póyáng.
On the day Wù Xū,
Xiāo Sīhuà, General Who Guards the West, passed away.
On the day Jǐ Yǒu,
Liú Xiùzhī, Inspector of Yìzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Yǐngzhōu.
The state of Pánpán sent envoys to present local products.
On the day Jiǎ Yín,
Dào Yuándù, Grand Administrator of Yìxīng, was appointed Inspector of Yìzhōu.
In the eighth month, on the day Gēng Shēn,
Wǔchāng Wáng Hún, Inspector of Yōngzhōu, committed a crime
and was demoted to commoner.
He committed suicide.
On the day Xīn Yǒu,
Liú Yánsūn, Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, was appointed General Who Guards the Army and Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
The state of Jīntuólì sent envoys to present local products.
The people of Sānwú suffered from famine.
On the day Guǐ Yǒu,
an imperial edict ordered relief loans to be issued wherever needed.
On the day Bǐng Zǐ,
an imperial edict stated:
"The restrictions on imperial parks are too extensive and far-reaching,
hindering people's livelihoods.
They should be thoroughly reviewed for areas to be opened or relaxed
and granted to the poor."
On the day Rén Wǔ,
Wáng Xuánmó, newly appointed Inspector of Yùzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Qīng and Jì prefectures;
Shēn Tián, Inspector of Qīngzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Yùzhōu.
On the day Jiǎ Shēn,
Tán Hézhī, General of the Right Guard, was appointed Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the day Dīng Hài,
the imperial carriage reviewed military exercises at Xuānwǔ Cháng.
On the day Gēng Xū,
an imperial edict stated:
"The nation's path has twice faced difficulty,
with hardships and perils fully gathered.
Though I am of meager virtue,
I have ultimately received great blessings.
The fortune of renewal
is indeed profound for a hundred kings;
yet the decrees of grace and pardon
have not differed from ordinary generosity.
I often consider this with earnest thought,
pondering it day and night.
Prior to my ascension to the throne,
all who were banished due to crimes
are permitted to return to their native places.
Families implicated in offenses,
if there are still survivors,
their sons and younger brothers may be appointed to official positions according to their talent."
In winter, tenth month, on the day Rén Wǔ,
Yìgōng, Prince of Jiāngxià, Grand Tutor, concurrently held the position of Inspector of Yángzhōu;
Dàn, Prince of Jìnglín, General-in-Chief of Cavalry, Inspector of Yángzhōu, was appointed Sīkōng (Minister of Works) and Inspector of Nánxúzhōu;

Hóng, Prince of Jiànpíng, Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, General of the Central Army, was appointed Shàngshū Lìng (Director of the Department of State Affairs);
their general titles remained as before.
In the eleventh month, on the day Wù Zǐ,
Yù, Prince of Xiāngdōng, Zhōnghùjūn, was transferred;
Liú Yánsūn, General Who Guards the Army, was appointed Hùjūn Jiāngjūn (Protector-General of the Army).
Wáng Xuánmó, Inspector of Qīng and Jì prefectures, was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
On the day Jiǎ Wǔ,
Yuán Hùzhī, Grand Minister of War, was appointed Inspector of Qīng and Jì prefectures.
[一一]On the day Xīn Hài,
the state of Gāolì sent envoys to present local products.
In the twelfth month, on the day Guǐ Hài,
Xiāo Jǐngxiàn, formerly Inspector of Jiāozhōu, was reappointed Inspector of Jiāozhōu.
In the third year, spring, first month, on the day Xīn Hài (which was the first day of the month),
the eighteenth imperial younger brother, Xiūfàn, was enfeoffed as Prince of Shùnyáng;
the nineteenth imperial younger brother, Xiūruò, was enfeoffed as Prince of Bālíng.
On the day Wù Xū,
Zǐshàng, the second imperial son, was enfeoffed as Prince of Xīyáng.
On the day Xīn Chǒu,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifice at the southern suburb.
On the day Rén Zǐ,
the Empress Dowager's consort, Hè Shì, was established.
On the day Jiǎ Yín,
a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
In the second month, on the day Guǐ Hài,
Wáng Yǎn, Yòu Guānglù Dàfū, passed away.
On the day Jiǎ Zǐ,
Zōng [⿱⿰売⽎心], Inspector of Guǎngzhōu, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yùzhōu.
On the day Dīng Mǎo,
Wáng Yì, newly appointed Censor-in-Chief, was appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
[一二]On the day Dīng Chǒu,
it was first decreed that on the first and fifteenth day of each month, the emperor would hold court at the Western Hall to receive officials of various ranks
and hear their memorials.
On the day Rén Wǔ,
officials, both internal and external, who possessed fields near the capital,
were permitted to send their assigned clerks and servants to engage in agricultural work.
In the third month, on the day Guǐ Chǒu,
Zǐshàng, Prince of Xīyáng, was appointed Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu.
In the intercalary month, on the day Wù Wǔ,
Liú Zūnkǎo, Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred.
On the day Guǐ Yǒu,
Xiūyè, Prince of Póyáng, passed away.
On the day Gēng Chén,
the inspections and purges of military artisans from before the thirtieth year of Yuánjiā were suspended.
In summer, fifth month, on the day Xīn Yǒu,
it was decreed that within the seven prefectures of Jīng, Xú, Yǎn, Yù, Yōng, Qīng, and Jì,
any household possessing one horse
would be exempt from corvée labor for one adult male.
On the day Rén Xū,
Liú Yǔ, General of the Right Guard, was appointed Inspector of Yìzhōu.
In the sixth month,
the Emperor heard legal cases in Huálín Yuán.
In autumn, seventh month,
Yìgōng, Prince of Jiāngxià, Grand Tutor, resigned from his post as Inspector of Yángzhōu.
On the day Bǐng Zǐ,
Zǐshàng, Prince of Xīyáng, Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Yángzhōu;
Xiūrén, Prince of Jiàn'ān, Supervisor of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu.
In the eighth month, on the day Wù Xū,
Fèi Yān, Consulting Military Adviser to the Northern Central Guard General, was appointed Inspector of Jiāozhōu.
[一三]On the day Dīng Wèi,
Wáng Kūn, Director of the Bureau of Civil Office in the Department of State Affairs, was appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
[一四]
In the ninth month, on the day Rén Xū,
Liú Zūnkǎo, Prefect of Dānyáng, was appointed Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
[一五]
In winter, tenth month, on the day Guǐ Wèi,
Zhāng Yuè, Grand Administrator of Xúnyáng, was appointed Inspector of Yìzhōu.
On the day Bǐng Wǔ,
Yìgōng, Prince of Jiāngxià, Grand Tutor, was promoted to Tàizǎi (Grand Preceptor),
and concurrently held the position of Sītú (Minister over the Masses).
On the day Dīng Wèi,
Liǔ Yuánjǐng, General of the Palace Guard, was additionally granted the title of General-in-Chief of Cavalry;
Hóng, Prince of Jiànpíng, Director of the Department of State Affairs, was additionally granted the titles of Supervisor of the Central Secretariat and General of the Guards;
Huī, Prince of Dōnghǎi, General Who Comforts the Army, Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, was promoted to the title of General Who Pacifies the South.
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐ Chǒu,
Yuán Jǐng, Grand Administrator of Huáinán, was executed in the marketplace for his crimes.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐng Wǔ,
Kǒng Língfú, Imperial Household Grandee, was appointed Inspector of Yǐngzhōu.
In the first year of Dàmíng, spring, first month, on the day Xīn Hài (which was the first day of the month),
the reign title was changed,
and a general amnesty was declared throughout the realm.
Elderly people, orphans, and the sick and disabled were granted grain and silk according to their needs.
On the day Gēng Wǔ,
Liú Yánsūn, Protector-General of the Army, was transferred;
Yù, Prince of Xiāngdōng, General of the Right Guard, was appointed Zhōnghùjūn.
There was heavy rain in the capital.
On the day Xīn Wèi,
envoys were dispatched to inspect,
and firewood and rice were distributed.
In the second month, on the day Jǐ Hài,
public fields for officials who govern the people were restored.
The Suǒ Captives invaded Yǎnzhōu.
In the third month, on the day Rén Xū,
it was decreed that ministers granted additional ceremonial swords
were not permitted to enter the palace city gates.
The Liao people of Liángzhōu requested to become internal subjects,
and Huáihàn Commandery was established.
In summer, fourth month,
there was an epidemic in the capital.
On the day Bǐng Shēn,
envoys were dispatched to inspect,
and medicines were distributed.
For those who died without proper burial,
the officials arranged for their collection and interment.
On the day Gēng Zǐ,
Sòngjiàn Commandery and Línhè in Xiāngzhōu were abolished.
In the fifth month,
Wúxīng and Yìxīng experienced great floods,
and the people suffered from famine.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
envoys were dispatched to open granaries and provide relief.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the emperor heard lawsuits in Huálínyuán.
On the day Yǐhài,
Shěn Tánqìng, the General of the Left Guard, was appointed Inspector of Xúzhōu.
Liáng Jǐncōng, the General Who Assists the State, was appointed Inspector of Hézhōu and King of Dàngchāng.
In the sixth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Liú Zhǐzǐ Xīn, formerly a Commandant of Infantry to the Crown Prince, succeeded Lǎng as King of Nánfēng.
On the day Xīnsì,
Shānyáng Wáng Xiūyòu, the Commandant of Chángshuǐ, was appointed Inspector of Dōngyángzhōu.
On the day Dīnghài,
Xiūyòu was reassigned as Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
Yán Jùn, the Prefect of Dānyáng, was appointed Inspector of Dōngyángzhōu.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Xīnwèi,
the migrant commanderies and counties in Yǒngzhōu were settled on the land.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùxū,
Yángpíng Commandery was established in Yǎnzhōu.
On the day Rén'yín,
the emperor heard lawsuits in Huálínyuán.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Jìnglíng Wáng Dàn, the Minister of Works and Inspector of Nánxúzhōu, was reassigned as Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu.
Liú Yánsūn, the Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, was appointed General Who Guards the Army and Inspector of Nánxúzhōu.
In winter, the tenth month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
an imperial edict stated:
“The way of the 'beaded cap' (a metaphor for governance),
has its origins in the knotted cords [of ancient administration].
The diligence of the 'midday sun' (a metaphor for tireless work),
is as urgent as that of Empress Jī.
Furthermore, the world is in decline, and teachings are superficial;
the times are superficial and decadent.
Although We strive within the realm,
and rise before dawn,
Our wisdom is inferior to former kings,
and Our efforts are less extensive than past eras.
When We reflect on Our meager virtues,
Our shame is indeed profound.
Complaints from court and grievances from the countryside
rarely reach Us directly.
Matters that benefit the people and are advantageous to the public good
are often obscured.
From now on, all high officials and common administrators,
as well as common people and humble servants,
who harbor sincere thoughts and aspirations,
or suffer injustice and remain confined to their homes,
or are wronged and bear false accusations,
and whose voices have not yet reached the imperial court,
are all permitted to personally present their petitions.
All matters, great or small, shall be reported.
On days when We hold court,
We shall personally review them face to face.”
On the day Jiǎchén,
Yú Qìng, the King of Bǎijì, was appointed Grand General Who Guards the East.
In the twelfth month, on the day Dīnghài,
Shùnyáng Wáng Xiūfàn was re-enfeoffed as King of Guìyáng.
On the day Wùxū,
the emperor heard lawsuits in Huálínyuán.
In the second year, spring, the first month, on the day Xīnhài,
the imperial carriage performed sacrifices in the southern suburbs.
On the day Rénzǐ,
an imperial edict stated:
“Last year, the eastern region suffered extensive flood disasters.
Spring farming is now due,
and extra preferential measures should be given.
The necessary grain and seeds
should be lent out in a timely manner.”
On the day Bǐngchén,
land taxes for commanderies and counties were restored,
along with the salaries and stipends for the Nine Kinsmen.
On the day Rénxū,
an imperial edict stated:
“When the late emperor’s divine mandate first arose,
he soared like a dragon from Xīchǔ.
With the passing of many years,
reflection on the past stirs Our heart.
Those civil and military officials who welcomed him
hold deep feelings of loyalty.
We wish to extend a special benevolence
to express Our eternal remembrance.
Officials may be granted one rank,
and military households are exempted from military service to become commoners.”
In the second month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
an imperial edict stated:
“The path of governance is not yet established,
and social ills are still profound.
The powerful and extravagant engage in encroachment and annexation,
while the poor and weak are distressed and in dire straits.
The living lack adequate clothing,
and the deceased are without proper burial shrouds.
We are deeply grieved by this.
Guardians and prefects are hereby clearly instructed
to diligently provide care and relief.
Regulations for posthumous gifts and aid
shall be promptly drafted.”
On the day Yǐyǒu,
Chǔ Zhànzhī, the Grand Master of Golden and Purple Guanglù, was appointed Left Palace Assistant of the Department of State Affairs.
On the day Bǐngxū,

Jiànpíng Wáng Hóng, the Central Secretariat Supervisor, Palace Grandee, and General of the Guards, was granted the privilege of establishing an office with the Three Ducal Ministers, while retaining his original titles.
His position as Central Secretariat Supervisor remained as before.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Liǔ Yuánjǐng, the General of Agile Cavalry, was granted the privilege of establishing an office with the Three Ducal Ministers, while retaining his original title.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Yìyáng Wáng Chǎng, the Palace Attendant, was appointed General of the Central Army.
In the third month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Jiànpíng Wáng Hóng, the Central Secretariat Supervisor, Palace Grandee, and General of the Guards, passed away.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
as it was a crucial month for farming,
the Grand Provisioner’s office stopped slaughtering cattle.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the emperor heard lawsuits in Huálínyuán.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Liú Jìzhī, the General Who Pacifies the North, was appointed Inspector of Sīzhōu.
Summer, the fourth month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
imperial son Zǐsuí was enfiefed as King of Ānlù.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Hǎilíng Wáng Xiūmào was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
there was an earthquake.
In the fifth month, on the day Wùshēn,
Xīyáng Commandery was re-established.
In the sixth month, on the day Wùyín,
one additional Palace Grandee of the Department of Personnel was established,
and the Palace Grandee of the Five Arms was abolished.
On the day Dīnghài,
Hé Shàngzhī, the Left Grand Master of Guanglù, was granted the additional privilege of establishing an office with the Three Ducal Ministers.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Yáng Xuánbǎo, the Grand Master of Golden and Purple Guanglù, was appointed Right Grand Master of Guanglù.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
an imperial edict stated:
“Due to past military campaigns,
many people have absconded.
Some, implicated in rebellion,
fear military law;
others shirk labor service and evade punishment.
Although We have simplified the laws
and striven to extend leniency,
and benevolent edicts have been frequently issued,
those who remain in hiding are still numerous.
Is it that they are accustomed to foolishness and their nature is difficult to change?
Or is it that the local officials
have failed to properly guide them?
General clemency shall be widely extended,
and all shall be granted a fresh start.”
Autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jiǎchén,
Gāo Shé and other commoners from Péngchéng plotted rebellion and were executed.
On the day Guǐhài,
Yán Shībó, the General of the Right Guard, was appointed Inspector of Qīng and Jì provinces.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
the King of Hénán dispatched an envoy to present local products.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Wáng Sēngdá, the Central Secretariat Director, was found guilty
and died in prison.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
Dù Shúwén, the General of Strong Crossbows, was appointed Inspector of Níngzhōu.
Fèi Yān, the Inspector of Jiāozhōu, was appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
Yuán Làng, the Administrator of Nánhǎi, was appointed Inspector of Jiāozhōu.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Shěn Sēngróng, the General Who Pacifies the North, was appointed Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
the emperor heard lawsuits in Huálínyuán.
On the day Rénxū,
Liú Dàolóng, the General Who Pacifies the North, was appointed Inspector of Xúzhōu.
Xiāngyáng experienced great floods,
and envoys were dispatched to inspect and provide relief.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
the offices of General of the Martial Guard and Palace Attendant of Mounted Cavalry were established.
Winter, the tenth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Yìyáng Wáng Chǎng, the General of the Central Army, was appointed Inspector of Jiāngzhōu.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the state of Gāolì dispatched an envoy to present local products.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Xīyáng Wáng Zǐshàng, the Inspector of Yángzhōu, was given the additional title of General Who Soothes the Army.
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐhài,
imperial princes and princesses whose ranks were equivalent to ducal ministers
were permitted to set up "inauspicious gates" (mourning gates) for funerals;
all others were prohibited.
In the intercalary month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"For those dwelling in mountains and rocky abodes,
fish and turtles are not considered proper gifts.
In recent years, there have been many troubles,
and military levies have been frequent and urgent.
Imposing taxes contrary to local conditions
was originally to provide temporary relief,
but those in charge became accustomed to it,
and it thus became a permanent system.
Materials like *chúnqín*, *yáo*, and *kūn* [various timbers and jades],
when used as local tribute,
accumulate like a pile of feathers, seemingly light,
but ultimately lead to profound harm.
I constantly reflect on broad reforms,
and my resolve shall not change.
All tribute duties from the prefectures and garrisons,
and all hunting and fishing from mountains and depths,
must be thoroughly investigated based on their production and growth,
and assessed according to the favorable seasons.
Do not let them be levied for empty quotas,
disrupting the natural order.
I hope that the spirit of simplicity
will be trusted by all people;
and the instruction of kindness and perceptiveness
will not be overlooked in remote and hidden places."
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor heard legal cases in the Huálín Yuán.
On the *rénxū* day,
the state of Lín Yì sent envoys to present local products.
That winter,
the Suǒ Lǔ invaded Qīngzhōu.
The Inspector, Yán Shībó, repeatedly defeated them.
In the third year, in the first month, on the *dīnghài* day,
Liángjùn of Yùzhōu was transferred to Xúzhōu.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Liǔ Yuánjǐng, the General of Agile Cavalry and General of the Palace Guard, was appointed Minister of the Imperial Secretariat.
Liú Zūnkǎo, the Right Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed General of the Palace Guard.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the state of Póhuáng sent envoys to present local products.
In the second month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
the six commanderies under Yángzhōu were designated as the royal domain (wángjī).
Dōngyángzhōu was renamed Yángzhōu.
but it was abandoned after the chief culprit had already been appointed.
Sīmǎ Zishàng, Prince of Xīyáng, the General Pacifying Army and Inspector of Yángzhōu, was transferred to be Inspector of Yángzhōu.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the office of Supervisor of the Grand Judge (Tíngwèi Jiānguān) was re-established.
Jīngzhōu suffered from famine.
In the third month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
land rent and cloth taxes were remitted to varying degrees.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Yuán Làng, the Administrator of Yìxīng, was appointed Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
On the *rénchén* day,
Xiāngdōng Wáng Yù, the Central Protector, was promoted from his post.
Dōnghǎi Wáng Huī, the Central Secretariat Director, was appointed General of the Palace Guard and Protector General.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Jiāngxià Wáng Yìgōng, the Grand Tutor, was additionally appointed Supervisor of the Central Secretariat.
In the summer, in the fourth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
the Emperor heard legal cases in the Huálín Yuán.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Fú Zhòngzǐ, the Administrator of Jiànníng, was appointed Inspector of Níngzhōu.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Jìnglín Wáng Dàn, the Minister of Works and Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, was found guilty
and demoted in rank.
Dàn did not accept the order,
occupied Guǎnglíng City, and rebelled,
killing Yuán Làng, the Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
Shěn Qìngzhī, Duke of Shǐxīng, was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Cavalry with Open Residence, and Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu to suppress Dàn.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
the Emperor personally led the Six Divisions,
and the imperial carriage camped at Xuānwǔ Hall.
Liú Jìzhī, the Inspector of Sīzhōu, rebelled.
Liú Dàolóng, the Inspector of Xúzhōu, attacked and beheaded him.
In the autumn, in the seventh month, on the *jǐsì* day,
Guǎnglíng City was captured,
and Dàn was executed.
All male inhabitants in the city were executed,
and female inhabitants were distributed as military rewards.
On that day, the state of emergency was lifted.
On the *xīnwèi* day,
a general amnesty was granted to the empire.
All old and sick laborers of the Imperial Workshops and slaves of the Xi Officials were released.
Filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and chaste wives
were granted grain and silk to varying degrees.
Impoverished households within the royal domain
and those whose land was used for nearby encampments
were all exempted from one year's rent.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Liú Xiùzhī, the Administrator of Dānyáng, was appointed Right Vice Minister of the Imperial Secretariat.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the area north and south of the Huái River was divided, and two Yùzhōu were re-established.
Shěn Qìngzhī, the newly appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry, Grand Master of Cavalry with Open Residence, and Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, was appointed Minister of Works,
retaining his post as Inspector.
On the *wùzǐ* day,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Huī, the General of the Palace Guard and Protector General, was appointed Inspector of Nányùzhōu,
retaining his post as General of the Palace Guard.
Yìyáng Wáng Chǎng, the Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, was appointed Protector General.
Guìyáng Wáng Xiūfàn, the General Who Exhibits Prowess, was appointed Inspector of Jiāngzhōu.
On the *guǐsì* day,
Wáng Xuánmó, the former General of the Left Palace Guard, was appointed Inspector of Yǐngzhōu.
In the eighth month, on the *bǐngshēn* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Recently, during the northern campaign, civil and military officials
perished in the army.
Some died by arrows and stones,
others from plague or illness.
All diligently served the king's cause,
yet their burials were humble and meager.
They should all be generously compensated and provided for,
ensuring ample provisions."
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Yǔ Shēnzhī, the Chief Clerk of the General of Chariots and Cavalry, was appointed Inspector of Yùzhōu.
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"In ancient times, when the Jī Way was solid,
punishments and laws were set aside;
when the Hàn virtue first shone,
prisons were simplified.
This was truly because the superiors unified their principles,
and the inferiors purified their nature.
Now, the people are frivolous and customs are thin,
sincerity is shallow, and deceit is deep.
Compounded by my lack of virtue,
I have been unable to transform hearts.
Thus, those who understand the way are few,
while those who seek to evade it are truly many.
When I recently conducted an inspection,
I saw two laborers from the Imperial Workshops,
shackled with iron chains and collars,
and felt pity for them.
Furthermore, with the nation celebrating and the people in harmony,
they alone are excluded from the joyous beneficence,
which causes me even greater shame.
Therefore, a thorough review for their pardon is to be conducted."
In the ninth month, on the *jǐsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The Five Punishments and Three Interrogations [judicial complexities]
have been difficult since ancient times.
Intricate laws and severe decrees
have become especially pronounced in later eras.
Thus, by following human feelings and observing disputes,
the Master of Lǔ achieved swift justice;
by not disturbing the city prisons,
the Hàn Historian gained renown.
For the Grand Judge, the resolution of doubtful and ambiguous cases from near and far
is where decisions ultimately reside.
Yet, once one enters the dark prison,
it often exceeds months and years.
The people suffer from this hardship,
and officials exploit it for their private gain.
From now on, when a prisoner's confession is complete,
it must be reported immediately.
I will personally review and decide all cases,
hoping to have no lingering cases.
If there are complex writings and delayed indictments,
or if evidence requires extensive pursuit,
a personal investigation is necessary
to ascertain the full truth.
Thereafter, legal cases will be heard as before."
On the *rénchén* day,
the Shànglín Yuàn was established north of Xuánwǔ Lake.
In the winter, in the tenth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"In ancient times, offerings were made on green altars
to pray for many blessings,
and silkworms were distributed in the northern suburbs
to provide for pure robes.
Next year, the imperial concubines of the six palaces
shall perform the ritual of personally tending silkworms."
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Liú Yánsūn, the General Who Guards the Army and Inspector of Nánxúzhōu, was promoted to the title of General of Chariots and Cavalry.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the state of Héxī sent envoys to present local products.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Dà Jùqú Ānzhōu, the King of Héxī, was appointed General Who Conquers Barbarians and Inspector of Liángzhōu.
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐsì* day,
the state of Gāolí sent envoys to present local products.
The state of Sùshèn, through multiple interpreters, presented *húshǐ* (barbed arrows) and stone arrowheads.
The Western Regions presented dancing horses.
In the twelfth month, on the *wùwǔ* day,
the Emperor heard legal cases in the Huálín Yuán.
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
the office of Servant-in-Waiting (Yèzhě Púshè) was established.
In the spring, the first month of the fourth year, on the *xīnwèi* day,
the imperial carriage performed a sacrifice at the southern suburb.
On the *jiǎxū* day,
the King of Dàngchāng presented a memorial with local products.
On the *yǐhài* day,
the imperial carriage personally ploughed the ceremonial field.
A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the empire.
All artisans sentenced to forced labor by the Shàngfāng department and all outstanding rent arrears and old debts
from before the first year of Dàmíng
were entirely pardoned and cancelled.
Farmers who excelled in their work
were to be employed according to their talents.
Those who showed filial piety and brotherly submission, and who were righteous and compliant,
were granted one rank of nobility.
Orphans, the elderly, the poor, and the sick
were each given ten *hú* of grain.
Officials in charge of the ceremonial field
received generous and widespread rewards.
For the common people lacking grain seeds,
loans were provided as appropriate.
Officials who promoted and exhorted with distinction
were to be highly commended and promoted.
On the *rénwǔ* day,
Liǔ Shūyīn, the *sīmǎ* of the Northern Central Army Commander, was appointed Inspector of Liáng and Nánqín prefectures.
Zhū Xiūzhī, the General of the Left and Inspector of Jīng prefecture, was promoted to General of the Garrison.
On the *gēngyín* day,
the third imperial prince, Zǐxūn, was enfeoffed as the King of Jìn'ān;
the sixth imperial prince, Zǐfáng, as the King of Xúnyáng;
the seventh imperial prince, Zǐxù, as the King of Lìyáng;
and the eighth imperial prince, Zǐluán, as the King of Xiāngyáng.
In the second month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Liú Xiūrén, the King of Jiàn'ān and Attendant-in-ordinary, was appointed Inspector of Xiāng prefecture.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Fèi Jǐngxù, the External Gentleman of the Palace and Cavalier Attendant, was appointed Inspector of Níng prefecture.
In the third month, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Liú Xiūruò, the King of Bālíng and General of the Gentlemen of the Household, was appointed Inspector of Xú prefecture.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Zǐsuí, the Prince of Ānlù, was appointed Inspector of Yǐng prefecture.
On the *guǐyǒu* day,
Liú Dàolóng, the Inspector of Xú prefecture, was appointed Inspector of Qīng and Jì prefectures.
The Sǎluǒ invaded Kǒngtí in Běiyīnpíng.
The Prefect Yáng Guīzǐ attacked and defeated them.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Empress personally picked mulberries in the western suburb.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *guǐmǎo* day,
Nánlángyé was made subordinate to Wángjī.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"In ancient times, those who wore coarse clothes governed the realm,
condemning extravagance to demonstrate frugality; those who used earthenware bowls to rule the world
admonished for thrift to manifest their principles.
My thoughts of using coarse cloth and silk
have never left my mind.
Although I have repeatedly instructed officials
to reduce non-essential expenses and focus on practical matters,
the annual expenditures have accumulated,
and the annual quotas are excessively large.
How can discarding abundance for reduction
truly be called a frugal mind?
The four seasons' supply limits
can be drastically reduced by more than half.
May the use of furs and fine silks conform to tradition,
and may the ostentation of the people be curtailed;
may intricate weaving and embroidery cease to harm labor,
and may the markets not compete in luxury."
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The climate in the capital and surrounding areas has not yet stabilized,
and epidemics are still numerous.
Thinking of the suffering of the people,
my heart is filled with pity and sorrow.
Envoys should be sent to inquire after them
and provide medicine;
as for those who have died,
appropriate relief and assistance should be given."
In the fifth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
judgments were heard in the Huálín Garden.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Liáng Commandery of Xú prefecture was returned to Yù prefecture.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
Chǔ Zhànzhī, the Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs of the Left, passed away.
Liú Sīkǎo, the Chief Clerk of the General of the Household, was appointed Inspector of Yì prefecture.
On the *gēngyín* day,
Nánxiàpí was merged with Nánpéngchéng Commandery.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Hé Shàngzhī, the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left and Minister who Opens a Mansion with the Three Ducal Ministers, passed away.
In the eighth month, on the *rényín* day,
the King of Dàngchāng sent envoys to present local products.
On the *jǐyǒu* day,
Zǐxūn, the King of Jìn'ān, was appointed Inspector of Nányǎn prefecture.
Yōng prefecture experienced severe floods.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
troops were dispatched to provide relief.
In the ninth month, on the *xīnwèi* day,
Yuán Hùzhī, the General of the Gentlemen of the Household, was appointed Inspector of Yù prefecture.
On the *jiǎshēn* day,
the Emperor heard judgments in the Huálín Garden.
On the *dīnghài* day,
Zǐluán, the Prince of Xiāngyáng, was re-enfeoffed as the King of Xīn'ān.
In the winter, the tenth month, on the *gēngyín* day,
Shěn Qìngzhī, the newly appointed Minister of Works, was dispatched to quell the Man tribes along the river.
On the *rénchén* day,
an edict ordered prefectures and counties to reduce salaries,
and these savings were to first cover public expenses.
In the eleventh month, on the *wùchén* day,
the Director of the Fine Works Office was renamed Director of the Left and Right Imperial Workshops.
On the *bǐngxū* day,
the office of Grand Minister of Agriculture was reinstated.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
the Emperor heard judgments in the Huálín Garden.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
the imperial carriage visited the Imperial Court of Justice.
All prisoners were fully pardoned and released.
The Sǎluǒ sent envoys to request peace.
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the imperial carriage visited Jiànkāng county,
and imprisoned criminals were pardoned and released.
The Wō kingdom sent envoys to present local products.
In the spring, the first month of the fifth year, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Liáng Tángzǐ, the King of Dàngchāng, was appointed Inspector of Hé prefecture.
In the second month, on the *guǐsì* day,
the imperial carriage reviewed military exercises.
An imperial edict stated:
"In ancient times, people asked what came first in human affairs,
and said it was the military.
Though it may not be used for a long time,
forgetting it leads to peril.
During my leisure from governing,
I discuss matters according to the season,
so that sitting and standing have their proper ceremonies,
and advances and retreats are without error.
All from the military banners downwards
are to be generously rewarded.
Recently, transformation has not been effective,
and the people do not know the prohibitions,
evading service and violating regulations,
thereby falling into the nets of punishment.
All those who have fled
before this morning
are all pardoned.
Those already detained in prison
shall be released and returned to their original duties.
Outstanding debts from before the third year of Dàmíng
are all to be pardoned and suspended.
From this point onwards,
the poor, sick, and elderly
shall have their reductions detailed.
Families of those who pacified the Man tribes
shall be exempted from half of their taxes.
The recent revision of the household registration system
has been implemented in various places,
but there are many errors in practice.
It should be universally reissued,
and allowed to begin from now.
If anyone has previously violated the regulations,
it shall also be wiped clean."
On the *jiǎyín* day,
Yáng Xuánbǎo, the Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Right, was given the special appointment of *tèjìn*.
In the summer, the fourth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Zǐshàng, the Prince of Xīyáng, was re-enfeoffed as the King of Yùzhāng.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
Liǔ Yuánjǐng, the Director of the Department of State Affairs, was given the title of Grand Master of Splendid Happiness of the Left and Minister who Opens a Mansion with the Three Ducal Ministers.
On the *wùxū* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"In the past year, Nánsú and Yǎn prefectures suffered damage to their harvests from floods and rain,
and many people are in distress.
Outstanding rent arrears that have not been paid
can be deferred until the autumn harvest."
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Hǎi Língwáng Xiūmào, the Inspector of Yōng prefecture, killed his *sīmǎ* Yǔ Shēzhī,
raised troops in rebellion.
Xuē Jìkǎo, the Administrator of Yìchéng, attacked and beheaded him.
On the *jiǎyín* day,
the ninth imperial prince, Zǐrén, was appointed Inspector of Yōng prefecture.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐhài* day,
an edict stipulated that imperial relatives within the period of mourning,
who were not salaried officials,
should be given 100,000 *qián* monthly.
On the *bǐngchén* day,
the imperial carriage visited the Yuèwǔ Hall to hear judgments.
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Yìyángwáng Chǎng, the General of the Household, was appointed General of the Central Army.
On the *rénzǐ* day,
Pèi Commandery was established by dividing Guǎnglǐng,
and Dōngpíng Commandery was abolished and merged into Guǎnglǐng.
In the autumn, the seventh month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Rainfall has been abundant,
and streets and alleys are overflowing.
Envoys should be sent to inspect.
Poor and destitute households
shall be granted firewood and grain."
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the Gāolì Kingdom sent envoys to present local products.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
a partial amnesty was granted to Yōng prefecture.
In the eighth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the ninth imperial prince, Zǐrén, was enfeoffed as Yǒngjiā Wáng.
The eleventh imperial prince, Zǐzhēn, was enfeoffed as Shǐ'ān Wáng.
Fèi Bóhóng, a Cānjūn of the Běi Zhōngláng, was made Níngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
an imperial edict stated:
"Since the beginning of the spiritual mandate,
the sagely plan has been far-reaching and profound.
By aligning with and rectifying our duties,
we evoke the response of the gods and spirits;
by cultivating and establishing the rites,
we illuminate the light of supreme virtue.
When sound and substance are in harmony,
and literary refinement is used to regulate them evenly,
it transforms their customs,
and shapes their nature.
Thus, facing the established principles,
they shine forth brilliantly.
When the Way declines and the world is troubled,
learning withers and years drag on.
Litigation lacks the art of gradual decline,
and the common people forget the method of withdrawing to simplicity.
Now, with alarms ceased in the tranquil mountains,
and waves calmed on the river islets,
traveling over mountain paths and sailing the seas,
people turn towards virtue and admire righteousness.
To transform the people and establish customs,
this is now the opportune time.
〔十九〕Next year, the schools and academies should be repaired,
and the imperial lineage honored and extended."
On the day Gēngyín,
a decree was issued that for the white-board commanderies and counties temporarily granted to frontier commanders,
the term limit should follow those appointed by the imperial court,
and they should receive one-third of the emolument,
without provision for escorting the deceased.
The Wèi Jiāngjūn, Dōnghǎi Wáng Huī, was appointed Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī with his original title.
In the ninth month, on the first day, Jiǎyín,
there was a solar eclipse.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
the imperial carriage proceeded to Lángyé Jùn,
and all prisoners were pardoned and released.
On the day Jiǎxū,
the seat of Nányùzhōu was moved from Huáinán to Hú Xiàn.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
the Guānjūn Jiāngjūn, Xúnyáng Wáng Zǐfáng, was made Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the intercalary month, on the day Wùzǐ,
the Crown Princess Hé Shì passed away.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
a imperial road was first established,
from Chānghé Mén to Zhūquè Mén,
and also from Chéngmíng Mén to Xuánwǔ Hú.
On the day Rényín,
Lìyáng Wáng Zǐxū was restyled Línhǎi Wáng.
In the winter, tenth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
the Chējì Jiāngjūn and Nánxúzhōu Cìshǐ, Liú Yánzūn, was made Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè and Lǐng Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
The Shàngshū Yòu Púyè, Liú Xiùzhī, was made Ānběi Jiāngjūn and Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ.
The Guānjūn Jiāngjūn, Línhǎi Wáng Zǐxū, was made Guǎngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Yǐmǎo,
the Dōng Zhōnglángjiāng, Xīn'ān Wáng Zǐluán, was made Nánxúzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the eleventh month, on the day Rénchén,
an imperial edict stated:
"The royal domain serves the capital within,
and represents all of Xià outside.
With abundant people and extensive affairs,
it is fitting to consider simplicity and benevolence.
The Shàngshū should be sent to conduct a detailed inspection,
and together with the local officials, rectify various prisons.
Any cases of doubt or delay
should be reported in full."
On the day Dīngyǒu,
one additional Shǎofǔ Chéng was appointed.
In the twelfth month, on the day Rénhēn,
the Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn, Liú Zūnkǎo, was made Shàngshū Yòu Púyè.
On the day Jiǎxū,
a decree ordered that every household in the realm should pay four bolts of cloth annually.
On the day Gēngchén,
the Tàicháng, Wáng Xuánmó, was made Píngběi Jiāngjūn and Xúzhōu Cìshǐ.
In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the Xiāngzhōu Cìshǐ, Jiàn'ān Wáng Xiūrén, was granted the additional title of Píngnán Jiāngjūn.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the imperial carriage personally offered sacrifices at the southern suburb.
On this day,
ancestral sacrifices were also offered at the Míngtáng.
A general amnesty was proclaimed throughout the realm.
Filial sons, obedient grandsons, righteous husbands, and respectful younger brothers
were granted one rank of nobility.
Kind mothers-in-law, chaste wives, and the orphaned, elderly, and those with six infirmities
were granted five bolts of silk
and ten hù of grain.
An edict was issued to the four quarters to commend and reward exceptional individuals.
Those who possessed genuine virtue and embraced simplicity,
whose aspirations and conduct were pure and unblemished,
who were content to withdraw and uphold themselves,
not engaging with contemporary society;
or those whose knowledge spanned ancient and modern times,
whose talents were equal to military and state affairs,
who served the public honestly and uprightly,
and enjoyed high renown among the people,
should all have their names reported.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the offices of Wǔguān Zhōnglángjiāng and Zuǒ Yòu Zhōnglángjiāng were established.
In the second month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
the salaries of all officials were restored.
In the third month, on the day Gēngyín,
the thirteenth imperial prince, Zǐyuán, was enfeoffed as Shàolíng Wáng.
On the day Rényín,
the crown prince of Wōguó, Xīng, was made Āndōng Jiāngjūn.
On the day Yǐsì,
the Nánliáng Jùn of Yùzhōu was renamed Huáinán Jùn.
The former Huáinán Jùn was merged with Xuānchéng.
On the day Dīngwèi,
the Fǔguó Jiāngjūn, Zhēnglǔ Chángshǐ, and Guǎnglíng Tàishǒu, Shěn Huáiwén, committed a crime,
was imprisoned and died.
In the fourth month, on the day Gēngshēn,
arrears of rent from Nányǎnzhōu prior to Dàmíng three years were pardoned.
The Dàháng Mén was newly constructed.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngxū,
an ice house was established,
and the ritual of storing ice was performed.
On the day Rényín,
the Tàizǎi, Jiāngxià Wáng Yìgōng, was relieved of his concurrent post as Sītú.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
the Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè and Hùjūn Jiāngjūn, Liú Yánzūn, passed away.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Gēngchén,
the Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ, Zhū Xiūzhī, was made Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn.
The Guǎngzhōu Cìshǐ, Línhǎi Wáng Zǐxū, was made Jīngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
there was an earthquake.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the Fǔguó Jiāngjūn, Wáng Yìzhī, was made Guǎngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
the Xīyáng Tàishǒu, Tán Yìzhī, was made Jiāozhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the nineteenth imperial prince, Zǐyún, was enfeoffed as Jìnlíng Wáng.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐhài,
arrears of rent from Yōngzhōu prior to Dàmíng four years were pardoned.
On the day Yǐhài,
the office of Qīngtái Lìng was established.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùyín,
a decree ordered Buddhist monks to pay respects to the ruler.
On the day Wùzǐ,
the former Jīnzǐ Guānglù Dàfū, Zōng Qì, was made Zhōng Hùjūn.
On the day Yǐwèi,
the Shàngshū Yòu Púyè, Liú Zūnkǎo, was made Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè.
The Dānyáng Yǐn, Wáng Sēnglǎng, was made Shàngshū Yòu Púyè.
In winter, tenth month, on the day Dīngsì,
Shìhóng, son of Shānyáng Wáng Xiūyòu, was appointed to succeed Pòyáng Āi Wáng Xiūyè.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
an imperial edict stated that commoners' graves within the Shànglín Yuàn who wished to rebury their dead together
〔二一〕should not be prohibited.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Chénliú Wáng Cáo Qiánxiù passed away.
On the day Xīnsì,
the Shàngshū Lìng, Liǔ Yuánjǐng, was made Sīkōng,
retaining his title of Shàngshū Lìng.
In the seventh year, spring, first month, on the day Guǐwèi,
an imperial edict stated:
"The ritual of spring hunt
was established in the Zhou ordinances;
the accounts of military exercises
were recorded in the Lǔ history.
This was to manifest and proclaim virtue and conduct,
and to show the people the proper rules.
This year, the harvest is bountiful, the climate is favorable,
and both inside and outside the capital are peaceful and tranquil.
During the agricultural slack season,
these ancient regulations should be restored.
A date can be set for a grand review of the naval forces at Xuánwǔ Hú,
and also to patrol the right bank of the Jiāng,
and conduct military drills and hunts."
On the day Dīnghài,
the Shàngshū Yòu Púyè, Wáng Sēnglǎng, was made Tàicháng.
The Wèi Jiāngjūn, Yán Shībó, was made Shàngshū Yòu Púyè.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the Shàngshū Lìng, Liǔ Yuánjǐng, was made Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
On the day Gēngyín,
the Nányǎnzhōu Cìshǐ, Jìn'ān Wáng Zǐxūn, was made Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ.
On the day Guǐsì,
Wú Jùn was cut off and assigned to Nánxúzhōu.
In the second month, on the *Jiǎyín* day,
the imperial carriage toured the two prefectures of Nányù and Nányǎn.
On the *Bǐngchén* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"The Jiāng and Hàn rivers, a view of Chǔ,
are always subject to the Zhou dynasty's sacrificial rites;
paying respects to Jiǔyí in Shèng Táng,
and sacrificing to Pénglái in Bóhǎi,
these are all teachings passed down from previous generations,
and models left by sagely emperors.
Mount Huò is called the Southern Peak (Nányuè),
it is truly a guardian of the state,
containing spiritual power and displaying auspicious signs,
it initiated the brilliance of the Sòng Dao.
I am stationed in the wilderness,
having business at Qíyáng,
gazing at the wind and clouds,
wandering with thoughts.
An envoy should be sent to offer sacrifices."
On the *Dīngsì* day,
the imperial carriage hunted at Wūjiāng in Lìyáng.
On the *Jǐwèi* day,
the imperial carriage ascended Liùhé Shān in Wūjiāng Xiàn.
On the *Gēngshēn* day,
Lìyáng and Qín Jùn were partitioned to establish Línjiāng Jùn.
On the *Rénxū* day,
"I received the heavenly mandate eleven years ago.
Relying on the spiritual power of the seven ancestral temples,
and receiving the strength of the Supreme Emperor,
my rites extend across the four seas,
and my might shakes the eight wildernesses.
I am currently touring the Three Xiāng to offer sacrifices at Héngyuè,
and next visiting the Nine Hé to inspect Yún and Dài.
Now, I have broadly reviewed the accomplishments,
observed the customs in the capital region,
inspected the people in Liùhé,
and conducted a grand hunt at Chángzhōu.
Sand flew and pebbles scattered,
mountains were leveled and seas churned,
war drums and Jin music were in harmony,
nāo and zhēng cymbals kept time,
the sacrificial *chàng* wine was offered according to ritual,
and game animals filled the plains.
I respectfully raised the cup of the kings and dukes,
and widely received the long lives of the gentry and common people.
The eight winds circulated smoothly,
and auspicious clouds gathered,
exhausting the heavens' auspiciousness,
and making everyone in the realm overjoyed.
I wish to spread the spring of the Great Ultimate,
to bless beyond all bounds.
A general amnesty for the entire realm shall be granted,
and in the areas the imperial procession passed through,
no land tax or cloth tax shall be collected for the current year.
Outstanding rent and remaining debts
shall not be collected again.
The people shall be granted one rank of nobility,
and women in one hundred households shall receive cattle and wine.
Governors, administrators, county magistrates, and common laborers who participated in the hunt
shall all receive generous rewards."
"In my youth, I took charge,
governed Sīyōng,
administered government and spread influence,
for many years.
The state faced obstacles,
and I led military campaigns in the Jiāng region.
The difficulty of overcoming obstacles, and the bonds of affection and duty,
were truly held in my heart.
Now, I have trained troops and held hunts,
passing through these areas and villages.
Among the elders of the former towns,
few remain in sight.
Not many years have passed,
yet more than half have perished.
Contemplating these traces, I am filled with emotion,
and deeply moved.
Tàizōng extended kindness to the old residents of Yàn,
and Jìnyáng received his grace;
Shìzǔ bestowed benevolence,
and the capital region was filled with his favor.
Recalling past achievements,
I wish to further extend previous benefits.
Therefore, Lìyáng Jùn's land tax and tributes shall be remitted for three years.
Envoys shall be dispatched to tour and comfort,
and inquire about the people's suffering.
The poor, widows, orphans, elderly, and those with six disabilities who cannot support themselves
shall be generously given grain and silk.
The aged shall also be given lamb and wine.
Anyone with a single good quality
shall be evaluated and promoted according to their talent;
former officials of the state and auxiliary officers of prefectures and commanderies
shall receive grants according to their contributions.
Even if a person has passed away,
the benefits shall extend to their descendants."
On the *Rénshēn* day,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
In summer, the fourth month, on the *Jiǎyín* day,
Zhū Xiūzhī, the General of the Imperial Guard (Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn), was made Special Advance (Tèjìn).
On the *Bǐngchén* day,
Yù, Prince of Xiāngdōng, the Minister (Shàngshū), was made General of the Imperial Guard (Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn).
On the *Jiǎzǐ* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"Unless it is in a military battle formation,
no one is permitted to execute summarily.
For those whose crimes are punishable by severe capital punishment,
The authorities shall strictly investigate and hear cases.
Those who violate this shall be judged as murderers."
In the fifth month, on the *Yǐhài* day,
Zǐshàng, Prince of Yùzhāng, the General Who Guards the Army (Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn) and Governor of Yángzhōu (Yángzhōu Cìshǐ), was promoted to General of Cavalry (Chēqí Jiāngjūn).
Zǐzhēn, Prince of Shǐ'ān, the General Who Assists the State (Fǔguó Jiāngjūn), was made Governor of Guǎngzhōu (Guǎngzhōu Cìshǐ).
On the *Bǐngzǐ* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"From now on, governors and magistrates,
when mobilizing the people or raising an army,
must all receive a hand-written imperial decree for implementation.
Only in cases of border alarms,
or internal treachery erupting,
where sudden changes occur,
shall this rule not apply."
In the sixth month, on the *Jiǎchén* day,
Liǔ Yuángù, the North Central Lang Sīmǎ, was made Governor of Liáng and Nánqín prefectures.
On the *Wùshēn* day,
envoys from the Rùiruì kingdom and Gāolí kingdom sent local products as tribute.
On the *Wùchén* day,
Liú Déyuàn, the Administrator of Qín Jùn, was made Governor of Yùzhōu.
In the seventh month, on the *Yǐhài* day,

Gāo Lián, King of Gāolí and Grand General Who Attacks the East (Zhēngdōng Dàjiāngjūn), was promoted to Grand General of Cavalry (Chēqí Dàjiāngjūn) and granted the privilege of establishing a government office (Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī).
On the *Bǐngshēn* day,
"A previous edict stated that the fields and ponds of the rivers and seas
should be shared for the benefit of the people.
Not many years have passed,
yet it has gradually become slack and neglected.
Famous mountains and great rivers
are often privately occupied.
The authorities shall strictly investigate and correct this,
and reiterate the old regulations."
In the eighth month, on the *Dīngsì* day,
an imperial edict stated:
"In ancient times, when a common woman held resentment,
the mountains in the northern frontier scorched;
when a widow mourned deeply,
a tower in the eastern kingdom collapsed.
This is because what sincerity moves,
even if subtle, will manifest;
what emotion shakes,
even if solid, will crumble.
I inspect the nine wildernesses,
with a deep resolve to await the dawn,
but I have been unable to make things clearly regulated,
each in its proper order.
Consequently, the fiery essence has harmed the river,
and the sun's warmth has not spread evenly,
the year is said to be unfruitful,
the blame truly lies with me.
The provisions for the imperial kitchen
should be reduced.
Near the capital, criminal cases
should be personally reviewed.
Within the royal domain and the areas governed by Shénzhōu,
a Minister (Shàngshū) should be dispatched to thoroughly investigate with the local authorities;
for the prefectures outside the capital domain,
it shall be entrusted to the governors.
They shall also thoroughly review the laws and regulations,
and consider what benefits the people.
As for *kǎozé màoxí* (harsh taxes and compulsory labor or levies for military supplies), those before the seventh year of Dàmíng,
shall all be exempt from collection.
For especially distressed households,
granaries shall be opened for relief.
On the *Yǐchǒu* day,
the sixteenth imperial prince, Zǐmèng, was enthroned as Prince of Huáinán (Huáinán Wáng),
and the eighteenth imperial prince, Zǐchǎn, was enthroned as Prince of Línhè (Línhè Wáng).
The imperial carriage visited Mòlíng Xiàn in Jiànkāng to review legal cases."
In the ninth month, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
an edict stated:
"Recently, the extreme heat of summer [炎精亢序]
has severely damaged the crops.
Now, as the planting of the two types of wheat is not yet too late,
and abundant rain has frequently fallen,
it is permissible to send [officials] to the eastern border commanderies [東境郡]
to diligently encourage cultivation.
For especially impoverished households,
a suitable amount of wheat seeds should be loaned."
On the *wùzǐ* day,
an edict stated:
"In ancient times, the hoof prints of the Zhou [Zhōu] kings [周王]
truly reached the four seas;
the phoenix carriages of the Han [Hàn] emperors [漢帝]
had long visited the five sacred mountains [Wǔyuè].
These were all means by which they could respond to the spirits above [幽靈],
and govern the people's land below.
Since the Heavenly Way [天昌] has changed its mandate [替馭],
and the [new] court has established its plans,
the rites have withered in place of the old [禮代夭鬱],
and the world's fortunes have risen and fallen.
When the imperial house founded the Sòng [Sòng] dynasty,
the sun and moon shone brightly again,
the celestial spheres [xuánjī] were restored to order,
and the five planets [wǔxīng] followed their destined paths.
Yet, military chariots move annually,
and the poetic tradition [Chén Shī] is lacking in righteousness [義闕].
I [朕] have embraced the five virtues [wǔguāng]
and pacified all under Heaven [tiānxià].
I contemplate exhausting the rules of precious restraint [bǎojiè]
to block the paths of perilous schemes.
It is necessary to follow the times and inspect the regions [shěngfāng],
observing the customs.
Furthermore, I will meticulously examine the old statutes [jiùdiǎn]
to fulfill the earnest expectation [cèxí zhī huái]."
On the *gēngyín* day,
Liú Zǐluán [劉子鸞], Prince of Xīn'ān [Xīn'ān Wáng], Inspector of Nán Xúzhōu [Nán Xúzhōu Cìshǐ], was additionally appointed Grand Minister of Education [Sītú].
On the *yǐwèi* day,
the imperial carriage visited the Grand Judge [Tíngwèi] to personally try prisoners.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
the seventeenth imperial prince, Liú Zǐsì [劉子嗣], was made Prince of Dōngpíng [Dōngpíng Wáng].
In winter, tenth month, on the *rényín* day,
the crown prince [tàizǐ] came of age [guān],
and kings, dukes, and officials below them were granted silk, each in varying amounts.
On the *wùshēn* day,
the imperial carriage toured Nán Yùzhōu [Nán Yùzhōu].
An edict stated:
"Wherever I tour,
those aged one hundred years or more whom I encounter first,
as well as orphans, widows, the elderly, and the infirm,
shall all be granted grain and silk.
Prisoners and those charged with crimes
shall all have their cases personally heard by me.
If any officials or commoners feel resentment, oppression, or are in a precarious state,
or have been suppressed by local officials,
or are secluded and upright [yǐnyuē jiélì],
or have been ostracized by their hometowns,
they are all permitted to approach me [朕]
and present their grievances in person.
If anyone is loyal and trustworthy, filial and righteous,
or is skilled in farming and grain cultivation,
or possesses even a single talent [yījiè zhī néng],
or a single beautiful skill,
they shall all be recognized and rewarded.
Although the autumn rains have fallen frequently,
the summer drought has caused hardship.
The traveling granaries [xíngcāng] should be opened immediately,
and additional relief and grants distributed." [二六]
On the *guǐchǒu* day,
the imperial retinue visited Jiāngníng [Jiāngníng] County to try prisoners.
Liú Zǐshàng [劉子尚], Prince of Yùzhāng [Yùzhāng Wáng], General of Agile Cavalry [Chējì Jiāngjūn] and Inspector of Yángzhōu [Yángzhōu Cìshǐ], was additionally appointed *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī* [開府儀同三司].
On the *guǐhài* day,
Liú Huī [劉褘], Prince of Dōnghǎi [Dōnghǎi Wáng], General of the Guards [Wèi Jiāngjūn] and *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*, was made Minister of Works [Sīkōng].
Liú Chǎng [劉昶], Prince of Yìyáng [Yìyáng Wáng] and General of the Central Army [Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn], was additionally appointed *Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī*.
On the *bǐngyín* day,
an edict stated:
"Rewards, celebrations, punishments, and authority
are the unchanging norms of the state;
dismissing the obscure and promoting the enlightened [chùyōu shēngmíng]
are the principles that govern the realm.
Therefore, by collecting words and listening to reports [cǎiyán língfēng],
we observe extravagance and simplicity,
and the demotion of ranks and granting of lands [biǎnjié jiādì]
reside in these principles.
Now, I worship the Emperor [Lèi Dì Yí Shè] and personally tour the Jiāngdìan [Jiāngdiàn] region,
thereby meeting the provincial governors [yuèshǒu]
and personally seeking out the people's ailments.
I wish to promote the ordinances of clear examination [míngshì zhī diǎn]
to extend the meaning of evaluating merits [kǎojì zhī yì].
Wherever my imperial retinue passes,
for officials who govern the people,
if their achievements are heard of,
they shall immediately receive special commendation.
If they neglect their duties and cause harm to the people,
they shall be punished according to their faults.
The responsible officials should thoroughly investigate and report."
On the *jǐsì* day,
the imperial carriage hunted at Gūshú [Gūshú].
In the eleventh month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
a partial amnesty was granted to Nán Yùzhōu [Nán Yùzhōu] for those with crimes of death and below.
Wherever the imperial tour passed,
the land tax for the current year was greatly reduced.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
an edict ordered offerings to be sent to the tombs of Huán Wēn [Huán Wēn], Grand Marshal of Jìn [Jìn Dàsīmǎ], and Má Huì [Má Huì], General Who Conquers the West [Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn].
The Emperor [Shàng] personally tried prisoners from Lìyáng [Lìyáng], Yǒngshì [Yǒngshì], and Dānyáng [Dānyáng] counties at his touring location.
On the *guǐsì* day,
the imperial carriage conducted naval exercises at Liángshān [Liángshān].
Two white jays [bái jué] landed on the imperial canopy [huágài].
The responsible officials proposed changing the seventh year of Dàmíng [Dàmíng] to the first year of Shénjué [Shénjué].
The edict did not permit this.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
prisoners in the traveling jails were pardoned and released.
The eastern commanderies suffered a severe drought.
On the *rényín* day,
emissaries were dispatched
to open granaries for loans and relief,
and to accept miscellaneous goods in lieu of rent. [二七] [二八]
In the twelfth month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the imperial retinue visited Lìyáng [Lìyáng].
On the *jiǎyín* day,
a general amnesty was granted to all under Heaven.
Long-term prisoners specially confined in Nán Yùzhōu [Nán Yùzhōu]
were all pardoned and released.
All conscription for soldiers and punishment by frontier garrison duty [kǎoxí zhéshù]
were halted.
The hundred households of Lìyáng [Lìyáng] Commandery were given oxen and wine.
The elderly, orphans, and infirm
were granted ten bolts of silk,
and the commandery's taxes were exempted for ten years.
On the *jǐwèi* day,
Liú Yìgōng [劉義恭], Prince of Jiāngxià [Jiāngxià Wáng] and Grand Tutor [Tàizǎi], was additionally appointed President of the Imperial Secretariat [Shàngshū Lìng].
Twin gate towers [shuāngquè] were erected at Bówàng [Bówàng] and Liángshān [Liángshān].
On the *guǐhài* day,
the imperial carriage returned from Lìyáng [Lìyáng].
In the eighth year, spring, first month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
an edict stated:
"The eastern region experienced a poor harvest last year,
so trade and commerce should be expanded.
For those near and far who sell rice and grain,
miscellaneous taxes on the roads shall be suspended.
Those who carry weapons for self-defense
shall not be prohibited at all." [二九]
On the *guǐwèi* day,
Liú Xiùzhī [劉秀之], General Who Pacifies the North [Ānběi Jiāngjūn] and Inspector of Yōngzhōu [Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ], passed away.
On the *wùzǐ* day,

Liú Xiūrén [劉休仁], Prince of Jiàn'ān [Jiàn'ān Wáng], General Who Pacifies the South [Píngnán Jiāngjūn] and Inspector of Xiāngzhōu [Xiāngzhōu Cìshǐ], was appointed General Who Pacifies the South [Ānnán Jiāngjūn] and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu [Jiāngzhōu Cìshǐ].
Liú Zǐxūn [劉子勛], Prince of Jìn'ān [Jìn'ān Wáng], was appointed General Who Guards the Army [Zhènjūn Jiāngjūn] and Inspector of Yōngzhōu [Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ].
Liú Zǐluán [劉子鸞], Prince of Xīn'ān [Xīn'ān Wáng] and Inspector of Nán Xúzhōu [Nán Xúzhōu Cìshǐ], was appointed General Who Comforts the Army [Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn],
and retained his titles of Grand Minister of Education [Sītú] and Inspector.
Liú Bóqín [劉伯禽], heir of the Prince of Jiāngxià [Jiāngxià Wáng] and General Who Assists the State [Fǔguó Jiāngjūn], was appointed Inspector of Xiāngzhōu [Xiāngzhōu Cìshǐ]. [三０]
In the second month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Zhū Xiūzhī [Zhū Xiūzhī], Grand Master with Special Advancement [Tèjìn], passed away.
On the *rényín* day,
an edict stated:
"Last year, the eastern region suffered a partial drought,
and fields had poor harvests.
Many of those who came as emissaries [from there]
have become utterly destitute.
Some have fallen into destitution and homelessness,
collapsed in the streets and alleys,
which I [朕] greatly pity.
Granary rice should be released to Jiànkāng [Jiànkāng] and Mòlíng [Mòlíng] counties,
to provide relief as appropriate.
If aid is not provided in a timely manner,
leading to abandonment [and death],
severe impeachment shall be imposed." [三一]
On the *yǐsì* day,

Liú Yù [劉彧], Prince of Xiāngdōng [Xiāngdōng Wáng] and General Who Guards the Army [Zhènjūn Jiāngjūn], was appointed General Who Guards the North [Zhènběi Jiāngjūn] and Inspector of Xúzhōu [Xúzhōu Cìshǐ].
Wáng Xuánmó [Wáng Xuánmó], General Who Pacifies the North [Píngběi Jiāngjūn] and Inspector of Xúzhōu [Xúzhōu Cìshǐ], was appointed General of the Palace Guard [Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn].
In summer, intercalary fifth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Xiāo Huìkāi [Xiāo Huìkāi], former Palace Assistant Censor [Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng], was appointed Inspector of Qīng [Qīng] and Jì [Jì] Prefectures.
On the *rényín* day,
Liú Yìgōng [劉義gōng], Prince of Jiāngxià [Jiāngxià Wáng] and Grand Tutor [Tàizǎi], was additionally appointed Grand Commandant [Tàiwèi].
Yáng Xuánbǎo [Yáng Xuánbǎo], Grand Master with Special Advancement [Tèjìn] and Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Right [Yòu Guānglù Dàfū], passed away.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
the Emperor [Dì] passed away at Yùzhú [Yùzhú] Palace,
aged thirty-five.
In autumn, seventh month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
he was buried at Jǐngníng [Jǐngníng] Mausoleum on Yánshān [Yánshān] in Mòlíng [Mòlíng] County, Dānyáng [Dānyáng].
The court historian [Shǐchén] says: To exert oneself for the benefit of all under Heaven [tiānxià]
is the heart of Yáo [Yáo] and Shùn [Shùn];
to benefit oneself and thereby reach all things
is the aspiration of a mediocre ruler;
to exhaust the people's lives to sustain oneself
is the conduct of Jié [Jié] and Zhòu [Zhòu].
Observing the era of Dàmíng [Dàmíng],
was it not exhausting the people's lives?
Even with the talent and excellence of Zhōu Gōng [Zhōu Gōng],
it still ended in chaos.
Of what benefit was that!
Collated Notes [Jiàokāojì]
Basic Annals 7: Former Deposed Emperor [Běnjì Dì Qī Qiánfèidì]
The former deposed emperor's personal name was Zǐyè,
his childhood name was Fǎshī.
He was Emperor Xiàowǔ's eldest son.
He was born on the `jiǎshēn` day of the first month in the twenty-sixth year of Yuánjiā (449 CE).
When Shìzǔ was stationed in Xúnyáng,
Zǐyè remained in Jīngyì.
In the thirtieth year (453 CE),
when Shìzǔ entered to campaign against the prime culprit [Yuánxiōng],
Zǐyè was imprisoned in the Xiàshěng of the Shìzhōng's office.
He was on the verge of being harmed many times,
but ultimately escaped unscathed.
When Shìzǔ ascended the throne,
Zǐyè was established as the Crown Prince.
Initially, before he moved to the Eastern Palace,
the Zhōngshùzǐ and the two Shuaì (Commanders) both reported for duty at Yǒngfúshěng.
In the second year of Dàmíng (458 CE),
he moved out to reside in the Eastern Palace.
In the fourth year (460 CE),
he lectured on the Xiàojīng (Classic of Filial Piety) in Chóngzhèngdiàn.
In the seventh year (463 CE),
he underwent the capping ceremony [came of age].
On the `gēngshēn` day of the intercalary fifth month in the eighth year (464 CE),
Shìzǔ passed away.
On that same day,
the Crown Prince immediately ascended the imperial throne.
A general amnesty was granted to the empire.
The Tàiwèi, Prince Yìgōng of Jiāngxià, was relieved of his post as Shàngshūlìng,
and granted the additional title of Zhōngshūjiān.
The Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn, Liǔ Yuánjǐng, was granted the additional title of Shàngshūlìng.
On the `jiǎzǐ` day,
the office of Lù Shàngshū was established,
and the Tàiwèi, Prince Yìgōng of Jiāngxià, was appointed Lù Shàngshū Shì.
The Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn, Liǔ Yuánjǐng, was granted the additional title of Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī.
Prince Zǐrén of Yǒngjiā, the Dānyáng Yǐn, was made the Cìshǐ of Nányùzhōu.
On the `xīnwèi` day of the sixth month,
an imperial edict stated:
"I, with my humble person,
have early succeeded to this great enterprise.
I respectfully command the heavenly majesty,
and reverently respond to the spiritual mandate.
Looking up to follow the established foundation,
and observing the precedents daily,
I ought to govern by simply doing nothing and maintaining the status quo,
passing on a legacy for generations to come.
However, with the beginning of this august position,
and the change of allegiance of the myriad lands,
my virtue is not illustrious,
and I am ignorant of the Great Way.
I wish to propagate sagely principles,
and introduce these compassionate considerations.
Let all officials be thoroughly consulted,
and the grievances of the people extensively sought out.
All intricate and confidential decrees,
which are cumbersome and detrimental to governance,
and the taxes on markets and rents,
which are temporary measures,
often lead to corrupt officials manipulating the law,
arbitrarily wielding power and influence.
Furthermore, with conflicting cosmic influences,
partiality has become rampant.
It is fitting to relax corvée labor and lighten punishments,
to alleviate the people's distress.
The various departments of the Imperial Household [Yùfǔ]
do not need to be expanded.
Elaborate decorations and engravings
have no place in the present.
All should be merged and reduced,
to fulfill the people's wishes.
Trade by princely vassals [fānwáng] is to be entirely prohibited.
Let specific articles be externally submitted for my consideration."
On the `wùyín` day,
Huáinán Commandery of Yùzhōu was restored as Nánliáng Commandery.
Xuānchéng Commandery was again separated to re-establish Huáinán Commandery.
On the `gēngchén` day,
Yuán Tányuǎn, the Tàishǒu of Nánhǎi, was made Cìshǐ of Guǎngzhōu.
In the seventh month of autumn, on the `jǐhài` day,
Prince Zǐxūn of Jìn'ān, the Zhènqūn Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ of Yōngzhōu, was changed to Cìshǐ of Jiāngzhōu.
Zōng Qī, the Zhōnghùjūn, was made Ānxī Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ of Yōngzhōu.
Prince Yù of Xiāngdōng, the Zhènběi Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ of Xúzhōu, was made Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
Prince Chǎng of Yìyáng, the Zhōngjūn Jiāngjūn, was made Zhēngběi Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ of Xúzhōu.
On the `gēngxū` day,
the country of Bóhuáng dispatched envoys to present local products.
Chóng Huáng Tàihòu was honored as Tài Huáng Tàihòu.
Huánghòu was called Huáng Tàihòu.
On the `yǐmǎo` day,
the two north and south imperial roadways (chídào) were abolished.
All systems revised since Xiàojiàn [period]
