were restored to the Yuánjiā [period] arrangements.
On the `bǐngchén` day,
Consort Xiàn was posthumously honored as Empress Xiàn.
On the `yǐchǒu` day,
Prince Zǐluán of Xīn'ān, the Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ of Nánxúzhōu, was relieved of his concurrent post as Sītú.
In the eighth month, on the `dīngmǎo` day,
Wáng Xuánmó, the Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn, was made Zhènběi Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ of Qīng and Jì Two Zhōu.
On the `jǐsì` day,
Xiāo Huìkāi, the Cìshǐ of Qīng and Jì Two Zhōu, was made Cìshǐ of Yìzhōu.
On the `jǐchǒu` day,
the Empress Dowager [Huáng Tàihòu] passed away.
There was heavy rain in the capital.
On the `gēngyín` day,
imperial censors and officials were dispatched to provide relief as appropriate.
In the ninth month, on the `xīnchǒu` day,
Prince Yù of Xiāngdōng, the Hùjūn Jiāngjūn, was made Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn.
On the `guǐmǎo` day,
Liú Zūnkǎo, the Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè, was made Tèjìn and Yòu Guānglù Dàfū.
On the `yǐmǎo` day,
Empress Wénmù was interred alongside [the emperor] in Jǐngníng Líng.
In the tenth month of winter, on the `jiǎxū` day,
Prince Xiūrén of Jiàn'ān, the Tàicháng, was made Hùjūn Jiāngjūn.
On the `wùyín` day,
Zōng Yuè, the Fǔguó Jiāngjūn, was made Cìshǐ of Sīzhōu.
On the `gēngchén` day,
the outstanding taxes from the seventh year of Dàmíng in Yáng and Nánxú Zhōu were pardoned.
In the twelfth month, on the `yǐyǒu` day,
Yán Shībó, the Shàngshū Yòu Púyè, was made Shàngshū Púyè.
On the `rénchén` day,
the various commanderies of the royal domain [wángjī] were made Yángzhōu.
Yángzhōu was made Dōngyángzhōu.
On the `guǐsì` day,
Prince Zǐshàng of Yùzhāng, the Chējì Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ of Yángzhōu, was made Sītú and Cìshǐ of Yángzhōu.
Last year and this year,
the eastern commanderies suffered a severe drought.
In the worst affected areas, a sheng of rice cost several hundred [cash],
and in the capital, it also reached over a hundred.
Six or seven tenths of the population died of starvation.
Since the Xiàojiàn period,
a mint had also been established to cast coins.
The common people consequently engaged in illicit minting,
causing coins to become progressively false and smaller,
and trade to cease.
In the first month of spring in the first year of Yǒngguāng, on the `yǐwèi` day (the new moon),
the reign title was changed.
A general amnesty was granted to the empire.
On the `yǐsì` day,
the imperial post stations (táichuán) in all zhōus were abolished.
On the `wùwǔ` day,
Prince Yù of Xiāngdōng, the Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn, was made Wèi Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ of Nányùzhōu.
Prince Xiūrén of Jiàn'ān, the Hùjūn Jiāngjūn, was made Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn.
Prince Xiūyòu of Shānyáng, the Mìshūjiān, was made Cìshǐ of Yùzhōu.
Prince Xiūfàn of Guìyáng, the Zuǒ Wèi Jiāngjūn, was made Zhōnghùjūn.
Prince Zǐfáng of Xúnyáng, the Cìshǐ of Nányùzhōu, was made Cìshǐ of Dōngyángzhōu.
In the second month, on the `yǐchǒu` day,
the land tax (tiánlù) for zhōu, jùn, and xiàn was reduced by half.
[一０] On the `gēngyín` day,
two-zhu coins were cast.
In the third month, on the `jiǎchén` day,
Língjiāng Commandery was abolished.
In the fifth month, on the `jǐhài` day,
Suí Commandery of Yǐngzhōu was detached and assigned to Yōngzhōu.
On the `bǐngwǔ` day,
Zhāng Mù, the Hòujūn Sīmǎ, was made Cìshǐ of Jiāozhōu.
In the sixth month, on the `jǐsì` day,
Liú Dàolóng, the Zuǒjūn Chángshǐ, was made Cìshǐ of Liáng and Nánqín Two Zhōu.
On the `yǐhài` day,
Zōng Qī, the Ānxī Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ of Yōngzhōu, died.
On the `rénwǔ` day,
Prince Yù of Xiāngdōng, the Wèi Jiāngjūn and Cìshǐ of Nányùzhōu, was changed to Cìshǐ of Yōngzhōu.
[一一] Liǔ Yuánjǐng, the Shàngshūlìng and Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn, was granted the additional title of Cìshǐ of Nányùzhōu.
In the eighth month of autumn, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Dài Fǎxīng (戴法興), Commander of the Vanguards (Yuèqí Xiàowèi), was found guilty
and granted death.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Yán Shībó (顏師伯), Palace Administrative Assistant (Shàngshū Púyè), was appointed Left Palace Administrative Assistant (Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè),
Wáng Jǐngwén (王景文), Minister of Personnel (Lìbù Shàngshū), was appointed Right Palace Administrative Assistant (Shàngshū Yòu Púyè).
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Emperor personally led the Palace Guard (Sùwèi Bīng)

to execute Jiāngxià Wáng (江夏王) Yìgōng (義恭), Grand Preceptor (Tàizǎi); Liǔ Yuánjǐng (柳元景), Director of the Palace Secretariat (Shàngshū Lìng) and General of Agile Cavalry (Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn); Yán Shībó (顏師伯), Left Palace Administrative Assistant (Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè); and Liú Déyuàn (劉德願), Minister of Justice (Tíngwèi).
The reign title was changed to Jǐnghé (景和) first year.
Civil and military officials were granted a two-grade promotion.
Jiàn'ān Wáng (建安王) Xiūrén (休仁), General of the Palace Guard (Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn), was appointed General of the Pacified West (Ānxī Jiāngjūn) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Yōngzhōu (雍州).
Xiāngdōng Wáng (湘東王) Yù (彧), General of the Guards (Wèijiāngjūn), was restored as Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Nányùzhōu (南豫州).
On the day Jiǎxū,
Yùzhāng Zǐ (豫章子) Shàng (尚), Grand Minister of Works (Sītú) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Yángzhōu (揚州), was additionally appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat (Shàngshū Lìng).
Shěn Wénxiù (沈文秀), Commander of Archers (Shèshēng Xiàowèi), was appointed Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Qīngzhōu (青州).
Cuī Dàogù (崔道gù), Left Army Chief Clerk (Zuǒjūn Sīmǎ), was appointed Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Jìzhōu (冀州).
On the day Yǐhài,
an imperial edict stated:
"In ancient times, (rulers) focused their minds and awaited the reclusive,
and Pánxī (磻溪) praised the Way.
They deeply contemplated and sought talent,
and Fùyán (傅巖) assisted in transformation.
I, occupying the supreme position,
have clarified the world's atmosphere.
With the swiftness of an axe and lightning,
Zhèng Mǎo (正卯) was executed.
I reflect on how to propagate the achievements of my predecessors
and extend the magnificent reign below.
Every night, I dream of the cooking pot,
and day, I gaze upon the mud walls,
toiling until sunset,
never forgetting the dawn.
Therefore, let enquiries be made in the commanderies and states,
and talent be recruited from villages and regions: those with filial piety and loyal integrity,
who dwell reclusively and seek retreat,
of faithfulness, sincerity, and righteous conduct,
of integrity and uprightness that serve as models for society,
who are eloquent, sharp, and broadly learned,
capable of handling affairs and governing the people,
should be diligently praised and promoted,
appointed according to their abilities.
May all officials be compliant,
and the constant relationships be well ordered.
Let those in charge thoroughly investigate and deliberate,
to fulfill My intentions."
Shěn Qìngzhī (沈慶之), Duke of Shǐxīng (始興公), was appointed Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi).
Wáng Xuánmó (王玄謨), General Who Guards the North (Zhènběi Jiāngjūn) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Qīngzhōu (青州) and Jìzhōu (冀州), was appointed General of the Palace Guard (Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn).
On the day Gēngchén,
Shítouchéng (石頭城) was made Chánglè Gōng (長樂宮).
Dōngfǔ Chéng (東府城) was made Wèiyāng Gōng (未央宮).
Dōngyángzhōu (東揚州) was abolished and merged with Yángzhōu (揚州).
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Běidǐ (北邸) was made Jiànzhāng Gōng (建章宮).
Nándì (南第) was made Chángyáng Gōng (長楊宮).
Shàolíng Zǐ (邵陵子) Yuán (元), General of the Champions (Guānjūn Jiāngjūn), was appointed Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Xiāngzhōu (湘州).
On the day Bǐngxū,
arrears of rent from before the eighth year of Dàmíng (大明) in the five commanderies of Wú (吳), Wúxīng (吳興), Yìxīng (義興), Jìnlíng (晉陵), and Lángxié (琅邪) were pardoned and waived.
On the day Jǐchǒu,
the two northern and southern imperial roads (Chídào) were re-established.
In the ninth month, on the day Guǐsì,
the imperial carriage visited Húshú (湖熟),
and drum and wind music was performed.
On the day Wùxū,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Yǒngjiā Zǐ (永嘉子) Rén (仁), Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Nányǎnzhōu (南兗州), was appointed Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Nánxúzhōu (南徐州).
Shǐ'ān Zǐ (始安子) Zhēn (真), Administrator of Dānyáng (Dānyáng Yǐn), was appointed Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Nányǎnzhōu (南兗州).
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Xīn'ān Zǐ (新安子) Luán (鸞), General Who Guards the Army (Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Nánxúzhōu (南徐州), was dismissed to commoner status
and granted death.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
Xuē Āndū (薛安都), Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Yǎnzhōu (兗州), was appointed General Who Pacifies the North (Píngběi Jiāngjūn) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Xúzhōu (徐州).
On the day Dīngwèi,
Xiāngdōng Wáng (湘東王) Yù (彧), General of the Guards (Wèijiāngjūn), was granted the honorific position of Kōifǔ Yítóng Sānsī (開府儀同三司).

Liú Zūnkǎo (劉遵考), Special Advance (Tèjìn) and Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness (Yòu Guānglù Dàfū), was appointed General of the Pacified West (Ānxī Jiāngjūn) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Nányùzhōu (南豫zhou).
Yīn Xiàozǔ (殷孝祖), General Who Pacifies the Barbarians (Níngshuò Jiāngjūn), was appointed Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Yǎnzhōu (兗州).
On the day Wùshēn,
Liǔ Yuángǔ (柳元怙), former Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Liáng (梁) and Nánqín (南秦) two prefectures, was reappointed Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Liáng (梁) and Nánqín (南秦) two prefectures.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
the imperial carriage set out to suppress Yìyáng Wáng (義陽王) Chǎng (昶), General Who Conquers the North (Zhēngběi Jiāngjūn) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Xúzhōu (徐州),
and strict internal and external alerts were ordered.
Chǎng (昶) fled to the northern barbarians (suǒlǔ 索虜).
On the day Xīnhài,
Shānyáng Wáng (山陽王) Xiūyòu (休祐), Right General (Yòu Jiāngjūn) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Yùzhōu (豫州), was promoted to the title of Grand General Who Guards the West (Zhènxī Dàjiāngjūn).
On the day Jiǎyín,
Yuán Yǐ (袁顗), Chief Clerk of the Pacified West (Ānxī Zhǎngshǐ), was appointed Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Yōngzhōu (雍州).
On the day Wùwǔ,
Liú Sīkǎo (劉思考), Left Minister of the People (Zuǒmín Shàngshū), was appointed Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Yìzhōu (益州).
On this day, the alert was lifted,
and the imperial carriage visited Guānbù (瓜步).
Commoners were permitted to mint coins.
In the tenth month of winter, on the day Guǐhài,
a partial amnesty was granted to Xúzhōu (徐州).
On the day Bǐngyín,
the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
Jiàn'ān Wáng (建'ān Wáng) Xiūrén (休仁) was appointed General Who Protects the Army (Hùjūn Jiāngjūn).
On the day Jǐmǎo,
Wáng Zǎo (王藻), Administrator of Dōngyáng (Dōngyáng Tàishǒu), was imprisoned and died.
Palace Lady Xiè Guìpín (謝貴嬪) was made a Fūren (夫人),
and granted tiger-head halberds (hǔbēn sānjǐ)
and phoenix chariots with dragon banners (luánlù lóngqí),
with ceremonial guards upon departure and entry (chūjǐng rùbì).
She was actually Princess Xīncài (Xīncài Gōngzhǔ).
On the day Yǐyǒu,

Shānyáng Wáng (山陽王) Xiūyòu (休祐), Grand General Who Guards the West (Zhènxī Dàjiāngjūn) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ) of Yùzhōu (豫zhou), was appointed Grand General Who Guards the Army (Zhènjūn Dàjiāngjūn) and Kōifǔ Yítóng Sānsī (開府儀同三司).
In the eleventh month,
on the day Rénchén,
Hé Mài (何邁), General Who Pacifies the Barbarians (Níngshuò Jiāngjūn), was imprisoned and died.
Shěn Qìngzhī (沈慶之), the newly appointed Grand Commandant (Tàiwèi), passed away.
On the day Rén'yín,
Empress Lù (路) was enthroned,
and music was played in the four palace wings.
Amnesty was granted to Yángzhōu (揚州) and Nánxúzhōu (南徐州).

Jiàn'ān Wáng (建'ān Wáng) Xiūrén (休仁), General Who Protects the Army (Hùjūn Jiāngjūn), was granted the additional titles of Special Advance (Tèjìn) and Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness (Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū).
Guìyáng Wáng (桂陽王) Xiūfàn (休範), Central Protector-General (Zhōng Hùjūn), was transferred.
On the day Dīngwèi,
an imperial prince was born,
son of Liú Shèngzhī (劉勝之), Minor Minister (Shǎofǔ).
A general amnesty was declared throughout the empire.
All crimes of corruption, defilement, licentiousness, and theft
were pardoned and remitted.
Those who became successors to their fathers were granted one rank of nobility.
On the day Rénzǐ,

Jiàn'ān Wáng (建'ān Wáng) Xiūrén (休仁), Special Advance (Tèjìn), Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness (Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū), and General Who Protects the Army (Hùjūn Jiāngjūn), was appointed General of Agile Cavalry (Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn) and Kōifǔ Yítóng Sānsī (開府儀同三司).
On the day Wùwǔ,
Nánpíng Wáng (南平王) Jìngyóu (敬猷), Lúlíng Wáng (廬陵王) Jìngxiān (敬先), and Ānnán Hóu (安南侯) Jìngyuān (敬淵) were all granted death.
At this time, the Emperor's tyranny and depravity grew daily,
and executions followed one after another.
Officials, both inside and outside the court,
could not guarantee their own safety.
Before this, a rumor circulated saying:
"An Emperor will emerge from Xiāngzhōng (湘中)."
The Emperor intended to tour the southern prefectures of Jīngzhōu (荊州) and Xiāngzhōu (湘zhōu) to suppress this.
He first wanted to execute his various uncles
and then set forth.
Tàizōng (太宗) secretly conspired with his attendants Ruǎn Diànfū (阮佃夫), Wáng Dàolóng (王道隆), Lǐ Dào'ér (李道兒), and the Emperor's close guards Shòu Jìzhī (壽寂之), Jiāng Chǎnzhī (姜產之), and eleven others,
planning to depose the Emperor.
On the night of Wùwǔ,
the Emperor was shooting ghosts in the Zhúlín Táng (竹林堂) of Huálín Yuán (華林園).
At that time, shamans said:
"There are ghosts in this hall."
Therefore, the Emperor himself was shooting at them.
Shòu Jìzhī (壽寂之) entered directly, carrying a knife,
with Jiāng Chǎnzhī (姜產之) as his aide.
The Emperor tried to flee,
but Jìzhī (寂之) pursued and killed him.
He was seventeen years old at the time.

The Grand Empress Dowager issued an order, addressing the Grand Minister of Works (Sītú) and General Who Protects the Army (Hùjūn Jiāngjūn), and the Eight Ministers: "Though Zǐyè (子業) was the eldest legitimate son,
he inherited cruelty and venom from a young age.
His lack of benevolence and filial piety
was evident since childhood.
When Xiàowǔ (孝武) passed away,
he happened to
ascend the throne.
Since the funerary carriage was in mourning,
he wore a smiling face without shame.
When the heavens punished with a double misfortune,
his joyous indulgence grew even more excessive.
Forced by internal and external restraints,
his cruelty was not yet fully exposed,
but
his vicious brutality was hard to suppress.
One day, he unleashed disaster,
and then wantonly executed the prime ministers
and annihilated his aiding officials.
Zǐluán (子鸞) and his brothers,
whom the late Emperor deeply loved,
harbored resentment in the past,
but were wrongly subjected to
brutal slaughter.
Chǎng (昶), a close relative, bravely defended,
but was unjustly attacked.
Princess Xīncài (Xīncài Gōngzhǔ) was forced to leave her husband's family,
imprisoned in the deep palace,
and falsely declared deceased.
After the funeral affairs were barely done,
the mourning
rites were immediately abandoned.
He indulged in drunkenness throughout the long nights,
neglecting all state affairs.
Court worthies and old meritorious officials
were discarded like dirt.
Music and dance never ceased,
and rare delicacies were always prepared.
He cursed and insulted his ancestors
and parents,
treating it as a joke.
His travels and excursions were endless,
his debauchery boundless.
He held feasts in imperial tombs and mausoleums,
planning to excavate them.
He executed innocent people
and seized women by force.
He established
He established a false heir,
and no one knew whose descendant he was.
He appointed a concubine as empress,
an extravagance beyond ritual.
Imperial relatives and close kin
were treated like maidservants and slaves,
whipped, beaten, dragged, and humiliated,
with no distinction of rank.
The Nánpíng family
especially suffered his cruelty.
Defying heaven and destroying reason,
his atrocities manifested in myriad ways.
Harsh punishments and cruel decrees
were endless and without limit,
even Xià Jié and Yīn Xīn
were insufficient
to compare.
The entire court was terrified,
no one felt safe,
and the common people were distraught,
with nowhere to rest their hands or feet.
His conduct was fouler than beasts,
his crimes exceeding three thousand.
The enterprise of Gāozǔ was on the verge of
extinction,
and the sacrifices at the Seven Temples were almost cut off.
I, old and gravely ill,
have often worried about calamity and poison,
anxious with each passing moment,
my life's breath nearly gone.
Since the dawn of creation,
such things have never
been heard of.
From far and near, nine out of ten households
wish to rise up.
General Wèi and the Prince of Xiāngdōng, Tǐ, born of Tàizǔ,
are naturally sagacious and heroic,
deeply beloved by Wénhuáng,
their favor surpassing all other princes.
I recognized their divine wisdom early,
and they exceptionally
possessed traditional courtesy.
Secretly executing a grand plan,
righteous warriors threw up their sleeves.
The sole tyrant having perished,
his head was hung on a white banner.
The altars of soil and grain revived,
the ancestral temple permanently secured.
Gods and men gave their hearts,
and the great mandate
was truly gathered.
Moreover, his meritorious virtue is lofty and distant,
the great enterprise belongs to him,
and he should follow the precedents of Hàn and Jìn,
to succeed to the imperial throne.
Let the officials in charge thoroughly examine the old rituals and carry them out in due course.
This widow, in her remaining years, has unfortunately endured these myriad hardships,
ever contemplating these matters,
though living, as if dead.
What more can be done!
What more can be done!
The deposed emperor was buried west of the altar in the southern suburbs of Mòlíng county, Dānyáng.
The emperor was impetuous and irritable in his youth,
and while in the Eastern Palace, was often rebuked by Shìzǔ.
When Shìzǔ went on a western tour,
Zǐyè presented a memorial on supervising his daily life.
His handwriting was not careful,
and the emperor questioned and reproached him.
Zǐyè presented a memorial apologizing,
and the emperor replied again:
"Your handwriting has not improved;
this is but one issue.
I hear you have always been negligent,
and your irritability and rebelliousness worsen daily.
Why are you so obstinate!"
When he first ascended the throne,
receiving the imperial seal and ribbon,
he was perverse and showed no sign of grief.
Initially, he hesitated before the high officials and Dài Fǎxīng and others,
but after killing Fǎxīng,
none of the high officials were not terrified.
Then he also executed the various dukes.
From Yuánkǎi downwards,
all were beaten, whipped, and dragged.
Inside and outside the court, there was fear and alarm,
and the palace chambers were in chaos.
At first, when the empress dowager was gravely ill,
she sent for the emperor.
The emperor said:
"There are many ghosts among the sick;
it is frightening,
how can I go?"
The empress dowager was enraged,
and told her attendants:
"Bring a knife,
and cut open my belly!
How could I have given birth to such a child!"
A few days after the empress dowager's death,
the emperor dreamed that the empress dowager said to him:
"You are unfilial and inhumane,
originally not having the appearance of a ruler.
Your son is also foolish and perverse to this extent,
nor is he destined for the throne.
Xiàowǔ, cruel and destructive of the Dao,
accumulated resentment among men and gods.
Though his sons are many,
none possess the Mandate of Heaven.
The great mandate belongs,
as it should, to the son of Emperor Wén."
Later, the Prince of Xiāngdōng succeeded to the throne,
and indeed he was the son of Emperor Wén.
Therefore, the emperor gathered his various uncles in the capital,
fearing they would cause trouble if left outside.
Princess Shānyīn was excessively licentious,
and said to the emperor:
"Between your sister and Your Majesty,
although there is a difference in gender,
we both share the same father.
Your Majesty has tens of thousands of women in your six palaces,
while I only have one consort.
This is not fair,
how can it be like this!"
The emperor then provided her with thirty male attendants as lovers;
she was promoted to the title of Grand Princess of Kuàijī Commandery,
her rank equal to a commandery prince,
enjoying a tax-exempt enfeoffment of two thousand households,
[一六]given a complete set of drum and wind instruments,
and twenty additional armed guards.
Whenever the emperor went out,
she would often ride in the imperial carriage with his court officials.
The princess, finding Chǔ Yuān, a clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, handsome,
asked the emperor to let him serve her.
The emperor agreed.
Yuān served the princess for ten days,
experiencing intense coercion,
but swore to die rather than yield,
and thus managed to escape.
The eunuch Huá Yuàn'ér, favored by the emperor,
rose to the rank of Sànqí Chángshì,
and was given the titles of General and Commandery Administrator.
The emperor was fond of reading in his youth,
[一七]and was quite knowledgeable about ancient affairs.
He personally composed elegies for Shìzǔ and various other literary pieces,
which often possessed literary elegance.
Because Wèi Wǔdì had 'Gravedigging Colonel' and 'Gold-touching Captain' as titles,
he established these two offices.
He appointed Liú Xiūrén, Prince of Jiàn'ān, and Liú Xiūyòu, Prince of Shānyáng, to lead them.
[一八]Other events
are described in the various biographies.
The historian comments: The deeds and conduct of the deposed emperor are recorded in this chapter.
If King Wǔ enumerated the transgressions of Yīn Zhòu,
he could not list even one ten-thousandth of them;
if Huò Guāng recorded the faults of Chāngyì,
it would not be enough to mention a hair's breadth.
If a ruler of average talent
had even one of these faults,
it would be enough to collapse the altars of soil and grain, ruin the imperial clan,
destroy the palaces, and inundate the temples.
How much more so when all these evils are concentrated in one person!
That he perished can be considered fortunate.
Collation Notes
Basic Annals 8: Emperor Míng
Emperor Míng (明) Tàizōng (太宗), whose personal name was Yù (彧),
courtesy name Xiūbǐng (休炳),
and childhood name Róngqī (榮期),
was the eleventh son of Emperor Wéndì (文帝).
He was born on the *wùyín* day of the tenth month of Yuánjiā (元嘉) 16 (439 CE).
In the 25th year (448 CE),
he was enfeoffed as Prince of Huáiyáng (淮陽),
with a stipend of two thousand households.
In the 29th year (452 CE),
he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Xiāngdōng (湘東).
When the primary culprit usurped the throne and established himself,
he was appointed General of Galloping Cavalry (Xiāoqí Jiāngjūn, 驍騎將軍),
with the additional post of Attendant-in-ordinary (Jǐshì Zhōng, 給事中).
When Shìzǔ (世祖) ascended the throne,
he became Director of the Imperial Library (Mìshū Jiān, 祕書監),
then was promoted to General of the Champion Army (Guànjūn Jiāngjūn, 冠軍將軍), Grand Administrator (Tàishǒu, 太守) of the two commanderies of Nánlánlíng (南蘭陵) and Xiàpī (下邳),
and concurrently oversaw the affairs of Shítóu (石頭) outpost.
In Xiàojiàn (孝建) 1 (454 CE),
he was transferred to be Grand Administrator of the two commanderies of Nánpéngchéng (南彭城) and Dōnghǎi (東海),
with his general title remaining as before,
and garrisoned at Jīngkǒu (京口).
In the same year,
he was summoned to be Central Protector of the Army (Zhōnghùjūn, 中護軍).
In the 2nd year (455 CE),
he was promoted to Attendant-in-ordinary (Shìzhōng, 侍中),
and concurrently Commander of the Roaming Cavalry (Yóujī Jiāngjūn, 游擊將軍).
In the 3rd year (456 CE),
he was transferred to be Grand Commandant (Wèiwèi, 衞尉),
with his Attendant-in-ordinary post remaining as before.
He was also appointed General of the Left Guard (Zuǒwèi Jiāngjūn, 左衞將軍),
with his Grand Commandant post remaining as before.
In Dàmíng (大明) 1 (457 CE),
he was transferred to Central Protector of the Army (Zhōnghùjūn, 中護軍),
with his Grand Commandant post remaining as before.
In the 3rd year (459 CE),
he became Minister of the Department of State Affairs (Dōuguān Shàngshū, 都官尚書),
and concurrently Commander of the Roaming Cavalry (Yóujī Jiāngjūn, 游擊將軍),
with his Grand Commandant post remaining as before.
In the 7th year (463 CE),
he was promoted to General Overseeing the Army (Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn, 領軍將軍).
In the 8th year (464 CE),

he was sent out as Bearer of Credentials (Shǐchíjié, 使持節), Regional Inspector (Dūdū, 都督) of military affairs of Xú (徐) and Yǎn (兗) provinces, as well as the Liang (梁) commandery of Yù (豫) province, General Who Guards the North (Zhènběi Jiāngjūn, 鎮北將軍), and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ, 刺史) of Xú province,
and was granted one set of drums and pipes (gǔchuī, 鼓吹).
In the same year,
he was summoned to be Attendant-in-ordinary (Shìzhōng, 侍中) and General Protector of the Army (Hùjūn Jiāngjūn, 護軍將軍).
Before he was invested,
he was again made General Overseeing the Army (Lǐngjūn Jiāngjūn, 領軍將軍),
with his Attendant-in-ordinary post remaining as before.
In Yǒngguāng (永光) 1 (465 CE),

he was again sent out as Bearer of Credentials (Shǐchíjié, 使持節), Cavalier Attendant-in-ordinary (Sànqí Chángshì, 散騎常侍), Regional Inspector (Dūdū, 都督) of military affairs of the four provinces of Nányù (南豫), Yù (豫), Sī (司), and Jiāng (江), as well as Xuānchéng (宣城) commandery of Yáng (揚) province, General of the Guard (Wèijiāngjūn, 衞將軍), and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ, 刺史) of Nányù province,
and garrisoned at Gūshú (姑孰).

He was then transferred to be Regional Inspector (Dūdū, 都督) of military affairs of the four provinces of Yōng (雍), Liáng (梁), Nánqín (南秦), and Běiqín (北秦), as well as Jìnglíng (竟陵) commandery of Yǐng (郢) province, Calming-the-Barbarians Commandant (Níngmán Xiàowèi, 寧蠻校尉), and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ, 刺史) of Yōng province,
with his Bearer of Credentials, Attendant-in-ordinary, and General titles remaining as before.
Before he was invested,
he returned to his original position.
Soon after, he was granted the honorific title of Founding Grand Administrator with the status of a Grand Minister (Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, 開府儀同三司) with his original rank.
At the end of Jǐnghé (景和) era of the deposed emperor (465 CE),
His Majesty entered the court,
and was detained in the capital.
The deposed emperor executed and harmed his chief ministers and advisors,
slaughtered high-ranking officials,
and, fearing conspiracies against him,
became suspicious and afraid of his paternal uncles.
He confined them all within the palace,
treating His Majesty disrespectfully;
details are in the biographies of the Wén (文) princes.
He then had His Majesty arrested and handed over to the Grand Judge (Tíngwèi, 廷尉),
but he was pardoned after one night.
Those who intended to harm him
were not just one person, both before and after.
Later, the intention to harm His Majesty was firm,
and he was to face misfortune the next morning.
His Majesty had already secretly conspired with his trusted confidants Ruǎn Diànfū (阮佃夫), Lǐ Dào’ér (李道兒), and others.
At that time, the deposed emperor’s attendants constantly feared that misfortune would befall them,
and each harbored different intentions.
Only a few, such as the Palace Guard General (Zhíhé Jiāngjūn, 直閤將軍) Zōng Yuè (宗越), Tán Jīn (譚金), and Tóng Tàiyī (童太一), were his close confidants.
They were fierce and capable like tigers and rhinoceros,
and had been in the palace for a long time.
Everyone feared and submitted to them,
so no one dared to act.
That night,
Yuè (越) and the others were all sleeping outside.
Diànfū (佃夫) and Dào’ér (道兒) then instigated Shòu Jìzhī (壽寂之) and others to kill the deposed emperor in the rear hall.
This was on the night of the 29th day of the eleventh month.
When the affair was settled,
His Majesty did not yet know what to do.
Xiūréng (休仁), Prince of Jiàn’ān (建安), then called himself a subject and escorted His Majesty to the west hall,
where he ascended the imperial throne.
He summoned the various high ministers for an audience.
At that time, events happened suddenly,
and His Majesty lost his shoes,
arriving at the west hall barefoot,
still wearing a black cap.
Once he was seated,
Xiūréng (休仁) called for the chief wardrobe official to replace it with a white cap,
and arranged for the imperial ceremonial regalia.
Although he had not yet formally ascended the throne,
all public affairs were carried out by imperial decree.
On the *jǐwèi* day (December 10, 465 CE),
Zǐshàng (子尚), Prince of Yùzhāng (豫章), who was Minister of Works (Sītú, 司徒) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ, 刺史) of Yáng (揚) province, and Princess Shānyīn (山陰) were both granted death.
Zōng Yuè (宗越), Tán Jīn (譚金), and Tóng Tàiyī (童太一) were executed for treason.
On the *gēngshēn* day, the first day of the twelfth month (December 11, 465 CE),
an imperial decree appointed Huī (褘), Prince of Dōnghǎi (東海), who was Minister of Education (Sīkōng, 司空), as Director of the Central Secretariat (Zhōngshū Jiān, 中書監) and Grand Master (Tàiwèi, 太尉).

Zǐxūn (子勛), Prince of Jìn’ān (晉安), who was General Who Stabilizes the Army (Zhènjūn Jiāngjūn, 鎮軍將軍) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ, 刺史) of Jiāng (江) province, was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry (Chējì Jiāngjūn, 車騎將軍) and Founding Grand Administrator with the status of a Grand Minister (Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, 開府儀同三司).
On the *guǐhài* day (December 14, 465 CE),

Xiūréng (休仁), Prince of Jiàn’ān (建安), newly appointed General of Agile Cavalry (Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn, 驃騎大將軍), was made Minister of Works (Sītú, 司徒), Director of the Imperial Secretariat (Shàngshū Lìng, 尚書令), and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ, 刺史) of Yáng (揚) province.

Xiūyòu (休祐), Prince of Shānyáng (山陽), who was General Who Stabilizes the Army (Zhènjūn Jiāngjūn, 鎮軍將軍) and Founding Grand Administrator with the status of a Grand Minister (Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, 開府儀同三司), was promoted to General of Agile Cavalry (Piàojì Dàjiāngjūn, 驃騎大將軍) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ, 刺史) of Jīng (荊) province.

Xiūfàn (休範), Prince of Guìyáng (桂陽), who was Grand Commandant of the Palace (Chóngxiàn Wèiwèi, 崇憲衞尉), was made General Who Guards the North (Zhènběi Jiāngjūn, 鎮北將軍) and Provincial Governor (Cìshǐ, 刺史) of Nánxú (南徐) province.
On the *yǐchǒu* day (December 16, 465 CE),
Zǐsuī (子綏), Prince of Ānlù (安陸), was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jiāngxià (江夏).
On the *bǐngyín* day of the twelfth month of the winter of Tàishǐ (泰始) 1 (January 1, 466 CE),
His Majesty ascended the imperial throne.
An imperial edict declared: “Emperor Gāozǔ Wǔhuángdì (高祖武皇帝)’s virtue permeated the four seas,
and his transforming influence spread throughout the nine regions.
Emperor Tàizǔ Wénhuángdì (太祖文皇帝) established the foundation with great clarity;
Emperor Shìzǔ Xiàowǔhuángdì (世祖孝武皇帝) pacified chaos
with martial might.
Wherever the sun and moon shone,
people built ladders up mountains and sailed the seas;
wherever the wind and rain reached,
people cut their robes and girded their waists [in submission].
Thus, his enterprise was as solid as the flourishing Hàn,
and his renown surpassed the glorious Zhōu.
Zǐyè (子業) was a savage
and foolish monster from heaven,
whose cruelty and perversity became his nature.
He had the face of a human but the heart of a beast,
evident from his childhood.
He subverted the Dao and corrupted virtue,
manifest from recent years.
He insulted the Five Constants,
abandoned the Three
Rectitudes,
falsely accused Heaven,
and poisoned the lower realm,
a situation unprecedented since creation,
and unheard of in written records.
He twice suffered the silence of mourning,
yet showed not a single day of sorrow;
with his mourning attire
still upon him,
he indulged deeply in the pleasures of Běilǐ (北里).
Tigers and rhinos are hard to contain in a box,
and crossing a river will surely reveal danger.
Thus, he executed and destroyed the chief ministers,
exhausting the cruelty of his perverse transgressions.
He tyrannized and harmed the pillars of the state,
and carried out punishments of
enslavement and slaughter.
He eliminated Zǐluán (子鸞), his blood brother,
due to old grudges.
He annihilated Jìngyóu (敬猷) and his brothers
over trivial slights.
He coerced and threatened Yìyáng (義陽),
intending to slaughter them.
He humiliated
and disgraced his imperial relatives,
and flogged and beat his consorts and princesses.
He seized and appointed his attendants,
and secretly placed his illegitimate son as heir.
He indulged in drunkenness in court,
and proclaimed his licentiousness throughout the nation.
His deeds defiled the Eastern Mausoleum,
and his conduct shamed even birds and beasts.
His accumulated transgressions were boundless,
deepening with each passing day.
Recently, he even plotted to violate the imperial tombs,
and intended to peer into the inner burial chamber,
planning to unleash the calamity of *xiāo* (梟) and *jìng* (鏡) [tortures],
and indulge the ambitions of Shāng (商) and Dùn (頓).
He also wished
to poison Chóngxiàn (崇憲),
and inflict cruelty upon his paternal uncles.
His deeds were known in the imperial palace,
and his reputation spread throughout the capital.
Vicious little villains [like owls and panthers] were all favored and intimate,
while loyal and honest officials in court
were surely slaughtered
and
defeated.
Regarding the decrees for arrests and confinement,
fierce tigers [sent to execute them] formed continuous tracks;
for those sent to plunder,
white blades were seen everywhere.
The hundred officials felt their lives were in peril,
with none safe;
the myriad common people were heartbroken,
their wives and children unable to protect each other.
Thus, ghosts wailed and mountains roared,
blood rained from the stars.
The sacred imperial instruments were almost in the hands of ropes [of arresters],
and the grand imperial fortune was as precarious as a dangling tassel.
I feigned sleep in deep sorrow,
weeping blood until dawn,
fearing that the foundation of the Great Sòng (宋)
would thereby perish,
and the achievements of Wǔ (武) and Wén (文)
would fall into the abyss.
Relying on the seven ancestral temples'
Líng,
by the good fortune of eight hundred years,
the great villains have been exterminated,
the vast plagues now dispelled.
The imperial order, once broken, is now re-established;
the celestial weave, once rent, is now mended.
Unworthily, with meager virtue,
I have been
entrusted with the imperial succession,
to uphold the gravitas of the three luminaries above,
and to look upon the difficulties of the common people below.
Anxiously and with caution,
as if treading on thin ice,
I wish with the myriad people
to achieve this renewal.
Let there be
a great amnesty throughout the realm,
and the first year of Jǐnghé be changed to the first year of Tàishǐ.
Grant two ranks of nobility to the people.
For the widowed, orphaned, and solitary who cannot support themselves,
give five hú of grain per person.
Arrears of taxes and old debts are not to be collected again.
Those who violated local public opinion and pure discourse,
and were guilty of bribery, licentiousness, and theft,
are all to have their names cleared.
Those serving long sentences
are specially granted pardons and release.
Those who lost their official positions or
titles,
or were banned from office due to old offenses,
are all to be dealt with according to old statutes.
All erroneous appointments and mistaken enfeoffments from the former corrupt regime
are to be abolished.
On the day Jǐsì,
Liú Zūnkǎo, General of the Pacified West and Inspector of Nányùzhōu, was appointed Grand Master of Imperial Counsel with Special Advancement and Right Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
Jǐngsù, Prince of Jiànpíng, General Who Aids the State and Administrator of the two commanderies of Lìyáng and Nánqiáo, was appointed Inspector of Nányùzhōu.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Zǐxù, Prince of Línhǎi and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was appointed General Who Guards the Army.
Zǐrén, Prince of Yǒngjiā and Inspector of Nánxúzhōu, was appointed General of the Central Army.
Liú Dàolóng, General of the Left Guard, was appointed Protector-General of the Central Army.
On the day Xīnwèi,
Zǐchǎn, Prince of Línghè, was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Nánpíng.
Zǐyú, Prince of Jìnxī, was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Lúlín.
On the day Rénshēn,
Wáng Jǐngwén, Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat, was appointed Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
The newly appointed Protector-General of the Central Army, Liú Dàolóng, died.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
an imperial edict stated:
"I have pacified the rebellion and brought peace to the people,
happening to receive this auspicious blessing.
The grand system is newly established,
the way of governance is renewed.
Yet, the misfortunes of the state have been frequent,
and benevolent grace has been obstructed in places.
Every time I reflect upon this, my heart aches in my sleep,
and I know not how to remedy it.
To tour the regions and inquire into customs
is the priority in extending governance.
Therefore, send out imperial envoys
to widely seek out the people's sufferings,
to examine the merits of administrators,
and to gather the good deeds within the villages.
If there are wrongful imprisonments
that harm the people and damage moral instruction,
report them fully.
For the widowed, orphaned, and solitary,
the disabled and those with six chronic illnesses,
who cannot support themselves,
the commanderies and counties should generously assess and provide relief.
For chaste women and filial sons,
those of high conduct and diligent farmers,
detail and report them thoroughly.
Strive to inquire into public opinion
and broadly accept excellent counsel,
always fulfilling the purpose of imperial inspection,
as if I were personally observing."
On the day Yǐhài,
Shěn Jiéyú, the emperor's birth mother, was posthumously honored as Xuān Huáng Tàihòu.
Yuán Hóng, General of the Rear Army, was appointed Inspector of Sīzhōu.
Yīn Yǎn, former Chief Clerk to the Right General, was appointed Inspector of Yùzhōu.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
an imperial edict stated:
"The imperial house has faced many difficulties,
and expenses have grown excessively.
Furthermore, for many years there have been poor harvests,
leading to scarcity and hardship for both public and private sectors.
I intend to diligently practice frugality
and broadly alleviate the difficulties of the time.
As the way of governance has not yet fully taken effect,
I am filled with regret and shame.
For the imperial kitchen's provisions,
detail what can be reduced.
Useless items with carved patterns and inscriptions from the imperial workshops and treasuries
are all to be abolished.
Strive for simplicity and economy,
to accord with my heart."
On the day Wùyín,
the Empress Dowager was elevated to Chóngxiàn Huáng Tàihòu.
Empress Wáng was enthroned.
Zǐxūn, Prince of Jìn'ān, General Who Guards the Army and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, raised an army in rebellion.
Dèng Wǎn, Chief Clerk to the General Who Guards the Army, became his chief strategist.
Yuán Yǐ, Inspector of Yǒngzhōu, led his troops to join him.
On the day Xīnsì,
Xiūyòu, Prince of Shānyáng, General of Agile Cavalry and former Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was reassigned as Inspector of Jiāngzhōu.
Zǐxù, Prince of Línhǎi and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, remained in his original post.
Wáng Xuánmó, General Who Leads the Army, was promoted to General Who Guards the Army.
On the day Rénwǔ,
the imperial carriage paid homage at the ancestral temple.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Zǐsuí, Prince of Ānlù, General of the Rear Army and Inspector of Yǐngzhōu, was promoted to General Who Conquers the South.
Zǐfáng, Prince of Xúnyáng, Right General and Administrator of Kuàijī, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the East.
Zǐxù, Prince of Línhǎi, Former General and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.
Zǐsuí, Zǐfáng, and Zǐxù all refused the appointments
and raised armies in concerted rebellion.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Zǐrén, Prince of Yǒngjiā, the newly appointed General of the Central Army, was made Protector-General.
In the second year, on the first day of the first month, Jǐchǒu,
due to military matters, there was no court assembly.
On the day Gēngyín,
Wáng Sēnglǎng, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness with Gold and Purple, was appointed Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness and Minister with Rank Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers.
On the day Rénchén,
Xiūyòu, Prince of Shānyáng, General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, was reassigned as Inspector of Nányùzhōu,
and stationed in Lìyáng.
Wáng Xuánmó, General Who Guards the Army and General Who Leads the Army, was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu.
Xuē Āndū, General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Xúzhōu, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.
Āndū also refused the appointment.
On the day Guǐsì,
Xiūrúo, Prince of Bālíng and General of the Left Guard, was appointed General Who Guards the East.
Zǐfáng, Prince of Xúnyáng, the newly appointed General Who Pacifies the East, was made General Who Consoles the Army.
Yuán Mǐnsūn, Left Chief Clerk to the Grand Minister of Works, was appointed General Who Leads the Army.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
martial law was declared both inside and outside the capital.
Xiūrén, Prince of Jiàn'ān and Grand Minister of Works, was appointed Commander-in-Chief of all forces for punitive expeditions,
leading the assembled armies in a southern campaign.
Liú Zhī, Inspector of Qīngzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Shēn Lìngsūn, Sīmǎ for General Who Conquers the Barbarians, was appointed Inspector of Xúzhōu.
Páng Mèngqiú, Administrator of Yìyáng, was appointed Inspector of Sīzhōu.

Lìngsūn, Mèngqiú, as well as Yīn Yǎn, Inspector of Yùzhōu, Shěn Wénxiù, Inspector of Qīngzhōu, Cuī Dàogù, Inspector of Jìzhōu, Hé Huìwén, Acting Inspector of Xiāngzhōu, Yuán Tányuǎn, Inspector of Guǎngzhōu, Xiāo Huìkāi, Inspector of Yìzhōu, and Liǔ Yuángù, Inspector of Liángzhōu, all joined the rebellion.
Yīn Xiàozǔ, Inspector of Yǎnzhōu, entered the capital to defend it,
and was then dispatched as the vanguard for the southern expedition.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Xiàozǔ was promoted to General Who Consoles the Army.
On the day Bǐngwǔ,
the emperor personally commanded the six armies,
and encamped at Zhōngxīng Táng.
On the day Xīnhài,
Xiūyòu, Prince of Shānyáng, General of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Nányùzhōu, was reassigned as Inspector of Yùzhōu,
leading the assembled armies in a western campaign.

Gù Chēn, Administrator of Wújùn, Wáng Tánshēng, Administrator of Wúxīng, Liú Yánxī, Administrator of Yìxīng, Yuán Biāo, Administrator of Jìnlíng, and Chéng Tiānzuò, Administrator of Shānyáng, all raised armies in rebellion.
Xiūrúo, Prince of Bālíng and General Who Guards the East, led the assembled armies in an eastern campaign.
On the day Rénzǐ,
Chóngxiàn Huáng Tàihòu passed away.
On this day,
Rèn Nóngfū and Liú Huáizhēn, both military commanders, pacified Yìxīng.
Shǐ Yìzōng, a commoner from Yǒngshì county, seized the county in rebellion,
but Lù Yōuzhī, General of the Palace Guard, attacked and pacified him.
On the day Bǐngchén,

Wáng Sēnglǎng, the newly appointed Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness and Minister with Rank Equal to the Three Ducal Ministers, was appointed Grand Master of Imperial Counsel with Special Advancement,
retaining his position as Left Grand Master of Glorious Happiness.
In the second month, on the day Yǐchǒu,
Sēnglǎng died.
Wáng Jǐngwén, Director of the Imperial Secretariat, resigned due to his father's mourning.
A partial amnesty was granted to the four commanderies of Wú, Wúxīng, Yìxīng, and Jìnlíng.
Cài Xīngzōng, Minister of Personnel, was appointed Left Assistant Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
Zhāng Yǒng, Administrator of Wúxīng, and the Prince of Qí, Right General, led an eastern campaign,
and pacified Jìnlíng.
On the day Guǐwèi,
a partial amnesty was granted to the five commanderies east of the Zhèjiāng River.
On the day Dīnghài,
Xiūrúo, Prince of Bālíng and General Who Guards the East, was promoted to General Who Guards the Capital.
Wú Xǐgōng, General Who Establishes Martial Might, led various armies to defeat the rebels in Wú, Wúxīng, and Kuàijī,
pacifying the three commanderies,
and all the collaborators in the rebellion were executed.
The Prince of Qí, General Who Aids the State, led the vanguard in a northern campaign.
Liú Miǎn, General Who Aids the State, led the vanguard in a western campaign.
The rebel Liú Hú led forty thousand troops and occupied Zhèqí.
In the third month, on the day Gēngyín,
General Fǔjūn Yīn Xiàozǔ attacked Zhěqí
and died there.
Shěn Yōuzhī, General Fǔguó, was appointed to replace him as the southern vanguard.
The bandit forces gradually grew stronger.
Yuán Yǐ camped at Quèwěi,
with continuous encampments extending to Nónghú,
amounting to over 100,000 men.
On the day Rénchén,
Zhāng Yǒng, newly appointed Crown Prince Zhan事, was made Inspector of Qīng and Jì Prefectures.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
Liú Xiūfàn, Prince Guìyáng, General Zhènběi and Inspector of Nánxú Prefecture, was made Commander-in-Chief of all northern expeditionary forces.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Liú Sīkǎo, Shàngshū, was made Inspector of Xú Prefecture.
On the day Wùxū,
Zǐfáng, Prince of Xúnyáng, was demoted in rank to Marquis of Sōngzī County.
On the day Yǐsì,
Zhèng Hēi, Fèngcháoqǐng, was made Inspector of Sī Prefecture.
On the day Xīnhài,
Liú Xiūfàn, Prince Guìyáng, General Zhènběi and Inspector of Nánxú Prefecture, was also made Inspector of Nányǎn Prefecture.
On the day Rénzǐ,
the use of new money was abolished,
and only old money was used.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
a general pardon was granted to prisoners in Yáng and Nánxú Prefectures;
all fugitives were not to be questioned.
In summer, the fourth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Míng Sēnggǎo, Sànqí Shìláng, was made Inspector of Qīng Prefecture.
In the fifth month, on the day Rénchén,
Shěn Yōuzhī, General Fǔguó, was made Inspector of Yōng Prefecture.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
a partial pardon was granted to Yù Prefecture.
On the day Dīngwèi,
Wáng Jǐngwén, newly appointed Shàngshū Púyè, was made General Zhōngjūn;
Zhāng Yǒng, Inspector of Qīng and Jì Prefectures, was made General Zhènjūn.
On the day Gēngxū,
Liú Chéngmín, General Níngshuò, was made Inspector of Jì Prefecture.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Empress Dowager Chóngxiàn was interred at Xiūníngling.
Xiāo Huìkāi, General Guānjūn and Inspector of Yì Prefecture, was promoted to General Píngxī.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Zhāng Yǒng, General Zhènjūn, was also made Inspector of Xú Prefecture.
As there was continuous rain in the capital,
on the day Dīngmǎo,
General Diànzhōng was dispatched to inspect and grant relief.
Yuán Gōngzǔ, General Zuǒjūn, was made Inspector of Liáng and Nánqín Prefectures.
In autumn, the seventh month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Liú Xiūfàn, Prince Guìyáng, General Zhènběi and Inspector of Nánxú and Yǎn Prefectures, was promoted to Grand General Zhēngběi.
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Zhāng Yǒng, General Zhènjūn and Inspector of Xú Prefecture, was changed to Inspector of Nányǎn Prefecture.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
Yáng Sēngsì, Prefect of Qiúchí, was made Inspector of Běiqín Prefecture and King of Wǔdū.
On the day Rényín,
Shí Lángzhī, a man, was made Inspector of Běiyù Prefecture.
On the day Yǐsì,
Liú Dàofú, General Lóngxiáng, pacified Shānyáng.
On the day Xīnhài,
Zhèng Shújǔ, commander of the righteous army, was again made Inspector of Běiyù Prefecture;
Zhāng Yǒng, General Zhènjūn and Inspector of Nányǎn Prefecture, was again made Inspector of Xú Prefecture.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Cuī Dàogù, Inspector of Jì Prefecture, was again made Inspector of Xú Prefecture.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Liú Xiūrén, Prince Jiàn'ān and Sītú, led the combined forces and inflicted a great defeat on the bandits,
beheading the false Shàngshū Púyè Yuán Yǐ.
He then advanced to attack the five prefectures of Jiāng, Yǐng, Jīng, Yōng, and Xiāng,
and pacified them.
Zǐxūn, Prince of Jìn'ān; Zǐsuī, Prince of Ānlù; Zǐxū, Prince of Línghǎi; and Zǐyuán, Prince of Shàolíng, were all given death.
All their accomplices were executed.
The various generals and commanders were rewarded according to their different achievements.
On the day Jiǎshēn,
Zǐrén, Prince of Yǒngjiā and General Hùjūn, was made General Píngnán and Inspector of Xiāng Prefecture.
In the ninth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
a partial pardon was granted to the five prefectures of Jiāng, Yǐng, Jīng, Yōng, and Xiāng;
the local officials were not allowed to leave their posts.
On the day Rénchén,
Liú Xiūyòu, Prince of Shānyáng, Grand General Piàojí and Inspector of Yù Prefecture, was changed to Inspector of Jīng Prefecture.
Yù Prefecture was divided to establish Nányù Prefecture.
On the day Guǐsì,
the six armies were demobilized.
A general amnesty was granted to the empire,
and the common people were granted one rank of nobility.
On the day Jiǎwǔ,
Wáng Jǐngwén, General Zhōngjūn, was made General Ānnán and Inspector of Jiāng Prefecture.
On the day Wùxū,
Wáng Xuánmó, General Chējì and Inspector of Jiāng Prefecture, was made Left Guānglù Dàfū, Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, and General Hùjūn.
On the day Gēngzǐ,
Bóróng, heir to Liú Xiūrén, Prince Jiàn'ān, was made Inspector of Yù Prefecture.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
Liú Xiūruò, Prince of Bālíng and General Wèi, was appointed Inspector of Yōng Prefecture under his original title.
Shěn Yōuzhī, Inspector of Yōng Prefecture, was made Inspector of Yǐng Prefecture.
On the day Gēngxū,
Liú Jǐngsù, Prince of Jiànpíng and Crown Prince Zuǒwèilǜ, was made Inspector of Nányǎn Prefecture.
In the tenth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Zǐrén, Prince of Yǒngjiā; Zǐzhēn, Prince of Shǐ'ān; Zǐmèng, Prince of Huáinán; Zǐchǎn, Prince of Nánpíng; Zǐyú, Prince of Lúlíng; and Zǐfáng, Marquis of Sōngzī, were all given death.
On the day Dīngmǎo,
Shěn Yōuzhī, Inspector of Yǐng Prefecture, was made Zhōnglǐngjūn
to lead the northern expedition with Zhāng Yǒng.
On the day Gēngwǔ,
Gù Jìzhī, Prefect of Wújùn, was made Inspector of Xiāng Prefecture.
On the day Wùyín,
Imperial Son Yù was established as Crown Prince.
A partial pardon was granted to Yáng and Nánxú Prefectures.
Liú Miǎn, General Fǔguó, was made Inspector of Guǎng Prefecture;
Zhāng Shì, General Zuǒjūn, was made Inspector of Yù Prefecture.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
Liú Xí, Prefect of Ānchéng, was made Inspector of Yǐng Prefecture.
On the day Rénchén,
an imperial edict stated:
"Governance that values simplicity
and a transformation that rejects extravagance,
closely tied to the rise and fall of the distant past,
are clearly evident principles.
I, who have taken up this fallen dynasty
and encountered these extreme difficulties,
followed by desolation and exhaustion,
and then by military campaigns,
yet with a dim understanding compared to former kings,
have undertaken tasks more arduous than those of previous generations.
The old taxes are already burdensome,
and expenditures are too vast.
Reflecting on the myriad affairs,
I constantly think of great reforms.
I wish to ease labor services and lighten taxes,
making the welfare of the people the priority.
The responsible officials should carefully implement leniency and generosity,
and establish new regulations.
As for local products and tributes,
each should conform to the local suitability,
and the submission of offerings and tributes
All customs that harm the people,
occupations that pursue trifles and deviate from fundamentals,
extravagant decorations,
and rare or exotic crafts
should all be strictly curtailed and cut short,
with an emphasis on practicality.
The Left and Right Shàngfāng and Yùfǔ departments and other bureaus,
responsible for imperial manufacturing,
should all maintain frugality.
May the pure customs and excellent teachings
somewhat follow the ancient times,
enriching wealth and promoting humility,
and less strengthening the decadent customs of later ages."
Another edict stated:
"Indeed, holding the reins of power and consulting on governance
promoting the worthy and inviting the reclusive
is the basis for spreading civilization.
Thus, by advancing strategies with the tripod,
the Yīn dynasty prospered;
by leaving the fishing rod to become an assistant,
the Zhōu dynasty flourished.
I have just inherited this great enterprise,
and my instructions and guidance have not yet been fully spread.
Although I eagerly await loyal counsel
and dream of hermits from mountains and humble dwellings,
no excellent plans have been presented,
nor have extraordinary individuals been heard of.
Reflecting perpetually on the past and present,
I do not forget this even in my sleep.
Now, the border regions are at peace,
and the spread of civilization is just beginning.
I frequently harbor thoughts of good governance
and truly hope for advice to rectify shortcomings.
Princes, dukes, ministers, and magistrates,
and all officials and subordinates,
if you have good plans or direct suggestions
to rectify customs and aid the times,
you must earnestly present them in memorial,
without any concealment.
As for those who live virtuously in forests and swamps,
or are pure and upright in hills and gardens,
who are broadly learned in ancient and modern times,
and uphold filial piety and humility,
those in office in the four directions
should clearly write and seek them out,
reporting fully to me,
so that they may be honored and appointed accordingly."
Yánnián, son of Liú Jǐngsù, Prince Jiànpíng, was made Prince of Xīn'ān.
Wáng Xuánmó, newly appointed Left Guānglù Dàfū and Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī, was made General Chējì and Inspector of Nányù Prefecture.
On the day Bǐngshēn,
an edict ordered that those from the eastern lands who had been displaced and scattered
should all return to their hometowns,
and all their taxes and levies would be remitted for two years.
On the *jǐwèi* day of the twelfth month,
Liú Shànmíng (劉善明), Gold Bureau Director of the Department of State Affairs (Shàngshū Jīnbù Láng), was appointed Inspector of Jìzhōu (Jìzhōu Cìshǐ).
On the *yǐchǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“Recently, many vassal states (zhòngfān) have risen in rebellion,
most of them having been implicated in crimes.
However, some were truly loyal to the court (běncháo),
and their actions were due to duress.
Their indiscriminate conviction and imprisonment
is truly disheartening.
The Way of Heaven (tiāndào) values benevolence,
applying both virtue and punishment.
When thunder and lightning strike,
rain and clouds will surely disperse.
Meditating deeply on this,
We wish to extend Our beneficence.
Therefore, all who should have been banned or removed
are hereby pardoned.
Those civil and military officials who are capable
shall be appointed according to their talents.”
On the *xīnwèi* day,
Liú Miǎn (劉勔), newly appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu (Guǎngzhōu Cìshǐ), was made Inspector of Yìzhōu (Yìzhōu Cìshǐ).
Fèi Hùn (費混), former Administrator of Bāxī and Zǐtóng Commanderies (Bāxī, Zǐtóng Èr Jùn Tàishǒu), was made Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
Liú Miǎn recaptured Shòuyáng,
and Yùzhōu was pacified.
On the *xīnsì* day,
Liú Língyí (劉靈遺), General Who Assists the State (Fǔguó Jiāngjūn), was appointed Inspector of Liáng and Nánqín Commanderies (Liáng, Nánqín Èr Zhōu Cìshǐ).
and Zhāng Yǒng (張永) and Shěn Yōuzhī (沈攸之) suffered a great defeat,
resulting in the loss of the four northern Huái Commanderies and the Huáixī region of Yùzhōu.
In the spring of the third year, on the *gēngzǐ* day of the first month,
as agricultural labor was about to commence,
the Grand Provisioner (Tàiguān) ceased the slaughter of cattle.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
a partial amnesty was granted to Yù and Nányù Commanderies.
Bālíng Wáng Xiūròu (巴陵王休若), General of the Guard (Wèi Jiāngjūn), had his title downgraded to General Who Guards the West (Zhènxī Jiāngjūn).
In the intercalary month, on the *gēngwǔ* day,
there was heavy snow in the capital (Jīngshī).
Envoys were dispatched to inspect,
and relief and grants were distributed according to need.
On the *wùyín* day,
Yuán Hóng (垣閎), General of Agile Cavalry (Yóují Jiāngjūn), was appointed Inspector of Yìzhōu.
In the second month, on the *jiǎshēn* day,
Yáng Xī (羊希), Censor-in-Chief (Yùshǐ Zhōngchéng), was appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
the emperor held a mourning ceremony for the fallen officers and soldiers.
On the *jǐchǒu* day,
Liú Liàng (劉亮), Commander of the General Who Guards the West (Zhènxī Sīmǎ), was appointed Inspector of Liáng and Nánqín Commanderies.
The Suǒlǔ (索虜) attacked Rǔyīn,
but Administrator Zhāng Jǐngyuǎn (張景遠) defeated them.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
a partial amnesty was granted to Qīng and Jì Commanderies.
In the third month, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Cài Xīngzōng (蔡興宗), Left Grand Master of Remonstrance (Shàngshū Zuǒ Púyè), was appointed General Who Pacifies the West (Ānxī Jiāngjūn) and Inspector of Yǐngzhōu (Yǐngzhōu Cìshǐ).
On the *wùyín* day,
Wáng Xuánzài (王玄載), General of the Vanguard (Guànjūn Jiāngjūn), was appointed Inspector of Xúzhōu (Xúzhōu Cìshǐ),
and Cuī Píng (崔平), General Who Pacifies the North (Níngshuò Jiāngjūn), was appointed Inspector of Yǎnzhōu (Yǎnzhōu Cìshǐ).
In the summer of the fourth month, on the *guǐsì* day,
Zhèng Hēi (鄭黑), former Inspector of Sīzhōu (Sīzhōu Cìshǐ), was reappointed Inspector of Sīzhōu.
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Yáng Sēngsì (楊僧嗣), General of the Vanguard and Inspector of Běiqínzhōu (Běiqínzhōu Cìshǐ), was promoted to General Who Conquers the West (Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn).
On the *gēngzǐ* day,
Déxì (德嗣), the second son of Guìyáng Wáng Xiūfàn (桂陽王休範), was enfeoffed as Lúlíng Wáng (廬陵王).
Xiǎn (銑), the second son of Attendant Counselor Liú Yùn (侍中劉韞), was enfeoffed as Nánfēng Wáng (南豐王).
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Cài Xīngzōng, General Who Pacifies the West, had his title downgraded to General Who Pacifies the West (Píngxī Jiāngjūn).
In the fifth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
concerning the Empress Dowager Chóngníng's mausoleum (Chóngníng Líng), those interred in forbidden private burial chambers
and those who had been relocated were granted burial funds
and had their household members (jiādīng) exempted from labor.
On the *wùwǔ* day,

Wáng Xuánmó (王玄謨), General of Chariots and Cavalry (Chējì Jiāngjūn) and Inspector of Nányùzhōu (Nányùzhōu Cìshǐ), was appointed Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left (Zuǒ Guānglù Dàfū) and Minister with Powers of the Three Excellencies (Kāifǔ Yítóng Sānsī).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
Nányùzhōu was abolished and merged into Yùzhōu.
On the *rénxū* day,
Yuán Càn (袁粲), Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince (Tàizǐ Zhānsì), was appointed Grand Master of Remonstrance (Shàngshū Púyè).
In the sixth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
Liú Yùn, Attendant Counselor, was appointed Inspector of Xiāngzhōu (Xiāngzhōu Cìshǐ).
In the autumn of the seventh month, on the *rénzǐ* day,

Wáng Xuánmó, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left and Minister with Powers of the Three Excellencies, was appointed Special Advanced Officer (Tèjìn), Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left, and General Who Protects the Army (Hùjūn Jiāngjūn).
Xuē Āndū’s son, Bólìnglǜ (伯令略), occupied four commanderies in Yōngzhōu (Yōngzhōu).
Bālíng Wáng Xiūròu, the Inspector, attacked and beheaded him.
In the eighth month, on the *dīngyǒu* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“In ancient times, marshals and foresters were established,
and young insects were not collected.
What was produced in rivers and lakes
was presented as tribute.
This was to enrich the people's wealth
and nurture their innate virtue.
Recently, merchants pursue trivialities,
competing for early and new products,
plucking unripe fruit
to profit wealthy families,
and caging non-edible birds
for the amusement of children.
How can this be a return to ancient customs and an abandonment of extravagance for practicality?
It is fitting to cultivate the Way and spread benevolence
to reform this evil.
From now on, all aquatic creatures, birds,
and various delicacies
that are not in season or necessary for sustenance
are to be entirely prohibited
with strict regulations.”
On the *rényín* day,
Shěn Yōuzhī (沈攸之), Commander of the Central Army (Zhōnglǐngjūn), was appointed Acting Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu (Nányǎnzhōu Cìshǐ)
and led troops to campaign in the north.
On the *guǐmǎo* day,
an imperial edict stated:
“The use of legal strictures
is for a certain period,
while the way of clemency
is spread according to the times.
Moreover, We uphold virtue to quell rebellion
and govern the populace with benevolence.
It is fitting to always be magnanimous and lenient
to achieve great peace.
However, having frequently endured warfare,
taxes and levies have not ceased.
Among soldiers and commoners, there are many cunning and deceitful acts
that have caused numerous incidents,
leading to violations of the law.
Truly, these are not of a single category.
Some have falsely claimed military ranks
or secretly obtained noble titles in private.
Others have deserted during battle
or feigned fear to evade service.
Furthermore, though those who were previously suppressed
have received multiple pardons,
the number of those who have absconded and hidden
is still quite large.
Reflecting on this at night,
We feel profound pity and remorse.
We wish to once again spread Our great beneficence
to cover the entire realm.
Therefore, a general amnesty is granted to all under Heaven.”
Wáng Xuánmó, newly appointed Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Left,
was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day,
Chǔ Yuān (褚淵), Minister of Personnel (Lìbù Shàngshū), was dispatched to comfort and reward the generals and commanders along the Huái River
according to circumstances.
On the *wùshēn* day,
Liú Miǎn, newly appointed General of the Right Guard (Yòu Wèi Jiāngjūn),

In the ninth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,

Cài Xīngzōng, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yǐngzhōu, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the West.
On the *yǐmǎo* day,
Zhōu Níngmín (周寧民), Commandant of Elite Cavalry (Yuèjì Xiàowèi), was appointed Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
On the *wùwǔ* day,
one thousand sets of miscellaneous clothing and
one thousand golden hairpins from the Empress's six palaces and below
were distributed to the generals and soldiers campaigning in the north.
On the *gēngshēn* day,
Cuī Dàogù (崔道固), General of the Vanguard and concurrently Inspector of Jìzhōu, was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North (Píngběi Jiāngjūn).
On the *jiǎzǐ* day,
a partial amnesty was granted to Xú, Yǎn, Qīng, and Jì Commanderies.
In the winter of the tenth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Yánnián (延年), Prince of Xīn'ān (Xīn'ān Wáng), was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Shǐpíng (Shǐpíng Wáng).
On the *wùzǐ* day,
the Ruìruì (芮芮) state sent envoys to present local products.
On the *xīnchǒu* day,
public lands in commanderies and counties were restored.
Tǔyùhún Shíyīn (吐谷渾拾寅), Grand General Who Guards the West (Zhènxī Dà Jiāngjūn) and Inspector of Xīqín and Hé Commanderies, was promoted to Grand General Who Conquers the West (Zhēngxī Dà Jiāngjūn).
In the eleventh month,
Bóyóu (伯猷), the second son of Jiàn'ān Wáng Xiūrén (建安王休仁), was enfeoffed as Jiāngxià Wáng (江夏王).
Chǎng (昶), Prince of Yìyáng (Yìyáng Wáng), was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jìnxī (Jìnxī Wáng).

In the twelfth month, on the *gēngchén* day,
Liú Xiūbīn (劉休賓), General Who Pacifies the North, was appointed Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
In the spring of the fourth year, on the *jǐwèi* day of the first month,
the emperor personally performed sacrifices in the southern suburb,
and a general amnesty was granted to all under Heaven.
On the *gēngwǔ* day,
Bālíng Wáng Xiūròu, General of the Guard, had his title downgraded to General of the Left (Zuǒ Jiāngjūn).
On the *yǐhài* day,
Sīmǎ Xù (司馬勗), Prince of Línglíng (Línglíng Wáng), passed away.
In the second month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
Cháng Zhēnjī (常珍奇), former General of the Dragon Cavalry (Lóngxiāng Jiāngjūn), was appointed General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Sīzhōu.
His son, Cháoyuè (超越), was appointed Inspector of Běijìzhōu (Běijìzhōu Cìshǐ).
Wáng Xuánmó, Grand Master of Glorious Happiness of the Right (Yòu Guānglù Dàfū), General of Chariots and Cavalry, and General Who Protects the Army, passed away.

On the *wùchén* day,

Bandits attacked Guǎngzhōu
and killed Inspector Yáng Xī.

the land revenue of commanderies and counties was again reduced by half.
〔二一〕On the day Bǐngshēn,
Liú Huī, Prince of Dōnghǎi, was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Lújiāng.
〔二二〕Liú Xiūyòu, Prince of Shānyáng, was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Jìnpíng.
Jìn'ān Commandery was renamed Jìnpíng Commandery.
On the day Xīnchǒu,
the Rúiruì state and the King of Hénán both sent envoys to present local products.
On the day Jiǎchén,
Zhāng Biàn, Administrator of Yùzhāng, was appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
In the fifth month, on the day Yǐsì,
〔二三〕a partial amnesty was granted in Guǎngzhōu.
On the day Guǐhài,
Liú Xiūruò, Prince of Bālíng, acting Inspector of Yōngzhōu, was appointed acting Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
Zhāng Yǒng, Administrator of Kuàijī, was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
Liú Yùn, Inspector of Xiāngzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu.

Wáng Kūn, Administrator of Wúqùn, was appointed Central Leader of the Army.

Liú Xí, Palace Attendant, was appointed Central Protector of the Army.

Liú Bó, Chancellor of Nánkāng, was appointed Inspector of Jiāozhōu.

〔二五〕On the day Dīngyǒu,
Wáng Jǐngwén, General Who Pacifies the South and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, was promoted to the title of General Who Guards the South.
In the ninth month, on the day Bǐngchén,
Zhāng Yuè, Chief Clerk to the General of Agile Cavalry, was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu.
On the day Wùchén,
an imperial edict stated:
“Offenses have degrees of severity,
and laws vary in leniency or strictness.
Thus, the five punishments are applied differently,
and the three codes are administered distinctly.
However, descending from major punishments to minor ones,
it extends even to branding and flogging.
If one seeks this in legal statutes,
the distinctions are far removed.
We are committed to reverence and compassion,
and frequently grant clemency.
Yet, upon examining the crimes of coercion and restraint,
〔二六〕their severity is equated with capital punishment,
which, when judging the facts and the intentions,
is not truly impartial.
From now on, regarding all cases of stealing official weapons,
resisting patrols and watchmen,
or attacking official posts and temples,
or harming officials and common people,
all these aforementioned categories
shall follow the old system.
For those who, being five persons or fewer, compel and rob,
a special grant of branding and amputation may be given,
and they shall be banished to the remote regions.
This shall substitute for execution,
which is superior to ancient practices.
It preserves lives for a long time,
and its application is like that of the Creator.
We hope that the benevolent transformation
will be trusted by all people,
and the virtue of cherishing life
will not overlook even the obscure.”
On the day Gēngwǔ,
a partial amnesty was granted in the four prefectures of Yáng, Nánxú, Yǎn, and Yù.
In winter, tenth month, on the first day Guǐyǒu,
there was a solar eclipse.
Troops from all prefectures were mobilized for a northern expedition.
The four commanderies of Nánkāng, Jiàn'ān, Ānchéng, and Xuānchéng,
having not collaborated with the southern rebels in the past,
were exempted from this levy.
On the day Jiǎxū,
Yìxīng Commandery of Yángzhōu was detached and assigned to Nánxúzhōu.
In the fifth year, spring, first month, on the day Guǐhài,
the imperial carriage personally plowed the sacrificial field.
A general amnesty was granted to the empire,
and those who diligently tilled the fields were bestowed one rank of nobility.
In the second month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Nányùzhōu was established by dividing Yùzhōu and Yángzhōu.
Liú Huī, Prince of Lújiāng and Grand Commandant, was appointed General of Chariots and Cavalry,
with the ceremonial privilege of establishing an official residence, and Inspector of Nányùzhōu.
In the third month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Nányìyáng Commandery was established in Nányùzhōu.
On the day Bǐngyín,
the imperial carriage visited the Central Hall to hear lawsuits.

the King of Hénán sent envoys to present local products.
In summer, fourth month, on the day Xīnwèi,

On the day Yǐyǒu,
Yìyáng Commandery of Yùzhōu was detached and assigned to Yǐngzhōu,
and Xīyáng Commandery of Yǐngzhōu was assigned to Yùzhōu.
On the day Wùzǐ,
Cuī Gōngliè, General Who Pacifies the North, was appointed Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
On the day Wùxū,
Dù Yǒuwén, newly appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Internal Service, was appointed Inspector of Liángzhōu and Nánqínzhōu.
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnwèi,
Liú Xuānyào, son of Liú Xiūyòu, Prince of Jìnpíng, was established as Prince of Nánpíng.
〔二七〕On the day Rénshēn,
Cài Xīngzōng, General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yǐngzhōu, was appointed General Who Guards the East.
On the day Guǐyǒu,
Shěn Yōuzhī, General of the Left Guard, was appointed Inspector of Yǐngzhōu.
Because of the ongoing military campaign,
officials’ salaries were suspended
and they were all given raw food instead.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Liú Huī, Prince of Lújiāng, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Inspector of Nányùzhōu, was stripped of his official post and noble rank.
On the day Wùyín,
Liú Xiūruò, Prince of Bālíng, General of the Left and acting Inspector of Xiāngzhōu, was appointed General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
On the day Rénwǔ,
Nányùzhōu was abolished.
On the day Bǐngxū,
Liú Liàng, newly appointed Gentleman of the Yellow Gate for Internal Service, was appointed Inspector of Yìzhōu.
In autumn, seventh month, on the day Jǐyǒu,
Wáng Liàng, General Who Assists the State, was appointed Inspector of Xúzhōu.
Chén Bóshào, Administrator of Dōngguǎn, was appointed Inspector of Jiāozhōu.
On the day Jiǎyín,
Lǐ Língqiān, Administrator of Shānyáng, was appointed Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
On the day Rénxū,
the title General Who Assists the State was changed to General Who Assists the Army.
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Liú Miǎn, General of the Right and acting Inspector of Yùzhōu, was appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yùzhōu.
On the day Rénchén,
Liú Chóngzhì, Administrator of Hǎilíng, was appointed Inspector of Jìzhōu.
In the ninth month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Liú Yánzhī, son of Liú Zuǎn, Prince of Chángshā, was established as Prince of Shǐpíng.
On the day Wùwǔ,
Wáng Kūn, Central Leader of the Army, was transferred from his post.
On the day Jǐwèi,
an imperial edict stated:
“The integrity of Jī and Yǐng
has been esteemed since antiquity;
the purity and simplicity of their conduct
were highly regarded by sagacious kings.
We have faced times of widespread turmoil
and encountered an era of difficulty and obscurity.
In suppressing the violent and quelling the chaos,
we have been ceaselessly occupied.
Although today Guān and Lǒng are still hazy,
and the various districts and counties are troubled by disturbances,
the time for sheathing weapons and cultivating culture
is now upon us.
We contemplate upholding integrity and modesty,
to quiet the prevalent frivolity,
and have already contemplated this with sincere heart,
pondering it whether sleeping or waking.
Therefore, those who lead chaste and reclusive lives,
settling affairs in their humble abodes,
〔二八〕abandoning worldly honors like breaking a pot,
refusing appointments like a recluse who fishes,
whose ambition is at peace with rivers and seas,
and whose conduct is superior to the common world—
these individuals should be meticulously sought out in every place,
and their names reported in due course.
We shall honor their virtue in their gardens
and grandly manifest our courtesy towards them.
All officials should recommend those they know,
and bestow titles upon them in a timely manner.”
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Liú Miǎn, newly appointed General Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yùzhōu, was appointed Central Leader of the Army.
In winter, tenth month, on the first day Dīngmǎo,
there was a solar eclipse.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngwèi,
the Suǒlǔ sent envoys to present local products.
In the intercalary month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Liú Xiūyòu, Prince of Jìnpíng, General-in-Chief of Agile Cavalry and Inspector of Jīngzhōu, was appointed Inspector of Nánxúzhōu with his existing title.
Liú Xiūruò, Prince of Bālíng, General Who Conquers the South and Inspector of Xiāngzhōu, was appointed General Who Conquers the West and Inspector of Jīngzhōu.
Mèng Cìyáng, General Who Assists the Army, was appointed Inspector of Yǎnzhōu.
〔二九〕Lǚ Ānguó, Administrator of Yìyáng, was appointed Inspector of Sīzhōu.
In the twelfth month, on the day Wùxū,
Liú Xiūrén, Prince of Jiàn'ān and Grand Minister of Works, was relieved of his post as Inspector of Yángzhōu.
On the day Jǐwèi,

Liú Xiūfàn, Prince of Guìyáng, General-in-Chief Who Conquers the North and Inspector of Nánxúzhōu, was appointed Supervisor of the Central Secretariat, General of the Central Army, and Inspector of Yángzhōu.
〔三０〕Liú Jǐngsù, Prince of Jiànpíng and Administrator of Wúxīng, was appointed Inspector of Xiāngzhōu.
Bó Róng, Heir Apparent to the Prince of Jiàn'ān and General Who Assists the Army, was appointed Inspector of Guǎngzhōu.
〔三一〕On the day Gēngshēn,
the Three Bā Commandery Commandant was established by dividing five commanderies from Jīngzhōu and Yìzhōu.
In the sixth year, spring, first month, on the day Yǐhài,
it was initially decreed that sacrifices to the southern suburbs should be performed once every two years,
and sacrifices to the Míngtáng once every year.

An imperial edict stated:
"Since I ascended the throne over the countless people,

Although I have always sought to promote virtuous transformation,

the army and state are depleted,
and punishments and lawsuits have not ceased.
Now, my illness is critical and dangerous,
causing me deep sorrow and lamentation.
Corvée labor should be eased and taxes reduced,
and excessive regulations abolished in favor of simplicity.
Regarding necessary reforms,
a detailed and appropriate plan should be chosen.
It is imperative to prioritize loving the people,
to fulfill my dying wish."
Yuán Càn, Chǔ Yuān, Liú Miǎn, Cài Xīngzōng, and Shěn Yōuzhī jointly received the dying imperial command.

When he ascended the great throne,

After pacifying the empire,

those who possessed talent

The historiographer remarks: When sages establish laws and promulgate regulations,

for the enduring legacy of their teachings and customs

Tàizǔ (Emperor Wǔ of Sòng) faced south from behind the screen,
truly possessing the virtue of a ruler;
though his principles for governing the state were grand,

Péngchéng Wáng Zhào did not look to antiquity,

Although the gravity of familial bonds

As for changing clothes and going out,

Tàizōng (Emperor Míng of Sòng), taking advantage of the ready-made rifts in sentiment,

pruned the flourishing branches,

Consequently, without protection for the root,

The imperial regalia, weakened by circumstance, shifted,

This is like treading on frost, which gradually
leads to solid ice,

ANNALS NINE: THE LATER DEPOSED EMPEROR
The deposed Emperor's taboo name was Yù,
his courtesy name DéRóng,
and his childhood name Hùizhèn,
he was Emperor Míng's eldest son.
On the Xīnchǒu day of the first month of the seventh year of Dàmíng,
he was born in the residence of the Wèiwèi.
When Tàizōng's sons were in the womb,
all were divined using the *Zhōu Yì*,
and their childhood names were taken from the hexagrams obtained.
Thus, the Emperor's childhood name was Hùizhèn,
and other imperial princes were likewise named.
In the second year of Tàishǐ,
he was established as the Crown Prince.

it was first decreed that the Crown Prince's given name be changed to Yù.
He rode in an Ānchē (comfort carriage) drawn by elephants.

On the *rénchén* day of the sixth month,
an edict stated:
"The establishment of regulations by a prospering monarch
must truly prioritize the people's hidden concerns,
and in seeking to broadly teach and instruct,
set an example for the four quarters.
I, being young and insignificant,
received the imperial mandate early.
When I consider the governance of the people,
I have not yet fully engaged in listening and observing.
I look upon my realm with care,
never forgetting to reflect upon it in my sleep.
Therefore, grand envoys may be dispatched to travel to the four directions,
to observe and collect popular ballads,
and inquire into the people's hardships and suffering.
If there are matters that displease the people,
or laws that are inconvenient to customs,
they should all be reported in detail.
If governors and magistrates are noteworthy for their prestige and kindness,
and truly distinguished by their integrity and diligence,
they should be reported according to the facts.
If there are false accusations in legal cases,
or errors in official duties,
or idleness in public service for private gain,
or actions that harm the people for personal benefit,
none should be concealed or obscured.
Broadly accept the opinions of commoners,
and widely seek proposals from those with skills.
The path of inspection
must be thorough and meticulous,
and those with deep insight and experience should be carefully selected,
so that it is as if I personally observe it."
Another edict stated:
"Seeking worthy individuals through dreams
is a beautiful tradition from ancient edicts.
Searching for good people through observation
is highly praised in former writings.
I, being young and ignorant,
succeeded to the imperial task,
and aspire to follow the sagely path,
striving to promote the way of governance.
Speaking of the many scholars,
I constantly hope to find the right people.
Therefore, a general order may be issued to all provincial governors and magistrates,
to broadly search and gather.
Those who are known for filial piety and fraternity in their clans,
or whose righteousness and humility illuminate their communities,
or who conceal themselves as butchers or fishermen,
or hide their identities as farmers or herdsmen,
who are sufficient to rectify corrupt customs,
and assist in the flourishing of pure transformation—
of all their good deeds,
none should be left out.
My carriage awaits with empty wheels,
awaiting news of their excellent recommendations."
