In this month,
Chéngdū and Héjiān issued a proclamation to Chángshāwáng to attack him.
Jǐng and they engaged in battle,
attacking and burning the palaces.
Jǐng's army was defeated and annihilated,
and his elder brother, the Shàngjūn Jiāngjūn Shí, and over twenty others were also killed.
In the second year of Tàiaān,
Chéngdū attacked Chángshā.
At this time, both public and private sectors suffered from hunger and hardship,
and the common people's strength was exhausted.
In the second month of the second year of Tàiaān of Jìn Huìdì,
Táibái (Venus) entered Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"The empire will be disturbed,
and great wars will break out."
In the third month,
a comet was seen in the east,
pointing at Sāntái.
The prognostication said:
"This is an omen of war and death.
Sāntái represents the Sāngōng."
In the seventh month,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"War will break out and the state will be in chaos."
This autumn,
Táibái (Venus) guarded Tàiwēi Shàngjiàng.
The prognostication said:
"The Shàngjiàng will perish by war."
In the winter of this year,
Chéngdū and Héjiān attacked Luòyáng.
In the first month of the third year,
Dōnghǎiwáng Yuè arrested Chángshāwáng,
and Zhāng Fāng then killed him.
In the eighth month of the second year of Tàiaān,
Chángshāwáng, escorting the Emperor, went out to resist the two princes.

they stayed at Xuánwǔguǎn.
On this day, the sky in the middle split into two,
with a sound like thunder.
Three omens were the same as those in Yuánkāng,
an omen of ministers monopolizing power and usurping authority.
At this time, Chángshāwáng wielded autocratic power.
Later, Chéngdū, Héjiān, and Dōnghǎi successively monopolized authority and issued commands.

In the eleventh month, on the day Xīnsì, of the second year of Tàiaān,

According to the prognostication,
"It is called Yíngshǒu.

The next year,

Wáng Jùn raised an army in Yān and Dài,

In the eleventh month, on the day Gēngchén, of the second year of Tàiaān,

Wáng Jùn killed Yōuzhōu Cìshǐ Hé Yǎn,

Chén Mǐn also caused chaos in Yángtǔ.
Liú Yuān, Shí Lè, Lǐ Xióng, and others rose from humble origins,

Empress Yángshì was repeatedly imprisoned and deposed.
In the first year of Guāngxī,
Huìdì died,
ultimately without an heir.
In the seventh month, on the *yǐchǒu* day of the first year of Yǒngxīng,
stars fell with sound.
In the tenth month of the second year,
stars again fell with sound.
According to Liú Xiàng's explanation,
this is an omen of the people abandoning their land.
After this, Zhōngxià was eventually lost.
On the *rén yín* night of the twelfth month of the first year of Yǒngxīng,
a red *qì* stretched across the sky,
with a rumbling sound.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the tenth month of the second year,
a red *qì* appeared in the north,
extending across the sky from east to west.
The prognostication stated:
"Both foretell great war.
The rumbling sound
is an omen of anger."
After this, the Four Seas were in turmoil,
and the Nine Provinces engaged in battle.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day of the fourth month of the second year of Yǒngxīng,
Tàibái transgressed the Lángxīng (Sirius).
The prognostication stated:
"Great war will arise."
In the ninth month,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) guarded Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be war.
Jǐng also corresponds to Qín territory."
In this year,
Gǒu Xī defeated Gōng Shīfān,
Zhāng Fāng defeated Fányáng Wáng Xiāo,
the generals west of the pass attacked Héjiān Wáng Yōng.
Yōng fled,
and the Dōnghǎi Wáng met and killed him.
In the eighth month of the second year of Yǒngxīng,
a comet appeared in Mǎo and Bì.
The prognostication stated:
"This signifies war and mourning."
Mǎo and Bì
also correspond to Zhào and Wèi territory.
On the *dīngchǒu* day of the tenth month,
a comet appeared in the Běidǒu (Big Dipper).
The prognostication stated:
"The Xúanjī will change hands,
and the Son of Heaven will flee."
It also said:
"Strong nations will raise armies,
and feudal lords will contend for power."
After this, all these things came to pass.
The following year,
Huìdì died.
In the fourth month of the first year of Guāngxī of Jìn Huìdì,
Tàibái deviated from its course,
moving from Yì into Wěi and Jī.
The prognostication stated:
"When Tàibái deviates from its course and goes north,
this is called 'returning to life.'
If there is no army destroyed,
there will surely be a city massacred."
In the fifth month,
Jí Sāng attacked Yè.
Wèijùn Tàishǒu Féng Sōng went out to battle and was greatly defeated.
Sāng then harmed Dōngyàn Wáng Téng,
killing over ten thousand people,
and completely burned down the palaces and temples of the Wèi period.
In the fifth month of the first year of Guāngxī,
a shooting star flowed southwest.
The prognostication stated:
"This is an omen of using disorder to suppress disorder."
At this time, Sīmǎ Yuè defeated Héjiān in the west,
and welcomed the imperial carriage.
Soon after, he arrested Miào Yìn, Hé Suí, and others,
displaying his disloyal intentions;
the world detested him.
After his death, Shí Lè burned his corpse and coffin,
which was the fulfillment of this omen.
On the *dīngwèi* day of the ninth month of the first year of Guāngxī,
Yínghuò (Mars) guarded Xīn.
The prognostication stated:
"The king will be displeased by this."
On the *jǐhài* day,
Tiánxīng (Saturn) guarded Fáng and Xīn,
and also transgressed Suìxīng (Jupiter).
The prognostication stated:
"When Tǔ guards Fáng,
there will be many disasters and deaths.
Guarding Xīn,
there will be domestic turmoil,
and a general amnesty for the realm."
It also said:
"Tián and Suì combining signifies internal strife."
At this time, Sīmǎ Yuè held power,
and eventually perished due to his impropriety,
which was the fulfillment of the omen of internal strife.
In the eleventh month,
Huìdì died,
Huáidì ascended the throne,
and a general amnesty was granted to the realm.
On the *guǐwèi* day of the twelfth month of the first year of Guāngxī,
Tàibái transgressed Tiánxīng (Saturn).
The prognostication stated:
"This signifies internal warfare,
and a great battle."
After this, Héjiān Wáng was killed by Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè.
In the following January,
Dōnghǎi Wáng Yuè killed Zhūgě Méi and others.
In the fifth month,
Jí Sāng defeated Féng Sōng
and killed Dōngyàn Wáng.
In the eighth month,
Gǒu Xī greatly defeated Jí Sāng.
On the *jiǎshēn* day of the twelfth month of the first year of Guāngxī,
a white *qì* like a rainbow,
descended from the center of the sky to the north, reaching the ground.
It was seen for five nights before disappearing.
The prognostication stated:
"Great war will arise."
The following year,
Wáng Mí rose up in Qīng and Xú,
Jí Sāng brought chaos to Héběi,
and poison spread throughout the realm.
On the *xīnhài* day of the ninth month of the first year of Yǒngjiā of Xiàohuáidì,
a large star flowed from southwest to northeast,
with smaller ones like a *shēng* following it.
The sky was entirely red,
and there was a sound like thunder.
The prognostication stated:
"A flowing star signifies noble envoys."
In the fifth month of this year,
Jí Sāng killed Dōngyàn Wáng Téng,
and then occupied Héběi.
In the eleventh month,
Hé Yù was first sent as Zhēngběi Jiāngjūn to garrison Yè.
However, Tián Zhēn and others greatly defeated Jí Sāng,
and beheaded him in Lèlíng.
Therefore, Zhēn was made Jíjùn Tàishǒu,
and his younger brother Lán was made Jùlù Tàishǒu.
The smaller stars following
were an omen of minor generals and separate commanders.
Sīmǎ Yuè was indignant that the area east of Wèijùn
and south of Píngyuán
all sided with Sāng,
and he awarded it all to Zhēn and others.
Thus, there was aggression and devastation of the land.
The sound like thunder
was an omen of anger.
On the *dīnghài* day of the twelfth month of the first year of Yǒngjiā,
stars flowed and scattered with a tremor.
According to Liú Xiàng's explanation:
"The celestial officials and arrayed constellations
are omens of those in high positions,
while the nameless small stars
are akin to the common people.
This is an omen that officials and common people will be scattered and dispersed."
After this, the world was in great chaos,
officials and countless common people
were displaced, moved, and died.
On the *gēngwǔ* day of the first month of the second year of Yǒngjiā,
Tàibái was hidden and not seen.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the second month,
it was first seen in the east at dawn.
This means it was supposed to be seen but wasn't,
the prognostication is the same as the previous entry.
Afterward, armies were shattered and generals were killed,
beyond counting.
The emperor died in a barbarian court,
and Zhōngxià was overthrown.
On the *gēngzǐ* day of the first month of the third year of Yǒngjiā,
Yínghuò (Mars) transgressed Zǐwēi.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be a king who dies in the wilderness.
It also means the palace will be burned by fire."
At this time, Tàishǐlìng Gāotáng Chōng reported
that the imperial carriage should move to another auspicious location,
otherwise Luòyáng would surely be lost.
In the sixth month of the fifth year,
Liú Yào and Wáng Mí entered the capital,
burned the palaces and ancestral temples,
and the emperor died in Píngyáng.
In the third year of Yǒngjiā,
Zhènxīng (Saturn) long guarded Nándǒu.
The prognostication stated:
"Where Zhènxīng resides,
that country will have good fortune."
At this time, Āndōng Lángxié Wáng first gained control of Yángtǔ.
In the eleventh month of that year,
there was an earthquake,
Chén Zhuó considered this to be the fulfillment of the earthquake omen.
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐhài* day of the third year of Yǒngjiā,
there were four white streaks like ribbons, two each emerging from the north and south directions,
rising from the ground to the sky,
piercing Cān and Fá.
The prognostication said:
"Great wars will arise under Heaven."
In the third month of the fourth year,
Sīmǎ Yuè arrested Miào Yìn, Miào Bō, and others;
moreover, the three regions were thrown into chaos,
with incessant attacks and battles.
In the third month of the fifth year,
Sīmǎ Yuè died at Níngpíng Chéng.
Shí Lè attacked and defeated his forces,
with over one hundred thousand dead.
In the sixth month,
the capital was burned and destroyed,
and the Emperor was captured and taken to the barbarian court.
In the tenth month of the fifth year of Yǒngjiā,
Yínghuò guarded Xīn.
Two years later,
the Emperor passed away in the barbarian court.
In the seventh month of the sixth year of Yǒngjiā,
Yínghuò, Suìxīng, Zhènxīng, and Tàibái gathered between Niú and Nǚ,
hesitating and moving back and forth.
According to the prognostication, it said:
"Niú
is the division of Yángzhōu."
After this, both capitals were overthrown,
but Yuán Dì restored the dynasty in the lands of Yángzhōu,
which was the fulfillment of this omen.
In the fifth month, on the *guǐwèi* day of the first year of Jiànwǔ of Mǐn Dì,
Tàibái and Yínghuò conjoined in Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"When metal and fire conjoin, it is called 'shuò,'
and signifies mourning."
At this time, although the Emperor was captured in Píngyáng,
the empire still did not dare to occupy his vacant position,
and the calamity fell upon the Emperor.
In the sixth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Tàibái trespassed on Tàiwēi.
The prognostication said:
"Soldiers will enter the Son of Heaven's court,
and the ruler will suffer misfortune."
In the seventh month,
Mǐn Dì passed away in the rebel court,
and the empire observed mourning and great lamentation.
In the seventh month of the first year of Tàixīng of Jìn Yuán Dì,
Tàibái trespassed on Nándǒu.
The prognostication said:
"There will be war in Wú and Yuè,
and great men will worry."
In the second month, on the *jiǎshēn* day of the second year,
Yínghuò trespassed on Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"War will arise,
and noble officials will slay each other."
In the eighth month, on the *jǐmǎo* day,
Tàibái trespassed on the great star Xuānyuán.
The prognostication said:
"The empress's palace will have worries."
On the *yǐwèi* day,
Tàibái trespassed on Suìxīng,
in Yì.
The prognostication said:
"This signifies military unrest."
In the fourth month, on the *rénchén* day of the third year,
a shooting star emerged from Xū and Wēi,
disappearing into Yì and Zhěn.
The prognostication said:
"Where the shooting star touches,
the empire will attack.
Yì and Zhěn
are the division of Jīngzhōu."
In the fifth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
Tàibái entered Tàiwēi,
and also trespassed on Shàngjiāng.
The prognostication said:
"The Son of Heaven will personally lead,
and the commander-in-chief will be executed."
In the sixth month, on the *bǐngchén* day,
Tàibái conjoined with Suìxīng in Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"This signifies war and famine."
In the ninth month,
Tàibái trespassed on Nándǒu,
the prognostication being the same as in the first year.
In the tenth month, on the *jǐhài* day,
Yínghuò was in Dōngjǐng,
south of Wǔzhūhóu,
lingering and stopping,
for thirty days.
The prognostication said:
"If Yínghuò guards Jǐng for more than twenty days,
great men will worry;
if it guards Wǔzhūhóu,
there will be princes executed."
In the twelfth month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
Tàibái entered the Moon,
in Dǒu.
Guō Jǐngchún said:
"The Moon belongs to Kǎn,
the symbolic image of the underworld.
Tàibái, representing the Metal element, comes to transgress it,
meaning that Heaven's will is as if the administration of justice is out of balance,
destroying its own laws."
In the twelfth month, on the *dīnghài* day of the fourth year,
the Moon trespassed on Suìxīng in Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"That state will suffer war and famine,
and the people will flee."
In the third month of the first year of Yǒngchāng,
Wáng Dūn led the forces of Jiāng and Jīng
to attack the capital.
The six armies resisted in battle,
and were defeated.
Thereupon, Grand Protector-General Zhōu Yǐ and Grand Secretary Diāo Xié were killed,
and Cavalry General Liú Wèi fled.
In the fourth month,
Xiāngzhōu Inspector Qiáo Wáng Chéng and General Who Guards the South Gān Zhuó were also killed.
In the intercalary twelfth month,
Yuán Dì passed away.
A year later,
Dūn was also destroyed,
which was the fulfillment of the shooting star touching Yì.
In the tenth month,
Shí Tā entered Yùzhōu,
plundering the people of Chéngfù and Zhì counties and taking them north.
Inspector Zǔ Yuē dispatched an army to pursue them,
but it was wiped out by them,
and so Zǔ Yuē retreated and guarded Shòuchūn.
In the first month of the third year of Tàiníng of Míng Dì,
Yínghuò moved retrograde and entered Tàiwēi.
The prognostication said:
"This signifies war and mourning,
and the ruler will suffer misfortune."
In the intercalary eighth month,
the Emperor passed away.
In the second year of Xiánhé,
Sū Jùn rebelled,
attacking the palace.
The Empress Dowager died from grief and distress,
and the Son of Heaven was imprisoned and kidnapped at Shítóu.
There was war and unrest far and near,
which ceased only in the fourth year.
In the seventh month of the fourth year of Xiánhé of Chéng Dì,
a comet appeared in the northwest,
and extinguished after twenty-three days.
The prognostication said:
"This signifies military unrest."
In the twelfth month,
Guō Mò killed Jiāngzhōu Inspector Liú Yìn.
Jīngzhōu Inspector Táo Kǎn campaigned against Mò,
and the following year,
beheaded him.
At this time, Shí Lè also first usurped the title.
In the first month, on the *bǐngchén* day of the sixth year of Xiánhé,
the Moon entered Nándǒu.
The prognostication said:
"There will be war."
One interpretation said:
"There will be a great amnesty."
In this month, Hu bandits killed and plundered the people of Lóu and Wǔjìn counties.
Thereupon, garrisons were dispatched to the central islands.
The following year,
Hu bandits again plundered the people of Nánshā and Hǎiyú.
In the first month of this year,
there was a great amnesty,
an expedition against Huáinán,
and an attack on Xiāngyáng,
which was pacified.
In the eleventh month of the sixth year of Xiánhé,
Yínghuò guarded Wèi and Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"There will be war in Zhào and Wèi."
In the seventh month of the eighth year,
Shí Lè died,
and Shí Hǔ enthroned himself,
causing widespread destruction.
At this time, although Lè and Hǔ usurped titles,
their strength and weakness were always prognosticated from Mǎo,
and did not concern Tàiwēi Zǐgōng.
In the third month, on the *jǐsì* day of the eighth year of Xiánhé,
the Moon entered Nándǒu,
the prognostication being the same as in the sixth year.
In the seventh month of that year,
Shí Lè died,
Péng Biāo with Qiáo,
Shí Shēng with Cháng'ān,
and Guō Quán with Qínzhōu,
all submitted.
Thereupon, Inspector Gāo Qiú was dispatched to lead troops to rescue Biāo,
but Biāo was defeated and Qiú retreated.
Moreover, Shí Hǔ and Shí Bīn attacked and destroyed Shēng and Quán.
In the first month of the first year of Xiánkāng,
there was a great amnesty.
In the seventh month of the eighth year of Xiánhé,
Yínghuò entered Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"The Hú king will die."
Shí Hǔ conquered and destroyed many.
In the eighth month,
the moon encroached upon Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"The Hú will be uneasy."
In the sixth month of the ninth year,
the moon again encroached upon Mǎo.
At this time, although Shí Hóng succeeded to Lè's position,
Shí Hǔ wielded power and acted tyrannically.
In the tenth month,
he deposed Hóng and established himself,
then imprisoned and killed him.
On the Jǐhài day of the third month of the ninth year of Xiánhé,
Yínghuò entered Yúguǐ,
encroaching upon Jīshī.
The prognostication said:
"There will be troops in the northwest;
armies will be lost and generals will die."
In the fourth month,
Guō Quán, General Who Guards the West and Inspector of Yōngzhōu, first returned Qínzhōu to the fold,
but was soon annihilated by Shí Bīn,
and his people were relocated to Qīng and Xú.
On the Jǐhài day of the second month of the first year of Xiánkāng of Emperor Chéng of Jìn,
Tàibái encroached upon Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"War will break out,
and there will be a great drought this year."
In the fourth month,
Shí Hǔ's raiding cavalry reached Lìyáng.
The imperial court, fearing his forces,
promoted Sītú Wáng Dǎo to Dàsīmǎ,
mobilized troops and prepared for war.
They also dispatched garrisons to Cíhú, Niúzhǔ, and Wúhú.
In the fifth month, the alert was finally lifted.
At this time, the Hú bandits also besieged Xiāngyáng,
and Zhēngxī Jiāngjūn Yǔ Liàng sent Níngjù to repel them.
In the sixth month,
there was a drought.
On the Wùxū day of the eighth month of the first year of Xiánkāng,
Yínghuò entered Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"If there are no troops, troops will arise;
if there are troops, troops will cease."
In the summer of this year,
troops were raised and stationed as garrisons.
Wáng Dǎo was promoted to Dàsīmǎ
to guard against the Hú bandits.
On the Bǐngxū day of the third month of the first year of Xiánkāng,
the moon entered Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"The Hú king will die."
In the eleventh month,
the moon encroached upon Mǎo.
In the eighth month of the second year,
the moon again encroached upon Mǎo.
The prognostication was the same.
In the third year of Xiánhé,
Shí Hǔ dispatched seventy thousand troops.
In the second month of the fourth year,
he personally attacked Duàn Liáo at Jì,
and Liáo was defeated and fled.
He then attacked Mùróng Huǎng at Jíchéng,
but failed to overcome him and retreated.
Huǎng pursued him,
killing several hundred men.
Hǔ left his general Má Qiū to garrison Língzhī.
Huǎng defeated Qiū
and captured and killed Liáo.
On the Xīnsì day of the first month of the second year of Xiánkāng,
a comet was seen in the west at dusk,
in Kuí.
The prognostication said:
"This signifies war and mourning.
Kuí also represents border troops."
In the fourth year,
Shí Hǔ attacked Mùróng Huǎng but failed to overcome him.
Huǎng pursued and attacked him,
and again defeated Má Qiū.
At this time, Huǎng claimed vassalage,
which was the fulfillment of the "border troops" omen.
On the Xīnmǎo day of the first month of the second year of Xiánkāng,
the moon encroached upon the second star south of Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"Prime ministers and generals will have worries."
In the seventh month of the fifth year,
Prime Minister Wáng Dǎo died.
In the eighth month,
Grand Commandant Xī Jiàn died.
In the first month of the sixth year,
General-in-Chief Who Guards the West Yǔ Liàng died.
On the Gēngyín day of the ninth month of the second year of Xiánkāng,
Tàibái encroached upon Nándǒu,
and was seen during the day.
The prognostication said:
"Dǒu represents the prime minister and
also the division of Yángzhōu;
when Jīn encroaches upon it,
it symbolizes death and mourning.
Being seen during the day signifies disloyalty to the sovereign,
and also war and mourning."
In the third year,
Shí Hǔ usurped the title of Heavenly King.
In the fourth year,
Hǔ annihilated Duàn Liáo but was defeated by Mùróng Huǎng.
Huǎng
was a vassal of the state.
In the fifth year,
Wáng Dǎo died.
On the Xīnwèi day of the sixth month of the third year of Xiánkāng,
a meteor as large as two dòu kuí,
blue in color,
with a red glow illuminating the ground,
emerged from Kuí
and disappeared north of Lóu.
According to the prognostication, this signifies famine,
and that the five grains will not be stored.
In this month,
there was a great drought.
In the eighth month of the third year of Xiánkāng,
Yínghuò entered Yúguǐ,
encroaching upon Jīshī.
The prognostication said:
"Noble persons will have worries."
On the Jiǎxū day of the eighth month of the third year,
the moon encroached upon the Jù star of Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"The state will have worries,
and a general will die."
On the Wùzǐ day of the ninth month of the third year,
the moon encroached upon Jiànxīng.
The prognostication said:
"The prime minister will be replaced."
Another interpretation said:
"A great general will die."
In the fifth year,
Prime Minister Wáng Dǎo died,
and Yǔ Bīng took over as regent.
Grand Commandant Xī Jiàn and General-in-Chief Who Guards the West Yǔ Liàng died.
On the Yǐchǒu day of the eleventh month of the third year of Xiánkāng,
Tàibái encroached upon Suìxīng.
The prognostication said:
"This signifies war and famine."
In the second month of the fourth year,
Shí Hǔ conquered Yōuzhōu,
relocating over ten thousand households.
Lǐ Shòu killed Lǐ Qī.
In the fifth year,
fifty thousand Hú troops invaded Miǎnnán,
plundering over seven thousand households before leaving.
Twenty thousand cavalry also besieged and captured Zhūchéng,
killing and plundering over five thousand people.
On the Jǐsì day of the fourth month of the fourth year of Xiánkāng,
Tàibái was seen during the day in Liǔ.
The prognostication said:
"This signifies war
and disloyalty to the sovereign."
On the Yǐsì day of the seventh month,
the moon occulted Tàibái.
The prognostication said:
"The king will lose territory,
and a great war will break out."
The following year,
the Hú bandits greatly invaded Miǎnnán,
capturing Zhūchéng.
Máo Bǎo, Inspector of Yùzhōu, and Fán Jùn, Administrator of Xīyáng, both abandoned their cities and died by throwing themselves into the river.
Thereupon, martial law was declared internally and externally,
and the various armies of Zuǒwèi Huán Jiān and Kuāng Shù reached Wǔchāng,
then retreated.
In the seventh year,
Mùróng Huǎng proclaimed himself King of Yàn.
On the Wùwǔ day of the fifth month of the fourth year of Xiánkāng,
Yínghuò encroached upon the Right Executive star.
The prognostication said:
"Ministers will die,
and those in power will have worries."
In the ninth month,
Tàibái encroached upon the Right Executive star.
According to the prognostication,
"When the five planets are inauspicious together,
Jīn and Huǒ are especially severe."
On the Wùzǐ day of the eleventh month,
Tàibái encroached upon the Upper star of Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"The Prime Minister will have worries."
On the Jǐyǒu day of the seventh month of the fifth year,
the moon encroached upon the Upper star of Fáng,
with the same prognostication.
On the Gēngshēn day of this month,
Prime Minister Wáng Dǎo died.
In the fifth year of Xiánkāng, in the fourth month, on the day Xīnwèi
the moon trespassed on Suìxīng
The prognostication said:
"The nation will suffer famine and the people will flee."
On the day Yǐwèi,
the moon trespassed on Bìjùxīng.
The prognostication said:
"War will arise."
That night,
the moon again trespassed on Suìxīng
in Mǎo.
When winter came,
there was the defeat at Miànnán and Zhūchéng,
and over ten thousand households of common people fled.
In the sixth year of Xiánkāng, in the second month, on the Gēngwǔ new moon,
a shooting star as large as a dipper,
its light illuminating the ground,
emerged from Tiānshì
and traveled west into Tàiwēi.
The prognostication said:
"Great men will be affected."
On the day Yǐwèi,
Tàibái entered the moon.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler will die."
In the fourth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the moon trespassed on Tàibái.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler is troubled by this."
In the eighth year, in the sixth month,
Emperor Chéng died.
In the sixth year of Xiánkāng, in the third month, on the day Jiǎyín,
Yínghuò, following its course, trespassed on Tàiwēi Shàngjiàngxīng.
The prognostication said:
"The supreme general is troubled."
In the fourth month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Yínghuò trespassed on Yòuzhífǎ.
The prognostication said:
"The law enforcer is troubled."
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐhài,
the moon trespassed on the central star of Qiānniú.
The prognostication said:
"The great general is troubled."
At that time, the Shàngshūlìng Hé Chōng was the law enforcer.
Having been reproached, he wished to avoid the blame,
so the following year,
he requested to become Zhōngshūlìng.
In the second year of Jiànyuán,
Yú Bīng died.
All these were responses to the great generals being in power.
In the first month of that year,
the General who Conquers the West, Yú Liàng, died.
In the third month,
Yínghuò trespassed on Shàngjiàng.
In the ninth month,
Shí Hǔ's great general Kuí Ān died.
Yú Bīng died many years later.
Could it be that Yú Bīng was able to cultivate virtue
and transfer the misfortune to Kuí Ān?
In the sixth year of Xiánkāng, in the fourth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
Tàibái trespassed on Bìjùxīng.
The prognostication said:
"War will arise."
Another interpretation said:
"The empress is troubled."
In the sixth month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Tàibái trespassed on Xuānyuán Dàxīng.
The prognostication said:
"The empress is troubled."
In the seventh year, in the third month,
Empress Dù died.
In the seventh year of Xiánkāng, in the third month, on the day Rénwǔ,
the moon trespassed on Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"Generals and chancellors are troubled."
In the eighth year, in the sixth month,
Yínghuò trespassed on the second star above Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"The junior chancellor is troubled."
In the second year of Jiànyuán,
the General of Cavalry and Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, Yú Bīng, died.
At this time, the General of Agile Cavalry, Hé Chōng, was in the court,
and Yú Bīng was the junior chancellor.
In the seventh year of Xiánkāng, in the fourth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Tàibái entered Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"War will arise."
In the fifth month,
Tàibái was seen during the day.
Judging by its altitude,
it was either Qín or Wèi,
or Chǔ.
The prognostication said:
"Ministers will be strong,
and there will be soldiers."
In the eighth month, on the day Xīncǎo,
the moon trespassed on Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler is troubled."
In the eighth year, in the sixth month,
Emperor Chéng died.
In the eighth year of Xiánkāng, in the eighth month, on the day Rén'yín,
the moon trespassed on Bìchìxīng.
The prognostication said:
"Inferiors will transgress against superiors,
and war will arise."
In the tenth month,
the moon again obscured Bìchìxīng.
The prognostication was the same.
On the day Jǐyǒu,
Tàibái trespassed on Yínghuò.
The prognostication said:
"Great war will arise."
Afterward, Yú Yì raised a large army, planning to attack the Hú,
and exclusively controlled the upstream region,
which the imperial court feared.
In the first year of Jiànyuán of Emperor Kāng, in the first month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Tàibái entered Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"There will be war in the land of Zhào."
It also said:
"War will arise throughout the world."
In the fourth month, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Tàibái was seen during the day.
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngwèi,
Tàibái trespassed on Suìxīng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be great war."
In this year,
Shí Hǔ killed his crown prince Suì and his wife and children and over two hundred retainers.
He also dispatched General Liú Níng to plunder and seize Dí Dào.
He also sent General Zhāng Jǔ with over ten thousand men to garrison Jìdōng,
planning against Mùróng Huàng.
On the sixth day of the eleventh month of the first year of Jiànyuán,
a comet appeared in Kàng,
seven *chǐ* long,
with a white tail.
The prognostication said:
"Kàng represents the imperial court,
and presages military losses."
In the ninth month of the second year,
Emperor Kāng died.
In the first year of Jiànyuán,
Suìxīng trespassed on Tiānguān.
General of the West-Pacifying Army, Yú Yì, wrote to his elder brother Yú Bīng, saying:
"Suìxīng trespassed on Tiānguān.
The prognostication says: 'Passes and bridges will be obstructed.'
Recently, there have been no other incidents in Jiāngdōng,
and the river route is also not difficult;
but Shí Hǔ has repeatedly closed the passes and stopped communication for two years.
This is a sign that 'Heavenly Duke is confused and without discernment.'"
In the intercalary month of the second year of Jiànyuán, on the day Yǐyǒu,
Tàibái trespassed on Dòu.
The prognostication said:
"There will be mourning,
and the empire will receive titles and emoluments."
In the ninth month,
Emperor Kāng died,
the crown prince was enthroned,
and there was a grand amnesty and bestowal of titles.
In the first year of the Yǒnghé reign of Emperor Mù of Jìn, on the Dīngchǒu day of the first month,
the Moon entered Bì.
The prognostication stated:
"A great war will arise."
On the Wùyín day,
the Moon trespassed against Tiānguān.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be rebellious ministers who alter the laws of the Son of Heaven."
In the fifth month, on the Xīnsì day,
Tàibái was visible in daylight,
in Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication stated:
"Ministers will be powerful,
and Qín will have troops."
In the sixth month, on the Xīnchǒu day,
it entered Tàiwēi,
trespassing against the southwest of the Screen.
The prognostication stated:
"An assisting minister will be dismissed or retired."
In the seventh and eighth months,
the Moon again trespassed against Bì.
The prognostication was the same as in the first month.
On the Jǐwèi day,
the Moon trespassed against Yúguǐ.
The prognostication stated:
"A high minister will be executed."
In the ninth month, on the Gēngxū day,
the Moon again trespassed against Bì.
At the beginning of this year,
Yǔ Yì was in Xiāngyáng.
In the seventh month,
as Yǔ Yì's illness was nearing its end,
he presumptuously appointed his son Yuánzhī as the Inspector of Jīngzhōu,
to succeed him.
Yuánzhī was soon deposed.
The next year,
Huán Wēn again presumptuously led his troops to attack Shǔ,
captured Lǐ Shì,
and sent him to the capital.
Shǔ was originally Qín territory.
In the second year of Yǒnghé, in the second month, on the Rénzǐ day,
the Moon trespassed against the upper stars of Fáng.
In the fourth month, on the Bǐngxū day,
the Moon again trespassed against the upper stars of Fáng.
The prognostication was the same as before.
In the eighth month, on the Rénshēn day,
Tàibái trespassed against Zuǒzhífǎ.
This year,
Sītú Cài Mó was deposed.
In the third year of Yǒnghé, in the first month, on the Rénwǔ day,
the Moon trespassed against the fifth star of Nándǒu.
The prognostication stated:
"A general will die,
and close ministers will depart."
In the fifth month, on the Rénshēn day,
the Moon trespassed against the fourth star of Nándǒu,
then entered Kuí.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be troops."
Another interpretation stated:
"There will be a great amnesty."
In the sixth month,
the Moon trespassed against the main star of Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication stated:
"A general will die,
and the state will have worries."
On the Wùxū day,
the Moon trespassed against Wǔzhūhóu.
The prognostication stated:
"Feudal lords will be executed."
In the ninth month, on the Gēngyín day,
Tàibái trespassed against the fifth star of Nándǒu.
The prognostication stated:
"This signifies a military defeat."
In the fourth year, in the seventh month, on the Bǐngshēn day,
Tàibái trespassed against Zuǒzhífǎ.
On the Jiǎyín day,
the Moon trespassed against Fáng.
On the Dīngsì day,
the Moon entered Nándǒu and trespassed against the second star.
On the Yǐchǒu day,
Tàibái trespassed against Zuǒzhífǎ.
All these prognostication were the same as above.
In the tenth month, on the Jiǎxū day,
the Moon trespassed against Kàng.
The prognostication stated:
"War will arise,
and a military general will die."
In the eleventh month, on the Wùxū day,
it trespassed against Shàngjiāngxīng.
In the sixth month of the third year,
there was a great amnesty.
This month,
Chén Kuí campaigned against Shòuchūn,
was defeated, and returned.
In the seventh month,
the remaining Dī-Shǔ bandits rebelled and brought chaos to Yìtǔ.
In the ninth month,
Shí Hǔ attacked Liángzhōu,
but did not succeed.
In the fourth year of Yǒnghé, in the fourth month,
Tàibái entered Mǎo.
In the fifth month,
Yínghuò entered Lóu,
and trespassed against Zhènxīng.
In the seventh month,
Tàibái trespassed against Xuānyuán.
The prognostication was for Zhào,
and also for military defeat,
and worries for the empress.
In the eighth month of that year,
Shí Hǔ's crown prince Xuān killed his younger brother Tāo,
and Xuān also died.
In the first month of the fifth year,
Shí Hǔ presumptuously declared himself emperor,
and soon died of illness.
This year,
Chǔ Póu's northern expedition suffered a heavy loss of troops,
and he also soon passed away.
The Empress Dowager wore mourning attire.
In the first month of the sixth year,
court assemblies abolished music.
In the fifth year of Yǒnghé, in the fourth month, on the Dīngwèi day,
Tàibái trespassed against Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication stated:
"Qín will have troops."
In the ninth month, on the Wùxū day,
Tàibái trespassed against Zuǒjiǎo.
The prognostication stated:
"This signifies war."
In the tenth month,
the Moon trespassed against Mǎo.
The prognostication stated:
"The imperial court will have worries,
and a military general will die."
In the eleventh month, on the Yǐmǎo day,
a comet appeared in Kàng,
with its tail pointing westward,
white in color,
and one zhàng long.
The prognostication stated:
"This signifies military defeat."
In the eighth month of this year,
Chǔ Póu's northern campaign suffered a military defeat.
In the tenth month,
over twenty fortified settlements in Guānzhōng raised troops and pledged allegiance.
Shí Zūn attacked and captured Nányáng.
In the eleventh month,
Rǎn Mǐn killed Shí Zūn,
and then slaughtered over one hundred thousand Hú people,
whereupon the Central Plains fell into great chaos.
In the twelfth month,
Chǔ Póu passed away.
In the eighth year,
Liú Xiǎn, Fú Jiàn, and Mùróng Jùn all presumptuously assumed imperial titles.
Yīn Hào's northern expedition failed,
and he was deposed.
In the sixth year of Yǒnghé, second month, on the Xīnyǒu day,
the Moon violated the great star Xīn.
The divination said:
"Great officials will suffer anxiety.
Xīn corresponds to the division of Yùzhōu."
On the Dīngchǒu day,
the Moon violated Fáng.
The divination said:
"Generals and chancellors will suffer anxiety."
In the third month, on the Wùxū day,
Yínghuò (Mars) violated Suìxīng (Jupiter).
The divination said:
"There will be war."
In the sixth month, on the Jǐchǒu day,
the Moon violated Mǎo.
The divination was the same as above.
On the Yǐwèi day,
the Moon violated Wǔzhūhóu.
The divination was the same as in the third year.
In the seventh month, on the Rén-yín day,
the Moon first appeared in the west,
and violated Zuǒjiǎo.
The divination said:
"A great general will die."
One interpretation said:
"There will be warfare in the realm."
On the Dīngwèi day,
the Moon violated Jī.
The divination said:
"Military commanders will die."
On the Bǐngyín day,
Yínghuò (Mars) violated Yuèxīng.
The divination said:
"High officials will be executed."
In the eighth month, on the Xīnmǎo day,
the Moon violated Zuǒjiǎo,
Tàibái (Venus) was seen in daylight in Nándǒu,
and the Moon violated Yòuzhífǎ.
The divinations were all the same as above.
In the seventh year, second month,
Tàibái (Venus) violated Mǎo.
The divination was the same as above.
On the Yǐmǎo day,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Yúguǐ,
and violated Jīshī.
The divination said:
"Noble persons will suffer anxiety."
In the fifth month, on the Yǐwèi day,
Yínghuò (Mars) violated the great star Xuānyuán.
The divination said:
"The empress will suffer anxiety."
Tàibái (Venus) entered Bìkǒu,
and violated Zuǒgǔ.
The divination said:
"Generals and chancellors will be affected."
In the sixth month, on the Yǐhài day,
the Moon violated Jī.
On the Bǐngzǐ day,
the Moon violated Dǒu.
On the Dīngchǒu day,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Tàiwēi,
and violated Yòuzhífǎ.
In the eighth month, on the Gēngwǔ day,
Tàibái (Venus) violated Xuānyuán.
On the Wùzǐ day,
Tàibái (Venus) violated Yòuzhífǎ.
All divinations were the same as above.
In the seventh year,
Liú Xiǎn killed Shí Zhī and various Hú chieftains,
and the central plains fell into great chaos.
The Róng and Jìn peoples, numbering in the hundreds of thousands,
each returned to their former lands,
mutually invading and suffering from plague and death,
with only twelve or thirteen out of a hundred able to reach their destination.
In this year,
Huán Wēn presumptuously sought to lead a large army to cross the Jiāng and enter the Huái for a northern expedition,
causing fear and trembling in the imperial court.
In the eighth year,
Yùzhōu Inspector Xiè Shàng attacked Zhāng Yù,
but was defeated by Fú Xióng.
Yīn Hào's northern expedition failed,
and he was deposed.
In the tenth year,
Huán Wēn campaigned against Fú Jiàn,
but failed and returned.
In the eighth year of Yǒnghé, third month, on the Wùxū day,
the Moon violated the great star Xuānyuán.
On the Guǐchǒu day,
the Moon entered Nándǒu and violated the second star.
In the fifth month,
the Moon violated the Xīn star.
In the fourth month, on the Guǐyǒu day,
the Moon violated Fáng.
In the sixth month, on the Xīnsì day,
before the sun set,
there was a meteor like three Dǒukuí,
traveling southeast from the positions of Chénsì.
Calculated by its celestial longitude and latitude,
it was between Jī and Dǒu,
which is the division of Yān.
According to divination, it signified Yíngshǒu,
and beneath Yíngshǒu,
blood would flow profusely.
In the seventh month, on the Rénzǐ day,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) violated the Jùxīng of Dōngjǐng.
The divination said:
"Internal strife and military uprising will occur."
In the eighth month, on the Wùxū day,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Yúguǐ.
The divination said:
"Loyal officials will be executed."
On the Bǐngchén day,
Tàibái (Venus) entered Nándǒu,
and violated the fourth star.
The divination said:
"There will be rebellion."
One interpretation said:
"The chancellor will be dismissed."
In the ninth year, second month, on the Yǐsì day,
it entered Nándǒu,
and violated the third star.
In the third month, on the Wùchén day,
the Moon violated Fáng.
In the eighth month,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) violated the southeast star of Yúguǐ.
The divination was,
"the southeast star governs military affairs,
so military uprisings will occur."
In the twelfth month,
the Moon was in Dōngjǐng,
and violated Suìxīng (Jupiter).
The divination said:
"Qín will suffer famine and its people will migrate."
At this time, the emperor was young and immature,
the empress dowager exercised regency,
and there were rifts between generals and chancellors,
leading to continuous military conflicts.
Mùróng Jùn presumptuously proclaimed himself "Great Yān,"
engaging in endless conquests,
hence numerous calamities and anomalies appeared,
and Yīn Hào was deposed.
In the tenth year of Yǒnghé, in the first month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
the Moon eclipsed the Mǎo constellation.
The prognostication stated:
"Zhào and Wèi will have military conflict."
On the day Guǐyǒu,
the Planet of Soil (Saturn) overshadowed the Yuè star.
The prognostication stated:
"Axes and battle-axes will be employed."
In the second month, on the day Jiǎshēn,
the Moon encroached upon the Dàxīng of the Xīn constellation.
The prognostication stated:
"The king will be displeased by this."
In the fourth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
a shooting star, as large as a dipper,
reddish-yellow in color,
emerged from Zhīnǚ,
and disappeared into Zàofù,
with a sound like thunder.
The prognostication stated:
"Yān and Qí will have military conflict,
and the people will scatter."
On the day Wùwǔ,
the Moon encroached upon the Dàxīng of the Xīn constellation.
In the seventh month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Tàibái (Venus) was visible in daylight.
Calculating its gǔidù,
the disaster would be in Qín and Zhèng.
In the ninth month, on the day Xīnyǒu,
Tàibái encroached upon Zuǒzhífǎ.
In the eleventh month,
the Moon overshadowed the Planet of Soil,
in the Yúguǐ constellation.
The prognostication stated:
"Qín will have military conflict."
In the eleventh year, in the third month, on the day Xīnhài,
the Moon overshadowed Xuānyuán.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the fourth month, on the day Gēngyín,
the Moon encroached upon the southern star of the Niú constellation.
The prognostication stated:
"The state will have worries."
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Tàibái encroached upon Tiānjiāng.
The prognostication stated:
"The river crossings will be blocked."
In the twelfth year, in the sixth month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
Tàibái was visible in daylight,
in Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication was as above.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Moon encroached upon the Yuè star.
In the seventh month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Tàibái encroached upon the Planet of Soil,
in Liǔ.
The prognostication stated:
"The Zhōu territory will have great military conflict."
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐyǒu,
the Moon overshadowed Jiànxīng.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùyín,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Tàiwēi,
and encroached upon the Shàngjiàngxīng of Xīfán.
In the eleventh month, on the day Dīngchǒu,
Yínghuò encroached upon the Shàngxiàng of Tàiwēi Dōngfán.
In the fourth month of the tenth year,
Huán Wēn attacked Fú Jiàn,
and defeated his troops at Yáoliǔ.
Jiàn fortified Cháng'ān,
and Wēn retreated.
In the twelfth month,
Mùróng Kè attacked Qí.
In the eighth month of the twelfth year,
Huán Wēn defeated Yáo Xiāng at Yīshuǐ,
and pacified the Zhōu territory.
In the eleventh month,
the city of Qí fell,
Duàn Kān was captured,
and over three thousand people were killed.
Towards the end of Yǒnghé,
the Xiānbēi invaded Hé and Jì.
In the first year of Shēngpíng,
Mùróng Jùn then occupied Línzhāng,
taking full possession of the lands of Yōu, Bìng, Qīng, and Jì.
The various generals along the river gradually fled and dispersed,
and the river crossings were cut off.
In the third year,
the King of Kuàijī, due to the defeat of Xī Tán and Xiè Wàn,
requested to be demoted three ranks.
At this time, power was in the hands of the Fāngbó,
and military conflicts occurred throughout the Jiǔfú,
hence the ominous signs continued to appear.
In the first year of Shēngpíng of Emperor Mù of Jìn, on the Rénzǐ day of the fourth month,
Tàibái entered Yúguǐ.
On the Dīnghài day,
the Moon occulted the second star from the west head of the southern shaft of Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be soldiers in Qín territory."
Another said:
"A general will die."
In the sixth month, on the Wùxū day,
Tàibái was seen in daylight,
in Zhěn.
The prognostication was the same as above.
Zhěn
is the division of Chǔ.
On the Rénzǐ day,
the Moon trespassed against Bì.
The prognostication said:
"There will be border troops."
In the seventh month, on the Xīnsì day,
Yínghuò trespassed against Tiānjiāng.
The prognostication said:
"The Hékou pass will be blocked."
In the eleventh month,
Suìxīng trespassed against Fáng.
On the Rénwǔ day,
the Moon occulted Suìxīng,
in Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"The people will suffer famine."
Another said:
"Yùzhōu will suffer disaster."
In the second year, in the second month, on the Xīnmǎo day,
Tiánxīng trespassed against the great star of Xuānyuán.
On the Jiǎwǔ day,
the Moon trespassed against Dōngjǐng.
In the intercalary month, on the Yǐhài day,
the Moon trespassed against Suìxīng,
in Fáng.
All prognostication was the same as above.
In the fifth month, on the Dīnghài day,
a comet appeared from Tiānchuán,
within the longitude of Wèi.
Comets signify war and mourning,
abolishing the old and establishing the new;
appearing from Tiānchuán means
foreign barbarians will invade.
Another said:
"There will be great floods."
In the sixth month, on the Xīnyǒu day,
the Moon trespassed against Fáng.
In the eighth month, on the Wùwǔ day,
Yínghuò trespassed against Tiánxīng,
in Zhāng.
The prognostication said:
"A great war will arise.
Zhāng
is the division of Sānhé."
In the tenth month, on the Jǐwèi day,
Tàibái trespassed against Kūxīng.
In the twelfth month,
a Wǎngshǐ flowed from the southeast to the northwest,
its length half the sky.
In the third year, in the first month, on the Rénchén day,
Yínghuò trespassed against Jiànbì.
According to the prognostication,
"The ruler is worried."
In the third month, on the Yǐyǒu day,
Yínghuò retrograded and trespassed against Gōujíng.
According to the prognostication,
"The king dislikes this."
The Moon trespassed against Tàibái,
in Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"The sovereign will die."
Another said:
"There will be soldiers in Zhào territory,
and the court will be unsettled."
In the sixth month,
Tàibái trespassed against Dōngjǐng.
In the seventh month, on the Yǐyǒu day,
Yínghuò trespassed against Tiānjiāng.
On the Bǐngxū day,
Tàibái trespassed against Yúguǐ.
All prognostication was the same as above.
On the Wùzǐ day,
the Moon trespassed against the central great star of Qiānniú.
The prognostication said:
"Qiānniú
is the general of Heaven.
Trespassing against its central star means
the great general will die."
In the eighth month, on the Dīngwèi day,
Tàibái trespassed against the great star of Xuānyuán.
On the Jiǎzǐ day,
the Moon trespassed against the great star of Bì.
The prognostication said:
"There will be border troops."
Another said:
"The lower will offend the upper."
On the Gēngwǔ day,
Tàibái trespassed against Tiánxīng,
in Tàiwēi.
The prognostication said:
"The king dislikes this."
In the fifth month of the second year,
the Dī chieftain in Guānzhōng killed Fú Shēng and enthroned Jiān.
In the twelfth month,
Mùróng Jùn entered and garrisoned Yè.
In the eighth month,
General of the Pacified West and Inspector of Yùzhōu, Xiè Yì, passed away.
In the tenth month of the third year,
Zhūgě Yōu led a naval force into the river,
and was defeated.
Inspector of Yùzhōu, Xiè Wàn, entered Yǐng,
his troops scattered and he returned,
his name removed from the rolls and he became a commoner.
In the eleventh month,
the Grand Commandant, Prince of Kuàijī, requested to demote himself by three ranks due to the defeat of the two garrisons.
In the first month of the fourth year,
Mùróng Jùn died,
and his son Wěi succeeded him.
Mùróng Kè killed his Minister of the Imperial Secretariat, Yáng Wù, and others.
In the fifth month,
there was a great flood throughout the land.
In the fifth month of the fifth year,
Emperor Mù passed away.
In the first month of the fourth year of Shēngpíng, on the Yǐhài day,
the Moon trespassed against the central great star of Qiānniú.
The prognostication said:
"A great general will die."
In the sixth month, on the Xīnhài day,
Chénxīng trespassed against Xuānyuán.
The prognostication said:
"The empress is worried."
On the Jǐwèi day,
Tàibái entered the right flank gate of Tàiwēi,
and exited through Duānmén.
The prognostication said:
"The noble will seize power."
Another said:
"There will be soldiers."
Also said:
"Exiting Duānmén means
ministers will not be ministers."
In the eighth month, on the Wùshēn day,
Tàibái trespassed against Dī.
The prognostication said:
"The state has worries."
On the Bǐngchén day,
Yínghuò trespassed against the upper general of Tàiwēi's western rampart.
In the ninth month, on the Rénwǔ day,
Tàibái entered the mouth of Nándǒu,
and trespassed against the fourth star.
The prognostication said:
"There will be mourning,
an amnesty,
and the world will receive titles and emoluments."
In the tenth month, on the Gēngxū day,
Tiāngǒu was seen in the southwest.
The prognostication said:
"There will be great war."
On the Yǐyǒu day,
it occulted Bì.
The prognostication said:
"There will be border troops."
In the tenth month, on the Dīngmǎo day,
Yínghuò trespassed against Suìxīng,
in Yíngshì.
The prognostication said:
"A high minister has a hidden plot."
Another said:
"Wèi territory has soldiers."
On the Dīngwèi day,
the Moon trespassed against the red star of Bì.
The prognostication said:
"The lower will offend the upper."
Also said:
"There will be border troops."
In the eighth month,
Fàn Wāng was deposed.
In the first year of Lónghé, Mùróng Wěi dispatched Fù Mòbō to raid and [he] died.
In the fifth month,
Emperor Mù passed away,
Emperor Āi was enthroned,
a general amnesty and conferral of titles were issued,
and Empress Chǔ lost power.
In the seventh month,
Mùróng Kè attacked Inspector of Jìzhōu, Lǚ Hù, at Yěwáng,
and captured it;
Hù fled to Xíngyáng.
At this time, Huán Wēn, with a large army, was at Wǎn;
hearing of Hù's defeat, he retreated.
In the sixth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day of the fifth year of Shēngpíng,
the moon eclipsed the northeast star of Dī.
The divination said:
"A great general shall be affected by this."
In the ninth month, on the *yǐyǒu* day,
there was an eclipse of Bì.
The divination said:
"There will be border troops."
In the tenth month, on the *dīngmǎo* day,
Yínghuò trespassed against Suìxīng,
in Yíngshì.
The divination said:
"A high minister has a hidden plot."
Another interpretation said:
"There will be troops in Wèi territory."
On the *dīngwèi* day,
the moon trespassed against the red star of Bì.
The divination said:
"The lower will offend the upper."
It also said:
"There will be border troops."
In the eighth month,
Fàn Wāng was deposed.
〔一三〕In the first year of Lónghé,
Mùróng Wěi sent Fù Mòbō to raid Héyīn,
and Chén Yòu was in great danger.
In the eighth month of the first year of Jìn Āidì's Xīngníng era,
a comet appeared near Dàjiǎo and Kàng,
entering Tiānshì.
According to divination,
"this portends war and mourning."
In the first month of the third year,
Empress Wáng died.
In the second month,
Emperor Āi died.
In the third month,
Mùróng Kè attacked Luòyáng,
and Shěn Jìn and others died in battle.
In the tenth month, on the *bǐngxū* day, of the first year of Xīngníng,
the moon eclipsed Tàibái,
in Xūnǚ.
The divination said:
"The people of the world will scatter."
Another interpretation said:
"The disaster is in Yángzhōu."
In the third year,
Luòyáng fell.
Thereafter, Huán Wēn depleted the resources of Yángzhōu
to attack the Xiānbēi, suffering a defeat,
with more than half of his forces dead.
And when he campaigned against Yuán Zhēn,
Huáinán was ravaged.
Later, the Dī and Dōnghú invaded and pressed,
and military service was ceaseless.
In the first month, on the *yǐmǎo* day, of the third year of Xīngníng,
the moon eclipsed Suìxīng,
in Shēn.
Shēn
is the division of Yìzhōu.
In the sixth month,
Zhōu Fǔ, the General of the West and Governor of Yìzhōu, died.
In the tenth month,
Sīmǎ Xūn, the Governor of Liángzhōu, entered Yìzhōu and rebelled.
Zhū Xù led his troops to assist Governor Zhōu Chǔ in suppressing him.
In the seventh month, on the *gēngxū* day, of the third year of Xīngníng,
the moon trespassed against Nándǒu.
The divination said:
"The empress will be worried."
Suìxīng trespassed against Yúguǐ.
The divination said:
"The ruler will be worried."
In the tenth month,
Tàibái appeared in daylight,
in Kàng.
The divination said:
"Kàng represents the imperial court,
and there will be war and mourning,
and ministers will be strong."
Emperor Āi died in the second month of this year,
and these disasters all occurred after Hǎixī.
In the fifth month of the following year,
Empress Yǔ died.
On the *bǐngzǐ* day, the second day of the first year of Jìn Hǎixī's Tàihé era,
the moon eclipsed Yínghuò,
in Shēn.
The divination said:
"This portends internal strife."
Another interpretation said:
"Shēn
is the territory of Wèi."
In the first month of the second year,
Tàibái entered Mǎo.
In the fifth year,
Mùróng Wěi was destroyed by Fú Jiān,
and the four provinces of Sī, Jì, Yōu, and Bìng all came under the Dī.
In the eighth month, on the *wùwǔ* day, of the second year of Tàihé,
Tàibái trespassed against Suìxīng,
in Tàiwēi.
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎyín* day, of the third year,
Tàibái eclipsed Yínghuò,
within the Duānmén of Tàiwēi.
In the sixth year,
Duke Hǎixī was deposed.
In the second month of the fourth year of Tàihé,
a guest star appeared in the western wall of Zǐgōng,
and disappeared in the seventh month.
The divination said:
"When a guest star guards Zǐgōng,
a minister will kill his lord."
In the intercalary month, on the *yǐhài* day,
there was a lunar halo around Zhěn,
and again a white halo pierced the moon,
and a northern halo around the three stars of Dǒubǐng.
The divination said:
"The king will be displeased by this."
In the sixth year,
Huán Wēn deposed the emperor.
In the tenth month, on the *rénshēn* day, of the fourth year of Tàihé,
a large meteor fell to the west,
with a sound like thunder.
According to divination,
"a meteor signifies a noble envoy,
and a large star indicates a great envoy."
The following year,
an envoy was sent to demote Yuán Zhēn to a commoner.
Huán Wēn campaigned against Shòuchūn.
Zhēn died of illness,
and his son Jǐn succeeded him,
seeking aid from Fú Jiān.
Wēn defeated the Dī army.
In the sixth year,
the city of Shòuchūn fell,
with a sound like thunder,
an omen of the anger of the generals and soldiers.
In the intercalary month of the sixth year of Tàihé,
Yínghuò guarded the Duānmén of Tàiwēi.
The divination said:
"The Son of Heaven will lose his country."
It also said:
"Feudal lords and the Three Dukes will conspire against their superior."
Another interpretation said:
"There will be an executed minister."
On the *xīnmǎo* day,
the moon trespassed against the large star of Xīn.
The divination said:
"The king will be displeased by this."
In the eleventh month,
Huán Wēn deposed the emperor,
and also requested the execution of the King of Wǔlíng.
Jiǎnwén did not permit it,
so Wēn then moved him to Xīn'ān.
Collation Notes
Treatise 15, Astronomy 3
In the twelfth month, on the *xīnmǎo* day, of the first year of Jìn Jiǎnwén's Xián'ān era,
Yínghuò retrograded into Tàiwēi,
and did not retreat until the third month of the second year.
The divination said:
"The country is uneasy,
and there is sorrow."
At this time, the emperor was pressured by Huán Wēn,
and was filled with sorrow and grief.
In the seventh month,
the emperor died.
In the first month, on the *jǐyǒu* day, of the second year of Xián'ān,
Suìxīng trespassed against Tiánxīng,
in Xūnǚ.
The divination said:
"This portends internal strife."
In the fifth month,
the form and color of Suìxīng were like Tàibái.
The divination said:
"Advancing and retreating according to measure,
evil will cease.
If its color changes and it moves irregularly,
the ruler will have no fortune.
When Suìxīng is confined in midsummer,
it should be small and bright.
This is its departure from the norm.
It also indicates that ministers will be strong."
In the sixth month,
Tàibái appeared in daylight in Qīxīng.
On the *yǐyǒu* day,
Tàibái trespassed against Yúguǐ.
The divination said:
"The country has sorrow."
In the seventh month,
the emperor became gravely ill and
issued an edict to Huán Wēn, saying:
"If my young son can be assisted, assist him;
if not,
you may take the throne yourself."
Fortunately, the Attendant Wang Tǎnzhī destroyed the imperial rescript
and changed it to be like the precedent of Wáng Dǎo assisting in governance.
When Wēn heard of this, he was furious
and intended to execute Tǎnzhī and others,
which was the manifestation of internal strife.
In this month,
the emperor died.
In the second year of Xián'ān, fifth month, on the *dīngwèi* day,
Tàibái invaded Tiānguān.
The prognostication said:
"Troops will rise."
In the sixth month,
Yǔ Xī entered the capital city.
In the eleventh month,
Lú Sǒng entered the palace.
Both were executed and annihilated.
In the first year of Níngkāng of Jìn Xiàowǔ, first month, on the *wùshēn* day,
the Moon eclipsed the great star in Xīn.
Examining the prognostication,
the calamity will not befall the ruler,
but rather Yùzhōu.
One interpretation says:
"It portends evil for the lord's mandate."
In the third month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day,
the Moon eclipsed the fifth star of Nándǒu.
The prognostication said:
"A high official will have sorrow,
sorrow of death."
One interpretation says:
"A general will die."
In the seventh month,
Huán Wēn passed away.
In the second year of Níngkāng, first month, on the *dīngsì* day,
a comet appeared in Nǚxū,
passing through Dī, Kàng, Jiǎo, Zhěn, Yì, and Zhāng.
In the ninth month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
a comet appeared in Tiānshì.
In the eleventh month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Tàibái eclipsed Yínghuò,
located in Yíngshì.
The prognostication said:
"When metal and fire combine, it creates a 'scorching' phenomenon,
these calamities all signify military conflict and deaths."
In the fifth month of the first year of Tàiyuán,
the Dī chieftain Fú Jiān attacked Liángzhōu.
In the seventh month,
the Dī conquered Liángzhōu
and captured Zhāng Tiānxī.
In the eleventh month,
Huán Chōng dispatched troops from three prefectures to the Huái and Sì rivers.
Huán Huò also sent troops to guard the border.
In the intercalary month of the second year of Níngkāng, on the *jǐwèi* day,
the Moon eclipsed the southern star of Qiānniú.
The prognostication said:
"The Left General will die."
In the fifth month of the third year,
the Northern Central Protector-General Wáng Tǎnzhī passed away.
In the sixth month of the third year of Níngkāng, on the *xīnmǎo* day,
Tàibái invaded Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be military conflict in the Qín region."
In the ninth month, on the *wùshēn* day,
Yínghuò eclipsed the Left Law Enforcement star.
The prognostication said:
"The law enforcer will die."
In the first year of Tàiyuán,
Fú Jiān conquered Liángzhōu.
In the tenth month,
the Minister of Personnel Wáng Biāozhī died.
In the fourth month of the first year of Tàiyuán of Jìn Xiàowǔ, on the *bǐngxū* day,
Yínghuò invaded the third star of Nándǒu.
On the *bǐngshēn* day,
it again eclipsed the fourth star.
The prognostication said:
"A great war will arise,
and the Central Plains will suffer famine."
One interpretation says:
"There will be a general amnesty."
In the eighth month, on the *guǐyǒu* day,
Tàibái appeared during the day in Dī.
Dī
is the astronomical division of Yǎnzhōu.
In the ninth month,
Yínghuò invaded the Kūqì star,
and then entered Yǔlín.
The prognostication said:
"The Son of Heaven will have cause for weeping,
and the central army will rise."
In the eleventh month, on the *jǐwèi* day,
the Moon eclipsed the Left Horn.
The prognostication said:
"The Son of Heaven will have troops."
One interpretation says:
"The state will have sorrow."
In the sixth month of the third year,
Yínghuò guarded Yǔlín.
The prognostication said:
"The palace guard troops will rise in force."
In the ninth month, on the *rénwǔ* day,
Tàibái appeared during the day in Jiǎo,
the division of Yǎnzhōu.
In the fifth month of the first year,
there was a general amnesty.
In the eighth month of the third year,
the Dī bandit Wéi Zhōng entered Hànzhōng and descended eastward.
Fú Róng raided Fán and Dèng.
Mùróng Wěi besieged Xiāngyáng.
The Dī Governor of Yǎnzhōu, Péng Chāo, besieged Péngchéng.
In the second month of the fourth year,
Xiāngyáng city fell,
and the bandits captured Zhū Xù.
Péng Chāo abandoned Péngchéng
and captured Jí Yì.
Péng Chāo and others gathered a force of fifty thousand from Guǎnglíng Sānhé.
Thereupon, the General Who Punishes Rebels, Xiè Shí, advanced to Túzhōng.
The Right Guard, Máo Ānzhī, and the Attacking General, Prince Tánzhī of Héjiān, advanced to Tángyì.
Civilian laborers from Dānyáng were conscripted,
and the Administrator Yǐn Zhāngshè was ordered to garrison and defend the capital city.
In the sixth month,
the Governor of Yǎnzhōu, Xiè Xuán, attacked the bandits,
thoroughly defeating them,
and all remaining stragglers fled.
At this time, internal and external forces were engaged in war,
and there had been consecutive years of famine.
In this year,
ten thousand people from Yángzhōu were again conscripted to garrison Xiàkǒu.
In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Tàiyuán, on the *dīngsì* day,
Tàibái invaded the Kūsīng star.
The prognostication said:
"The Son of Heaven will have cause for weeping."
In the seventh month of the fifth year, on the *bǐngzǐ* day,
Chénxīng invaded Xuānyuán.
The prognostication said:
"A female ruler will be affected by this."
In the ninth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Empress Wáng passed away.
In the tenth month of the sixth year of Tàiyuán, on the *yǐmǎo* day,
a shooting star traveled southeast through Yì and Zhěn,
with a sound like thunder.
The treatise on stars says:
"When light and trace are connected, it is called a 'flow' (流);
when the trace disappears as it departs, it is called a 'run' (奔)."
Examining the prognostication,
"There will be military conflict in the Chǔ region."
One interpretation says:
"Armies will be defeated, and people will flee."
In the twelfth month,
the Dī Governor of Jīngzhōu, Liáng Chéng, and the Administrator of Xiāngyáng, Yán Zhèn, led their forces to attack Jìnglíng.
Huán Shíqián attacked and thoroughly defeated them,
capturing Zhèn alive,
beheading seven thousand,
and capturing ten thousand alive.
The sound like thunder
is an omen of generals and commanders becoming enraged.
In the ninth month of the seventh year,
Zhū Chuò attacked Xiāngyáng,
evacuating over six hundred households and returning.
In the eleventh month of the seventh year of Tàiyuán,
Tàibái appeared during the day,
located in Dǒu.
The prognostication said:
"There will be military conflict and deaths in Wú."
In the fourth month of the eighth year, on the *jiǎzǐ* day,
Tàibái again appeared during the day,
located in Cān.
The prognostication said:
"There will be military conflict and deaths in Wèi."
In this month,
Huán Chōng campaigned in Miǎnhàn.
Yáng Liàng attacked Shǔ,
both capturing cities and seizing territory.
In the eighth month,
Fú Jiān personally led a force numbering a million.
In the ninth month,
he attacked and captured Shòuyáng.
In the tenth month,
Liú Láozhī defeated and beheaded Fú Jiān's general Liáng Chéng,
killing and capturing over ten thousand men.
Xiè Xuán and others again defeated Fú Jiān at Féishuǐ,
beheading his younger brother Fú Róng,
and Fú Jiān's vast army collapsed and fled.
In the sixth month of the ninth year,
Empress Dowager Chǔ passed away.
In the eighth month,
Xiè Xuán garrisoned Péngchéng,
planning to recover the Central Plains.
In the eighth month of the tenth year,
Fú Jiān was killed by his general Yáo Cháng.
In the twelfth month of the tenth year of Tàiyuán, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Tàibái invaded Suìxīng.
The prognostication said:
"This signifies war and famine."
At this time, the region north of the Yellow River was not unified,
and wars were continuous abroad.
In winter,
there was a great famine.
In the third month, on the day *wùshēn*, of the eleventh year of Tài-yuán,
Táibái (Venus) was seen in daylight,
in Dōngjǐng (Eastern Well).
The divination said:
“Qín will have troops,
and its ministers will be strong.”
In the sixth month, on the day *jiǎwǔ*,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) was seen in daylight,
in Wèi (Stomach).
The divination said:
“Lǔ will have troops,
and its ministers will be strong.”
In the twelfth year,
Mùróng Chuí invaded Dōng'ā,
Zhái Liáo invaded Héshàng,
Yáo Cháng proclaimed himself at Āndìng,
Fú Dēng established himself in Lǒngshàng,
and Lǚ Guāng usurped Liángtǔ.
In the third month of the eleventh year of Tài-yuán,
a guest star was in Nándǒu (Southern Dipper),
and it disappeared only in the sixth month.
The divination said:
“There will be troops.”
One interpretation said:
“There will be an amnesty.”
After this, Sì, Yōng, Yǎn, and Jì continually had military service.
In the first month of the twelfth year,
there was a general amnesty.
In the eighth month,
there was another amnesty.
In the second month, on the day *wùyín*, of the twelfth year of Tài-yuán,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered the Moon.
The divination said:
“There will be rebellious ministers who die,
or high officials who are executed.”
One interpretation said:
“Female relatives will cause ruin,
and the empire will be in chaos.”
At this time, the Prince of Lángxié was regent,
and his consort’s elder brother, Guóbǎo, gained favor through their marital connection.
Also, Yuán Yuè, a man from Chénjùn, was corrupt and advanced improperly,
colluding with the emperor and the regent,
and stirring up factions.
In the thirteenth year,
the Emperor killed Yuè.
Thus, a rift formed between the emperor and the regent,
and the seeds of chaos were sown.
In the tenth month, on the day *gēngwǔ*, of the twelfth year of Tài-yuán,
Táibái (Venus) was seen in daylight,
in Dǒu (Dipper).
In the intercalary month, on the day *wùchén*, of the thirteenth year,
a Tiāngǒu (Heavenly Dog) descended from the northeast with a sound.
In the twelfth month, on the day *wùzǐ*,
Chénxīng (Mercury) entered the Moon,
in Wēi (Rooftop).
The divination said:
“Rebellious ministers want to kill the ruler;
within three years,
there will certainly be internal evil.”
In this month,
Yínghuò (Mars) was in Jiǎojiǎo (Horn) and Kàng (Neck),
with a fierce and strong appearance.
The divination said:
“If Yínghuò deviates from its normal course,
officials will abandon their laws,
and feudal lords will disrupt their governance.”
After this, Mùróng Chuí, Zhái Liáo, Yáo Cháng, Fú Dēng, and Mùróng Yǒng all took up arms and vied for power.
In the first month of the fourteenth year,
an evil rebel in Péngchéng again proclaimed himself at Huángqiū,
but Liú Láozhī defeated and annihilated him.
In the third month,
Zhāng Dào broke through Héxiāng,
besieged Tài Shān,
and Xiàng Qīnzhī attacked and repelled him.
In this year,
Zhái Liáo again attacked and occupied Xíngyáng,
and encroached upon Chén and Xiàng.
At this time, state affairs were mostly corrupt,
and the path of governance had declined.
In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year of Tài-yuán,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Yǔlín (Feathered Forest).
On the day *yǐwèi*,
the Moon encroached upon Suìxīng (Jupiter).
The divinations were the same as above.
In the fifteenth year,
Zhái Liáo plundered Sì and Yǎn by land,
and although many armies repeatedly attacked him, they could not overcome him.
The Xiānbēi also advanced and expanded into Bìng and Jì.
In the seventh month,
there was a drought.
In the eighth month,
there were great floods in all commanderies,
and Yǎnzhōu also had locusts.
In the seventh month, on the day *rénshēn*, of the fifteenth year of Tài-yuán,
a comet appeared in Běihé Jiè (North River Guard),
passed through Tàiwēi (Supreme Palace Enclosure), Sāntái (Three Terraces), Wénchāng (Literary Glory),
and entered Běidǒu (Northern Dipper),
with a length of over ten *zhàng*.
In the eighth month, on the day *wùxū*,
it entered Zǐwēi (Purple Palace Enclosure),
and then disappeared.
The divination said:
“Běihé Jiè
is also called Húmén (Barbarian Gate).
If there is a comet in Húmén, there will be troops and death.
If it sweeps through Tàiwēi,
and enters Zǐwēi,
it concerns the king.
Sāntái represents the Three Dukes,
and Wénchāng represents the generals and prime ministers;
generals, prime ministers, and the Three Dukes will suffer disaster.
If it enters Běidǒu,
strong states will raise armies,
feudal lords will contend for power,
and high officials will worry.”
In the eleventh month,
Táibái (Venus) entered Yǔlín (Feathered Forest).
The divination said:
“The Son of Heaven will form an army to defend himself,
and there will be rebellious ministers.”
In the ninth month of the twenty-first year,
Emperor Xiàowǔ died.
In the first year of Lóng'ān,
Wáng Gōng, Yīn Zhòngkān, Huán Xuán, and others all raised armies to impeach and execute Wáng Guóbǎo;
the imperial court complied and killed him,
and also executed his cousin, Xù.
Sīmǎ Dàozǐ thus lost power,
and chaos ensued.
In the eleventh month, on the day *guǐsì*, of the sixteenth year of Tài-yuán,
the Moon eclipsed the star in front of Xīn (Heart).
The divination said:
“The Crown Prince will be troubled.”
At this time, the Crown Prince often suffered from a severe illness.
In the ninth month, on the day *dīngchǒu*, of the seventeenth year of Tài-yuán,
Suìxīng (Jupiter), Yínghuò (Mars), and Zhēnxīng (Saturn) were all in Kàng (Neck) and Dī (Root).
The divination said:
“When the three stars converge,
this is called ‘disturbing the position and cutting off movement,’
and there will be internal and external troops, death, and famine,
and a change in the established kings and dukes.”
In the first month, on the day *yǐyǒu*, of the eighteenth year of Tài-yuán,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered the Moon.
The divination said:
“Trouble in the palace,
not from rebels but from thieves.”
One interpretation said:
“There will be rebellious ministers,
or those who are executed.”
In the ninth month of the twenty-first year,
the Emperor suddenly died in the inner palace,
and the common people declared that Lady Zhāng had secretly committed high treason.
At this time, the imperial government was dark and slow,
and did not carry out public executions,
but only silently blamed her.
Also, Wáng Guóbǎo was treacherous and cunning,
and eventually suffered his due punishment.
In the second month of the eighteenth year of Tài-yuán,
a guest star was in Wěi (Tail),
and disappeared only in the ninth month.
The divination said:
“Yān will have troops and death.”
In the fourth month, on the day *jǐsì*, of the nineteenth year,
the Moon eclipsed Suìxīng (Jupiter),
in Wěi (Tail).
The divination said:
“There will be famine,
and the state of Yān will perish.”
In the twentieth year,
Mùróng Chuí sent his son Bǎo to attack Shí Guī,
but was defeated by Guī,
with tens of thousands of casualties.
In the twenty-first year,
Chuí died,
and his state subsequently declined and perished.
In the tenth month, on the day *guǐchǒu*, of the nineteenth year of Tài-yuán,
Táibái (Venus) encroached upon Suìxīng (Jupiter),
in Dǒu (Dipper).
The divination said:
“There will be famine,
and internal troops.
Dǒu represents
the division of Wú and Yuè.”
By the first year of Lóng'ān,
Wáng Gōng and others raised armies to declare Wáng Guóbǎo's crimes,
and the imperial court granted an amnesty.
After this, there were successive years of floods, droughts, and famine among the people.
In the sixth month of the twentieth year of Tài-yuán,
Huỳnh-huò entered Tiān-qūn.
The prognostication said:
"There will be famine throughout the land."
In the seventh month, on the day Dīng-hài,
Tài-bái entered Tài-wēi.
The prognostication said:
"If Tài-bái enters Tài-wēi,
the state will have worries.
If it is seen in daylight,
it signifies war and mourning."
In the ninth month,
a bushy star, like shredded cotton, appeared,
traveling southeast,
passing through Nǚ-xū to Kū-xīng.
The prognostication said:
"If a bushy star appears,
within three years,
a rebellious minister will surely be executed in the marketplace."
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐ-sì,
the moon encroached upon Jiàn-bì and the eastern and western Xián.
The prognostication said:
"Jiàn-bì governs the heart, abdomen, throat, and tongue;
the eastern and western Xián preside over conspiracies."
At this time, Wáng Guó-bǎo was colluding to control the court.
In the ninth month of the twenty-first year,
the Emperor passed away.
In the first year of Lóng-ān,
Wáng Gōng and others raised troops,
and the imperial court executed Wáng Guó-bǎo and Wáng Xù.
There were also consecutive years of floods and droughts,
coupled with military mobilizations in three directions,
causing the people to suffer famine.
In the third month of the twenty-first year of Tài-yuán,
Tài-bái was seen in daylight repeatedly,
in Yǔ-lín.
The prognostication said:
"There will be powerful ministers,
and casualties from war;
the central army will rise."
In the fourth month, on the day Rén-wǔ,
Tài-bái entered Tiān-qūn.
The prognostication said:
"This portends famine."
In the sixth month,
Suì-xīng encroached upon Kū-xīng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be matters of weeping."
In the ninth month of that year,
Emperor Xiào-wǔ passed away.
In the first year of Lóng-ān,
Wáng Gōng raised troops to threaten the court,
whereupon the capital and provinces were put on high alert,
and Wáng Guó-bǎo was executed to appease him.
In the first month, on the day Guǐ-hài, of the first year of Lóng-ān of Emperor Jìn Ān-dì,
Huỳnh-huò encroached upon Kū-xīng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be matters of weeping."
In the second month,
Suì-xīng and Huỳnh-huò both entered Yǔ-lín.
The prognostication said:
"Armies will rise."
In the fourth month, on the day Dīng-chǒu,
Tài-bái was seen in daylight,
in Dōng-jǐng.
Qín suffered casualties from war.
In this month,
Wáng Gōng raised troops,
and the capital and provinces were put on high alert.
Soon after, Wáng Guó-bǎo and others were killed.
In the sixth month,
Qiāng bandits attacked Luò-yáng,
and Xī Huī dispatched troops to rescue it.
Yáo Cháng died,
and his son, LǖE, succeeded him.
Shí Guī proclaimed himself at Zhōng-shān.
In the sixth month, on the day Gēng-wǔ, of the first year of Lóng-ān,
the moon eclipsed Tài-bái,
outside the Duān-mén of Tài-wēi.
The prognostication said:
"The state will suffer from war."
On the day Yǐ-yǒu,
the moon eclipsed Suì-xīng,
in Dōng-bì.
The prognostication said:
"This portends famine.
Wèi territory will suffer from war."
In the eighth month,
Huỳnh-huò guarded Jǐng-yuè.
The prognostication said:
"A high minister will be executed."
In the sixth month, on the day Wù-chén, of the second year,
Shè-tí shifted its course abnormally,
and Suì-xīng was seen in daylight in Wèi.
Wèi
is the division of Yǎn-zhōu.
In the sixth month of that year,
Xī Huī dispatched Dèng Qǐ-fāng and others with ten thousand men to ravage the captives at Huá-tái.
Huá-tái
is Wèi territory.
Qǐ-fāng and his men were defeated and returned.
In the ninth month,
Wáng Gōng, Yǔ Kǎi, Yīn Zhòng-kān, Huán Xuán, and others all raised troops, petitioning for the execution of Wáng Yú and the Sī-mǎ Shàng-zhī brothers.
Thereupon, the capital and provinces were put on high alert,
and a large number of common people were mobilized.
Zhòng-kān's army reached Xún-yáng,
capturing Wáng Yú, the Inspector of Jiāng-zhōu.
Kǎi's general Duàn Fāng attacked Shàng-zhī at Yáng-hú,
but was defeated by him,
and Fāng died.
Wáng Gōng's Sī-mǎ, Liú Láo-zhī, turned against Gōng,
and Gōng was defeated.
Huán Xuán reached Bái-shí,
but also fled.
Zhòng-kān returned to Jiāng-líng.
In the winter of the third year,
Yīn Zhòng-kān, the Inspector of Jīng-zhōu, was killed by Huán Xuán.
In the intercalary month of the second year of Lóng-ān,
Tài-bái was seen in daylight,
in Yǔ-lín.
On the day Dīng-chǒu,
the moon encroached upon Dōng Shàng-xiàng.
In the fifth month, on the day Xīn-yǒu, of the third year,
the moon again eclipsed Dōng Shàng-xiàng.
On the day Xīn-wèi,
Chén-xīng encroached upon Xuān-yuán-xīng.
All prognostication are as above.
In the first month of that year,
Yáng Quán-qī defeated Xī Huī,
taking his post,
and Yīn Zhòng-kān then killed him.
In the sixth month,
the Xiān-bēi attacked and took Qīng-zhōu.
In the tenth month,
Qiāng bandits attacked and took Luò-yáng.
Huán Xuán conquered Jīng and Yōng,
killing Yīn Zhòng-kān and Yáng Quán-qī.
Sūn Ēn gathered followers and attacked and took Kuài-jī,
killing the Administrator Wáng Níng-zhī,
and Liú Láo-zhī attacked him in the east and drove him away.
In the seventh month of the fourth year,
Empress Dowager Lǐ passed away.
In the first month, on the *yǐhài* day of the fourth year of Lóng'ān,
the moon encroached upon the planet Tiánxīng (Saturn)
in Qiānnú (Ox).
The prognostication said:
"Wú and Yuè will suffer military disaster.
The empress will be in distress."
In the second month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
a broom star appeared in Kuí (Andromeda),
three *zhàng* long,
extending upwards to Gé Dào and the western border of Zǐ Gōng (Purple Palace),
entering Dǒu Kuí (Big Dipper),
reaching Sān Tái (Three Terraces), Tài Wēi (Supreme Palace Enclosure), Dì Zuò (Emperor's Throne), and Duān Mén (Front Gate).
The prognostication said:
"A comet sweeping the emperor's court and gates
is a sign of a change of ruler."
Passing Sān Tái
and entering Běi Dǒu (Northern Dipper),
the prognostication was the same as the previous entry.
In the sixth month, on the *yǐwèi* day,
the moon again encroached upon Tiánxīng (Saturn)
in Qiānnú (Ox).
On the *xīnyǒu* day,
it again encroached upon Kū Xīng (Crying Star).
In the tenth month,
the planet Suìxīng (Jupiter) appeared to be lurking in Běi Hé (Northern River).
The prognostication said:
"It signifies famine."
In the twelfth month, on the *wùyín* day,
a broom star appeared in Guànsǔo (Coiled Thong), Tiān Shì (Heavenly Market), and Tiānjīn (Celestial Ford).
The prognostication said:
"Noble officials will die in prison,
and there will be military disaster both internally and externally.
Tiānjīn (Celestial Ford) being cut off by bandits
means the kingly way throughout the world will be obstructed."
In the twelfth month,
Tàibái (Venus) was seen in Dǒu (Dipper) during the day,
continuing until the first month, on the *yǐmǎo* day, of the fifth year.
According to the prognostication,
the calamity would be in Wú and Yuè.
In the third month, on the *jiǎyín* day,
many red meteors
travelled westward through Qiānnú (Ox), Xū (Emptiness), Wēi (Rooftop), Tiānjīn (Celestial Ford), and Gé Dào (Gallery Road),
piercing Tài Wēi (Supreme Palace Enclosure) and Zǐ Gōng (Purple Palace).
The prognostication said:
"Stars represent the common people;
this is an omen of many flowing westward.
Passing through the emperor's court,
the ruler will be weak and his ministers strong,
and the feudal lords' armies will not be restrained."
In the seventh month, on the *guǐhài* day,
the star Dà Jiǎo (Arcturus) scattered and flickered in five colors.
The prognostication said:
"The king will be scattered and dispersed."
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
the moon encroached upon Tiān Guān (Celestial Pass).
The prognostication said:
"The king will be distressed."
In the ninth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Yínghuò (Mars) encroached upon Shǎo Wēi (Minor Palace Enclosure)
and then guarded it.
The prognostication said:
"Hermits will be executed."
In the tenth month, on the *wùzǐ* day,
the moon encroached upon Dōng Fān Cì Xiàng (Eastern Barrier, Second Minister).
In the fifth month of the fourth year,
Sūn Ēn again captured Kuàijī,
killing the Internal Scribe Xiè Yǎn.
Gāo Yǎzhī and others were dispatched to suppress him.
In the seventh month,
Empress Dowager Lǐ passed away.
In the tenth month,
the rebellious bandit Sūn Ēn heavily defeated Gāo Yǎzhī at Yúyáo,
with seventeen or eighteen tenths of his men killed.
In the second month of the fifth year,
Sūn Ēn attacked Gōuzhāng,
and Gāozǔ resisted him.
In the fifth month,
Yuán Shānsōng, the Internal Scribe of Wújùn, went out to battle
and was killed by him,
with several thousand men dying.
In the sixth month,
Sūn Ēn reached Jīngkǒu,
