where Gāozǔ defeated him.
Sūn Ēn's army camped at Púzhōu,
whereupon internal and external areas were put on high alert,
camps and formations were established for defense,
and the Huái River mouth was blocked with palisades.
Sūn Ēn dispatched a separate general to attack Guǎnglíng,
killing over three thousand people.
Sūn Ēn fled and occupied Yùzhōu.
In that month,
Gāozǔ again pursued and defeated him.
In the ninth month,
Huán Xuán's memorial arrived,
defying the imperial decree and insulting the emperor.
In the tenth month,
Sīmǎ Yuánxiǎn greatly organized a navy,
intending to attack Huán Xuán.
In the first month of the first year of Yuánxīng,
Huán Xuán marched eastward.
In that month,
Sūn Ēn was in Línhǎi,
his people dying of starvation or scattering,
and Sūn Ēn himself drowned himself.
Lú Xún styled himself General of Suppressing Barbarians,
leading Sūn Ēn's remaining forces
to conquer Yǒngjiā and Jìn'ān.
In the second month,
the emperor wore military attire and dispatched the western army.
On the *dīngmǎo* day,
Huán Xuán reached Gūshú,
defeated Lìyáng,
Sīmǎ Shàngzhī was killed,
and Líu Láozhī surrendered to Huán Xuán.
In the third month,
Huán Xuán conquered the capital,
killed Sīmǎ Yuánxiǎn,
and exiled Grand Tutor Dàozǐ.
In the seventh month,
there was a great famine,
and people resorted to cannibalism.
Sixteen or seventeen tenths of the population east of the Zhèjiāng River died of starvation or fled,
and the households in Wújùn and Wúxīng were reduced by half.
Additionally, tens of thousands fled westward.
In the tenth month,
Huán Xuán dispatched a general to attack Líu Guǐ,
defeating him and forcing him to flee to Qīngzhōu.
In the fourth year,
Huán Xuán eventually usurped the throne,
moving the emperor to Xúnyáng.
In the third month, on the *wùzǐ* day, of the first year of Yuánxīng of Emperor Ān of Jìn,
Tàibái (Venus) encroached upon Wǔ Zhūhóu (Five Feudal Lords),
and was consequently seen during the day.
In the fourth month, on the *xīnchǒu* day,
the moon occulted Chénxīng (Mercury).
In the seventh month, on the *wùyín* day,
Yínghuò (Mars) was in Dōngjǐng (Eastern Well),
and Yínghuò (Mars) encroached upon Yúguǐ (Ghost Car) and Jīshī (Piled Corpses).
All prognostication was the same as above.
In the eighth month, on the *gēngzǐ* day,
Tàibái (Venus) encroached upon Suìxīng (Jupiter),
to the southeast of Shàngjiāng (General).
The prognostication said:
"The Chǔ army will suffer famine."
Another account says:
"Calamity will be upon the Shàngjiāng."
On the *bǐngyín* day,
Tàibái (Venus) occulted Yòu Zhífǎ (Right Law Enforcer).
In the ninth month, on the *guǐwèi* day,
Tàibái (Venus) encroached upon Jìnxián (Advancing Worthies).
The prognostication said:
"Worthy men will be executed."
In the tenth month,
a guest star, white as powder or floss,
was to the west of Tài Wēi (Supreme Palace Enclosure),
and by the twelfth month,
it entered Tài Wēi (Supreme Palace Enclosure).
The prognostication said:
"Troops will enter the emperor's court."
In the second month of the second year,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) encroached upon Xī Shàngjiāng (Western General).
In the sixth month, on the *jiǎchén* day,
it occulted the fourth star of Dǒu (Dipper).
The prognostication said:
"High officials will be executed,
within three years."
In the eighth month, on the *guǐchǒu* day,
Tàibái (Venus) encroached upon the second star north of Fáng (Chamber).
In the ninth month, on the *jǐchǒu* day,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) encroached upon Jìnxián (Advancing Worthies),
and Yínghuò (Mars) encroached upon Xī Shàngjiāng (Western General).
In the tenth month, on the *jiǎxū* day,
Tàibái (Venus) encroached upon Qì Xīng (Weeping Star).
In the eleventh month, on the *dīngchǒu* day,
Yínghuò (Mars) encroached upon Tiánxīng (Saturn).
On the *xīnsì* day,
the moon encroached upon Yínghuò (Mars).
In the twelfth month, on the *yǐsì* day,
the moon occulted the second star of Xuānyuán (Regulus).
All prognostication was the same as above.
In the winter of the first year,
the Suǒtóu (Tuoba) broke the Qiāng army.
In the twelfth month of the second year,
Huán Xuán usurped the throne,
exiling and relocating the emperor and empress to Xúnyáng,
and naming Empress Hé of Yǒng'ān as Lady of Línglíng.
In the second month of the third year,
Gāozǔ executed all of the Huán clan.
In the third year of Yuánxīng, in the first month, on the day Wùxū,
Yínghuò (Mars) moved retrograde, encroaching upon Tàiwēi's western upper minister.
The prognostication said:
"The Son of Heaven will battle in the wilds,
and the upper minister will die."
In the second month, on the day Jiǎchén,
the Moon obscured Suìxīng (Jupiter) at Zuǒjiǎo.
The prognostication said:
"War will break out across the land."
On the day Bǐngchén,
Yínghuò moved retrograde to the northwest of Zuǒzhífǎ.
The prognostication said:
"The law-enforcers will be troubled."
In the fourth month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the Moon obscured the second star of Xuānyuán,
and Zhēnxīng (Saturn) entered Yǔlín.
In the twelfth month,
Yínghuò and Tàibái (Venus) both encroached upon Yǔlín.
The prognostication was the same as above.
In the second month of that year, on the day Bǐngchén,
Gāozǔ killed Huán Xiū and others.
In the third month, on the day Jǐwèi,
Huán Xuán was defeated and fled,
and an army was dispatched to campaign in the west.
On the day Xīnyǒu,
the Left Prime Minister Wáng Yú and his son, the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, Suí, were executed.
Huán Xuán abducted the emperor to Jiānglíng.
In the fifth month,
Xuán descended to Zhēngróngzhōu,
where the righteous army defeated and destroyed him.
Huán Zhèn then attacked and took Jiānglíng again,
imprisoning and abducting the Son of Heaven.
In the first month of the following year,
the combined armies attacked him,
Zhèn fled,
and the imperial carriage then returned.
In the seventh month,
Empress Hé of Yǒng'ān passed away.
In the third month,
Huán Zhèn again attacked Jiānglíng,
and the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, Sīmǎ Xiūzhī, was defeated and fled.
In that month,
Liú Huáisù attacked Zhèn and annihilated him.
In the second month of that year,
Qiáo Zòng of Bāxī killed the Inspector of Yìzhōu, Máo Qú, and Qú's younger brother, the Western Barbarian Commandant Jǐn,
occupying the western lands,
and proclaimed himself King of Shǔ.
In the first year of Yìxī of Emperor Ān of Jìn, in the third month, on the day Rénchén,
the Moon obscured Zuǒzhífǎ.
The prognostication was the same as above.
On the day Dīngyǒu,
the Moon obscured the front star of Xīn.
The prognostication said:
"Yùzhōu will suffer disaster."
Tàibái encroached upon Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"Qín will have war."
In the fourth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
the Moon encroached upon Zhēnxīng,
which was in Dōngbì.
The prognostication said:
"That territory will lose its state."
Another interpretation said:
"A nobleman will die."
In the seventh month, on the day Gēngchén,
Tàibái appeared brighter than in daylight,
in Yì and Zhěn.
The prognostication said:
"Ministers will be powerful.
Jīngzhōu will suffer military losses."
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Moon obscured Zhēnxīng,
which was in Dōngbì.
The prognostication said:
"That state will perish by conquest."
Another interpretation said:
"The people will become refugees."
In the eighth month, on the day Dīngsì,
the Moon encroached upon the first star of Dǒu.
The prognostication said:
"There will be war across the land."
Another interpretation said:
"High ministers will be troubled."
According to records from the time when the court moved east of the Jiāng,
if Nándǒu suffers disaster,
then Wúyuè, Kuàijī, Dānyáng, Yùzhāng, and Lújiāng will each be affected according to their respective stars.
If Huáinán loses territory,
it is likely not prognosticated.
The historians omitted its explanation,
thus it is not listed here.
In the ninth month, on the day Wùzǐ,
Yínghuò encroached upon Shàowēi.
The prognostication said:
"Hermits will be punished."
On the day Gēngyín,
Yínghuò encroached upon Yòuzhífǎ.
On the day Guǐmǎo,
Yínghuò encroached upon Zuǒzhífǎ.
The prognostication for both was the same as above.
In the tenth month, on the day Dīngsì,
the Moon obscured Zhēnxīng in Yíngshì.
The prognostication was the same as in the seventh month.
In the eleventh month, on the day Bǐngxū,
Tàibái obscured Gōoqián.
The prognostication said:
"Ministers who are the 'throat and tongue' will be troubled."
In the twelfth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Suìxīng encroached upon Tiānjiāng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be military rebellion,
and the river crossings will be impassable."
In the sixth month of that year,
the Suǒtóu bandits invaded Pèitǔ,
causing the false Inspector of Yùzhōu, Suǒ Dùzhēn, to garrison Xiàngxiàn.
The Grand Tutor, King Jǐng of Chángshā, attacked and drove them away.
In the eleventh month,
the Inspector of Jīngzhōu, Wèi Yǒngzhī, passed away.
In the second month of the second year,
Sīmǎ Guófán and others attacked and took Yìyáng.
In the fourth month,
the Qiāng attacked Qiúchí,
and Duke Yáng Shèng of Qiúchí attacked and drove them away.
In the ninth month,
the Inspector of Yìzhōu, Sīmǎ Róngqí, was murdered by his staff officer Yáng Chéngzǔ.
At that time, Wén Chùmào had repeatedly achieved successes in campaigning against Shǔ.
Coinciding with Róngqí's death,
he then withdrew.
In the twelfth month of the third year,
the Grand Minister and Inspector of Yángzhōu, Wáng Mì, passed away.
In the first month of the fourth year,
the Grand Guardian, King Zūn of Wǔlíng, passed away.
In the third month,
the Left Prime Minister Kǒng Ānguó died.
In the fifth year,
Gāozǔ campaigned against the Xiānbēi,
and pacified the old territory of Yǎn.
In the second year of Yìxī, in the second month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
the Moon encroached upon the rear star of Xīn.
The prognostication said:
"Yùzhōu will suffer disaster."
In the fourth month, on the day Guǐchǒu,
the Moon encroached upon Tàiwēi's western upper general.
On the day Jǐwèi,
the Moon encroached upon the second southern star of Fáng.
On the day Yǐchǒu,
Suìxīng encroached upon Tiānjiāng.
All prognostication were the same as above.
In the fifth month, on the day Guǐwèi,
the Moon encroached upon Zuǒjiǎo.
The prognostication said:
"The Left General will die,
and there will be war across the land."
On the day Rén'yín,
Yínghuò encroached upon Dǐ.
The prognostication said:
"Dǐ is the imperial lodging,
the ruler will be troubled."
In the sixth month, on the day Gēngwǔ,
Yínghuò encroached upon the second northern star of Fáng.
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐhài,
Yínghuò encroached upon the fifth star of Dǒu.
On the day Dīngsì,
it encroached upon Jiànxīng.
In the ninth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Yínghuò encroached upon Kūxīng,
and also upon Qìxīng.
All prognostication were the same as above.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the Moon obscured Tàibái,
which was in Wēi.
The prognostication said:
"Qí will lose its state."
Another interpretation said:
"The ruler of a powerful state will die."
On the day Dīngwèi,
Yínghuò and Tàibái both entered Yǔlín.
In the second month of that year, on the day Jiǎxū,
Sīmǎ Guófán and others attacked and took Yìyáng.
In the first month of the third year,
the Xiānbēi invaded Běixúzhōu,
reaching Xiàpī.
In the eighth month,
Liú Jìngxuān was dispatched to campaign against Shǔ.
In the twelfth month,
the Grand Minister Wáng Mì passed away.
In the first month of the fourth year,
King Zūn of Wǔlíng passed away.
In the fifth year,
the Xiānbēi again invaded Huáinán.
In the fourth month,
Gāozǔ's great army campaigned against them.
In the sixth month,
there was a major battle at Línqú City,
and they advanced to besiege Guǎnggù.
In the tenth month,
Shíguī was murdered by his son, the false Duke of Qīnghé.
In the second month of the sixth year,
Guǎnggù was captured,
Muróng Chāo was taken captive,
and over three thousand of his followers were buried alive or beheaded.
In the third year of Yìxī (407 CE), in the first month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Tàibái (Venus) was seen in daylight,
in the Kuí (Andromeda) constellation.
In the second month, on the day Gēngyín,
the Moon eclipsed the star behind Xīn (Antares).
The prognostication was entirely the same as above.
On the day Guǐhài,
Yínghuò (Mars), Tiánxīng (Saturn), Tàibái (Venus), and Chénxīng (Mercury) gathered in the Kuí (Andromeda) and Lóu (Aries) constellations,
following Tiánxīng (Saturn).
Its explanation can be found nine years prior.
〔一二〕In the fifth month, on the day Jǐchǒu,
Tàibái (Venus) was seen in daylight,
in the Shēn (Orion) constellation.
The prognostication said:
"There will be military disasters in Yìzhōu,
and ministers will become powerful."
In the sixth month, on the day Xīnmǎo,
Yínghuò (Mars) violated Chénxīng (Mercury),
in the Yì (Crater) constellation.
The prognostication said:
"War will break out throughout the realm."
In the eighth month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
Tàibái (Venus) eclipsed Yínghuò (Mars),
and also violated Zhífǎ (Regulus).
The prognostication said:
"When it eclipses Yínghuò (Mars),
there will be a major war."
On the day Xīnmǎo,
Yínghuò (Mars) violated the Left Zhífǎ (Regulus).
In the ninth month, on the day Rénzǐ,
Yínghuò (Mars) violated Jìnxián (Lambda Scorpii).
In the first month of this year, on the day Dīngsì,
the Xiānbēi invaded Northern Xú,
reaching Xiàpī.
In the eighth month,
Liú Jìngxuān attacked Shǔ,
but failed and returned.
In the fourth year (408 CE), in the third month,
Left Púshè Kǒng Ānguó died.
In the seventh month,
Sīmǎ Guófán and others attacked and captured Zōushān.
〔一三〕The Grand Administrator of Lǔ Jùn, Xú Yōng, defeated and routed them.
Yáo Lüè dispatched troops to conquer Fófó,
but was greatly defeated by them.
In the fifth year (409 CE),
Gāozǔ attacked the Xiānbēi.
In the sixth year (410 CE), in the third month,
the rebel Xú Dàofù killed the Grand Administrator of Jiāngzhōu and General Guarding the South, Hé Wújì, in Yùzhāng.
In the fourth month,
the rebel Lú Xún attacked Bālíng in Xiāngzhōng.
In the fifth month, on the day Bǐngzǐ,
Xún and Dàofù defeated Fǔjūn Jiāngjūn and Grand Administrator of Yùzhōu, Liú Yì, at Sāngluòzhōu.
Yì barely escaped with his life.
On the day Dīngchǒu,
Xún and others reached Càizhōu,
and sent a separate general to burn Jīngkǒu.
On the day Gēngchén,
the rebels attacked and burned Zhāpǔ.
The commander of the Zhāpǔ garrison fought back but was unsuccessful.
Gāozǔ sent troops across the Huái River to attack,
and greatly defeated them.
Sīmǎ Guófán raided Dàngshān,
and Zhú Kuí attacked and defeated him.
In the seventh month,
the rebels fled south and occupied Xúnyáng.
Gāozǔ sent Liú Zhōng and others to pursue them.
In the eighth month,
Sūn Jìgāo sailed the sea to attack Guǎngzhōu.
Huán Qiān gathered Shǔ troops at Zhījiāng.
〔一四〕Lú Xún's general, Xún Lín, raided Huáróng,
with the two forces about a hundred *lǐ* apart.
The Earl Wǔ of Línchuān attacked Huán Qiān,
and also attacked Xún Lín.
Xún Lín retreated and fled.
The Grand Administrator of Póyáng, Yúqiū Jìn, defeated the rebel's separate commander at Shàngráo.
〔一五〕In the ninth month,
the Earl Wǔ of Línchuān ordered Liú Zūn to attack Xún Lín at Bālíng,
and decapitated him.
Huán Dào'ér led Cài Měng towards Dàbó.
He also sent Liú Jī to attack them,
and decapitated Cài Měng.
In the tenth month,
Gāozǔ led a naval force on a southern expedition.
At this time, Xú Dàofù led more than 20,000 men to attack Jīngzhōu.
The Earl Wǔ of Línchuān resisted them.
They fought at Jiāngjīn,
and he greatly defeated them,
slaying and annihilating eighteen or nineteen tenths of their force.
Dàofù abandoned his warships and fled.
In the eleventh month,
Liú Zhōng defeated the rebel army at Nánlíng.
On the day Guǐchǒu,
the Grand Administrator of Yìzhōu, Bāo Lòu, died at Báidì.
Qiáo Dàofú attacked and captured his forces.
On the day Gēngxū,
Sūn Jìgāo attacked Guǎngzhōu,
and captured it.
In the twelfth month,
Gāozǔ was at Dàléi,
and engaged the rebels in battle,
greatly defeating them.
The rebels fled to Zuǒlǐ,
where he advanced and attacked,
again defeating them.
Eighteen or nineteen tenths of them died.
The rebels returned to Guǎngzhōu,
and Liú Fān and others pursued them.
In the seventh year (411 CE), in the second month,
Liú Fān captured Shǐxīng city,
and decapitated Xú Dàofù.
Lú Xún returned to Pānyú,
and attacked and besieged Sūn Jìgāo but could not conquer him.
He fled to Jiāozhōu,
where the Grand Administrator of Jiāozhōu, Dù Huìdù, decapitated him.
In the fourth month,
Dào Yànzhī attacked Qiáo Dàofú at Báidì,
and captured it.
In the fourth year of Yìxī (408 CE), in the first month, on the day Gēngzǐ,

Empress Wáng died.

Liú Fān and Xiè Hùn were executed,

In the third month of the ninth year (413 CE),
Zhūgě Chángmín was executed.
The western barbarians attacked the Qiāng garrison at Āndìng

In the twelfth month,
Zhū Língshí marched to conquer Shǔ.
In the seventh month of the ninth year,
Zhū Língshí destroyed Shǔ.
In the second month, on the *bǐngwǔ* day, of the 9th year of Yìxī
Yínghuò and Zhēnxīng both encroached upon Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"Qín will have troops."
In the third month, on the *rénchén* day,
Suìxīng, Yínghuò, Zhēnxīng, and Tàibái gathered in Dōngjǐng,
following Suìxīng.
Yínghuò entered Yúguǐ.
Tàibái encroached upon Nánhé.
Initially, in the 3rd year of Yìxī,
four stars gathered in Kuí.
Kuí and Lóu
are the division of Xúzhōu.
At that time, Mùróng Chāo usurped the title in Qí,
invading Xú and Yǎn,
plundering for years,
reaching the Huái and Sì Rivers.
Yáo Xīng and Qiáo Zòng usurped the false Qín and Shǔ.
Lú Xún and Mù Mò
invaded from both north and south.
In the 5th year,
Gāozǔ eliminated the Xianbei in the north;
this was the fulfillment of the four stars gathering in Kuí.
In the 9th year,
they again gathered in Dōngjǐng.
Dōngjǐng
is the division of Qín.
In the 13th year,
Gāozǔ pacified Guānzhōng,
which was also its fulfillment.
And the multitudes of villains like Zòng and Xún
had all been eliminated.
At this, heaven and humanity turned their hopes,
and the state was established in old Xú.
In the 2nd year of Yuánxī,
he received the mandate and accepted the abdication;
these were all its omens.
The Star Canon says:
"If four stars combine,
this is called Tàiyáng.
That country will have both military disasters and mourning,
noblemen will worry,
and commoners will flee.
If five stars combine,
this is called Yìxíng (change of mandate).
The virtuous will receive blessings,
a king will be established anew,
and possess the four quarters;
the unvirtuous will receive punishment,
their country will be separated,
and their ancestral temples destroyed."
Now, examining the surviving old texts,
there are three instances of five stars gathering: Zhōu and Hàn achieved kingship, Qí achieved hegemony.
(When Zhōu was about to attack Yīn,
five stars gathered in Fáng.
When Qí Huán was about to become hegemon,
five stars gathered in Jī.
When Hàn Gāo entered Qín,
five stars gathered in Dōngjǐng.)
As for Qí, it remained a marquis-earldom to the end,
and ultimately had no change of dynastic era.
Thus, there are instances where a five-star gathering does not signify Yìxíng.
There are nine instances of four stars gathering: Hàn Guāngwǔ and Jìn Yuándì both achieved restoration,
while Wèi and Sòng both changed their dynastic eras.
Thus, there are instances where a four-star gathering does signify Yìxíng.
In the past, in the 4th year of Yuánshǐ of Hàn Píngdì,
four stars gathered in Liǔ and Zhāng,
each for five days.
Liǔ and Zhāng
are the division of Sānhé.
Later there were the rebellions of Wáng Mǎng and Chìméi,
but Guāngwǔ restored the empire in Luò.
In the 6th year of Yǒngjiā of Jìn Huáidì,
four stars gathered in Niú and Nǚ.
Later there were the rebellions of Liú Cōng and Shí Lè,
but Yuánhuáng restored the empire in Yángtǔ.
In the 1st year of Chūpíng of Hàn Xiàndì,
four stars gathered in Xīn,
and again gathered in Jī and Wěi.
Xīn
is the division of Yùzhōu.
Later there were the tyrannical rebellions of Dǒng Zhuó and Lǐ Què,
and the rampant disturbances of the Huángjīn and Hēishān,
but Wèi Wǔ escorted the emperor to Xǔ,
and thus pacified Yǎn and Yù;
this was its fulfillment.
One account says:
"Xīn represents the Son of Heaven.
Great armies ascend the palace,
a sign of great chaos in the world."
Hán Fù believed Wěi and Jī were omens of Yān's rise,
and therefore supported Liú Yú, the governor of Yōuzhōu.
Yú both refused him
and soon perished,
which was indeed wrong.
Wěi represents Yān,
and also Wú.
This refers either to Gōngsūn Dù
or Sūn Quán.
Dù, though occupying a remote and humble region,
still performed suburban sacrifices and prepared offerings,
all of which constituted a change from Hàn.
In the 22nd year of Jiàn'ān,
four stars again gathered.
In the 25th year, Wèi Wén received the abdication;
this was the third gathering of four stars signifying Yìxíng.
The officials of Shǔ also cited a later gathering as a fulfillment for Liú Bèi.
According to records, in the 19th year of Tàiyuán and the 9th month of the 3rd year of Yìxī,
four stars each gathered once,
and Sòng possessed the empire,
which is the same as Wèi.
Yú Huàn said:
"Five stars gathered in Jìfāng,
and Wèi possessed the empire."
Yínghuò entered Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"Military disasters and mourning."
Tàibái encroached upon Nánhé.
The prognostication said:
"Troops will rise."
All were later fulfilled.

That winter,
Tàizǐ Zhànshì Fàn Yè plotted rebellion and was executed.
In the first month of the twenty-third year of Yuánjiā,
Jīn (Venus) and Huǒ (Mars) shone against each other.
That month,
the Suǒ ("Barbarian") bandits raided Qīngzhōu,
driving away and seizing households.
In the first month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuánjiā,
the Moon violated the great star of Xīn.
All the celestial stars flowed westward,
many were small,
none larger than a chicken's egg,
with tails of varying lengths.
There must have been several hundred,
stopping only when the daylight stabilized at dawn.
Some entered Běidǒu Zǐgōng.
The prognostication:
"Wherever groups of meteors rush,
troops will gather there,
and there will be great urgency."
Another prognostication:
"When many stars flow together,
generals will all raise armies.
Follow where the stars go,
to respond to the celestial omen."
Another prognostication:
"When a meteor enters Zǐgōng,
there will be a death,
and an imbalance of floods and droughts."
Another prognostication:
"When a meteor enters Běidǒu,
a high official will be imprisoned."
Another prognostication:
"Meteors represent the people;
large stars are high officials falling,
small stars are common people falling."
In the fourth month,
Tàibái (Venus) was seen in daylight.
In the eighth month,
Zhēngběi Dàjiāngjūn Héngyángwáng Yìjì passed away.
In Yùzhāng, the commoner Hú Dànshì led his clan to break into commanderies and counties,
killing the Administrator and the County Magistrate.
In the first month of the twenty-fifth year of Yuánjiā,
Mars and Mercury entered Yǔlín.
The moon encroached upon Suìxīng.
Tàibái was seen in daylight traversing the sky.
In the tenth month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuánjiā,
a comet entered Tàiwēi.
In the eleventh month,
a white qi pierced the Běidǒu.
In the summer of the twenty-seventh year,
Tàibái was seen in daylight traversing the sky.
In the ninth month,
Tàibái encroached upon Suìxīng.
In the tenth month,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi.
In the fifth month of the twenty-eighth year of Yuánjiā,
a comet was seen in Juǎnshé,
entered Tàiwēi,
approached Dìzuò,
encroached upon Shàngxiàng,
brushed Píng,
exited Duānmén,
and extinguished Yì and Zhěn.
Yì and Zhěn
are the division of Jīngzhōu.
Tàibái was seen in daylight encroaching upon Kūxīng.
In the thirtieth year,
the crown prince's sorcery and curses were discovered,
and he consequently murdered court officials.
In the first year of Xiàojiàn,
the two prefectures of Jīng and Jiāng rebelled,
and both were annihilated.
Juǎnshé
is an omen of sorcery and curses,
and the appearance of the comet
was its manifestation.
In the first month of the twenty-ninth year of Yuánjiā,
Tàibái was seen in daylight,
traversing the sky.
The following year,
the Eastern Palace committed regicide.
In the second month of the first year of Xiàowǔ Xiàojiàn,
a shooting star as large as the moon traveled westward.
That year,
Rú Shuǎng, the Inspector of Yùzhōu, rebelled and was executed.
On the Rén-yín day of the ninth month of the first year of Xiàojiàn,
Yínghuò encroached upon Zuǒzhífǎ.
Jiànpíngwáng Hóng, the Minister of the Left of the Department of State Affairs, submitted a memorial requesting to resign,
but it was not granted.
On the Yǐ-chǒu day of the tenth month of the first year of Xiàojiàn,
Yínghuò encroached upon Jìnxiánxīng.
Xiè Zhuāng, the Minister of Personnel, submitted a memorial requesting to resign,
but it was not granted.
On the Yǐ-wèi day of the fifth month of the second year of Xiàojiàn,
Yínghuò entered Nándǒu.
On the Jiǎ-chén day of the tenth month,
it again entered Nándǒu.
In the summer of the first year of Dàmíng,
the capital suffered an epidemic.
On the Wù-xū day of the fourth month of the third year of Xiàojiàn,
Tàibái encroached upon Yúguǐ.
The prognostication stated:
"The people will suffer much illness."
In the summer of the following year,
the capital suffered an epidemic.
On the Jiǎ-wǔ day of the eighth month of the third year of Xiàojiàn,
Tàibái entered Xīn.
The prognostication stated:
"In nine years,
a great famine will arrive."
In the eighth year of Dàmíng,
the eastern lands suffered a great famine,
and twelve or thirteen out of ten died.
On the Guǐ-hài day of the third month of the first year of Dàmíng,
Tàibái was south of Kuí
and encroached upon Suìxīng.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be an extermination of feudal lords."
Three years later,
Sīkōng Jìnglǐngwáng Dàn rebelled and was executed.
On the Bǐng-shēn day of the sixth month of the first year of Dàmíng,
the moon was in Dōngbì
and obscured Yínghuò.
The prognostication stated:
"A general will suffer misfortune;
the period will not exceed three years."
In the third year,
Sīkōng Jìnglǐngwáng Dàn rebelled.
On the Xīn-wèi day of the third month of the second year of Dàmíng,
Yínghuò entered Dōngjǐng.
On the Jǐ-hài day of the fourth month,
Yínghuò was north of Dōngjǐng and encroached upon the second star of Xuānyuán.
Jǐng
is the division of Yōngzhōu.
In the fourth month of that year,
Hǎilíngwáng Xiūmào was appointed Inspector of Yōngzhōu;
in the fifth year,
Xiūmào rebelled and was executed.
On the Jǐ-sì day of the seventh month of the second year of Dàmíng,
the moon obscured the second star of Xuānyuán.
On the Xīn-mǎo day of the tenth month,
the moon obscured Xuānyuán.
On the Bǐng-xū day of the eleventh month,
the moon again obscured Xuānyuán.
Xuānyuán
represents the empress or female ruler.
At that time, there were public rumors that the ruler's inner court was not in order.
On the Gēng-xū day of the eleventh month of the second year of Dàmíng,
Yínghuò encroached upon Fáng and Gōuqín.
On the Rén-zǐ day,
Yínghuò again encroached upon Gōuqín.
The prognostication stated:
"There will be war."
That year,
the Suǒ cavalry attacked Lìxià,
and the Yǔlín army was dispatched to defeat them.
In the first month of spring in the third year of Dà Míng, one night,
a penetrating cloud reached the heavens.
Red vapors rose in the four directions,
three or four chi long,
appearing and disappearing suddenly,
then all vanished.
This phenomenon is named Suí Xīng,
or alternatively, Dāo Xīng.
It signifies that there will be wars in the world,
with battles and bloodshed.
The moon entered Tài Wēi
and trespassed upon Cì Jiāng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be rebellious subjects who die,
and generals will be executed."
In the third month,
the moon was in Fáng
and trespassed upon Gōu Qián,
then was eclipsed.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler is displeased;
generals will die."
In the third month,
the planet Saturn guarded Qiān Niú.
The prognostication said:
"Great personages will suffer from illness;
troops will rise;
there will be a great amnesty;
treacherous officials and wicked sons will plot to assassinate the ruler."
In the fourth month,
it trespassed upon Wǔ Zhū Hóu.
The prognostication said:
"Feudal lords will be executed."
Venus and Mercury conjoined in the west.
The prognostication said:
"Troops will rise."
In the fifth month,
Jupiter trespassed upon Dōng Jǐng Yuè.
The prognostication said:
"Axes and yue will be used;
high officials will be executed."
In the sixth month,
the moon entered Nán Dǒu.
The prognostication said:
"High officials and great generals will be executed."
Soon after, the Inspector of Nán Yān Zhōu, Jìng Líng Wáng Dàn, occupied Guǎng Líng and rebelled.
He dispatched Chē Qí Dà Jiāng Jūn Shěn Qìng Zhī to lead the elite Yǔ Lín troops, along with the forces of Yù Zhōu Cì Shǐ Zōng Yuè and Xú Zhōu Cì Shǐ Liú Dào Lóng, to attack and fight.
Upon the capture of the city,
all men and women, both secular and monastic, within the city
were beheaded and eliminated, none spared.
General Zōng Yuè particularly employed cruel tortures;
first, he would disembowel and gouge out eyes,
or whip faces and lash bellies,
pouring bitter wine into wounds,
and only then applying knives and saws.
This was the manifestation of a great war.
In the eighth month,
the moon trespassed upon Tài Bái.
Tài Bái trespassed upon Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler will have worries;
the Son of Heaven will be displeased."
Mars guarded Bì.
The prognostication said:
"The myriad people will starve;
there will be a great war."
In the ninth month,
Tài Bái trespassed upon Nán Dǒu.
The prognostication said:
"High officials will rebel."
In the ninth month,
the moon was in Wèi and was eclipsed;
afterward,
it again trespassed upon Mars in Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"Troops will rise;
a female ruler will be affected;
the ruler will be displeased."
Another interpretation said:
"A female ruler will have worries;
kings will die;
the people will starve."
In the tenth month,
Tài Bái trespassed upon Kū Xīng.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler will hear sounds of weeping."
Thereafter, there were many deaths in the six palaces;
princesses passed away,
and the Son of Heaven mourned repeatedly.
There was a great drought that year,
and the people starved.
In the first month of the fourth year of Dà Míng,
the moon obscured Dǐ.
The prognostication said:
"A great general will die."
It also trespassed upon the second star north of Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be rebellious officials plotting against their ruler."
In the second month,
there was a red vapor over one chi long,
north of the imperial seat in Tài Bái.
The prognostication said:
"Troops will rise;
officials will plot against their ruler."
In the fifth month,
the moon entered Tài Wēi.
The prognostication said:
"There will be rebellious officials;
high officials will die."
In the sixth month,
Tài Bái trespassed upon Jǐng Yuè.
The prognostication said:
"Troops will rise;
axes and yue will be used;
high officials will be executed."
The moon trespassed upon the star in front of Xīn.
The prognostication said:
"There will be rebellious officials;
the crown prince will be displeased."
The moon entered the center of Nán Dǒu Kuí.
The prognostication said:
"Great personages will have worries;
a female ruler will be displeased."
In the seventh month,
Jupiter trespassed upon Jī Shī.
The prognostication said:
"High officials will be executed."
In the twelfth month,
the moon trespassed upon the central great star of Xīn.
The prognostication said:
"Great personages will have worries."
In the twelfth month,
clouds permeated the heavens,
rising simultaneously in the west and northeast,
converging in eight places,
all four chi long,
appearing and disappearing suddenly,
then quickly vanishing completely.
The prognostication said:
"There will be wars in the world."
In the twelfth month,
the moon trespassed upon the northeast star of Jī.
A female ruler will be displeased.
The following year,
the Inspector of Yōng Zhōu, Hǎi Líng Wáng Xiū Mào, rebelled.
Tài Bái trespassed upon Dōng Jǐng.
This was the manifestation of the Yōng Zhōu military rebellion.
In the first month of the fifth year of Dàmíng,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) trespassed into Yúguǐ (Ghost Mansion) and Jīshī (Accumulated Corpses).
The prognostication stated:
“Ministers will be executed,
the ruler will have worries,
and treasures will be dispersed.”
The moon entered the center of Nándǒu (Southern Dipper) ‘s ladle.
The prognostication stated:
“High officials will have worries,
and there will be war under Heaven.”
Huǒ (Mars) and Tǔ (Saturn) were together in Xūnǚ (Maid).
The prognostication stated:
“The empress will dislike it.”
In the third month,
the moon occulted Xuānyuán (Regulus/Leo).
The prognostication stated:
“The empress will dislike it.”
There were tens of millions of meteors,
some long, some short,
some large, some small,
all moving westward,
and stopping at dawn.
The prognostication stated:
“The sovereign will dislike it,
and the people will scatter and perish.”
In the fourth month,
Tàibái (Venus) trespassed into Dōngjǐng (Eastern Well) ‘s Běiyuán (Northern Wagon).
The prognostication stated:
“Ministers will cause chaos,
and executions will be carried out.”
Tàibái (Venus) trespassed into Yúguǐ (Ghost Mansion).
The prognostication stated:
“Ministers will be executed,
executions will be carried out,
and the ruler will have worries.”
In the sixth month,
there was a white meteor,
as large as an earthenware bowl,
emerging from Wángliáng (Charioteer),
moving southwest,
disappearing into Tiānshì (Heavenly Market),
its tail tens of *zhàng* long,
and its afterglow lingering for a long time after it vanished.
The prognostication stated:
“There will be chaos under Heaven.”
In the eighth month,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Dōngjǐng (Eastern Well).
The prognostication stated:
“Ministers will bear the brunt.”
In the tenth month,
Suìxīng (Jupiter) trespassed into Tàiwēi (Supreme Palace) ‘s Shàngjiàngxīng (General Star).
Tàibái (Venus) entered Kàng (Neck),
and trespassed into the second southern star.
The prognostication stated:
“The top general will have worries,
a trusted minister will be executed,
and the ruler will dislike it.”
In the tenth month,
Tàibái (Venus) entered Dī (Root).
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Jǐng (Well).
The prognostication stated:
“The king will lose territory,
there will be a great amnesty,
war will break out,
and there will be famine.”
The moon entered Tàiwēi (Supreme Palace),
occulting Xīfān Shàngjiàng (Western Barbarian General),
and trespassing into Suìxīng (Jupiter).
The prognostication stated:
“There will be a rebel minister who dies.”
A large star, as large as a *dǒu* (ladle),
emerged from Liǔ (Willow), moving north,
its tail over ten *zhàng* long,
disappearing into Zǐgōng (Purple Palace),
its afterglow lingering for a long time before extinguishing.
The prognostication stated:
“Calamity under Heaven,
with war and death,
which the Son of Heaven will dislike.”
In the eleventh month,
the moon occulted the first star of Xīn (Heart),
and also trespassed into a large star.
The prognostication stated:
“High officials will have worries,
war will break out,
and there will be a great drought.”
In the twelfth month,
Tàibái (Venus) trespassed into Xījiàn (Western Establishment) ‘s central star.
The prognostication stated:
“Ministers will slander each other.”
The moon trespassed into Zuǒjiǎo (Left Horn).
The prognostication stated:
“The Son of Heaven will dislike it.”
Three years later,
Xiàowǔdì and Wénmù Huánghòu died one after another;
the successor to the throne, after one year in power,
executed chancellors, grand counselors, and generals,
brutally killed court officials,
and brought disaster upon the imperial clan,
subsequently suffering harm himself.
In the first month of the sixth year of Dàmíng,
the moon was in Zhāng (Extended Net),
and trespassed into Suìxīng (Jupiter).
The prognostication stated:
“The people will suffer famine and scatter to their deaths.”
The moon trespassed into the rear star of Xīn (Heart).
The prognostication stated:
“The prince will dislike it.”
In the second month,
the moon occulted Zuǒjiǎo (Left Horn).
The prognostication stated:
“The Son of Heaven will dislike it.”
In the third month,
Yínghuò (Mars) entered Yúguǐ (Ghost Mansion).
The prognostication stated:
“There will be war,
ministers will be executed,
and there will be many epidemics under Heaven.”
In the fifth month,
the moon was in Zhāng (Extended Net),
and also entered Tàiwēi (Supreme Palace),
trespassing into Yínghuò (Mars).
The prognostication stated:
“The ruler of the state will be uneasy,
and the empress will have worries.”
Huǒ (Mars) trespassed into Mù (Jupiter) in Yì (Wings).
The prognostication stated:
“There will be famine,
there will be drought,
and close officials and ministers will plot against the ruler.”
There was a star, red in front and white behind,
as large as an earthenware bowl,
its tail over ten *zhàng* long,
emerging from Dōngbì (Eastern Wall) ‘s north,
moving west and disappearing into Tiānshì (Heavenly Market),
making a chirping sound.
The prognostication stated:
“There will be war below it,
and chaos under Heaven.”
The moon occulted the seven stars of Mǎo (Pleiades).
The prognostication stated:
“Noble ministers will be executed,
the Son of Heaven will defeat the Xiōngnú,
and the Hú ruler will die.”
Suìxīng (Jupiter) trespassed into Shàngjiàng (General).
The prognostication stated:
“Trusted ministers will be executed,
and the top general will have worries.”
In the sixth month,
the moon entered Tàiwēi (Supreme Palace),
trespassing into Yòuzhífǎ (Right Law Enforcer).
The prognostication stated:
“The ruler will be uneasy,
there will be great alarm under Heaven,
the ruler will suffer ill fortune,
and the law enforcer will be executed.”
The moon trespassed into the rear star of Xīn (Heart).
The prognostication stated:
“The prince will dislike it.”
In the seventh month,
the moon trespassed into Jī (Winnowing Basket).
The prognostication stated:
“The empress will dislike it.”
In the eighth month,
the moon entered the center of Nándǒu (Southern Dipper) ‘s ladle.
The prognostication stated:
“Ministers will be executed,
executions will be carried out,
and Wú and Yuè will have worries.”
In the following year,
Yáng and Nánxúzhōu experienced a great drought,
fields and grains yielded no harvest,
and the people scattered and died.
For the three years thereafter,
the emperor and empress successively passed away;
the chancellors, Grand Masters of Records, and Directors of the Imperial Secretariat were executed;
the Sǔoluǒ ruler died;
the princes of Xīn'ān were harmed;
Sītú Yùzhāngwáng Zǐshàng died;
and the Yǔlín (Forest of Feathers) soldiers entered Sānwú to suppress rebels.
In the first month of the seventh year of Dà Míng, at night,
a celestial light pierced through thin clouds.
From the four directions, there were eight qi,
pale white,
two to three zhàng long,
appearing and disappearing abruptly.
They were named "dagger stars."
The prognostication said:
"There will be war in the land."
In the third month,
the moon encroached upon the star behind Xīn.
The prognostication said:
"The secondary sons will suffer misfortune."
In the fourth month,
Huǒ encroached upon Jīn,
in Lóu.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a funeral,
there will be war,
a great battle."
In the sixth month,
the moon encroached upon Jī.
The prognostication said:
"The empress will suffer misfortune."
Tài Bái entered Dōng Jǐng.
The prognostication said:
"A high minister will bear the consequences."
Tài Bái encroached upon Dōng Jǐng.
The prognostication said:
"High ministers will cause chaos,
and axes will be used."
In the seventh month,
Yíng Huò entered Dōng Jǐng.
The prognostication said:
"Troops will rise,
and a great general will bear the consequences."
The moon entered the first star of Nán Dǒu,
encroaching upon the second star.
The prognostication said:
"Important figures will be troubled,
and Wújùn will bear the consequences."
Tài Bái encroached upon Yú Guǐ.
The prognostication said:
"Troops will rise,
great generals will be executed,
the ruler will be troubled,
and wealth will be expended."
In the eighth month,
the moon entered the middle of Kū Xīng.
Tài Bái encroached upon Xuān Yuán Shǎo Wēi Xīng.
The prognostication said:
"The ruler will be troubled,
there will be sounds of crying,
and the people will suffer famine and become displaced."
Tài Bái entered Tài Wēi.
The prognostication said:
"Close ministers will raise troops,
and the state will be unstable."
Yíng Huò encroached upon Guǐ.
Tài Bái encroached upon Yòu Zhí Fǎ.
The prognostication said:
"High ministers will be executed."
In the tenth month,
Jīn and Shuǐ encroached upon each other.
The prognostication said:
"There will be famine in the land."
Yíng Huò guarded the second star of Xuān Yuán.
The prognostication said:
"There will be trouble in the palace,
and sorrow."
In the eleventh month,
Suì Xīng entered Dī.
The prognostication said:
"Among the feudal lords and rulers, there will be those who enter the palace."
In the twelfth month,
the moon encroached upon Wǔ Chē.
The prognostication said:
"The celestial armory's weapons will be set in motion."
Two years later,
the emperor and empress passed away,
high ministers and prime ministers were executed and annihilated,
imperial princes were murdered,
the Empress Dowager passed away,
troops rose in the four directions,
and various armies were dispatched to spearhead punitive expeditions.
In the first month of the eighth year of Dà Míng,
the moon occulted Yú Guǐ.
The prognostication said:
"High ministers will be executed."
The moon entered the middle of Nán Dǒu Kuí,
occulting the second star.
The prognostication said:
"Important figures will be troubled,
and the empress will suffer misfortune."
In the second month,
the moon encroached upon the fourth star of Nán Dǒu,
entering the middle of the first star.
The prognostication said:
"Important figures will be troubled,
and the empress will bear the consequences.
Yùzhāng will suffer disaster."
In the fourth month,
the moon entered the middle of Nán Dǒu Kuí,
encroaching upon the third star.
The prognostication said:
"Important figures will be troubled,
and the empress will suffer misfortune.
Dānyáng will bear the consequences."
Tài Bái entered Dōng Jǐng,
entered Tài Wēi,
and encroached upon Zhí Fǎ.
The prognostication said:
"Zhí Fǎ will be executed,
close ministers will raise troops,
and the state will be unstable."
In the sixth month,
Suì Xīng encroached upon Dī.
The prognostication said:
"The year will see a great famine."
There was a shooting star as large as a five-dǒu urn,
red and luminous,
illuminating human faces,
with a tail more than one zhàng long,
traveling from the north of Shēn to the east,
descending directly through Dōng Jǐng,
passing over Nán Hé,
and vanishing.
The prognostication said:
"The people will suffer famine,
and Wú and Yuè will have war."
In the seventh month,
Suì Xīng entered Dī.
In the tenth month,
Tài Bái guarded Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be war,
and a great funeral."
The moon occulted and eclipsed Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a funeral,
and a great famine."
After this, the state still had a great funeral;
Dānyáng Yǐn Yán Shībó and Yùzhāng Wáng Zǐshàng died.
The next year,
Zhāo Tài Hòu passed away.
Bandits rose in the four directions,
and the imperial armies campaigned by water and land.
A great battle occurred in Yìxīng Jìnlíng Xiàn,
with thousands killed and wounded.
In the first month Dīngyǒu of Yǒngguāng first year of the former Emperor Fèi,
Tài Bái occulted Qiān Niú.
Qiān Niú overran its boundary.
In the same month Gēngshēn,
the moon was in Xū Sù,
encroaching upon Tài Bái.
Xū
is the territory of Qí.
In the second month Jiǎshēn,
the moon entered Nán Dǒu.
Nán Dǒu
is the field of Yángzhōu.
It also represents high officials.
In the third month Gēngzǐ,
the moon entered Yú Guǐ,
encroaching upon Jī Shī.
Yú Guǐ presides over executions.
In the sixth month Gēngwǔ,
Yíng Huò entered Dōng Jǐng.
Dōng Jǐng
is the division of Yōngzhōu.
In the same month Rénwǔ,
there was a large shooting star,
red in front and white behind,
entering Zǐ Gōng.
In the ninth month Dīngyǒu of Jǐnghé first year,
Yíng Huò entered Xuān Yuán,
located north of the great star of the empress.
In the tenth month,
Yíng Huò entered Tài Wēi,
encroaching upon Xī Shàng Jiàng.
In the eleventh month Dīngwèi,
Tài Bái encroached upon Kū Xīng.
In the same month Yǐmǎo,
the moon encroached upon Xīn.
Xīn represents the Celestial King.
In that year,
Tài Zǎi Jiāngxià Wáng Yìgōng, Shàngshū Lìng Liǔ Yuánjǐng, Shàngshū Púyè Yán Shībó and others were all executed.
Tài Wèi Shěn Qìngzhī died.
Lúlíng Wáng Jìngxiān, Nánpíng Wáng Jìngyóu, Nán'ān Hóu Jìngyuān were all granted death.
The deposed emperor perished.
The next year,
Kuàijī Tàishǒu Xúnyáng Wáng Zǐfáng, Guǎngzhōu Cìshǐ Yuán Tányuǎn, Yōngzhōu Cìshǐ Yuán Yǐ, Qīngzhōu Cìshǐ Shěn Wénxiù all rebelled.
Zhāo Tài Hòu passed away.
In the first year of Tàishǐ of Emperor Míng, in the twelfth month, on the day Jǐsì,
Tàibái entered Yǔlín.
The prognostication said:
"Yǔlín's troops will move."
On the day Yǐhài,
white qi entered Zǐgōng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a funeral."
The next year,
Yǔlín's troops went out to attack.
Empress Dowager Zhāo collapsed.
In the second year of Tàishǐ, in the first month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
Yínghuò retrograded, residing southwest of Píng.
The prognostication said:
"There are troops in the center."
In that month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
the moon haloed Wǔchē,
extending through Bì and Mǎo.
The prognostication said:
"The empress dislikes this."
In that month, on the day Gēngzǐ,
the moon trespassed Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"A general will die."
In that month, on the day Jiǎyín,
a meteor shot out from Wǔchē,
and disappeared in the western wall of Zǐgōng.
The prognostication said:
"There will be troops."
In that month, on the day Bǐngchén,
black qi penetrated the constellations.
The prognostication said:
"Kings and marquises will have their bones returned."
In the third month, on the day Yǐwèi,
there were innumerable meteors, large and small, moving westward,
until dawn when they ceased.
The prognostication said:
"An omen of migrating people."
In the fourth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Yínghuò entered Tàiwēi,
and trespassed the Right Law Enforcer.
On the day Bǐngzǐ,
Suìxīng was seen during the day in the middle of Nándǒu's degree.
The prognostication said:
"That state will have military preparations,
and suffer a great defeat."
In that month, on the day Jǐmǎo,
throughout the night, there were over a hundred meteors moving southwest,
one as large as an earthenware bowl,
with a tail more than ten feet long,
black in color,
emerging from Hégǔ.
It was also said:
"There will be troops."
In that month, on the day Rénwǔ,
Tàibái was south of the moon and rose together in the east,
constituting a trespass.
The prognostication said:
"There will be a defeated army and a dead general,
and the ruler will lose territory."
In the seventh month, on the day Jiǎwǔ,
the moon trespassed Xīn.
Xīn is the territory of Sòng.
In that month, on the day Bǐngwǔ,
the moon trespassed Nándǒu.
The prognostication said:
"High officials will be executed."
In that month, on the day Yǐmǎo,
Yínghuò trespassed Dī.
Dī
is the division of Yǎnzhōu.
In the tenth month, on the day Xīnsì,
Tàibái entered Dī.
The prognostication said:
"Grain will be expensive in spring."
In the eleventh month, on the day Guǐsì,
Tàibái trespassed Fáng.
The prognostication said:
"Many oxen will die."
In that year,
the four directions rebelled,
the internal army was largely dispatched,
and the six armies personally went to war.
Empress Dowager Zhāo collapsed.
The Grand General Yīn Xiàozǔ was killed by southern bandits.
The Right Director of the Department of State Affairs, Cài Xīngzōng, on account of Yínghuò trespassing the Right Law Enforcer,
asked to resign,
but was not permitted.
In the ninth month,
all those who had rebelled in various regions were pacified,
and many surrendered.
Later, four prefectures north of the Huái River were lost,
Péngchéng and Yǎnzhōu were both overrun by the barbarians,
which was the verification of migrating people.
Péngchéng
is a division of Sòng.
That spring,
grain was expensive and the people starved.
The next year,
many oxen fell ill and died,
and an edict was issued to the Grand Provisioner to stop slaughtering oxen.
In the third year of Tàishǐ, in the sixth month, on the day Jiǎchén,
the moon trespassed Dōngjǐng.
The prognostication said:
"A military general will die."
Yínghuò trespassed Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"Gold and money will be dispersed."
It also said:
"Within sixty days,
there will certainly be a grand amnesty."
In the eighth month, on the day Guǐmǎo,
the Son of Heaven bestowed the empress's and the six palaces' clothing, gold hairpins, and sundry items upon the generals and soldiers on the northern expedition.
In the second month of the next year,
Protector-General Wáng Xuánmó died.
In the fourth year of Tàishǐ, in the sixth month, on the day Rén Yín,
Tàibái trespassed Yúguǐ.
The prognostication said:
"The people will suffer a great plague,
and their dead will not be collected."
In that year, a great epidemic spread throughout the realm.
In the fifth year of Tàishǐ, in the second month, on the day Bǐngxū,
the moon trespassed the Left Horn.
The prognostication said:
"The Son of Heaven will dislike it for three years."
In the third month, on the day Gēngshēn,
the moon trespassed Jiànxīng.
The prognostication said:
"The prime minister will be changed."
In the tenth month, on the day Rénwǔ,
the moon trespassed Bì.
The prognostication said:
"The Son of Heaven will apply the law,
and punishments will be severe;
there will be deaths among the nobles."
In that month, on the day Bǐngshēn,
Tàibái trespassed Kàng.
The prognostication said:
"Gather national troops to prepare against the north."
That winter,
Wáng Xiūrén, Prince of Jiàn'ān, was relieved of Yángzhōu,
and Wáng Xiūfàn, Prince of Guìyáng, became the governor of Yángzhōu.
The governor of Yángzhōu was always held by a prime minister,
which was the verification of a change in prime minister.
In the seventh year,
Wáng Xiūyòu, Prince of Jìnpíng, and Wáng Xiūrén, Prince of Jiàn'ān, were both killed.
At that time, Huáiběi was lost,
and garrisons were established to guard against the northern barbarians.
Three years later,
the imperial carriage departed (the emperor died).
In the sixth year of Tàishǐ, in the first month, on the day Xīnsì,
the moon trespassed the Left Horn.
The prognostication was the same as before.
In the eighth month, on the day Rénchén,
Yínghuò trespassed Nándǒu.
Nándǒu
is the division of Wú.
In the eleventh month, on the day Yǐhài,
the moon trespassed the Northeast Shaft.
The prognostication said:
"A great person will bear this."
It also said:
"There will be executions among the high officials."
Two years later,
Wáng Jǐngwén, Inspector of Yángzhōu, was killed.
The imperial carriage departed (the emperor died).
In the seventh month, on the day `bǐngshēn`, of the third year of Yuánhuī of the deposed Emperor Hòu,
Táibái entered Jué,
and encroached upon Suìxīng.
The divination stated:
"Jué is the gate of Heaven;
the state will have military affairs."
The divination also said:
"When Táibái and Mùxīng meet in Jué,
a killing army will be outside,
destroying armies and killing generals."
In that month, on the day `dīngsì`,
Táibái entered Dī.
Dī is the celestial palace of the Son of Heaven,
and Táibái is an inauspicious star for warfare.
In the eighth month, on the day `jǐsì`,
Táibái encroached upon the second star at the northern head of Fáng.
The divination stated:
"The king has lost his virtue."
In the ninth month, on the day `guǐmǎo`,
Táibái encroached upon the third star of Nándǒu.
The divination stated:
"A great person will be affected;
the state will change its government."
In the tenth month, on the day `bǐngxū`,
Suìxīng entered Dī.
The divination stated:
"A feudal lord or ruler will come and enter the palace."
In the eleventh month, on the day `gēngxū`,
the Moon entered Tàiwēi,
obscuring the southwestern star of the screen.
The divination stated:
"A noble will lose power."
In the seventh month of the fourth year,
Jiànpíng Wáng Jǐngsù rebelled at Jīngkǒu.
At that time, the deposed emperor's malevolence was boundless.
In the seventh month of the fifth year, he perished,
and Ānchéng Wáng ascended the imperial throne.
Three years later,
Qí received the abdication.
In the third month, on the day `yǐsì`, of the fourth year of Yuánhuī,
the Moon encroached upon the first star at the northern head of Fáng,
and further encroached upon the Jiànlì stars.
The divination stated:
"There are plans for hidden armed forces in the ancestral temple.
The Son of Heaven must not leave the palace or descend the hall;
there will be many violent events."
In the ninth month, on the day `jiǎchén`,
Zhēnxīng encroached upon the western wall of Tàiwēi.
The divination stated:
"A king will be established."
Another interpretation said:
"A king will be moved."
It also said:
"A great person will be troubled."
At that time, the deposed emperor's movements were unrestrained,
and he eventually perished because of this.
Ānchéng Wáng was established.
In the first month, on the day `wùshēn`, of the fifth year of Yuánhuī,
the Moon encroached upon the fifth star of Nándǒu.
The divination was the same as before.
In the fourth month, on the day `dīngsì`,
Yínghuò encroached upon the northwestern star of Yúguǐ.
The divination stated:
"A great person will be troubled;
the short term is sixty days,
the long term is six hundred days."
It also said:
"The ruler will suffer from it."
In that month, on the day `bǐngzǐ`,
Táibái encroached upon the northwestern star of Yúguǐ.
The divination stated:
"A grand amnesty."
In the fifth month, on the day `wùshēn`,
Táibái appeared in daylight at noon,
its light unusually bright.
The divination stated:
"A change of surname."
In the sixth month, on the day `rénxū`,
the Moon encroached upon the Gōugīng stars.
The divination stated:
"There will be a great decree."
In that month, on the day `yǐchǒu`,
the Moon encroached upon the fourth star of Nándǒu.
The divination was the same as before.
In the seventh month,
the deposed emperor perished,
and there was a grand amnesty throughout the realm.
Two years later,
Qí received the abdication.
In the eighth month, on the day `gēngshēn`, of the first year of Shēngmíng of Emperor Shùn,
the Moon entered Nándǒu,
and encroached upon the third star.
The divination was the same as before.
In the ninth month, on the day `dīnghài`,
Táibái was in Yì,
visible in daylight across the sky.
The divination stated:
"A change of surname."
On the night of the `guǐmǎo` day of the intercalary twelfth month,
the Moon obscured the fourth star of Nándǒu.
The divination was the same as before.
Collation Notes
Treatise 17, Auspicious Omens, Part 1
Those who embody wisdom and exhaust the subtleties,
containing divine essence and being uniquely outstanding,
are called sages.
They are able to rule the four seas and employ all things,
so that among living and inanimate beings,
none fail to find their proper place.
The hundred clans look up to them,
rejoicing as if with kin,
fragrant as pepper and orchids.
Therefore, flags, insignia, carriages, and robes are used to exalt them,
and the jade seal and yellow canopy to honor them,
with the gravity of divine artifacts,
placing them above the myriad people.
From those of average intelligence downwards,
they are merely servants to all things.
Nature and understanding vary in kind;
there truly exists the principle of folly and violence.
Seeing that a sage benefits the world,
they think the world can be used for their own benefit.
Seeing that all things return to the sage,
they claim to benefit all things.
Those who contend by force
even liken it to chasing a deer,
which is why there are so many rebellious officials and treacherous sons in the world.
A dragon soaring to the ninth-fifth position,
matching Heaven in its glorious abode,
possesses the symbols of receiving the mandate
and the harmony between Heaven and humanity.
The `Yì` says:
"The Yellow River brought forth the chart,
the Luò River brought forth the writing,
and the sage took them as models."
The meaning of auspicious omens is profound!
Before Hèxū and Suìrén,
nothing was heard of them.
Emperor Tàihào, Fúxīshì,
his mother was called Huáxū.
In the time of Suìrén,
there was a giant footprint in Léizé.
Huáxū stepped on it,
and gave birth to Fúxī in Chéngjì.
He had a serpent's body and a human head,
possessing sagely virtue.
When Suìrénshì died,
Fúxī succeeded him,
received the Dragon Chart,
and drew the Eight Trigrams.
This is what is meant by
"the Yellow River brought forth the chart."
He had the auspicious omen of the Brilliant Dragon.
Emperor Yándì, Shénnóngshì,
his mother was called Nǚdēng.
She wandered in Huáyáng,
and a divine dragon's head touched Nǚdēng on Chángyáng Shān,
giving birth to Yándì.
He had a human body and an ox head,
possessing sagely virtue,
and brought forth the auspicious omen of a great fire.
Auspicious grain grew,
and sweet springs emerged.
Huángdì Xuānyuánshì's
mother was Fùbǎo.
She saw a great flash of lightning encircling the pivot star of Běidǒu,
illuminating the wilds,
and conceived.
Twenty-five months later, Huángdì was born at Shòuqīu.
He could speak while still young,
had a dragon-like countenance,
and possessed sagely virtue.
He commanded a hundred deities to appear and serve him.
Yìnglóng attacked Chīyóu,
fighting with the strength of four beasts: tigers, leopards, bears, and grizzlies.
He used Nǚbá to stop the incessant rain.
When the world was settled,
his sagely virtue shone everywhere,
and all auspicious signs arrived.
There was a Qūyì zhí Cǎo (bending branch grass) growing in his courtyard;
when a fawning person entered the court,
the grass would point at them.
Thus, fawning people dared not approach.
There was the auspicious sign of Jǐngyún (auspicious clouds),
and a red qi and a blue qi were connected.
Within the red qi were two stars,
and within the blue qi was one star,
totaling three stars,
all yellow in color,
seen at Shèdī during clear weather.
They were named Jǐng Xīng (auspicious stars).
Huángdì, clad in yellow, fasted in the Central Palace,
sitting by the Xuánhù Luòshuǐ.
A Fènghuáng gathered,
not eating living insects,
not treading on living grass.
Sometimes it rested in the Emperor's eastern garden,
sometimes it nested in the Āgé pavilion,
and sometimes it sang in the courtyard.
Its male sang by itself,
its female danced by herself.
Qílín were in the park,
and divine birds came auspiciously.
There were great moles like sheep,
and great earthworms like rainbows.
Huángdì, by virtue of the ascendancy of the earth element,
therefore ruled as a king of earth virtue.
In the seventh month, Gēngshēn day, of the autumn of his fiftieth year,
heaven was foggy for three days and three nights,
with dim daylight.
Huángdì inquired of Tiānlǎo, Lìmù, and Róngchéng, saying:
"What do you gentlemen think?"
Tiānlǎo said:
"I have heard that
when a country is peaceful
and its ruler favors culture,
the Fènghuáng will reside there.
When a country is in chaos
and its ruler favors warfare,
the Fènghuáng will leave.
Now the Fènghuáng soars in the eastern suburbs and delights there;
its calls are in tune with Yízé,
matching Heaven.
Judging by this,
Heaven has a stern instruction to bestow upon the Emperor;
the Emperor must not transgress it."
Then he summoned the historian to divine,
but the tortoise shell scorched.
The historian said:
"I cannot interpret it.
One should ask a sage."
The Emperor said:
"I have already asked Tiānlǎo, Lìmù, and Róngchéng."
The historian, facing north, bowed twice and said:
"The tortoise does not contradict sagely wisdom,
hence it scorched."
When the fog cleared,
he traveled along the Luòshuǐ.
He saw a large fish,
and killed five sacrificial animals to offer a libation to it.
Then Heaven rained heavily
for seven days and seven nights.
The fish flowed into the sea,
and he obtained a chart and a book from it.
The Dragon Chart came out of the Hé,
and the Tortoise Book came out of the Luò,
with red patterns and seal script,
which were bestowed upon Xuānyuán.
Xuānyuán received all deities at Míngtíng;
this is now Hánmén Gǔkǒu.
Dì Zhì Shǎohào Shì's
mother was Nǚjié.
She saw a star like a rainbow
descend and flow into Huázhǔ.
Afterward, she dreamed of conception and was moved,
giving birth to Shǎohào.
Upon ascending the imperial throne,
there was the auspicious sign of the Fènghuáng.
Dì Zhuānxū Gāoyángshì's
mother was Nǚshū.
She saw the star Yáoguāng
pass through the moon like a rainbow,
and was moved at Yōufáng zhī Gōng,
giving birth to Zhuānxū at Ruòshuǐ.
He wore dry-ge (shield and dagger-axe) on his head,
and possessed sagely virtue.
At the age of ten, he assisted Shǎohào Shì;
at twenty, he ascended the imperial throne.
Dì Kù Gāoxīnshì
was born with fused teeth,
and possessed sagely virtue,
succeeding Gāoyángshì to rule the world.
He ordered drummers to beat the drums,
and strike bells and chimes;
the Fènghuáng flapped its wings and danced.
Di Yáo’s mother was named Qìngdū.
She was born in the wilds of Dǒuwéi,
where yellow clouds often covered and protected her.
When she grew up,
she observed the Sānhé,
and a dragon constantly followed her.
One day, a dragon arrived bearing a diagram.
Its inscription’s main message was:
“You also receive Heaven’s blessing.”
Her eyebrows had eight colors,
her temple hair was seven chi and two cùn long,
her face was sharp at the top and full at the bottom,
and her feet trod on the Yì constellation.
Soon, a yin wind gathered from all four directions,
and a red dragon was aroused by it.
She was pregnant for fourteen months and gave birth to Yáo at Dānlíng,
whose appearance was as described in the diagram.
When he grew up,
he was ten chi tall,
possessed sagely virtue,
and was enfeoffed in Táng.
He dreamt of climbing to heaven.
When Gāoxīnshì declined,
the world turned to him.
He was on the imperial throne for seventy years,
during which a auspicious star appeared in the Yì constellation,
phoenixes nested in the courtyard,
scarlet grass grew,
auspicious grain ripened,
sweet dew moistened,
and sweet spring water flowed.
The sun and moon were like a conjoined bi-disk,
and the five planets were like a string of pearls.
From within, meat grew spontaneously,
as thin as a fan.
When moved, it generated wind,
and the food remained cold and did not rot.
It was named
“Shàfǔ.”
There was also a plant that grew beside the steps.
On the first day of the lunar month, one pod would sprout;
by the middle of the month, fifteen pods would have grown.
After the sixteenth day,
one pod would fall each day,
until the end of the month when all were gone.
If the month was short, one pod would wither but not fall.
It was named
“Mìngjiá,”
also called
“Lìjiá.”
He attributed his achievements to Shùn,
and intended to abdicate the throne to him.
So he purified himself and prepared an altar site at the Hé and Luò rivers,
chose an auspicious day,
and led Shùn and others up Shǒushān,
following the riverbank.
There, five elders were strolling,
who were indeed the essences of the five planets.
They said to each other:
“The Hétú will soon come to inform the emperor of the appointed time.
He who knows me is the double-pupiled Huáng Yáo.”
The five elders then transformed into shooting stars,
and ascended into the Mǎo constellation.
In the dim light of the xīnchǒu day of the second month,
the rituals were completed.
Towards sunset,
a glorious light emerged from the Hé,
and auspicious energy filled the four quarters.
White clouds arose,
and swirling winds shook.
Then, a dragon-horse appeared, bearing a diagram,
with red patterns on a green body,
stopping at the altar.
It spat out the diagram and departed.
The diagram resembled a turtle,
nine chi wide on its back.
Its chart had a white jade cover,
with characters of red jade,
sealed with yellow gold,
and bound with blue cords.
The cover inscription read:
“Kǎisè will bestow upon Di Shùn.”
It meant that Yú, Xià, Yīn, Zhōu, Qín, and Hàn were destined to receive the Mandate of Heaven.
The emperor then copied its words
and stored them in the eastern wing.
Two years later, in the zhōngxīn month of the second month,
he led his ministers to sink bi-disks into the Luò river.
When the ritual was complete,
he waited.
Towards late afternoon,
a red light arose,
and a black turtle emerged bearing a book.
The red patterns on its back shell formed characters,
and it stopped at the altar.
The book spoke of abdicating to Shùn.
Thus, he yielded to Shùn.
Di Shùn Yǒuyúshì’s
mother was named Wòdēng.
She saw a great rainbow and conceived,
giving birth to Shùn at Yáoxū.
His eyes had double pupils,
hence he was named Chónghuá.
He had a dragon-like face and a large mouth,
was dark-skinned,
and six chi and one cùn tall.
Shùn’s parents hated Shùn.
They made him plaster the granary,
and then set fire to it from below.
Shùn wore a bird-worker's outfit and flew away.
They also made him dredge a well,
and then filled it with stones from above.
Shùn wore a dragon-worker's outfit and emerged from the side.
He farmed at Lìshān,
and dreamt that his eyebrows were as long as his hair.
When he ascended to the imperial throne,
mìngjiá grew on the steps,
phoenixes nested in the courtyard,
and when stones were struck and beaten,
all animals danced in unison.
An auspicious star appeared in the Fáng constellation,
and a chénghuáng horse emerged from the earth.
Xīwángmǔ presented white rings and jade jue-disks.
Shùn was on the throne for fourteen years.
While playing bells, chime stones, sheng flutes, and guan pipes, the music was not yet finished,
when a great thunderstorm occurred,
strong winds tore off roofs and uprooted trees.
The drumsticks and drums were scattered on the ground,
the bells and chime stones were in disarray,
the dancers collapsed,
and the music master ran wildly.
Shùn then embraced a xuán-jade and held a héng-bar, and laughed, saying:
“How clear it is!
Indeed, the world is not the world of one person,
and this is even manifested in the bells, chime stones, sheng flutes, and guan pipes!”
Then he recommended Yǔ to Heaven,
and allowed him to perform the duties of the Son of Heaven.
At this time, harmonious qi widely responded,
and auspicious clouds arose,
like smoke yet not smoke,
like clouds yet not clouds,
dense and swirling,
flowing and coiling.
All officials sang in harmony the Song of Auspicious Clouds.
The emperor then initiated the song, saying:
“Oh, the brilliant auspicious clouds,
how dense and boundless they are!
The sun and moon shine brightly,
day after day!”
All the ministers advanced,
bowed their heads and said:
“Oh, bright Heaven above,
how splendid are the arrayed stars!
The sun and moon shine brightly,
magnifying us, your humble servant!”
The emperor then sang again, saying:
“The sun and moon have their constant paths,
the stars have their courses.
The four seasons follow their order,
all the people are truly sincere.
When I discuss music,
it matches the spiritual essence of Heaven.
When it is transferred to the sages,
none do not listen.
Beat the drums loudly,
dance majestically!
When the essence is exhausted,
lift your skirts and depart!”
Thereupon, the eight winds flowed smoothly,
auspicious clouds gathered thickly,
coiling dragons stirred vigorously in their lairs,
and flood dragons and fish leaped in their abysses.
Turtles and soft-shelled turtles all came out of their holes,
and the Yú dynasty was transferred to serve the Xià dynasty.
Shùn then set up an altar at the Hé river,
following Yáo’s precedent.
Towards late afternoon,
glorious light and auspicious qi arrived.
A yellow dragon, bearing a diagram,
thirty-two chi long,
and nine chi wide,
emerged from beside the altar,
with red patterns and green markings.
Its inscription spoke of abdicating to Yǔ.
Di Yǔ 帝禹 of the Xià 夏 clan,
his mother was called Xiūjǐ 脩己.
While traveling,
she saw a shooting star pass through Mǎo 昴.
She dreamt and was moved by the omen,
and then swallowed a divine pearl.
Xiūjǐ’s 脩己 back split open,
and Yǔ 禹 was born at Shíniǔ 石紐.
He had a tiger nose and a large mouth,
his two ears were carved,
on his head he wore a hook and bell,
on his chest there was a jade dipper,
and the character “jǐ 己” was etched on his feet,
hence he was named Wénmìng 文命.
When he grew up, he possessed sagely virtue.
He was nine *chǐ* and nine *cùn* tall.
He dreamt he was washing himself in the Hé 河,
and took water with his hands to drink it.
There was also the auspicious sign of a white nine-tailed fox.
During the time of Yáo 堯,
Shùn 舜 promoted him.
Yǔ 禹 was observing the Hé 河,
when a tall person with a white face and a fish body
emerged and said:
“I am the spirit of the Hé 河.”
He called out to Yǔ 禹, saying:
“Wénmìng 文命, control the floods.”
Having spoken,
he bestowed upon Yǔ 禹 the Hétú 河圖,
and spoke of the matters concerning water control,
then retreated into the abyss.
When Yǔ 禹 had completed his water control work,
Heaven bestowed upon him a dark jade *guī*,
to announce his success.
When the Xià 夏 dynasty was about to rise,
plants and trees flourished,
a green dragon stopped in the outskirts,
and the god Zhùróng 祝融
descended upon Chóngshān 崇山.
He then received the abdication from Shùn 舜,
and ascended to the position of Son of Heaven.
The Luò 洛 river brought forth a turtle-book with sixty-five characters,
which became the Hóngfàn 洪範,
this is what is meant by
“the Luò 洛 brought forth the book.”
He made a southern inspection tour,
and crossed the Jiāng 江.
Midstream, two yellow dragons carried his boat,
and the boatmen were all afraid.
Yǔ 禹 laughed and said:
“I have received the mandate from Heaven,
and exert my strength to nourish the people.
Life
is nature.
Death
is fate.
Why fear dragons!”
Thereupon, the dragons dragged their tails and departed.
The consort of the time of Gāoxīnshì 高辛氏 was named Jiǎndí 簡狄.
On the day of the spring equinox when the xuánniǎo 玄鳥 arrived,
she followed the Emperor to sacrifice at the suburban *méi* altar,
and bathed with her sister in the waters of Xuánqiū 玄丘.
A xuánniǎo 玄鳥 held an egg in its beak and dropped it.
It had five beautiful colors.
The two competed to pick it up,
and covered it with a jade basket.
Jiǎndí 簡狄 was the first to obtain and swallow it,
and subsequently became pregnant.
Her chest split open and Qì 契 was born.
When grown, he became Sītú 司徒 for Yáo 堯,
achieved success for the people,
and was enfeoffed in Shāng 商.
Thirteen generations later,
Zhǔguǐ 主癸 was born.
Zhǔguǐ’s 主癸 consort was named Fúdū 扶都.
She saw a white *qì* penetrate the moon,
and was moved by the omen,
giving birth to Tāng 湯 on an *yǐ* day,
whose appellation was Tiānyǐ 天乙.
He was broad below and sharp above,
and had a beard,
a curved body and a loud voice.
He was nine *chǐ* tall,
and had four elbows on his arms.
This was Yīn Tāng 殷湯.
Tāng 湯 was in Bó 亳,
and was able to cultivate his virtue.
Yī Zhì 伊摯 was about to respond to Tāng’s 湯 command,
and dreamt he was sailing past the sun and moon.
Tāng 湯 then went east to Luò 洛,
observed the altar of Dì Yáo 帝堯,
submerged a jade *bì* and stood back.
Two yellow fish leaped up,
a black bird followed the fish and stopped at the altar,
transforming into black jade.
There was also a black turtle,
with red patterns forming characters,
which spoke of Xià Jié’s 夏桀 unrighteousness,
and that Tāng 湯 should replace him.
The spirit of Táowù 檮杌
appeared on Pīshān 邳山.
A spirit led a white wolf holding a hook and entered the Shāng 商 court.
When the power of Metal was about to flourish,
silver overflowed from the mountains.
Tāng 湯 was about to uphold the mandate of Heaven and depose Jié 桀.
He dreamt he reached Heaven and ascended it,
and thus possessed the world.
Later, the Shāng 商 people changed the name of the world to Yīn 殷.
In the era of Gāo Xīn-shì, his concubine was named Jiāng Yuán.
While assisting in the sacrifice at the jiāoméi altar,
she saw a giant footprint and stepped into it.
At that moment, she felt a sensation as if someone had touched her intimately,
and subsequently became pregnant and gave birth to a son.
Thinking it inauspicious,
she abandoned him in a narrow alley,
but sheep and cattle avoided him and did not trample him.
She then sent him to the mountains and forests,
where lumberjacks happened to cover him with wood.
Again, she took him and placed him on cold ice,
but a large bird came and covered him with one wing.
Jiāng Yuán considered this extraordinary,
so she took him back and raised him,
naming him Qì.
He had an unusual appearance, with a prominent chin.
When he grew up, he became an official under Yáo in charge of agriculture,
and made great contributions to the people.
Qì’s grandson was named Gōng Liú.
He possessed virtue,
and all the feudal lords treated him with the courtesy due to the Son of Heaven.
Initially, in the era of Huáng Dì,
a prophecy stated:
"The Northwest will become king;
the time is in the Jiǎzǐ cycle.
They will establish commands,
execute punishments,
and implement the Way at dawn."
After Gōng Liú,
thirteen generations later, Jì Lì was born.
In the tenth year of Jì Lì’s reign,
flying dragons filled the Mùyě of Yīn.
This was a symbol that a sage, though in a subordinate position, was about to rise.
Jì Lì’s consort was named Tài Rèn.
She dreamt that a giant touched her,
and she gave birth to Chāng in a pigsty.
This was Zhōu Wén Wáng.
He had a dragon face and tiger shoulders,
was ten chǐ tall,
and had four nipples on his chest.
Tài Wáng said:
"My lineage is destined to flourish,
and it will be through Chāng!"
Jì Lì’s elder brother was named Tài Bó.
Knowing that the Mandate of Heaven rested with Chāng,
he went to Yuè and never returned for the rest of his life.
His younger brother Zhòng Yōng followed him,
thus Jì Lì became the heir, and the succession ultimately passed to Chāng.
Chāng became Xī Bó,
and built his capital at Fēng.
Wén Wáng’s consort was named Tài Sì.
She dreamt that thorns grew in the court of Shāng,
and the crown prince Fā planted catalpa trees between the palace gates,
which transformed into pines, cypresses, elm-like trees, and oak-like trees.
She told this to Wén Wáng,
and Wén Wáng, offering ritual silks, informed his officials,
and together with Fā, bowed and announced the dream.
On a Jiǎzǐ day in late autumn,
a red sparrow carried a book to Fēng,
and landed at Chāng’s door.
Chāng bowed and kowtowed to receive it.
Its main text stated:
"Jī Chāng,
son of the Azure Emperor;
the one who will destroy Yīn is Zhòu Wáng."
When Wén Wáng was about to hunt,
the official diviner Bì divined for him,
saying:
"You will have a great catch.
It will be neither a bear nor a grizzly bear.
Heaven will send you a teacher to assist Chāng.
My ancestor, the official diviner Chóu, divined for Yǔ’s hunt,
and obtained Gāo Táo.
The omen is like this."
The King arrived at the waters of Pán Xī,
where Lǚ Shàng was fishing by the bank.
The King descended and hurried to bow, saying:
"I have awaited you for seven years,
and now I see your radiant presence here."
Lǚ Shàng immediately changed his name and replied:
"I caught a jade huáng,
the main text of which says: 'Jī receives the Mandate,
Chāng comes to uplift,
compile your Luò divination, report it in Qí.'"
Lǚ Shàng went out for a stroll
and saw a red man emerge from the Luò River,
who handed Lǚ Shàng a book, saying:
"Your name is Lǚ,
you are the one to assist Chāng."
Wén Wáng dreamt that the sun and moon were attached to his body,
and also that a Yuèzhuó bird sang on Qí Shān.
In the first month of spring, after sixty days,
the Five Planets gathered in Fáng constellation.
Later, a Phoenix carried a book,
and flew through Wén Wáng’s capital.
The book also stated:
"The Yīn Emperor is without the Way,
tyrannizing and causing chaos in the world.
The imperial mandate has already shifted,
it cannot last much longer.
Spirits and deities have departed afar,
a hundred gods have been blown away.
The Five Planets gather in Fáng,
to clearly govern the Four Seas."
After Wén Wáng’s death,
Crown Prince Fā succeeded to the throne,
this was Wǔ Wáng.
Wǔ Wáng had conjoined teeth and a gaze like a ram.
When he was about to attack Zhòu,
he reached Mèng Jīn,
where eight hundred feudal lords,
without prior arrangement, gathered.
All said:
"Zhòu can be attacked now."
Wǔ Wáng did not agree.
Later, when Zhòu killed Bǐ Gān,
imprisoned Jī Zǐ,
and Wēi Zǐ departed,
then Wǔ Wáng attacked Zhòu.
Crossing Mèng Jīn,
in the middle of the river,
a white fish leaped into the King’s boat.
The King bent down and took the fish,
which was three chǐ long,
and had red characters beneath its eyes,
saying that Zhòu could be attacked.
The King copied the characters into a record,
and the fish’s writing disappeared.
He burned the fish to announce it to Heaven.
A fire descended from Heaven and stopped at Wáng Wū,
flowing into a red crow,
which carried grain in its beak.
The grain
commemorated Qì’s virtue;
the fire
was the burning of the fish to announce it to Heaven,
and Heaven’s fire flowing down
was a felicitous omen in response.
Thereupon, he marched east to attack Zhòu,
victorious at Mùyě,
with his weapons not stained with blood,
and the world submitted to him.
Then he enfeoffed Lǚ Wàng in Qí.
As the virtue of Zhōu flourished,
plants and trees grew luxuriantly,
and artemisia was suitable for building palaces,
thus it was named Hāo Gōng.
After Wǔ Wáng died,
Chéng Wáng was young.
Zhōu Gōng Dàn acted as regent for seven years,
establishing rites and composing music.
The divine bird Fènghuáng appeared,
and Míngjiá plants grew.
Then, with Chéng Wáng, he observed the Hé and Luò rivers,
and sank a jade disk.
When the ritual was complete,
the King withdrew to wait.
As dusk approached,
a glorious light emerged from the Hé,
green clouds floated in,
a green dragon descended upon the altar,
carrying a diagram of a dark tortoise shell,
and after sitting, it departed.
The ritual at the Luò River
was also similar.
A dark tortoise, a green dragon, and a black rhinoceros stopped at the altar.
Their shells were engraved with writing,
red characters forming words.
Zhōu Gōng picked up a brush and copied the writing as it appeared.
When the writing was complete, the characters disappeared,
and the tortoise shed its shell and departed.
These words spoke of the rise and fall from Zhōu Gōng to Qín and Hàn.
Qílín roamed the park,
and Fènghuáng soared in the court.
Chéng Wáng took up his qín and sang:
"The Fènghuáng soars in the purple court!
What virtue do I possess to move the spirits?
It relies on the grace and blessings of the former kings,
thus we are happy and the people are at peace."
In the fourteenth year of Duke Āi of Lǔ,
Kǒngzǐ dreamt at night between three pagoda trees,
in the lands of Fēng and Pèi,
that a crimson smoke rose.
He then called Yán Yuān and Zǐxià to go and see it.
Driving their carriage, they arrived at Fànshì Jiē, northwest of Chǔ.
They saw a hay-gatherer plucking a qílín,
which had injured its left front foot.
He covered it with firewood.
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Child, come here.
Your surname is Chìsòng,
your given name is Zǐqiáo,
and your courtesy name is Shòujì."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"Have you seen anything?"
The child replied:
"I saw an animal,
as large as a lamb,
with a horn on its head,
fleshy at its tip."
Kǒngzǐ said:
"The world already has a master,
who is Chìliú,
with Chén and Xiàng as assistants.
The Five Planets have entered Jǐng, following the Jupiter star."
The child removed the firewood and revealed the qílín to Kǒngzǐ.
Kǒngzǐ hurried towards it.
The qílín covered its ears,
and spat out three scrolls of diagrams,
three cùn wide,
eight cùn long,
each scroll containing twenty-four characters.
They stated that Chìliú would rise,
saying:
"When Zhōu perishes,
crimson energy will rise,
Great Yào will flourish,
Xuánqiū will ordain the mandate,
and the Emperor will be Mǎojīn."
Kǒngzǐ composed the Chūnqiū [Annals],
and compiled the Xiàojīng [Classic of Filial Piety].
When they were completed,
