he made seventy-two disciples bend and stand facing the North Star.
He had Zēngzǐ hold the documents concerning the Hé and Luò rivers, facing north.
Kǒngzǐ purified himself and bowed towards the North Star,
announcing to Heaven that the preparations were complete, saying:
"Four scrolls of the Xiàojīng,
and the Chūnqiū, Hé, and Luò, totaling eighty-one scrolls,
have been respectfully completed."
Thereupon, Heaven caused a dense white mist to rise and sweep the ground,
and a crimson rainbow descended from above,
transforming into a yellow jade tablet,
three chǐ long,
with engraved text upon it.
Kǒngzǐ knelt, received it, and read it, saying:
"Precious writing appears,
Liú Jì grasps it.
Mǎojīndāo,
is north of Zhěn.
His courtesy name is Hézǐ,
the world will submit."
Hàn Gāodì’s father was named Liú Zhíjiā.
Zhíjiā’s mother
dreamed that a red bird, like a dragon, played with her,
and then gave birth to Zhíjiā,
who was later Tàishàng Huángdì.
His mother’s name was Hánshǐ,
who was later Zhāolíng Hòu.
Zhāolíng Hòu was strolling by Luòchí
when a jade chicken appeared, holding a red pearl
on which was engraved the words, “Yùyīng,
he who swallows this will be king.”
Zhāolíng Hòu took and swallowed it.
She also slept by a great marsh
and dreamed she encountered a spirit.
At that time, thunder and lightning obscured the sky,
and Tàishàng Huáng looked on,
seeing a flood dragon above her.
Consequently, she conceived and gave birth to Jì,
who was later Gāodì.
Gāodì had a prominent nose and a dragon-like countenance,
with a handsome beard and whiskers,
and seventy-two black moles on his left thigh.
When he was of humble status,
he frequently bought wine on credit from Wáng Ǎo and Wǔ Fù.
When he lay drunk,
there was always a strange light above him.
Every time he lingered to drink,
their sales would multiply several times over.
Wǔ Fù found this extraordinary
and would always tear up his debt slips.
Lǚ Gōng, a man from Dānfù, was skilled in physiognomy.
When he saw Gāodì,
he said:
“I have been fond of physiognomy since I was young,
and I have read many people’s faces,
but none are like Jì’s face.
I wish Jì would cherish himself.
I have a daughter,
and I wish she could be your broom-and-dustpan wife.”
Lǚ Gōng’s wife, a woman named Ǎo, angrily said to Lǚ Gōng:
“You always considered this daughter extraordinary,
wishing her to marry a noble man.
Pèilìng is good to you,
but you refused him when he sought her hand.
Why foolishly promise her to Liú Jì?”
Lǚ Gōng said:
“This is not something a woman can understand.”
He eventually married her to Gāodì.
They had Huìdì and Lǔyuán Gōngzhǔ.
Lǚ Hòu once lived in the fields with her two children.
An old man passed by
and asked for a drink.
Lǚ Hòu then offered him food.
The old man examined Lǚ Hòu’s face and said:
“Madam,
you are a noble person destined for greatness under heaven.”
He asked to read the faces of her two children.
Upon seeing Huìdì, he said:
“The reason for madam’s nobility
is indeed this son.”
He also read Lǔyuán Gōngzhǔ’s face,
predicting nobility for her as well.
After the old man had left,
Gāodì happened to come from a nearby house.
Lǚ Hòu told him everything.
Gāodì pursued and questioned the old man.
The old man said:
“The nobility of the lady and children just now
is all due to your appearance.
Your nobility is beyond words.”
Gāodì, having drunk,
traveled at night through a marsh.
A person ahead turned back and said:
“There is a large snake blocking the road,
please turn back.”
Gāodì, being drunk,
said:
“A brave man travels on,
what is there to fear?”
So he went forward,
drew his sword and cut the snake,
which split into two,
opening the road for him to pass.
Those who came later
saw an old woman guarding the snake, saying:
“The son of Chìdì passed by just now
and killed my son.”
The witnesses suspected the old woman of deceit
and wanted to whip her,
but she suddenly vanished.
They reported the full account to Gāodì,
and the emperor was pleased in his heart.
Qín Shǐhuángdì said:
“There is an aura of a Son of Heaven in the southeast.”
Thereupon, he traveled east to suppress it.
Gāodì hid in the mountains and marshes between Máng and Dàng,
and Lǚ Hòu always knew his whereabouts.
Gāodì asked her about it in wonder,
and she replied:
“Where Jì resides,
there is always a cloud of vapor above,
that is how I know.”
When Gāodì was Pèigōng
and entered Qín,
the five planets gathered in Dōngjǐng;
Suìxīng arrived first,
and the other four planets followed it.
The prognostication said:
“He will obtain the empire by righteousness.”
Initially,
Zhāng Liáng was strolling above the Yíshuǐ River in Xiàpī,
when an old man came
directly in front of Liáng
and dropped his shoe.
He looked at Liáng and said:
“Young man, pick up my shoe.”
Liáng was astonished
and wanted to hit him,
but considering his old age,
he went down to pick it up and knelt to offer it.
The old man received it with his foot,
smiled and left.
Liáng was greatly surprised.
The old man left for about a li and returned,
saying:
“Young man is teachable.
Five days later, at dawn,
meet me here.”
Liáng found it strange,
knelt and replied:
“Yes.”
Five days later,
Liáng went,
but the old man had already arrived first.
He angrily said:
“Why do you arrive late for a meeting with an elder?
In five days,
meet me here again.”
This happened three times before Liáng arrived first.
The old man happily said:
“Shouldn’t it be like this!”
He then took out a scroll from his bosom and gave it to him,
saying:
“Read this;
this will make you a teacher of kings.
Thirteen years later,
young man, you will see me at the foot of Gǔchéng Mountain in Jìběi,
and the yellow stone is me.”
At dawn, he looked at the book,
and it was Tàigōng Bīngfǎ.
Liáng spoke about the “Yellow Stone” chapter to others,
but none understood,
only Gāodì understood it.
Liáng said:
“This must have been bestowed by Heaven.”
Five years later, he accomplished the imperial enterprise.
Thirteen years later,
Zhāng Liáng indeed found the yellow stone at the foot of Gǔchéng Mountain,
treasured it and offered sacrifices to it,
and was buried with it after his death.
Wéndì’s mother, Bó Jī,
was taken into Wèi Bào’s inner palace
when Wèi Bào became King of Wèi.
Xǔ Fù read her face,
predicting she would give birth to a Son of Heaven.
King Wèi Bào then turned his back on Hàn.
Hàn Gāodì attacked and captured him,
and Bó Jī was sent to the weaving room.
Gāodì saw her and found her beautiful,
so he brought her into his inner palace.
More than a year passed before she gained his favor.
Just as she was about to be favored,
Bó Jī said:
“Last night, I dreamed a green dragon coiled around my heart.”
Gāodì said:
“I am that.
I will fulfill it for you.”
With one union, Wéndì was born.
Jǐngdì’s Empress Wáng was initially married to Jīn Wángsūn.
Her mother, Zāng Ér, performed divination, saying:
“She will be noble.”
So she took her away from the Jīn family and brought her into the crown prince’s palace,
where she bore a son.
While the son was still in her womb,
she dreamed the sun entered her bosom,
and she told the crown prince.
The crown prince said:
“This is an auspicious sign of nobility.”
She gave birth to a son,
who was later Wǔdì.
Emperor Wǔ's (Wǔdì) Concubine Zhào Jiéyú (Zhào Jiéyú),
whose family was from Héjiān (Héjiān),
was born with both hands clenched into fists,
unable to open them.
When Emperor Wǔ was on an inspection tour through Héjiān (Héjiān),
a diviner of auras said,
"There is an extraordinary woman here with the aura of an Empress."
She was summoned and presented to the Emperor.
Emperor Wǔ himself tried to pry open her hands,
and immediately they opened,
revealing a jade hook.
From then on, she gained favor,
and was called
"Lady Quán (Quán Fūrén)."
She was promoted to Jiéyú (Jiéyú),
resided in Gōuyì (Gōuyì) Palace,
and was greatly beloved.
After fourteen months, she gave birth to a son,
who was Emperor Zhāo (Zhāo Dì),
and was called
"Gōuyìzǐ (Gōuyìzǐ)."
Emperor Wǔ said:
"I heard that ancient Yáo (Yáo) was born after fourteen months;
now Gōuyìzǐ (Gōuyìzǐ) is the same."
Thereupon, he named her gate the Gate of Yáo's Mother (Yáomǔmén).
In the first month of the third year of Yuánfèng (Yuánfèng) of Emperor Zhāo (Zhāo Dì),
south of Mount Tàishān (Tàishān) and Mount Láiwú (Láiwú),
the common people heard a clamor of thousands of people at night.
When they went to see in the morning,
they saw a large stone standing on its own,
fifteen feet high,
forty-eight spans in circumference,
and eight feet buried in the earth,
with three stones forming its base.
After it stood,
several thousand white crows gathered beside it.
Furthermore, a willow tree in the Shànglín (Shànglín) Imperial Park broke and lay on the ground,
but one morning it stood up by itself and sprouted branches and leaves.
Insects gnawed its leaves to form characters,
which read:
"Gōngsūn Bìngyǐ (Gōngsūn Bìngyǐ) will ascend."
The shrine of Wáng Shè (Wáng Shè) in Xiāngyì (Xiāngyì), Chénliú (Chénliú) suddenly moved to Cháng'ān (Cháng'ān).
Doctor Suī Mèng (Suī Mèng) divined about it, saying:
"A stone
is of the Yin category.
Tàishān (Tàishān)
is Dàizōng (Dàizōng),
the place where kings abdicate and succeed.
There will be a discarded former house,
whose surname is Gōngsūn (Gōngsūn),
and whose personal name is Bìngyǐ (Bìngyǐ),
who will become Emperor from commoner status."
At that time, Emperor Zhāo (Zhāo Dì) was young,
and Huò Guāng (Huò Guāng) was regent,
so he had Mèng (Mèng) executed for his "demonic speech."
When Emperor Zhāo (Zhāo Dì) died,
and the King of Chāngyì (Chāngyì Wáng) was also deposed,
Huò (Huò) enthroned Emperor Xuān (Xuān Dì),
who was Emperor Wǔ's (Wǔ Dì) great-grandson,
originally named Bìngyǐ (Bìngyǐ),
who had been a commoner for three generations,
just as Mèng (Mèng) had said.
Empress Wáng (Wáng Huánghòu) of Emperor Yuán (Yuán Dì)
was a descendant of the Tián (Tián) clan of Qí (Qí).
Her grandfather, Wēng Rú (Wēng Rú),
moved from Dōngpínglíng (Dōngpínglíng) to Yuánchéng (Yuánchéng).
Jiàngōng (Jiàngōng) of Yuánchéng (Yuánchéng) said:
"In ancient times, in the Spring and Autumn period, when the sand deer collapsed,
the Jin (Jìn) historian divined it,
saying 'Yin (Yīn) is strong against Yang (Yáng),
earth and fire clash,'
hence the sand deer collapsed.
Six hundred forty-five years later,
a sagely woman should arise,
could it be from the Qí (Qí) Tián (Tián) clan?
Now Wēng Rú's (Wēng Rú) move
is precisely to that land,
and the sun and moon align with it.
To the east of Yuánchéng (Yuánchéng) city walls is the Ruins of Wǔlù (Wǔlù zhī Xū),
which is the land of Shālù (Shālù).
Eighty years later,
a noble woman will bring prosperity to the world."
Wēng Rú (Wēng Rú) begot Jìn (Jìn).
Jìn's (Jìn) wife, Lady Lǐ (Lǐ Shì), while pregnant,
dreamed that the moon entered her bosom.
She gave birth to a daughter,
who was Empress Yuán (Yuán Hòu).
Each time she was betrothed,
before the marriage took place,
the betrothed would invariably die.
A fortune-teller said:
"She is destined for great nobility."
Subsequently, she became the Empress of Emperor Yuán (Yuán Dì),
and gave birth to Emperor Chéng (Chéng Dì).
Initially,
during the reign of Qín Shǐhuáng (Qín Shǐhuáng),
there were twelve giants,
five *zhàng* (zhàng) tall,
with footprints six *chǐ* (chǐ) long,
who appeared in Líntáo (Líntáo), Lǒngxī (Lǒngxī).
Former historians considered this an omen of Qín's (Qín) demise,
but the imperial historian believed it to be a sign of Hàn's (Hàn) rise.
From Emperor Gāo (Gāo Dì) to Emperor Píng (Píng Dì),
there were twelve rulers.
Guāngwǔ Huángdì’s
father was the Prefect of Jìyáng.
Jìyáng had an imperial traveling palace for Wǔdì,
which was always kept locked.
On the night of jiǎzǐ in the twelfth month of the first year of Jiànpíng under Àidì,
when Guāngwǔ was about to be born,
it was opened and they resided there.
At that time, there was a red light,
and the whole room became bright.
His imperial father found this extraordinary,
and had the diviner Wáng Cháng divine about it.
Cháng dismissed those on either side and said:
“This is a good omen,
it cannot be spoken of.”
That year,
auspicious grain grew in the open air on the roof,
with one stalk bearing nine ears,
different from ordinary grain.
The county experienced a great harvest,
hence Guāngwǔ was named Xiù.
At that time, a phoenix also gathered in Jìyáng,
so the palace was painted with images of the phoenix.
The next year,
a fangshi named Xià Hèliáng
reported to Àidì, saying:
“The Hàn dynasty’s mandate is in decline in the middle of its cycle,
and it is due to receive the mandate again.”
Thereupon, the reign title was changed to Tàichū Yuánjiāng Yuánnián,
and he proclaimed himself Chénshèng Liú Tàipíng Huángdì to ward off evil.
During Wáng Mǎng’s time,
Sū Bó’ē, who was skilled at observing vital energy, observed the city walls of Chōnglíng, the county where Guāngwǔ resided,
and exclaimed:
“The vital energy is excellent!
Lush and vibrant.”
Mǎng disliked the Hàn,
and the coin script had the character jīn (gold) in it,
so he recast the huòquán (money-spring) coins to replace them.
Later, Guāngwǔ rose in Bái shuǐ Xiāng in Chōnglíng,
and the characters on the huòquán coins were
“Bái shuǐ Zhēnrén” (True Man of White Water).
When he first raised his army,
he saw a fire light south of his house.
He thought it was someone carrying fire,
and called out to them, but the light grew stronger,
then reached up to the sky,
and after a while, disappeared.
When he was in Hébĕi,
he was pressed by Wáng Láng
and was about to cross the Hūtuó River to the south.
The guide official returned and said:
“The river is flowing with ice floes,
there are no boats to cross.”
All his attendants were afraid.
The Emperor again sent Wáng Bà to inspect it.
Bà went and saw
it was as the official said.
Bà worried that if he reported the truth upon his return,
it would alarm everyone,
so he falsely said:
“The ice is solid and passable.”
The Emperor hastened forward.
By the time they arrived,
the river ice had all frozen together,
and it was firm enough to cross.
After crossing,
the ice broke before the remaining few carriages had finished crossing.
Earlier, when they reached the west of Xiàbó City,
he was unsure where to go.
An old man in white clothes was by the roadside,
and said:
“Strive on!
Xìndū is safeguarding Cháng’ān City,
it’s only eighty li from here.”
After speaking,
he disappeared.
They then reached Xìndū
and took refuge with the Grand Administrator Rèn Guāng.
Initially, when Guāngwǔ was obscure,
Cài Shǎogōng of Ráng said:
“The prophecy says Liú Xiù will raise an army to punish the unrighteous,
and Mǎo Jīn (referring to Liú Xiù) will cultivate virtue and become Son of Heaven.”
The State Master, Lord Liú Zǐjùn, was named Xiù.
Shǎogōng said:
“The State Master is he.”
Guāngwǔ smiled and said:
“How do you know it’s not me?”
The Daoist priest Xīmén Jūnhuì and others all said:
“Liú Xiù is destined to be the Son of Heaven.”
After Guāngwǔ pacified Hébĕi,
he returned to Zhōngshān.
General Wàn Xiū obtained the Chìfú Fú (Red Relief Talisman),
which said Guāngwǔ was destined to receive the mandate.
His ministers petitioned him to accept the imperial title,
but Guāngwǔ declined.
Later, when he reached Qū Xiàn,
the scholar Qiáng Huá again came from Cháng’ān to Qū
and presented the Chìfú Fú.
Its text matched Xiū’s.
His subordinates again requested, saying:
“The auspicious symbol for receiving the mandate, the human response is paramount.”
Guāngwǔ also dreamed of riding a red dragon ascending to heaven,
so he ascended the throne
and made Luòyáng his capital,
building palaces.
One night, gate timber arrived by itself.
At that time, the city gate of Kāiyáng County in Lángyá
disappeared without cause one night.
Upon examining the obtained timber,
it was exactly that,
so its gate was named Kāiyáng Mén.
Before this, during Qín Mùgōng’s time,
a person from Chéncāng dug up something
that resembled a sheep but wasn’t a sheep,
and resembled a pig but wasn’t a pig.
Amazed,
he intended to present it.
On the way, he met two young boys,
who told him:
“Do you know what that is?
Its name is Guī.
It often lives underground and eats the brains of the dead.
If you wish to kill it,
point at it with a cypress branch from the southeast,
and it will die.”
The Guī then spoke, saying:
“These two boys
are named Bǎo.
He who obtains the male will be king,
he who obtains the female will be hegemon.”
Thereupon, the person from Chéncāng abandoned the Guī and pursued the two boys.
The two boys transformed into pheasants
and flew into the forest.
The person from Chéncāng reported this to Mùgōng.
Mùgōng dispatched his followers for a great hunt
and obtained the female,
which transformed into a stone
and was placed between the Qiān and Wèi rivers.
When Wéngōng came,
he established a temple for it,
named Chénbǎo Cí.
The male flew south and settled in Ráng County, Nányáng,
and later Guāngwǔ rose in Nányáng.
When Guāngwǔ first rose,
Wēi Xiāo held a large army in Lǒngyòu,
recruiting heroes and elites,
while Gōngsūn Shù declared himself emperor in Shǔ.
The world was in turmoil,
the large factions occupied prefectures and commanderies,
the small ones held counties and towns.
Xiāo asked Bān Biāo from Fúfēng:
“In the past, when Zhōu fell,
the Warring States contended,
the world was divided,
and it took several generations to settle.
Will the affairs of 'vertical and horizontal alliances'
reappear now?
Or will the mandate pass, and one person rise
to unify all?
I wish, Sir, you would discuss this.”
He replied:
“The rise and fall of Zhōu differ from the Hàn.
In ancient times, Zhōu established five ranks of nobility,
and the feudal lords administered their territories.
The roots became weak,
while the branches and leaves grew strong,
thus in its later period there were affairs of 'vertical and horizontal alliances,'
such was the situation.
The Hàn dynasty inherited the system of Qín,
with commanderies and counties governing the people.
The sovereign held absolute authority,
and no minister held power for a hundred years.
As for Chéngdì,
he lent power to his maternal relatives;
Àidì and Píngdì had short reigns,
and the imperial succession was severed three times.
Calamity arose from above,
but did not harm those below.
Therefore, Wáng Shì’s family, though noble,
usurped the court,
and managed to steal the imperial title,
but without popular support.
Thus, after he usurped the throne,
everyone in the world yearned and sighed.
Within more than ten years,
there was unrest inside and outside,
rebellions erupted near and far,
false claimants gathered like clouds,
all proclaiming the Liú clan,
without prior consultation, yet speaking in unison.
The heroes who now control territories
all lack the hereditary foundation of the Seven States.
The Odes say: ‘Great is God on high,
shining down below.
He surveys the four quarters,
seeking the suffering of the people.’
Now, the people all sing and long for the Hàn,
looking up to the Liú clan,
which is already evident.”
Wěi Xiāo said:
“Sir, your words on the situations of the Zhōu and Hàn
are acceptable.
However, to merely see that the ignorant people are familiar with and recognize the surname and title of the Liú clan,
and then claim that the Hàn will be restored,
is shortsighted.
In the past, when Qín lost its deer,
did Liú Jì chase and seize it,
and at that time did the people again know the Hàn? ”
Biāo was moved by Xiāo’s words,
and also grieved by the relentless madness and cunning of the times.
He then composed the *Wáng Mìng Lùn* (Treatise on the Mandate of Kingship) to address the difficulties of the era.
The text says: In ancient times, when Dì Yáo abdicated, he said:
“Oh, you Shùn,
the heavenly calendar and destiny are now upon your person.”
Shùn likewise conferred this upon Yǔ.
Down to Jì and Qì,
both assisted Táng
and Yú,
illuminating and benefiting the four seas,
and through generations accumulated virtue,
until Tāng and Wǔ,
who then possessed the empire.
Although their encounters were in different times,
and the transitions of power were not the same,
they all responded to Heaven
and followed the people;
their fundamental principle was one.
Thus, the Liú clan inherited the legacy of Yáo,
and the lineage of their clan
is recorded in the *Chūnqiū*.
Táng was based on the virtue of fire,
and Hàn succeeded it.
When
it began in Pèizé,
the divine mother cried out in the night,
thereby manifesting the omen of the Red Emperor.
From this, it can be said:
The imperial legacy
must be accompanied by virtues of clarity, sagacity, prominence, and grace,
and by accomplishments of great deeds
and abundant benefits accumulated through generations.
Only then can sincerity reach the spirits and gods,
and beneficence flow to the living populace.
Therefore, they are blessed and favored by ghosts and spirits,
and the empire turns to them.
I have not seen anyone without a foundational lineage,
whose merits and virtues are not recorded,
who could suddenly rise to this position.
The common people see Gāozǔ rise from humble origins,
but do not understand the reason for it.
They
believe he merely encountered chaos and rebellion,
and was able to wield his sword.
The persuaders
even compare the empire to a deer chase,
where one is lucky to seize it and gain it.
They do not know that the divine artifact (imperial throne) has a mandate,
and cannot
be sought through wisdom and strength.
Alas!
This is why the world is plagued by many rebellious ministers and traitorous sons.
If such is the case,
how can they merely be ignorant of the Way of Heaven?
They are also un-
observant of human affairs.
Indeed, the starving and wandering,
cold and hungry on the roads,
who wish for a humble garment
and a bushel of provisions,
whose desires do not exceed one gold coin,
yet eventually perish in ditches
and ravines.
Why is this?
Poverty also has its destiny.
How much more so the exalted position of the Son of Heaven,
the wealth of the four seas,
the legacy bestowed by spirits and gods—
can these be seized recklessly?
Therefore,
even those who encounter calamitous opportunities
and usurp power,
brave as Xìn and Bù,
strong as Liáng and Jí,
successful as Wáng Mǎng,
yet ultimately end up scalded in cauldrons, subjected to axes,
chopped into mincemeat, and dismembered;
how much more so those insignificant ones who are not even comparable to these few individuals,
yet wish to secretly covet the heavenly throne?
Therefore, a worn-out, clumsy horse
cannot gallop a thousand *lǐ*;
a flock of sparrows
cannot
employ the strength of six wings;
timber for small supports
cannot bear the responsibility of beams and pillars;
and a person of limited capacity
cannot hold the weighty position of an emperor.
The *Yì* says:
“A tripod with a broken leg
overturns
the ducal meal.”
It cannot bear its responsibility.
At the end of Qín,
the heroes jointly pushed Chén Yīng to become king.
Yīng’s mother stopped Yīng, saying:
“Since I became a daughter-in-law in your family,
our family has always been poor and lowly,
to suddenly become rich and noble
is inauspicious.
It is better to assign your troops to someone else.
If things succeed,
you will receive a small share of the benefits;
if they fail,
the blame will fall elsewhere.”
Yīng followed her
advice,
and the Chén clan found peace.
Wáng Líng’s mother
also saw that the Xiàng clan was bound to perish,
and the Liú clan was about to rise.
At this time, Líng was a Hàn general,
and his mother
was captured by Chǔ.
When a Hàn envoy came,
Líng’s mother saw him
and said:
“Please tell my son,
the King of Hàn is a magnanimous person,
he will surely gain the empire.
My son, serve him diligently,
and harbor no
second thoughts.”
Then, in front of the Hàn envoy,
she fell upon her sword and died,
to firmly encourage Líng.
Afterward, the empire was indeed settled by Hàn,
and Líng became prime minister and was enfeoffed as a marquis.
If even a common woman’s
discernment
could infer the ultimate outcome of events,
and discern the crucial moment of fortune or misfortune,
preserving the ancestral sacrifices for eternity,
and leaving records for posterity,
how much more so should a great man’s endeavors be!
Therefore, success and failure are destined,
good and ill come from human actions.
Yīng’s mother knew of decline,
Líng’s mother knew of rising.
By discerning these two,
the imperial mandate is decided.
As for Gāozǔ,
his rise had five reasons: First, he was a descendant of Dì Yáo.
Second, his physical appearance had many peculiarities.
Third, his divine martial prowess had omens and responses.
Fourth,
he was broad-minded, enlightened, benevolent, and forgiving.
Fifth, he knew people well and was good at employing them.
Additionally, he was trustworthy and sincere, fond of strategic planning,
and open to listening and accepting advice.
He pursued goodness as if he could not catch up,
employed people as if they were
himself,
followed advice as if following a stream,
and adapted to the times like an echo.
While eating, he would spit out his food
to accept Zǐfáng’s strategy;
he would pull up his foot and wash it
to greet Lìshēng’s counsel;
he awakened to the words of a garrison soldier
and abandoned his longing for his homeland;
he honored the reputation of the Four White-Haired Elders
and sacrificed his personal affections;
he promoted Hán Xìn from the ranks,
and recruited Chén Píng from exile.
Heroes displayed
their strength,
and all talents were utilized.
This was Gāozǔ’s grand strategy by which
he achieved the imperial enterprise.
As for auspicious omens and portents,
they can also be briefly mentioned.
Initially, Liú Ǎo, when pregnant with
Gāozǔ, dreamed of encountering a spirit.
There was crashing thunder and darkness,
and the strangeness of dragons and snakes.
When he grew up, he had many spiritual peculiarities,
different from the multitude.
Therefore, Wáng and Wǔ were moved by this and
cast their lots;
Lǚ Gōng saw his appearance and offered his daughter;
Qín Huáng traveled east to suppress his qi;
Empress Lǚ would look at the clouds to know his whereabouts.
When he first received the mandate, the white snake was cut in two.
West
When entering the pass, the five planets converged.
Therefore, Huái Yīn and Liú Hóu were said to be granted by Heaven,
not by human effort.
Examining the successes and failures of ancient and modern times,
verifying the achievements and setbacks of actions,
investigating the generational fortune of emperors and kings,
and evaluating what these five factors indicate,
if one is not content with this position,
and the
omens and responses do not align with this measure,
yet one wishes to obscure the power and rights,
transgress the order and seize it presumptuously,
outwardly not assessing one's strength,
and inwardly not knowing one's destiny,
then one will surely lose the lord who protects the family,
lose
the lifespan allotted by Heaven,
encounter the misfortune of a broken foot,
and be subjected to execution by axe.
If a hero truly awakens and realizes this,
fears it like a warning of calamity,
looks far ahead with detachment,
and profoundly
understands,
receiving the clear mandate of Líng and Yīng,
cutting off the covetous ambitions of Xìn and Bù,
rejecting the blind talk of "chasing the deer,"
and discerning that divine regalia is bestowed,
without coveting what cannot be achieved,
thus becoming
the subject of laughter for the two mothers,
then blessings and fortune will flow to descendants,
and the heavenly emolument will last eternally.
Wěi Xiāo did not accept,
and indeed failed.
During the reigns of Hàn Yuán and Chéng,
Taoist priests said:
"The prophecies state: 'The 赤厄 (red calamity) is three sevens.'
Three sevens,
two hundred and ten years,
there will be usurpation by an imperial relative.
The fortune reaches three sixes,
there will be an outstanding figure like a soaring dragon,
restoring the ancestral lineage."
When Wáng Mǎng usurped Hàn,
Hàn had lasted two hundred and ten years.
Wáng Mǎng failed after eighteen years,
and Guāng Wǔ arose.
When Míng Dì was first born,
he had a full lower face and a narrow upper face,
red like Yáo,
and eventually ascended the imperial throne.
Hé Dì's Dèng Empress,
whose grandfather was Yǔ,
assisted Guāng Wǔ in establishing the dynasty,
and often said:
"Though I commanded a million men,
I never wrongly killed a single person;
my descendants will surely prosper greatly."
When the Empress was young,
the physiognomist Sū Wén saw her,
and exclaimed in surprise:
"This is the bone structure of Chéng Tāng,
her nobility is beyond words."
The Empress once dreamed of climbing a ladder,
touching the sky with her hand.
The sky was vast, perfectly blue and smooth,
with something like stalactites.
The Empress looked up and sucked them.
She consulted a dream interpreter about this.
The dream interpreter said:
"Yáo dreamed of climbing to the sky,
〔一０〕Tāng dreamed of reaching the sky and pulling it down.
〔一一〕These are all extraordinary dreams."
Later, she entered the palace,
and subsequently ascended to a position of great honor.
Before Ān Dì assumed the great position,
while he was in his residence,
there were several auspicious omens of divine light and red snakes,
illuminating the interior of the room,
and coiling between the palace halls, beds, and mats.
Later, he indeed inherited the great succession.
Initially, during the reign of Huán Dì,
a yellow star appeared in the regions of Chǔ and Sòng.
Yīn Kuí from Liáo Dōng said:
"After fifty years,
a true man will arise between Qiáo and Pèi,
and his spearhead will be unstoppable."
In the fifth year of Xī Píng of Líng Dì,
a yellow dragon appeared in Qiáo.
Guāng Lù Dà Fū Qiáo Xuán asked Tài Shǐ Lìng Shàn Yáng:〔一二〕
"What kind of omen is this?"
Shàn Yáng replied:
"Afterwards, a king will arise in that state,
and within fifty years,
celestial phenomena will appear again.
This is its sign."
Yīn Dēng of Nèi Huáng silently noted it.
Later, Cáo Cāo arose in Qiáo,
who became Wèi Wǔ Dì.
In the fifth year of Jiàn Ān,
the yellow star was seen again,
exactly fifty years had passed.
And Wǔ Dì defeated Yuán Shào,
having no rival in the world.
The *Chūnqiū Chèn* says:
"The one who will replace the Hàn,
is Gāotú."
There was a man in Hàn named Zhōu Shū,
who was skilled in esoteric studies.
Someone once asked him,
and Shū replied:
"Gāotú
is Wèi."
After Shū's death,
Qiáo Zhōu again asked the diviner Dù Qióng:
"Zhōu Zhēngjūn believed Gāotú
to be Wèi.
What is the meaning behind this?"
Qióng replied:
"Wèi
is a name of a palace gate.
'Towering over the thoroughfare' (dāng tú gāo) is how the sages spoke in analogy."
He further asked Zhōu:
"Is there anything else that troubles you?"
Zhōu replied:
"I have not fully understood."
Qióng said:
"In ancient times, official titles did not use the word 'Cáo' (曹).
Since the Hàn dynasty,
all official titles have included 'Cáo';
officials are referred to as 'Shǔcáo' (屬曹),
and soldiers as 'Shìcáo' (侍曹).
This is likely the will of Heaven."
Zhōu said:
"Wèi (魏)
means 'great.'
Cáo (曹)
means 'multitude.'
A multitude that is also great,
is that to which the world will return!"
In the eighteenth year of Jiàn'ān,
Wǔdì was made Duke,
and later advanced to the title of King.
In the twenty-fifth year,
Wǔdì passed away,
and Crown Prince Pī succeeded him as King of Wèi,
becoming Wéndì.
When Wéndì was first born,
a cloud of a blue color,
round as a carriage canopy,
appeared above him all day.
Astrologers believed it to be an omen of utmost nobility,
not the aura of a subject.
The skilled physiognomist Gāo Yuánlǚ said:
"His nobility is beyond words."
In the third month of the first year of Yánkāng,
a yellow dragon again appeared in Qiáo.
Yīn Dēng, who was still alive,
sighed and said:
"When a yellow dragon appeared in Xīpíng,
Dān Yáng said: 'In less than fifty years,
it will surely appear again.'
Now forty-five years have passed,
Dān Yáng's words are indeed proven here!"
In the fourth month,
Ráó'ān reported seeing a white tiger.
[一三] In the eighth month,
Shíyì reported a phoenix gathering,
and also the sighting of a qílín.
In the tenth month,
the Hàn emperor abdicated his throne to Wèi.
The King of Wèi humbly declined to accept.
The erudites Sū Lín and Dǒng Bā presented a memorial:
"We humbly observe that the movements of Heaven,
have their fixed divisions.
When a sage meets them,
it is clearly beyond doubt.
Thus Yáo renounced his flesh and blood to abdicate to Yǒuyú,
showing no regret.
Shùn rose from the fields to rule the world,
as if it had always been his.
In the interval of their succession,
without waiting for a moment,
the empire was already transmitted.
This was to expedite the mandate of Heaven,
and to make clear that the empire cannot be without a ruler for a single day.
Now the period and fortune of Hàn have ended,
and the cessation by ominous anomalies is clear.
Your Majesty receives the mandate of Heaven,
as reported by auspicious omens and portents,
which are detailed and comprehensive,
appearing repeatedly and exhaustively.
Even if one were to explain it verbally,
nothing could replace these signs.
Now that the imperial edict has been issued,
but the imperial seals and ribbons have not yet been accepted,
to stubbornly insist on humility and yielding,
is to defy the mandate of Heaven above,
and to go against the will of the people below.
We humbly consult the ancient classics,
and compare them with the *Túwěi* (圖緯) texts.
The fated course of Wèi and where the Dao of Heaven resides,
the validation of your ascension to the throne,
is in this year and this month,
shining brightly and clearly.
We respectfully present the following points.
May Your Majesty change your thoughts and intentions,
ascend the throne in due time,
openly declare it to the Supreme Emperor,
and promulgate the edict throughout the world.
Thereafter, reform the calendar,
change the color of vestments,
and rectify the grand title,
for which the world would be greatly fortunate."
The matters they presented were: Heaven has twelve mansions (cì),
which are taken as fields (fēnyě);
the states of kings and dukes
each have their corresponding mansion.
Zhōu was in Quánhuǒ,
and Wèi is in Dàliáng.
When the Jupiter star (Suìxīng) traverses
all
twelve mansions,
the Son of Heaven of the corresponding state receives the mandate,
and feudal lords are enfeoffed.
When King Wén of Zhōu first received the mandate,
Jupiter was in Quánhuǒ.
When King Wǔ attacked Zhòu,
thirteen
years later,
Jupiter was again in Quánhuǒ.
Hence the *Chūnqiū Zhuàn* says:
"When King Wǔ attacked Zhòu,
Jupiter was in Quánhuǒ."
It also says:
"Where Jupiter is located,
that is the field (fēnyě) of
Our Zhōu."
In the seventh year of Guānghé,
[一四] Jupiter was in Dàliáng.
King Wǔ (i.e., Cáo Cāo) first received the mandate to be a general,
to suppress the Yellow Turbans.
That year, the reign name was changed to Zhōngpíng Yuán
Nián.
In the first year of Jiàn'ān,
Jupiter was again in Dàliáng,
and he was first appointed Grand General.
In the thirteenth year,
it was again in Dàliáng,
and he was first appointed Chancellor.
Now in the twenty-fifth
year,
Jupiter is again in Dàliáng,
and Your Majesty receives the mandate.
This shows Wèi's acquisition of the 'Jupiter year' corresponds to the mandates received by Kings Wén and Wǔ of Zhōu.
This year, the Azure Dragon is in Gēngzǐ.
The *Shī Tuī Dù Zāi* says:
"Gēng (庚)
means 'to change' (gēng 更).
Zǐ (子)
means 'here' (zī 茲).
When the sage establishes laws, the world is governed."
It also
says:
"The King spreads virtue in Zǐ,
and governance is achieved in Chǒu."
This means that this year Heaven changes the mandate for the sage,
to establish laws for the world,
and spread virtue among the people.
Wèi's
reform of the world
aligns with the *Shī* text.
Zhuānxù received the mandate when
Jupiter was in Shǐwéi.
Wèi (衞, i.e., the ancient state) occupied that land,
also in Shǐwéi.
Therefore, the *Chūnqiū Zhuàn* says:
"Wèi (衞)
is the ruins of Zhuānxù."
Now in the tenth month,
where the Dipper points,
is the division of Zhuānxù's reception of the mandate.
Wèi receiving the abdication in the tenth month
is a corroborating sign of the first
ancestor receiving the mandate.
The clan of Wèi
originated from Zhuānxù,
sharing an ancestor with Shùn,
as seen in the *Chūnqiū Shìjiā*.
Shùn, with the virtue of Earth, succeeded the Fire of Yáo.
Now Wèi also, with the virtue of Earth,
succeeds the Fire of Hàn.
This succession, in terms of the cyclic phases, accords with the sequence of Yáo and Shùn's transfer of power.
The King of Wèi still did not consent.
The Grand Astrologer's Assistant, Xǔ Zhī, further presented astronomical omens: Since the twelfth month, Wùchén day, of the third year of Jiàn'ān,
an aura of a new Son of Heaven has appeared in the southeast,
accumulating for twenty-three years until now.
In the tenth year of Jiàn'ān,
Fú
A star emerged from Kùlóu,
then successively intruded upon the constellations Dī and Fáng,
and entered Tiānshì from the north,
offending the Běidǒu and Zǐwēi.
Dī represents the Son of Heaven’s palace,
where the sleeping chambers are located.
Fáng represents the Son
of Heaven’s Bright Hall, the head of government and education.
The seven stars of the Běidǒu
govern honored vassals and trusted close ministers.
Zǐwēi is
the most honored at the North Pole.
This was a great anomaly portending the sweeping away of the Hàn household.
In the autumn of the 18th year of Jiàn'ān,
Suìxīng, Zhènxīng, and Yínghuò all entered Tàiwēi,
retrograding and remaining stationary at the Emperor's Seat for over a hundred days.
Suìxīng entering Tàiwēi
means the ruler will change surname.
Zhènxīng entering Tàiwēi
means internal military unrest,
and the ruler will be weak.
These three
are anomalies of the Hàn changing surname and dynasty.
In the 19th
year of Jiàn'ān, in the first month,
a white rainbow pierced the sun.
The Yìzhuàn says:
"If the empress and concubines usurp power,
a white rainbow will pierce the sun."
On the day Jǐhài, the first day of the fifth month of the 21st year of Jiàn'ān,
there was a solar
eclipse.
In the third month of the 23rd year of Jiàn'ān,
a Fúxīng was seen in the east in the morning for over twenty days,
and appeared in the west in the evening,
trespassing through Wǔchē, Dōngjǐng, Wǔzhūhóu,
Wénchāng, Xuānyuán, and Tàiwēi,
with its fiery point stabbing at the Emperor's Seat.
Fú indicates the removal of the old and establishment of the new,
an anomaly signifying the demise of evil and the rise of a sage.
On the day Rénzǐ, the last day of the second month
of the 24th year of Jiàn'ān,
there was a solar eclipse.
The sun is the essence of yang,
the moon is a marquis or king,
and an eclipse on the days Hài and Zǐ
are all anomalies of water extinguishing fire.
On the tenth day of the ninth month of the first year of Yánkāng,
at dusk,
the moon eclipsed Yínghuò;
after the hour of Réndìng,
Yínghuò emerged from Yíngshì
and lodged in Yǔlín.
The moon is the symbol of ministers, marquises, and kings;
Yínghuò is the essence
of fire,
the element of the Hàn dynasty.
The prognostication says:
"The Hàn household will perish by military means."
On the twentieth day of the ninth month of the first year of Yánkāng,
the qi of the Son of Heaven in the Bō hexagram disappeared,
all anomalies of collapse
and demise.
Yínghuò, the essence of fire,
travels backward by more than one degree per day.
Therefore, the Grand Astrologer Wáng Yù considered it the ultimate sign of the Hàn household's decline and demise.
If Yínghuò is large and
red;
if its light is dim,
or if it is red and small,
indistinguishable from a small star,
these are all anomalies of the Hàn household's decline and demise.
The Yìzhuàn says:
"When above and below are in harmony, sages and worthies prosper,
their response to imperial virtue is the soaring of phoenixes,
and the myriad people are joyful without calamity or disaster."
The Yìzhuàn also says:
"When a sage
receives the mandate,
the response is the descent of phoenixes,
and the Son of Heaven becomes a captive."
The Yìzhuàn also says:
"When a yellow dragon appears,
heavenly calamities are nigh,
the Son of Heaven is deposed,
and a sage emerges."
If a yellow dragon appears
on a Wùjǐ day,
with all five colors and patterns complete,
a sage will obtain the mandate from Heaven.
If a yellow dragon appears on a Wùyín day,
this is the most prominent auspicious sign for an emperor to receive the mandate.
The Yìzhuàn also says:
"When a sage is pure, tranquil, and acts with impartiality,
worthies arrive,
and the people obey the mandate,
the response is the arrival of a Qílín."
The Chūnqiū Yùbǎn Chèn says:
"The one who replaces Chì is the Wèi prince."
The Chūnqiū Zuǒzhù Qī says:
"Hàn will lose the empire through Xǔchāng."
Therefore, Lǐ Yún of Gānlíng, the magistrate of Báimǎ, presented a memorial,
stating that the qi of Xǔchāng
had appeared,
that the "Túgāo" (high path) had already sprouted,
and wished to have the Hàn household guard against and cut off these sprouts.
Now the Hàn capital is Xǔ,
daily becoming weaker,
and it is destined to lose the empire by residing in Xǔchāng.
The "Túgāo"
is Wèi;
Wèi is
the name of the two tall and grand towers of the象魏 (xiàngwèi) at the roadside.
Wèi will replace Hàn,
just as Lǐ Yún said.
The Chūnqiū
Zuǒzhù Qī also says:
"Hàn will perish by Méngsūn."
Commentators explain that Méngsūn corresponds to the twenty-fourth Hàn emperor,
who, being childishly ignorant and deluded, perished in weakness.
The Hàn emperor, when young,
was named Dǒng Hóu;
his name was not upright,
he was confused, chaotic, and deluded,
and his descendants would perish in weakness.
The Xiàojīng Zhōnghuáng Chèn says:
"The sun carries the east,
recording fire's light.
Not one across,
sage and enlightened.
〔16〕Beyond four hundred [years],
the surname changes, and one becomes king.
All under heaven attribute merit and achieve great peace."
This clearly shows the surname and taboo name of the King of Wèi in the divinatory charts and prophecies.
The Yìyùn Qī says:
"The word is in the east,
west has wǔ,
two suns shine together, the sun is below.
He who is master
becomes a minister.
〔17〕Five eight forty,
yellow
qi received,
a true man emerges."
The words yán wǔ
form the character "Xǔ",
the two suns
form the character "Chāng";
Hàn is destined to perish at Xǔ,
and Wèi is destined to prosper at Xǔchāng.
Now the period of convergence is at
Xǔ,
which is its great manifestation.
The Yìyùn Qī also says:
"Ghost on the mountain,
grain and woman turn,
rule all under heaven."
Thereupon, the King of Wèi received the abdication of Hàn,
and performed a sacrifice at Fányáng,
when a yellow bird holding a red document
landed on the Shàngshūtái.
Thereupon, the era name was changed to Huángchū.
In the second year of Zhōngpíng of Hàn,
the people of Luòyáng circulated a rumor that there was a "yellow man" in the Hǔbēn Temple,
and tens of thousands came to observe daily,
blocking the roads.
In the first year of Zhōngpíng,
the Yellow Turban rebels rose,
saying:
"The Azure Heaven is dead,
the Yellow Heaven must be established."
This is the Wèi clan's reliance on Liú Xiàng's self-proclaimed symbol of Earth virtue.
Prior to this, in the forty-seventh year of King Jìng of Zhōu,
Duke Jǐng of Sòng asked the grand master Xíng Shǐzǐchén:
"What is the auspicious sign of the Way of Heaven?"
He replied:
"Five years from now, in the fifth month, on the day Dīnghài,
I will die.
Five years after my death, in the fifth month, on the day Dīngmǎo,
Wú will perish.
Five years after Wú's demise,
you, my lord, will die.
Four hundred years after your death,
Zhū will rule all under heaven."
All happened as he said.
Zhū ruling all under heaven
likely refers to the state after Wèi.
However, the mention of four hundred years is incorrect.
It is suspected that due to the long passage of time,
the chronicler made an error.
When Gāo Guì Xiāng Gōng was first born,
there was a radiant light that shone upon the rooms and houses.
Later, he ascended to a great position.
Liú Bèi was seven *chǐ* and seven *cùn* tall,
his hands hung down past his knees,
and he could see his own ears when he looked back.
The *Luò Shū Zhēn Yào Dù* says:
"For three *rì*, the red [emperor]
will have virtue flourish for nine generations, meeting Bèi,
together forming an imperial era."
〔一八〕The *Luò Shū Bǎo Yǔ Mìng* says:
"Heaven's measure of the imperial way, Bèi is called emperor,
to grasp the covenant and rule,
a hundred successes, never failing."
The *Luò Shū Lù Yùn Qí* says:
"Nine marquises and seven heroes contend for the people's lives,
bones cooked on the roads,
who will be the lord? Xuán will come."
〔一九〕Bèi's *zì* was Xuándé,
hence it says
"Xuán will come."
The *Xiàojīng Gōu Mìng Jué* says:
"The emperor will establish three,
nine will meet Bèi."
Before this,
the diviner Zhōu Qún said
that in the southwest, there was often yellow *qì*,
standing straight up for several *zhàng*,
persisting like this for years.
Whenever there were auspicious clouds and propitious winds,
they would descend from the celestial sphere to correspond.
〔二０〕In the middle of Jiàn'ān twenty-two,
there were often *qì* like banners,
moving from west to east,
traveling across the mid-heaven.
Divinatory texts say:
"There must be a Son of Heaven appearing in that direction."
Tàibái, Yínghuò, and Zhènxīng followed Suìxīng,
and a yellow dragon appeared in the Red Water of Jiānwéi Wǔyáng,
departing after nine days.
When Guān Yǔ was in Xiāngyáng,
men Zhāng Jiā and Wáng Xiū presented a jade seal.
Bèi later proclaimed himself emperor in Shǔ.
Sūn Jiān's ancestor was named Zhōng,
his family lived in Fùchūn, Wú Jùn,
residing solely with his mother.
His nature was extremely filial.
During a year of famine,
he made a living by growing melons.
Suddenly, three youths came to Zhōng asking for melons.
Zhōng treated them generously.
The three people said to Zhōng:
"This place below the mountain is good;
you can make a tomb here,
burying them,
and an Son of Heaven will emerge.
You can go down the mountain about a hundred paces,
look back and see us depart,
then you can bury them."
Zhōng went thirty paces,
then turned back,
and saw the three people riding white cranes and flying away.
When Zhōng died,
he was buried in that place.
The place was east of the county seat,
and above the tomb, there often appeared strange lights,
and five-colored cloud *qì* rose up to the heavens,
spreading for several *lǐ*.
The elders said to each other, "This is no ordinary *qì*;
the Sūn clan will surely rise."
When Jiān's mother was pregnant with Jiān,
she dreamt her intestines came out and wrapped around the Wú Chāngmén.
She told a neighbor's mother,
who said:
"How do you know it isn't auspicious?"
Chāngmén
was the outer gate of Wú.
When Jiān was born, his appearance was extraordinary.
Jiān's wife, the lady Wú, first became pregnant with her son Cè,
dreaming that the moon entered her bosom;
later, she conceived her son Quán,
and again dreamt that the sun entered her bosom.
She told Jiān:
"Previously, when I was pregnant with Cè,
I dreamt the moon entered my bosom.
Now I again dreamt the sun entered my bosom,
what does this mean?"
Jiān said:
"The sun and moon are the essence of *yīn* and *yáng*,
symbols of extreme nobility.
Will my descendants prosper?"
Quán had a square jaw, a large mouth, and a purple beard,
tall above and short below.
In the Han era, there was a man named Liú Wǎn,
who was skilled in physiognomy.
He saw Quán and his brothers,
and said:
"Although the Sūn brothers
each possess talent, intelligence, and discernment,
their prosperity will not last.
Only the middle brother, the *xiàolián*,
has an extraordinary and magnificent appearance,
his bones and body are not [imperfect],
he has the signs of great nobility,
and will also live the longest.
You should recognize this."
Quán was a *xiàolián* at that time.
Initially,
Qín Shǐhuáng made an eastern tour,
crossing the Jiāng.
A *wàngqì* observer said:
"Five hundred years later,
there will be an imperial *qì* in Jiāngdōng emanating from Wú,
and the land of Jīnlíng
will possess the potential for kingship."
Thereupon, Qín Shǐhuáng changed Jīnlíng's name to Mòlíng,
and excavated the northern mountain to sever its potential.
Upon reaching Wú,
he also ordered more than a hundred thousand prisoners to dig and pollute the land,
labeling it with an inauspicious name,
hence it was called Qiújuǎn Xiàn,
which is today's Jiāxīng Xiàn.
Han era diviners said:
"A yellow banner and purple canopy,
seen between Dǒu and Niú,
indicates imperial *qì* in Jiāngdōng."
During Xìngpíng in Xiàndì's reign,
a rhyme circulated in Wú:
"Golden carriage,
variegated ears.
Open the Chāngmén,
an emperor emerges."
In Huángchū three years of Wèi Wéndì,
Hàkǒu and Wǔchāng both reported seeing yellow dragons and phoenixes.
〔二一〕That year,
Quán assumed the imperial title.
He died at the age of seventy-one.
Quán's son Xiū was first enfeoffed as the King of Lángxié.
He dreamt of riding a dragon to heaven,
and looked back but could not see its tail.
Later he attained a great position,
but his son was deposed.
During the reigns of Emperor Yuán and Emperor Chéng of the Hàn dynasty,
prescient scholars said:
“When the Wèi kingdom has harmony,
a stone will be opened more than three thousand lǐ to the west,
with five horses tied to it,
and the inscription ‘討曹’ (tǎo Cáo – Punish Cáo).”
When the Wèi dynasty first rose,
in Liǔgǔ (Willow Valley) of Jīnshān (Golden Mountain) in Shāndān county, Zhāngyè commandery, a stone emerged.
Its circumference was seven xún,
[二二]its central height one rèn,
with a dark grey quality and a simple pattern,
and images of five horses, qílín, deer, phoenixes, and immortals.
It was first seen in Jiàn'ān,
formed in Huángchū,
and its inscription became complete in Tàihé.
By the third year of Qīnglóng,
the Xuánchuān (Mysterious Stream) in Liǔgǔ overflowed,
and the stone’s form changed,
resembling a cloud-turtle,
sixteen chǐ wide,
seventeen chǐ one cùn long,
[二三]and five zhàng eight cùn in circumference,
standing west of the stream.
There were twelve stone horses,
one ridden by an immortal,
one bridled,
[二四]five were shaped but not fully formed,
and five were fully formed.
There was also an ox, and images of the Eight Trigrams, constellations, and comets.
A jade casket with its lid open lay in front,
containing two jade jué and
one jade huáng.
Also, qílín, phoenixes, white tigers, horses, and oxen were arranged within it.
There was an inscription which read:

“上上三天王述大會討大曹金但取之金立中大金馬一疋中正大吉關壽此馬甲寅述水” (Shàng Shàng Sān Tiān Wáng shù dàhuì tǎo Dà Cáo jīn dàn qǔ zhī jīn lì zhōng dà Jīn Mǎ yī pǐ zhōngzhèng dàjí guān shòu cǐ mǎ Jiǎyín shù shuǐ – The supreme three Heaven Kings speak of a great assembly to punish the great Cáo; gold is taken from it; a great golden horse is established in the middle; upright, greatly auspicious; this horse secures longevity, Jiǎyín speaks of water).
In total, thirty-five characters.
[二五]The stone was dark grey,
but the figures and characters
were all written in white stone,
and all were raised.
Emperor Míng of Wèi disliked the character
“討” (tǎo – punish) in the inscription
and had it chiseled out, replacing it with
“計” (jì – plan),
filling it with dark grey stone.
Overnight, white stone filled it again.
At the time, it was hailed as an auspicious omen
and announced throughout the empire.
The recluse Zhāng Jiàn said:
“Divine omens are not yet manifest
and do not chase after past events.
This is an auspicious sign of the future,
and a strange anomaly of the present.”
Later, the Jìn dynasty received the abdication from Wèi, transferring power to the Sīmǎ clan.
The Grand Commandant’s subordinate Chéng Yī explained:
“‘大’ (dà – great) signifies the pinnacle of prosperity.
‘金’ (jīn – gold) is the elemental phase of Jìn.
‘中’ (zhōng – middle) is the convergence of things.
‘吉’ (jí – auspicious) is the beginning of blessings.
This speaks of the Sīmǎ clan’s rule over the empire,
born from an awakening of virtue,
a symbol corresponding to true auspiciousness for their rule.”
Yī also composed a eulogy:
“The imperial virtue extends far,
truly bringing down auspicious spirits.
Heaven gives birth to its image,
Earth nurtures its form.
The dark stone already manifest,
the plain inscription complete.
The auspicious tiger accords with benevolence,
the white qílín shines with essence.
Divine horses are self-depicted,
golden words describe their form.
Their body is righteous, and they rule;
the central fairness is clearly manifested.
Longevity is boundless,
for ten thousand years.”
Emperor Xuān had the appearance of a wolf’s gaze,
able to turn his face to look directly behind him
without changing the posture of his body.
Emperor Wǔ of Wèi once dreamed of three horses eating together in one trough.
Afterward, Emperor Xuān, and then Jǐng and Wén, successively served as chancellors,
eventually overthrowing the Cáo clan.
Emperor Wén had not yet established an heir,
and was considering Qí Xiàn Wáng Yōu.
Emperor Wǔ, then serving as Zhōngfǔjūn (Central Army Protector),
feared he would not be established.
He showed his physiognomy to Péi Xiù,
and Xiù told Emperor Wén:
“The Zhōngfǔjūn has hair that reaches the ground when unbound,
and hands that hang below his knees.
Such a celestial appearance
is not that of a subject.”
Because of this, he was established.
When he ascended to the Jìn throne,
in that very month,
Xiāngwǔ county reported a giant-like figure,
over three zhàng tall,
with footprints three chǐ one cùn long,
white-haired,
wearing a yellow single garment,
and a yellow turban,
who leaned on a staff and called out to the people, saying:
“Now there will be great peace.”
Soon after,
he received the abdication from Wèi.
In the first year of Xiánníng of Wǔdì,
a strong wind blew and broke the Emperor's she-tree.
A green qi emanated from the she-altar.
Diviners believed there was an emperor's qi in Dōngguǎn.
At that time, Liángyé Wǔwáng Zhòu was enfeoffed in Dōngguǎn.
Zhòu
was the ancestor of Yuándì.
Yuándì was born on a night in the second year of Xiánníng.
A light illuminated the room,
making the interior completely bright.
White hair grew on the left side of his rìjiǎo (sun-horn),
and his eyes shone with brilliant light.
He followed Huìdì to Yè.
Chéngdū Wáng Yǐng killed Dōng'ān Wáng Yáo.
Yáo
was Yuándì's paternal uncle.
The Emperor was afraid
and wanted to flee,
but the moon was bright,
the guards were urgent,
the four crossroads were cut off,
and he could not leave.
After a while,
the sky clouded over,
a great wind and rain descended,
the guards all took shelter,
and he was then able to leave.
Initially,
when Wǔdì attacked Wú,
Liángyé Wǔwáng Zhòu led his troops out through Túzhōng.
〔二六〕Wáng Hún pressed upon Lìyáng,
and Wáng Jùn had already reached the vicinity of the road.
Sūn Hào wished to surrender
and sent the Son of Heaven's imperial seal and ribbon.
He bypassed the two generals nearby
and sent them far away to Zhòu.
Those who knew the situation all found it strange.
Before Wú's downfall,
Línpíng Lake in Wújùn suddenly opened up.
A stone casket was found by the lake,
containing a small green stone
engraved with the character "Huángdì".
It was an old saying that if Línpíng Lake was blocked, the world would be in chaos;
if it opened, the world would be at peace.
The people of Wú considered it a good omen.
Soon after, Wú perished.
Later, Yuándì rose to power in Jiāngzuǒ.
After Wú fell,
purple clouds frequently appeared on Jiāng Shān.
Prognosticators also said
that there was still imperial qi in Jiāngdōng.
There was also a popular rhyme which said:
"Five horses roam and cross the Jiāng,
one horse transforms into a dragon."
Yuándì, along with the five kings of Xīyáng, Rǔnán, Nándùn, and Péngchéng, crossed the Jiāng,
and Yuándì ascended to the heavenly throne.
A chènshū (prophetic book) said:
"A bronze horse enters the sea, the period of Jiànyè."
Yuándì's childhood name was Tónghuán (Bronze Ring).
〔二七〕In the early Yǒngjiā era,
Yuándì, as Āndōng Jiāngjūn, was stationed in Jiànyè.
At that time, the four stars of Suì (Jupiter), Zhènxīng (Saturn), Chén (Mercury), and Tàibái (Venus) gathered between Niú and Nǚ constellations,
constantly hovering and moving back and forth.
In the fourth year of Jiànxīng of Mǐndì,
Chén Lóng, a man from Wǔjìn, Jìnlíng, found five bronze duó bells in a field.
The handles and mouths all had dragon and tiger shapes.
Furthermore, a hen with chicks and sparrows gathered in front of them;
though driven away, they returned again,
up to two or three times.
Also, three or four geese
flew high, honking,
circling east and west,
not descending day or night,
for six or seven days.
Chén Qīng from Shànyàn, Kuàijī, also found a zhànzhōng (stacking bell) in a well.
It was seven cùn and two fēn long,
with a mouth diameter of four cùn.
Although the instrument was small,
its craftsmanship was exquisite.
It had eighteen characters of ancient writing on it,
of which four characters were recognizable,
saying:
"Kuàijī huīmìng" (Illustrious decree of Kuàijī).
There was a large camphor tree in Yùzhāng,
thirty-five zhou (spans) in circumference.
It had been withered and dead for a long time.
During the Yǒngjiā era,
it suddenly flourished again.
Jǐngchún (Guō Pú) said these were all omens for Yuándì's restoration.
Initially, in the third year of Tàikāng of Wǔdì,
there was a bandit in Jiànyè.
Wǔ Zhèn, a man from Yúyáo, divined,
saying:
"The bandits are already annihilated.
In thirty-eight years,
there will be an emperor in Yángzhōu."
When Yuándì ascended the heavenly throne,
it was indeed thirty-eight years.
Before this,
Xuāndì had a favored general, Niú Jīn.
He had repeatedly achieved merits.
Xuāndì made a two-mouthed kě (wine vessel),
one mouth containing poisoned wine,
the other containing good wine.
He drank the good wine himself
and gave the poisoned wine to Jīn.
Jīn drank it and died immediately.
Jǐngdì said:
"Jīn is a famous general,
who could be greatly utilized.
Why harm him?"
Xuāndì said:
"Have you forgotten the stone omen, 'After the horse, there is an ox'?"
Yuándì's mother, Xiàhóu Fēi, had a secret affair with a junior official (xiǎoshǐ) of the Liángyé Kingdom whose surname was Niú,
and gave birth to Yuándì.
When Mǐndì was established,
Pílíng was renamed Jìnlíng.
At that time, Yuándì began to dominate Jiāng and Yáng,
while the Róng and Dí proclaimed themselves rulers,
and the Western Capital was weak.
Gān Bǎo believed this was a sign that Jìn would perish in the west and rise in the east.
Sòng Wǔdì lived in Dāntú.
On the night of his birth,
a divine light illuminated the chamber.
That evening,
sweet dew descended upon the grave trees.
His imperial father, considering Gāozǔ's extraordinary birth,
named him Qíjínú.
After his imperial mother passed away,
he was raised by his maternal uncle,
and his name was changed to Jìjínú.
When he was young, he was unrestrained and fond of wine.
Returning from the capital,
he rested at an inn.
The innkeeper's wife said,
"There is wine in the room;
help yourself."
The Emperor entered the room,
drank from the side of a jar,
and, drunk, lay on the floor.
At that time, Sītú Wáng Mì had a protégé living in Dāntú,
who, returning home,
also came to this inn.
The innkeeper's wife said,
"Liú Láng is in the room;
you can go in and drink with him."
This protégé entered the room,
then emerged startled and said to the innkeeper's wife,
"How can such a strange creature be in the room?"
The innkeeper's wife hurriedly went in
and saw that the Emperor had already woken up.
The innkeeper's wife secretly asked,
"What did you see just now?"
The protégé said,
"I saw a creature
of five colors like a蛟lóng;
it was not Liú Láng."
The protégé returned and reported this to Wáng Mì.
Wáng Mì warned him not to speak of it
and befriended Jìjínú.
The Emperor once traveled to Xiàpī
and met a Shāméi.
The Shāméi said,
"The region south of the Jiāng River will soon be in chaos,
and you will surely be the one to save it."
The Emperor had suffered from a hand wound for many years.
The Shāméi took out a packet of yellow powder from his bosom and gave it to the Emperor, saying,
"This wound is difficult to heal;
without this medicine, it cannot be cured."
The Shāméi suddenly disappeared.
When the powder was applied to the wound, it immediately healed.
The Emperor treasured and kept the remaining powder.
Later, during military campaigns, he was frequently wounded;
there were many instances of being pierced through.
When the powder was applied,
there was no wound that did not heal immediately.
From childhood to adulthood,
he constantly saw two dragons before his eyes.
Initially small,
they grew larger as he became more distinguished.
Chē Sǒu, a native of Jìnlíng, was skilled in physiognomy.

In the early years of Emperor Ān of Jìn's Yìxī reign,
the Emperor first quelled the Jìn disturbances

In Huòshān of Lújiāng, a bell would often chime twelve times.
When the Emperor was about to campaign against Guān and Luò,
Huòshān collapsed,
and six bells emerged.
Their craftsmanship was exquisite and marvelous,
and they bore one hundred and sixty characters of ancient writing.
In Jìzhōu, a Shāméi named Fǎchēng was about to die.
He told his disciple Pǔyán,
"The deity Sōnghuáng informed me that
there is a General Liú in Jiāngdōng,
a descendant of the Hàn house,
who is destined to receive the Mandate of Heaven.
I shall give thirty-two bì discs
and one ingot of gold,
as a token to the general.
The thirty-two bì discs
represent the number of generations for the Liú clan."
Pǔyán reported this to his fellow student Fǎyì.
In the seventh month of the thirteenth year, Fǎyì
found thirty-two jade bì discs
and one ingot of gold beneath the stone altar of the Sōnggāo Temple.
At the water's edge in Chénggù County, Hànzhōng,
there was a sudden sound of thunder.
Soon after, the bank collapsed,
and twelve bronze bells were discovered.
Also, Sòng Yáo, a commoner from Gǒng County, found nine ears of auspicious grain.
Two years later, he received the abdication from the Jìn dynasty.
Kǒngzǐ's Hélùo Chèn said:
"Two mouths, a erected spear, cannot be squared;
two metals carving each other emit a divine sharpness.
An empty hole with no master, 'qí' enters its center;
a woman standing alone also forms a pair."
"Two mouths, an erected spear"
form the character "Liú" (劉).
The Jìn dynasty was of the metal element,
and the surname Liú also contains metal,
hence it says "two metals carving each other."
"An empty hole with no master, 'qí' enters its center"
forms the character "Jì" (寄).
"A woman standing alone also forms a pair"
forms the character "nú" (奴).
After Jìn abdicated to Sòng,

"From the first year of Yìxī
to the tenth month of the first year of Yuánxī,

From the first year of Yìxī to the first day of the eleventh month of the first year of Yuánxī,

All eclipses began from the top,

On the eleventh day of the eighth month of the seventh year of Yìxī,

Dàhuǒ,

From the eleventh year until the first year of Yuánxī,

The prognostication: 'The moon entering Tàiwēi's court,

In the tenth month of the thirteenth year,

The prognostication: 'Zhènxīng guarding Tàiwēi,

On the seventeenth day of the fifth month of the fourteenth year,

The prognostication says: 'When a star obfuscates within Běidǒu,

On the twenty-ninth day of the seventh month of the fourteenth year,

The prognostication says: 'When a comet appears in Tàiwēi,

Another prognostication: 'The world will gain a Zhàorén.'
Zhàorén
is a sage ruler.

On the first day of the tenth month of the fourteenth year,

Yínghuò and Zhènxīng hooking into the celestial court of Tàiwēi

In the twelfth month of the fourteenth year,

Dǒu and Niú
are where calendrical calculations begin.
The prognostication says: 'The convergence of three stars
signifies the establishment of a new order.'
On the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month of the first year of Yuánxī,

The Yì Zhuàn says: 'When dragons appear in winter,

and a great man will respond to the omen of the Mandate of Heaven.'
The Jīn Cī Shī says: 'Dàhuǒ has a heart embraced by water;
a long hundred years is its time.'"
Huǒ,
the celestial field of Sòng.
Shuǐ,
the virtue of Sòng.
Jīn Cī Shī also says: "When clouds emerge and two gradually wish to rise,

The two clouds
form the character "Xuán".
The shortness refers to
the brevity of the clouds' blessings.
If the mountain is hidden and unseen,

The Yì says: "The southwest gains friends."
Therefore, it can trouble Huánfù.
Liú Xiàng's Chèn says: "The first five exhaust their efforts to bring about great peace,

The former phrase refers to Your Majesty's minor taboo name,

In the fifth month of the eleventh year,

During the Tàixīng reign,

From Jìn Xuāndì to the present,

In the eighth year of Yìxī,
mulberry trees grew at the Grand Altar of the Soil,
which was particularly conspicuous.
The number six
is a high position.
In the twenty-fifth year of Jiàn'ān of Hàn,
after one hundred and ninety-six years, it abdicated to Wèi.
From Huángchū to the second year of Xiánxī of Wèi,

From Tàishǐ to the current second year of Yuánxī of Jìn,

The count of the three dynasties ends,
all with six years."
When Shàodì ascended the throne,
in the fourth month of the third year of Jǐngpíng,
five-colored clouds appeared in the west.
At that time, Wéndì was the Inspector of Jīngzhōu,

During Wéndì's Yuánjiā reign,
rumors circulated that a Son of Heaven would emerge from Qiántáng.
Therefore, a garrison was stationed in Qiántáng to guard against it.
Later, Xiàowǔdì ascended the great position in the meditation hall of Xīntíng Sì.
The sound of "chán"
and
"qián"

When Tàizōng was the Inspector of Xúzhōu,

In the early Yǒngguāng reign of the former deposed emperor,
there was again a rumor that a Son of Heaven would emerge from Xiāngzhōu.
The young emperor wished to travel south to Xiāngchuān to suppress it.
Soon after, the Prince of Xiāngdōng ascended the exalted position,

The imperial historian respectfully notes that
what the Jìzhōu Daoist Fǎchēng said about thirty-two jade bi disks
being the number of generations for the Sòng clan
was probably the number of years.
To say it was the number of generations
was to misrepresent his words.
Thirty-two
is two times thirty,
which makes sixty.
From the Sòng clan receiving the mandate to abdicating to Qí,
it was a total of sixty years, it is said.

The Qílín
is a benevolent beast.
The male is called Qí,
the female is called Lín.
It appears when no fetuses are cut open and no eggs are broken.
It has the body of a roe deer and the tail of an ox,
the neck of a wolf and one horn,
a yellow color and the feet of a horse.
It embodies benevolence and upholds righteousness,
its voice is in tune with zhòng and lǚ,
its steps are in line with compasses and squares.
It does not tread on living insects,
nor break living grass.
It does not eat what is unrighteous,
nor drink from stagnant pools.
It does not enter pits and traps,
nor walk into nets.
It appears when a wise ruler's actions and movements are orderly.
The male's cry is called "departure of the sage,"
the female's cry is called "return to harmony."
A spring cry is called "nurturing the young,"
a summer cry is called "fostering peace."

The Fènghuáng
is a benevolent bird.
It appears when no fetuses are disemboweled and no eggs are broken.
Sometimes it soars, sometimes it perches.
The male is called Fèng,
the female is called Huáng.
It has a snake's head and a swallow's chin,
a tortoise's back and a soft-shelled turtle's belly,
a crane's neck and a chicken's beak,
a swan's front and a fish's tail,
a green head and paired wings,
it stands like a heron and thinks like a mandarin duck.
On its head it carries Dē, on its back it bears Rén,
on its neck it holds Yì, on its breast it embraces Xìn,
its feet tread Zhèng, and its tail embodies Wǔ.
Its small notes resonate with bells,
its large notes resonate with drums.
Stretching its neck and flapping its wings,
five colors radiate forth.
It stirs the eight winds,
brings seasonal rain,
eats with measure,
drinks with propriety,
its departure is refined,
its arrival is auspicious.
When it roams, it always chooses its ground;
when it drinks, it does not alight carelessly.
When it calls,
the male says
"jié jié" (節節),
and the female says
"zú zú" (足足).
A morning call is called Fāmíng,
a daytime call is called Shàngshuò,
an evening call is called Guīchāng,
a dusk call is called Gùcháng,
a night call is called Bǎocháng.
Its joy is expressed
by circling and hovering,
in harmonious and melodious tones.
Only the Fènghuáng can understand all things,
connect with heavenly blessings,
symbolize a hundred forms,
reach the royal way,
lead the five notes,
complete the nine virtues,
possess both civil and military accomplishments,
and set the lower states in order.
Therefore, when one obtains a vision of the Fèng,
if it's one, it passes by;
if it's two, it soars;
if it's three, it perches;
if it's four, it resides for spring and autumn;
if it's five, it resides for life.

, a yellow dragon was seen in a well in Shēnxian county.
In the third year of Jǐngyuán, in the second month
, a green dragon was seen in a well in Zhǐ county.
Before Liú Bèi ascended the throne
, a yellow dragon was seen in Chìshuǐ, Wǔyáng
, and it departed after nine days.
In the first year of Huángwǔ of Sūn Quán of Wú, in the third month
, Póyáng reported seeing a yellow dragon.
In the first year of Huánglóng of Sūn Quán of Wú, in the fourth month
, Xiàkǒu and Wǔchāng both reported seeing yellow dragons.
[一０]Quán subsequently changed the era name.
He had a "Yellow Dragon Tooth" banner made
, which was always with the army.
Advances and retreats were determined by its direction.
He ordered Hú Zōng to compose a *fù*.
In the fifth year of Chìwū of Sūn Quán of Wú, in the third month
, Hǎiyán county reported seeing two yellow dragons in a well in the county.
In the eleventh year of Chìwū
, Yúnyáng reported seeing a yellow dragon.
Two more yellow dragons were seen in Wǔlíng Wúshòu
, their colors shining brilliantly.
In the fourth year of Yǒng'ān of Sūn Xiū of Wú, in the ninth month
, Bùshān reported seeing a white dragon.
[一一]
In the fifth year of Yǒng'ān, in the seventh month
, Shǐxīn reported seeing a yellow dragon.
In the sixth year of Yǒng'ān, in the fourth month
, Quánlíng reported seeing a yellow dragon.
In the first year of Tàishǐ of Emperor Wǔ of Jìn, in the twelfth month
, two green dragons were seen in Dìngtáo, Jìyīn.
In the first year of Tàishǐ, in the twelfth month
, a green dragon was seen in Tāngyīn, Wèijùn.

, the relevant officials reported:
"Jiāo Shèng, the Administrator of Zhāngyè, reports that
a green dragon was seen at the entrance of the Dàliǔ Valley in Dǐchí county."
[一二]

, a black dragon was seen in Zhànshí village, Jìnlíng.

A numinous turtle (*língguī*)
is a divine turtle.
When the ruler's virtue and benevolence are profound and clear
, and hunting and fishing in mountains and rivers are done according to the season, they appear.
Their five colors are bright.
At three hundred years old, they swim upon lotus leaves;
at three thousand years old, they always swim upon *juǎněr* (a type of plant).
They know existence and non-existence
, and are clear about good and ill fortune.
When Yǔ lived in humble palaces
, a numinous turtle appeared.
The black turtle diagram (*xuánguī shū*)
is a heavenly talisman.
When the ruler's virtue reaches the deep springs
, then the Luò river brings forth the turtle diagram.
At the beginning of Emperor Wén of Wèi's reign
, a divine turtle emerged from Língchí.
During Sūn Quán of Wú's time
, a numinous turtle emerged in Zhāng'ān, Kuàijī.
In the second year of Xiánxī of Emperor Yuán of Wèi, on the *jiǎchén* day of the second month
, a numinous turtle was captured in Qú county and presented.
Jìn Chángshā Wáng was implicated in the affair of his half-brother Chǔ Wáng Wěi
, and was transferred to be enfeoffed in Chángshān
, later returning to his former state.
While in Chángshān, a well was dug
, four *zhàng* deep into the ground,
and white jade, three to four *chǐ* square, was found.
Beneath the jade was a large stone
, and within it was a turtle over two *chǐ* long
. People at the time considered it an auspicious sign for the restoration of his state.
In the nineteenth year of Yuánjiā of Emperor Wén of Sòng, on the *wùshēn* day of the fourth month
, a white turtle was seen in Yúháng, Wúxīng
, and Tàishǒu Wén Dào'ēn presented it.
In the twentieth year of Yuánjiā, on the *xīnmǎo* day of the fourth month
, a white turtle was seen in Yúháng, Wúxīng
, and Yángzhōu Cìshǐ Shǐxīng Wáng Jùn reported it.
In the twenty-fourth year of Yuánjiā, on the *jiǎwǔ* day of the tenth month
, Yángzhōu Cìshǐ Shǐxīng Wáng Jùn captured a white turtle and presented it.
In the third year of Dàmíng of Emperor Xiàowǔ, on the *wùzǐ* day of the third month
, a hairy turtle (*máoguī*) was seen in Guǎngdé, Xuānchéng, and Tàishǒu Zhāng Biàn presented it.
In the sixth month, on the day Rén-yín, of the fourth year of Dàmíng,
the imperial carriage proceeded to the Jítián (Sacrificial Field).
A white turtle was seen in the Qiānmǔ,
which Liú Xiùzhī, the Right Púshè of the Shàngshū, presented.
In the eighth month, on the day Yǐ-wèi, of the seventh year of Dàmíng,
a hairy turtle was seen at the residence of prince Xīn'ān, Zǐluán,
and captured to be presented.
In the eighth month, on the first day (Sok), Bǐng-chén, of the second year of Tàishǐ of Emperor Míng,
a four-eyed turtle was seen in Kuàijī.
Xiūruò, Prince of Bālíng and Grand Administrator of Kuàijī, presented it.
In the eighth month, on the day Bǐng-yín, of the second year of Tàishǐ,
a six-eyed turtle was seen in Chángshān, Dōngyáng,
its markings like Yáo and Guà.
Liú Xié, the Grand Administrator, presented it.
In the ninth month, on the day Jǐ-sì, of the sixth year of Tàishǐ,
an eight-eyed turtle was seen in Gùzhāng, Wúxīng.
Chǔ Yuān, the Grand Administrator, presented it.
In the tenth month, on the day Rén-xū, of the first year of Tàiyù of Emperor Míng,
a hairy turtle was captured in Yángxiàn county, Yìxīng.
Wáng Yùn, the Grand Administrator, presented it.
The Lóngmǎ (Dragon-Horse)
is a benevolent horse,
an essence of the Yellow River.
It is eight chi and five cun tall,
has a long neck and wings,
with drooping hair on its sides,
and its cry has nine laments.
(One version reads "sound".)
The Ténghuáng
is a divine horse.
Its color is yellow.
It appears when the king governs the four directions with virtue.
A white horse with a red mane
is seen when the king employs the worthy and good.
The Zémǎ (Marsh Horse)
arrives when the king toils for the common people.
The Xiàmǎ (Summer Horse)
has a black body and white mane and tail.
The Yīnmǎ Luò (Yīn Horse Luò)
has a white body and black mane and tail.
The Zhōumǎ Xīn (Zhōu Horse Xīn)
has a red body and black mane and tail.
In the Yuánhé reign of Emperor Zhāng of Hàn,
divine horses were seen in various commanderies and states.
In the second month, on the day Rén-zǐ, of the sixth year of Yǒngjiā of Emperor Huái of Jìn,
a divine horse neighed at the South City Gate.
In the sixth month, on the first day (Sok), Jiǎ-shēn, of the fourteenth year of Tàiyuán of Emperor Xiàowǔ of Jìn,
Fèi Tǒng, the Cǐshǐ of Níngzhōu, reported:
"In the Diānchí county of Jìnnìng, which is under my jurisdiction,
there used to be a river
about two hundred li in circumference.
On the twenty-eighth day, Xīn-hài, of the sixth month,
two divine horses,
one white and one black,
suddenly emerged from the river,
a hundred paces from the bank.
A county resident, Dǒng Cōng, saw them."
The white elephant
arrives when the ruler cultivates self-restraint with moderation.
In the twelfth month, on the day Bǐng-chén, of the first year of Yuánjiā of Emperor Wén of Sòng,
a white elephant was seen in Táoyáng, Línglíng.
In the third month, on the day Dīng-hài, of the sixth year of Yuánjiā,

In the third month of the second year of Yuánshòu of Emperor Wǔ of Hàn,

The white fox
arrives when the king is benevolent and wise.
In the seventh month of the eighth year of Xiánkāng of Emperor Chéng of Jìn,
Mùróng Huàng, King of Yàn, reported seeing a white fox within his state.
The red bear
enters the state
when sycophants are far away
and treacherous rogues cease.

The nine-tailed fox,
King Wén obtained it,
and the Eastern Yí submitted.

nine-tailed foxes were seen in various commanderies and states.
In the eleventh month, on the day Jiǎ-wǔ, of the first year of Huángchū of Emperor Wén of Wèi,
a nine-tailed fox was seen in Juànchéng,
and also in Qiáo.
The white deer
arrives when the king's enlightenment and kindness reach those below.
In the tenth month of the seventh year of Jiànchū of Emperor Zhāng of Hàn,
the imperial carriage was on a western tour,
and a white deer was obtained at the Línpíng Guān.
In the Yuánhé reign of Emperor Zhāng of Hàn,
white deer were seen in various commanderies and states.

The three-horned beast
appears when the laws and regulations of the former kings are cultivated.
(Omission)
The one-horned beast
appears when the world is unified and at peace.
(Omission)
The six-footed beast
appears when the ruler consults with the multitude of commoners.
(Omission)
The shoulder-to-shoulder beast
appears when the ruler's virtue extends to the lonely and widowed.
(Omission)
The Xièzhì knows right from wrong,
and appears when legal disputes are fair.
(Omission)
The white tiger.
When the ruler is not tyrannical,
the white tiger is benevolent
and harms no living things.

a white tiger was captured in Nánjùn.

〔二一〕the Emperor dreamt of Emperor Guāngwǔdì and Empress Guāngliè.
He awoke joyful from the dream,
but was sorrowful and could not sleep.
The next morning, he visited the imperial tomb.
All officials and foreign guests gathered.
The Grand Steward, Tàicháng Chéng, reported,
that on that day, the leaves of the tomb trees had sweet dew.
The Emperor ordered all officials to collect the sweet dew.
The Emperor himself lay prostrate on the imperial bed,
looking at the items in the Empress Dowager's dressing case,
weeping.
He then ordered to change the cosmetic items in the case.

Treatise 19: Auspicious Omens (Part 2)
Auspicious grain (Jiāhé),
the chief of the five grains,
appears when the king's virtue is flourishing.
Then two stalks bear ears together.
In the virtue of Zhōu,
three stalks bore ears together;
in the virtue of Shāng,
different stalks from the same root bore ears;
in the virtue of Xià,
different roots bore ears together.
In the fourth year of Yuánkāng of Hàn Xuāndì,
auspicious black millet
descended upon commanderies and states.
In the middle of Yuánhé of Hàn Zhāngdì,
auspicious grain grew in commanderies and states.

auspicious grain grew in Jiǔzhēn,
with one hundred and fifty-six stalks
