for heaven itself not to deviate [from this]
is the virtue of the sagely king.
Thus, he can influence the two luminaries (heaven and earth)
and mold all existence.
Examining
ancient and modern times,
and verifying with maps and wei-texts,
there has never been a case where virtue was lacking and transformation deficient,
yet auspicious objects manifested clearly.
Since the imperial mandate was received,
the celestial luminaries have harmonized,
hence plants and trees
Manifesting spiritual power,
mountains and abysses offer treasures.
We humbly consider that Your Majesty embodies the celestial and governs the world,
receiving auspicious omens continuously.
When a phoenix dances in the western suburbs,
and a dragon appears in the eastern city,
when the chieftain of the sea presents the changed
black feathers (of a mythical bird),
and the God of the Yellow River opens the source of clear water,
the symbolic virtues of the Three Dynasties
could not surpass this.
What is hidden is always revealed,
no distance is too far to reach;
interpreters of foreign languages arrive annually,
and auspicious
omens arrive monthly.
Previously, when Your Majesty personally tilled the southern fields,
auspicious grains were repeatedly planted,
and the response of the gods
was especially abundant in this regard.
With the Four Seas now pacified,
and the five peoples content in their livelihoods,
Your Majesty wished to emulate
Fényáng and
begin the construction of a spiritual park.
As soon as the fragrant orchids were planted,
sweet dew frequently flowed;
as soon as the simple structures were completed,
auspicious grains accumulated like a heap.
The omens of great peace
are thus present.
I, your humble subject,
with my meager standing,
fill a position in the highest ranks of officialdom,
bathed in fragrant dew,
and am privileged to witness these hidden blessings,
unable to contain my joy.
I respectfully present one essay on the Auspicious Grain and Sweet Dew,
though it is insufficient
to extol Your Majesty's splendid achievements,
and I am filled with awe and trepidation.
The頌 (sòng) says: When the two primal forces were divided,
the three spiritual beings delighted in their lord.
Their responses were in harmony and accord,
as true now as in ancient times.
Whom does the Heavenly Way favor?
Only the benevolent does it assist.
Imperial merits and deeds,
Your Majesty's governance
surpasses the world.
The four peoples equally follow the standard;
our Sovereign embodies this.
Both sagacious and divine,
Your Majesty brilliantly reveals wisdom and contemplation.
The nine clans are harmonious,
the myriad states are well-ordered.
Virtue establishes
Your position,
the Way leads to harmony and prosperity.
How profound and unceasing,
how clear and trustworthy is the Eastern Heir.
Born with wisdom and early sagacity,
his greatness is like a towering peak, his mind deep as an abyss.
By following his innate mind, he is discerning;
his good reputation spreads widely.
He continues
the glorious martial deeds,
his presence matches the sun and stars.
The Hàn Emperor Xuān built the Hégōng Palace,
the Hàn dynasty arose and flourished like Wèiyāng.
How much more so in this sacred dynasty,
when the entire realm is already at peace.
Following old customs,
Your Majesty considers the former
kings.
Thus, the Língxiāo Palace was built,
and then the Jǐngyáng Palace was erected.
How splendid is Jǐngyáng,
on the banks of the celestial abyss.
Cool and refreshing, standing firm,
cloud-kissing halls rise uniquely.
Plants are nurtured here,
and moving
creatures find their rest here.
Gazing far at the river's waves,
facing all around the towering peaks.
The transforming virtue is pervasive,
the auspicious omens are abundant.
Auspicious seeds are bestowed,
presenting good fortune at their initial growth.
Sweet dew congeals
in spring,
and auspicious grains ripen in autumn.
They contain richness without being ordinary,
and successive years remain abundant.
In the past, when Fàngxūn (Yáo) reigned,
he passed through several dynasties.
Down to Chónghuá (Shùn),
he leaned on a fan in his pure kitchen.
How resplendent are the imperial blessings,
all things compete to shine.
Comparing them to ancient records,
they are broadcast in these folk songs.
I, your subject, with my six deficiencies,
hold two official posts.
I am ashamed before Zhònggǔn (Rǎn Yǒu),
and also embarrassed before Zhèng
Zī (Zǐ Chǎn).
How can I forget the retired life,
and delight in the Way in an enlightened era?
I dare to recount these auspicious blessings,
ashamed of my lacking words.
The Cónglǐngjūn and Jíyángxiànhóu Shěn Yǎnzhī respectfully presented the頌 (sòng) on Auspicious Grain, which says:
"Brilliantly shining are the auspicious diagrams,
clearly manifested are the propitious rites.
When the destiny declines, they are hidden;
when the times prosper, they first appear.
The patterns on silken fabrics are distinct,
the bird writings are discernible.
How glorious is the sagely ruler,
who sustains all things over vast distances.
The sun and moon shine brightly,
their brilliant radiance extends to the heavens.
(Part 1)
His governance is subtle, his position lofty,
his service to the divine and his achievements are grand.
Profound is his benevolent grace,
empty and tranquil is his Daoist governance.
He harmonizes transformation and pacifies the heart,
adjusts music and changes nature.
The Jade Steelyard (celestial body) aligns with his person,
the Twinkling Jade (star) attains its proper place.
Great stars cast down their light,
auspicious clouds establish joy.
(Part 2)
The utmost benevolence he extends,
no darkness is left unvanquished.
The utmost harmony he inspires,
no circumstance is left unrevealed.
Mandarin ducks emerge from the cinnabar cave,
parrots rise from Western Xiāng.
White deer cross the sea,
white birds fly over the river.
Their sounds echo in the vast sky,
their forms appear at the sunny peak.
(Part 3)
Governing people, serving Heaven,
he is diligent and reverent.
When the dark plow first begins its task,
the high granaries are already full.
Auspicious grains grow repeatedly,
sweet dew flows like liquid.
They rise splendidly in the morning fields,
their ears sway in the moist ground.
The separate spikes gather their awns,
the glorious expanse provides shade.
(Part 4)
Full baskets signify Yin,
the mulberry piercing (silkworms) signifies Zhōu.
Now in our great Sòng dynasty,
divine blessings are intimately interwoven.
The Emperor ultimately shows humility,
his thoughts on it are ceaseless.
He personally presents them to the ancestral temple,
reverent and dutifully following tradition.
He bestows blessings with sincerity,
and piously offers sacrifices.
(Part 5)
He distributes ranks and promotes merits,
issues wise edicts to glorify virtue.
His grace extends to the hidden and the manifest,
rewards reach the distant frontiers.
The Yellow River clears, the sea is calm,
mountains blossom, and peaks shine.
Distant tributes are brought from afar,
overflowing bounty is offered.
Beyond the sun's reach,
they change their attire and request instruction.
(Part 6)
Responding grandly to a flourishing age,
pacifying all and enjoying frequent harvests.
Peacefully returning to simplicity,
orderly in great harmony.
The high (officials) store for future use,
the low (people) know what to follow.
They look up to the royal standard,
and sing the Nánfēng song.
The grand name is supreme,
eternally preserved without end.
(Part 7)"

On the *gēngwǔ* day of the eighth month of the eighteenth year of Yuánjiā of Emperor Wén of Sòng,
Shāng Shìbǎo of Shānyīn in Kuàijī captured a white dove,
whose eyes and feet were both red.
Shǐxīngwáng Jùn, the Inspector of Yángzhōu, presented it.
Hé Chéngzhī, the Grand Master of the Crown Prince's Household, submitted a memorial, saying: "I humbly examine the ancient canons
and consult previous records,
wherever the king's virtue extends,
things respond by appearing.
Thus, the black egret of Xuánhù
manifested the great achievements of Dì Xuān,
and the sparrows of Fēng
gōng
signified the glorious reign of Jī Wén.
I humbly consider that Your Majesty, in succeeding to the throne with renewed brilliance,
eternally emulates your ancestors,
spreading harmonious benevolence throughout the land,
and illuminating the imperial wisdom across the heavens
and regions.
Therefore, the nine domains are united in heart,
the myriad states embrace love,
the celestial spirits send down auspicious signs,
and the earthly deities offer blessings.
Precious rarities accumulate,
and propitious omens arrive in full.
In the first
ten days of last July,
at dawn,
the yellow radiance shone brightly,
the universe was clear and expansive,
auspicious winds harmonized with the musical scales,
and sweet dew sprinkled.
Even if the magnificent vermilion light on the celestial balance
and the glorious light
portended spirits in the River Records,
they cannot surpass this.
I, not measuring my humble ignorance,
secretly yearn to compose a song of praise by striking the ground,
[二０]or forming a chant by pounding pestles.
Recently, I also had the opportunity to observe the white doves,
my eyes delighting in their extraordinary beauty,
and my heart rejoicing in their magnificent splendor.
I humbly present one eulogy.
My rustic thoughts are ancient and crude,
my intentions common and unrefined,
insufficient to express such pure brilliance
or fully extol such profound
principles.
Looking forward and backward,
each follows their own aspiration.
I humbly venture to report this."
His Eulogy of the White Dove states: "The three powers harmonize their affections,
the five spirits meet in nature.
Principle moves in mystical accord,
the Dao is truly profoundly sacred.
Oh, how majestic is the Emperor,
matching Heaven in his mandate.
[二一]The morning light ascends
to its station,
the eight directions reflect it.
Auspicious signs arrive,
glorious light spreads joy.
The universe shines brightly,
the sun and moon radiate splendor.
Tempering mountains and refining marshes,
thus gentle beauty is born.
Returning
dragons signify purity,
separated ears of grain unite on the stem.
Fluttering doves,
how bright their radiance!
They preen their feathers in the imperial domain,
displaying their freshness in the imperial capital.
Without benevolence, they do not gather,
[二二]without virtue,
they do not return.
In the evening, they follow the ritual phoenix,
perching in the sheltered imperial chambers.
How earnest is the enlightened sovereign,
industrious from dawn till dusk!
His virtue is exalted,
towering like a mountain.
His beneficence is abundant,
nourishing like a deep abyss.
Ritual and music reach all four directions,
songs
of praise spread far and wide.
Distant regions with sparse vegetation offer tribute,
nine interpreters guide their words.
From the time of Táng's initial flourish,
love met with auspicious blessings.
My life is already auspicious,
yet the year is late.
With a heart
of old age,
I sing the king's rule.
In the morning, I bask in the eternal wind,
in the evening, I rinse my mouth with sweet dew.
I delight in the Spirit Terrace,
[二三]not far from its stronghold."
In the ninth month of the twenty-fourth year of Yuánjiā,
white doves were seen again.
On the *gēngxū* day,
Shěn Yǎnzhī, the Central Leader of the Military, submitted a memorial, saying: "I have heard that the beauty of integrity and prosperity
is bestowed upon enlightened kings,
and the arrival of auspicious omens
never fails to attend wise sovereigns.
Thus, the singing phoenix symbolizes the transformation brought by imperial rule,
and the soaring wren signifies the benevolence
of removing nets.
Your Majesty inherited the throne with virtue,
succeeding to the world with sagacity and brilliance.
Your teachings purify the records of birds,
your governance flourishes like the cloud officials,
ritual permeates like a common river,
and beneficence reaches the vermilion frontier.
Heaven bestows clarity
How splendid!
The people delight in the gentle breeze,
and by it the stars shine brightly,
the sun and moon glow with splendor.
Divine patterns and earthly threads,
filling the universe, revealing its secrets,
with white essence and black patterns,
filling the spiritual
garden.
All responsive omens have arrived,
but the auspicious signs awaited by the heart have not yet appeared.
However, as the plain-colored dove comes from afar,
flying back with its wings,
its nature gentle and refined,
its feathers and appearance fresh and beautiful,
having heard of it in earlier accounts,
and now personally witnessing this auspicious phenomenon,
I cannot help but dance with joy,
and respectfully present a eulogy.
The words do not follow classical precedents,
and the style lacks embellishment,
[二四]I am ashamed that it is insufficient to splendidly manifest
the imperial felicity,
or to magnificently praise its beauty;
it merely reflects common praises,
and is appended at the end of the chapter.
The eulogy says: There is a sage-like demeanor,
it is the gleaming dove.
Its nature aligns with the five teachings,
its name is recorded in the plain hills.
When the Yīn (殷) dynasty was flourishing,
it came gracefully to roam.
When the Hàn (漢) record was splendidly glorious,
it
descended and rested.
(First stanza) How manifest is the glorious Sòng (宋)!
Its sagely blessings are widely spread.
The sagely emperor is on the throne,
his Way illuminates the grand palace.
His administration is just,
his filial piety is forever spoken of.
People
are harmonious on earth,
spirits are joyful in heaven.
(Second stanza) Ritual and music are perfectly ordered,
spiritual creatures are all manifest.
White sparrows gather on sprouts,
red phoenixes perch in the suburbs.
Patterned zōu (騶) beasts follow in pairs,
auspicious grains
grow tall.
Brilliantly white-feathered,
they are tamed and submissive to the transforming influence of the court.
(Third stanza) How could it be that it goes to the forest,
and must be the zhǔ (栩) tree of Zhōu (周)?
How could it be that it returns to righteousness,
and must be the place of Shāng (商)?
It only
relies on virtue,
it only dwells in benevolence.
Nourishing its form on the sunny side of the mountain,
cleansing its posture in the imperial domain.
(Fourth stanza) When laws and calendars are promulgated and prosper,
and reason and feeling are connected in turn,
pheasants fly from Yuècháng (越常),
egrets rise from Xīyōng (西雍).
They all arrive and settle,
truly embodying this countenance.
This unites the people's hearing,
and makes the royal wind solemn.
(Fifth stanza)
Yuán Yáng (玉羊) (Jade Sheep):
appears when Shī Kuàng (師曠) comes.

In the fourth month of Yǒngxīng (永興) second year of Emperor Huán (桓) of Hàn (漢) [154 CE],
at the residence of the Guānglù Xūn (光祿勳) office clerk,
at night, a green vapor appeared beneath the wall,
and a jade hook and a jade jue (玦) were found, one of each.
The hook was seven cun (寸) and three fen (分) long,
the jue (玦) had a circumference of five cun (寸) and four fen (分),
and both were carved throughout their bodies.
On the rénzǐ (壬子) day of the second month of Yǒngjiā (永嘉) sixth year of Emperor Huái (懷) of Jìn (晉) [312 CE],

The inscription read
"May you live for ten thousand years."
He presented it to the King of Jìn (晉).

Lù Yǒng (路永), the Governor of Yùzhōu (豫州), presented it.
The Zùozuò Láng (著作郎) Cáo Pí (曹毗) presented a eulogy for the jade tripod.

Flounder (Bǐmùyú):
appears when the ruler's virtue extends to the hidden and obscure.
(Lacuna)
Coral hook (Shānhú Gōu):
appears when the ruler is respectful and trustworthy.
(Lacuna)
Spirit mushroom (Zhī Cǎo):
grows when the ruler is benevolent and compassionate.
Eating it allows one to transcend the world.
In Yuánfēng 2 (109 BCE) of Emperor Wǔ of Hàn,
spirit mushrooms grew in Gānquán Palace,
nine stalks with connected leaves.
In Yuánkāng 4 (62 BCE) of Emperor Xuān of Hàn,
golden spirit mushrooms with nine stalks
grew in a bronze pond in Hándé Hall.
In the spring of Yǒngpíng 17 (74 CE) of Emperor Míng of Hàn,
spirit mushrooms grew in the front hall.
In the fourth month of Jiànhé 1 (147 CE) of Emperor Huán of Hàn,
spirit mushrooms grew in the inner imperial treasury.
In Shēngmíng 2 (478 CE) of Emperor Cóng of Sòng,
a purple spirit mushroom grew in the mountains of Xuānchéng.
The local authorities obtained it and presented it.
Luminous Pearl (Míngyuè Zhū):
appears when the ruler does not exhaust aquatic creatures.
During the reigns of Empress Gāo of Hàn and Emperor Jǐng,
Zhū Zhòng, a person from Kuàijī, presented pearls of three to four inches.
In the Yuánhé era (84-87 CE) of Emperor Zhāng of Hàn,
commanderies and kingdoms presented luminous pearls.
Giant Black Millet (Jùchàng):
the grain of Sānyú,
one husk, two grains.
Appears when the ruler's ancestral temple rites are properly performed.
In the time of the Yellow Emperor,
southern barbarians came on white deer to present black millet.
In the Yuánhé era (84-87 CE) of Emperor Zhāng of Hàn,
black millet grew in commanderies and kingdoms.
Level Flowers (Huápíng):
their branches are perfectly level.
Grows when the ruler has virtue.
If virtue is strong, they point upwards;
if virtue is weak, they bend downwards.
In the Yuánhé era (84-87 CE) of Emperor Zhāng of Hàn,
level flowers grew in commanderies and kingdoms.
Level Dew (Pínglù):
like a canopy,
used to observe the governance of the four directions.
If a kingdom is not well-governed,
it will tilt towards that direction.
(Lacuna)
Rújiá:
also known as Lìjiá,
grows alongside the steps.
One leaf grows each day,
starting from the new moon,
stopping at the full moon.
On the sixteenth day,
one leaf falls each day.
If the month is short,
then one leaf withers but does not fall.
Grew on the steps during the time of Yáo.
(Lacuna)
Rèfǔ:
also known as Yǐshàn,
its form is like a tumbleweed,
large branches, small leaves,
roots like silk.
It rotates and generates wind,
killing flies.
Grew in the kitchen during the time of Yáo.
(Lacuna)
Red Grass (Zhū Cǎo):
the essence of grasses.
Grows when there is the virtue of a sage in the world.
In the fifth month of Jiànwǔ Zhōngyuán 1 (56 CE) of Emperor Guāngwǔ of Hàn,
In the Yuánhé era (84-87 CE) of Emperor Zhāng of Hàn,
red grass grew in commanderies and kingdoms.
In the early reign of Emperor Wén of Wèi,
red grass grew beside Wénchāng Hall.
In Yuánjiā 11 (434 CE) of Emperor Wén of Sòng,
red grass grew in the home of a person named Wáng in Píxiàn, Shǔjùn.
Zhēn Fǎchóng, the Inspector of Yìzhōu, reported it.
Auspicious Star (Jǐng Xīng):
a great star.
Its shape is like a half-moon.
It assists the moon in brightness during the dark and new moon phases.
(Lacuna)
Bīnlián Kuòdá:
grows in rooms.
Grows when the ruler regulates relations with empresses and consorts with moderation.
(Lacuna)
Qú Sōu:
came to present furs in the time of Yǔ.
(Lacuna)
Waving Well (Làng Jǐng):
forms naturally without being dug.
Responds when the ruler is pure and tranquil.
(Lacuna)
Queen Mother of the West (Xīwángmǔ):
came to present white jade rings and white jade tubes in the time of Shùn.
(Lacuna)
Yuècháng:
came to present white pheasants and elephant tusks in the time of Duke of Zhōu.
(Lacuna)
In the first month of Yuánshǐ 1 (1 CE) of Emperor Píng of Hàn,
Yuècháng, through multiple interpreters, presented one white pheasant
and two black pheasants.
An edict instructed the Three Dukes to offer them to the ancestral temple.
In the ninth month of Jiànwǔ 13 (37 CE) of Emperor Guāngwǔ of Hàn,
In the Yuánhé era (84-87 CE) of Emperor Zhāng of Hàn,
white pheasants were seen in commanderies and kingdoms.
In the eleventh month of Yǒngkāng 1 (167 CE) of Emperor Huán of Hàn,
white pheasants were seen in Xīhé.
On Dīngsì day, in the fourth month of Yánkāng 1 (220 CE) of Emperor Xiàn of Hàn,
Ráo'ān County reported seeing white pheasants;
additionally, nineteen commanderies and kingdoms reported seeing white pheasants.
On Dīngsì day, in the fourth month of Xiánníng 1 (275 CE) of Emperor Wǔ of Jìn,
white pheasants were seen in Ānfēng and Sōngzī.
On Bǐngwǔ day, in the twelfth month of Xiánníng 1,
white pheasants were seen in Suīyáng, Liáng State.
Liáng Wáng Róng obtained them and presented them.
In the eleventh month of Xiánníng 3 (277 CE),
white pheasants were seen in Ráo'ān, Bóhǎi.
Xiàng Ruǎn Wēn obtained them and presented them.
On Gēngxū day, in the ninth month of Tàikāng 1 (280 CE) of Emperor Wǔ of Jìn,
On Wùwǔ day, in the twelfth month of Jiànxīng 3 (315 CE) of Emperor Mǐn of Jìn,
white pheasants were seen in Xiāngpíng.
On Wùwǔ day, in the twelfth month of Jiànxīng 3,
white pheasants were seen.
In the fifth month of the seventh year of Yìxī of Emperor Ān,
a white pheasant was seen in Nánchāng, Yùzhāng.
On the *gēngchén* day of the fifth month of the fifth year of Yuánjiā of Emperor Wén of Sòng,
a white pheasant was seen in Jǔxiàn, Dōngguǎn.
The Grand Administrator, Liú Xuán, reported it.
In the second month of the sixteenth year of Yuánjiā,
a white pheasant was seen in Chénjùn.
The Inspector of Yùzhōu, Prince Yìxīn of Chángshā, presented it.
On the *guǐhài* day of the second month of the eighteenth year of Yuánjiā,
a white pheasant was seen in Sòngxiàn, Nánrǔyīn.
The Grand Administrator, Wén Dào'ēn, presented it.
In the sixth month of the twentieth year of Yuánjiā,
a white pheasant was seen in Fāngyǔxiàn, Gāopíng.
The Inspector of Xúzhōu, Zāng Zhì, presented it.
On the *wùyín* day of the third month of the twenty-sixth year of Yuánjiā,
a white pheasant was seen in Dōng'ān,
and one in Pèijùn.
The Inspector of the two prefectures, Xú and Yǎn, Prince Huò of Wǔlíng, presented them.
On the *jǐsì* day of the third month of the second year of Dàmíng of Emperor Xiàowǔ,
a pair of white pheasants, male and female, were seen in Hǎilíng.
The Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, Prince Dàn of Jìnglíng, presented them.
In the twelfth month of the fifth year of Dàmíng,
a white pheasant was seen in Qínjùn.
[(36)] The Inspector of Nányǎnzhōu, Prince Zǐxūn of Jìn'ān, presented it.
On the *dīngmǎo* day of the second month of the eighth year of Dàmíng,
a white pheasant was seen in Jiānglíng, Nánjùn.
The Inspector of Jīngzhōu, Prince Zǐxù of Línhǎi, presented it.
On the *bǐngwǔ* day of the first month of the first year of Yǒngguāng of the Former Deposed Emperor,
a white pheasant was seen in Bóhǎi.
The Inspector of Qīngzhōu, Wáng Xuánmó, presented it.
On the first day of the third month, *jiǎwǔ*, of the first year of Yǒngguāng,
a white pheasant was seen in Xīncài.
The Inspector of Yùzhōu, Liú Déyuàn, presented it.
Yellow Silver and Purple Jade:
If the king does not hoard gold and jade,
then yellow silver and purple jade will be seen glowing in the deep mountains.
In the eighth month of the second year of Tàishǐ of Emperor Míng of Sòng,
a section of purple jade was found south of Chèqí City,
three *chǐ* and two *cùn* in circumference,
one *chǐ* long,
and seven *chǐ* thick.
Tàizōng attacked
which he presented to the two temples of Wǔ and Wén.
Jade Maiden:
a concubine bestowed by Heaven.
*Lǐ Hán Wénjiā* says:
"Yǔ had humble palaces,
and devoted his strength to canals and ditches.
The hundred grains were brought to fruition,
and a divine dragon maiden descended."
(Lacuna)
Earth Pearls:
If the king does not consider wealth as treasure, then pearls will be produced.
(Lacuna)
Heavenly Deer:
a beast of pure spiritual essence.
Its five-colored radiance shines brightly;
it appears when the king's Dao is complete.
(Lacuna)
Cornered Beast (*Jiǎoduān*):
It travels eighteen thousand *lǐ* a day,
and also understands the languages of the four barbarians.
When an enlightened ruler and sage lord are on the throne,
and are clear-sighted regarding matters from distant lands and profound depths,
then it will arrive bearing a scroll.
(Lacuna)
Zhōuyìn:
the name of a divine beast,
a transformation of celestial constellations.
It arrives when the king's virtue is abundant.
(Lacuna)
Flying Hare (*Fēitú*):
the name of a divine horse,
it travels thirty thousand *lǐ* a day.
When Yǔ toiled diligently for years to control the floods,
saving the people from harm,
Heaven responded to his virtue and it arrived.
(Lacuna)
Marsh Beast (*Zéshòu*):
During the time of the Yellow Emperor, when he patrolled to the eastern shore,
a marsh beast emerged.
It could speak,
and knew the essence of all things,
using this to warn the people
and remove harm for the era.
It comes when a virtuous ruler has profound and distant enlightenment.
(Lacuna)
*Dǐng*:
a reclusive beast.
It comes when an enlightened king is on the throne,
to avert disasters for the era.
(Lacuna)
*Yǎodé*:
a divine horse,
similar to the Flying Hare.
They also arrive from their respective directions,
to demonstrate the ruler's virtue.
(Lacuna)
United Heart Birds (*Tóngxīn Niǎo*):
They arrive when the king's virtue reaches distant regions,
and the four barbarians are united.
(Lacuna)
*Juétí*:
a beast of Hòutǔ,
it can speak on its own.
It comes when the king is benevolent and filial to the country.
It arrived when Yǔ controlled the floods.
(Lacuna)
Purple Swift (*Zǐdá*):
It is seen when the king's benevolence and righteousness are practiced.
(Lacuna)
Small Bird Gives Birth to Large Bird:
It arrives when the king's land is opened up.
(Lacuna)
River Spirit (*Héjīng*):
human head, fish body;
the prophecy received by Shī Kuàng.
(Lacuna)
Yánxī:
It arrives when the king practices filial piety.
(Lacuna)
Large Cowries (*Dàbèi*):
They appear when the king is not greedy for wealth.
(Lacuna)
Wēiruí:
It grows before the palace when the king's rites are complete.
(Lacuna)
Sweet Spring (*Lǐquán*):
the essence of water,
sweet and delicious.
It appears when the king governs well.
In the fifth month of the first year of Jiànwǔ Zhōngyuán of Emperor Guāngwǔ of Hàn,
sweet springs appeared in the capital and various commanderies and kingdoms.
Those who drank from the sweet spring had all their chronic illnesses cured;
but the one-eyed and the lame were not cured.
At the beginning of Emperor Wén of Wèi's reign,
two sweet springs appeared in Shàoguó.
In the twelfth year of Yuánjiā of Emperor Wén of Sòng,
a sweet spring appeared in the county courtyard of Xiāngxiāng, Héngyáng.
The Inspector of Jīngzhōu, Prince Yìqìng of Línchuān, reported it.
On the *jiǎxū* day of the ninth month of the third year of Xiàojiàn of Emperor Xiàowǔ,
the spring in the *Xìzhàng Duì* courtyard, which in spring and summer never filled beyond a *chǐ* in depth,
suddenly reached one *zhàng*,
with five colors.
The water was clear and sweet,
and the supply inexhaustible.
On the *rénzǐ* day of the third month of the second year of Dàmíng of Emperor Xiàowǔ,
a sweet spring emerged from flat ground in Lóufán, Běirǔyīn.
The Inspector of Yùzhōu, Zōng [Xiān], reported it.
On the *yǐyǒu* day of the fourth month of the first year of Tàiyù of Emperor Míng,
a sweet spring appeared in Sīyì, Shānyīn, Kuàijī.
The Grand Administrator, Cài Xīngzōng, reported it.
Sun and Moon Emit Light:
The sun
is an emblem of the ruler.
If the ruler does not borrow power from his officials,
then the sun and moon will emit bright light.
(Lacuna)
Auspicious Ganoderma (*Zhīyīng*):
It grows
when the king cherishes and draws near to the elderly,
and nurtures those with the Way.
During the Yuánhé era of Emperor Zhāng of Hàn,
auspicious ganoderma grew in various commanderies and kingdoms.
Green Stones (*Bìshí*):
They arrive when cherished objects are discarded.
(Lacuna)
Jade Jar (*Yùwèng*):
It fills without drawing water.
It appears when the king is pure and incorruptible.
(Lacuna)
Mountain Chariot (*Shānchē*):
the essence hidden in the mountains.
If gold and jade are not hoarded,
and mountains and lakes are exploited at the right time,
connecting the riches of mountains and seas
to provide for all under heaven,
then the mountain forms its chariot.
(Lacuna)
Chicken Startles Rhinoceros (*Jīhài Xī*):
It appears when the king disdains difficult-to-obtain objects.
(Lacuna)
Mounds Produce Black Elixir (*Líng Chū Hēidān*):
It appears when the king cultivates utmost filial piety.
(Lacuna)
Divine Tripod (*Shéndǐng*):
the essence of simplicity and refinement.
It knows good fortune and ill fortune,
can be heavy or light,
boils without fire,
and spontaneously generates the five flavors.
It appears when the king's virtue is abundant.
On the fifth day of the fifth month of the first year of Yuándǐng of Emperor Wǔ of Hàn,
a tripod was found by the Fén River.
In the second month of the sixth year of Yǒngpíng of Emperor Míng of Hàn,
〔三七〕the Grand Administrator of Lújiāng presented a precious tripod.
It was unearthed from Mount Wángluò.
(Luò is sometimes written as Xióng.)
In the tenth month of the seventh year of Jiànchū of Emperor Zhāng of Hàn,
the imperial carriage made a western tour to Huáilǐ.
Yòu Fúfēng Jìnshàng from Měiyáng obtained a bronze vessel on Mount Qí,
resembling a wine *zūn*.
An edict commanded it be used morning and evening on the journey to warm wine for all officials.
In the first year of Yǒngyuán of Emperor Hé of Hàn,
Dòu Xiàn campaigned against the Xiōngnú,
and obtained the Zhòngshānfǔ tripod in Mòběi Jiǔquán,
with a capacity of five *dǒu*.
On the *wùxū* day of the sixth month of the twelfth year of Chìwū of Sūn Quán of Wú,
a precious tripod emerged from Línpíng Lake.
Another also emerged from Dōngbù Líng County.
In the eighth month of the first year of Bǎodǐng of Sūn Hào of Wú,
reports came from various places of large tripods being found.
On the *xīnmǎo* day of the tenth month of the first year of Xiánhé of Emperor Chéng of Jìn,
a mountain bank collapsed in Chōnggǔ County, Xuānchéng,
and a stone tripod weighing two *jīn* was obtained,
with a capacity of over one *hú*.
〔三八〕
In the fifth year of Xiánkāng of Emperor Chéng of Jìn,
a resident of Nánchāng, Yùzhāng, digging in the ground, found four bronze bells.
The Grand Administrator Chǔ Póu presented them.
On the *yǐwèi* day of the second month of the fifth year of Shēngpíng of Emperor Mù of Jìn,
a horse's foot sank into the ground at the Southern Yè Gate,
and one bronze bell was found.
On the *xīnchǒu* day of the fourth month of the thirteenth year of Yuánjiā of Emperor Wén of Sòng,
a miraculous tripod spontaneously emerged from the waterside of Zhāngshān, Wǔchāng County.
The Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, Nánqiáo Wáng Yìxuān, presented it.
On the *wùshēn* day of the ninth month of the nineteenth year of Yuánjiā,
nine stone bells emerged from the Shíliángjiàn ravine in Féirú, Guǎnglíng.
They were arranged in sequence, large and small,
lined up facing south.
The Inspector of Nányánzhōu, Línchuān Wáng Yìqìng, presented them.
In the twelfth month of the twenty-first year of Yuánjiā,
an ancient tripod was found at the waterside in Xīnyáng,
bearing forty-two characters in seal script.
The Inspector of Yōngzhōu, Xiāo Sīhuà, presented it.
In the twenty-second year of Yuánjiā,
a bronze bell emerged from Yùníng County, Yùzhāng.
The Inspector of Jiāngzhōu, Guǎnglíng Wáng Shào, presented it.
On the *dīnghài* day of the fourth month of the third year of Xiàojiàn of Emperor Xiàowǔ,
seven bronze bells were found in a field by a resident of Yíhuáng County, Línchuān.
The Internal Administrator Fù Huī presented them.
On the *jiǎchén* day of the fourth month of the third year of Xiàojiàn,
six ancient bells were found in Yánlíng, Jìnlíng.
The Inspector of Xúzhōu, Jìnglín Wáng Dàn, presented them.
In the sixth month of the seventh year of Dàmíng of Emperor Xiàowǔ,
a bronze road drum was found in Púqí, Jiāngxià,
with four sides and a single foot.
The Inspector of Yǐngzhōu, Ānlù Wángzǐ Suí, presented it.
On the *bǐngshēn* day of the second month of the fourth year of Tàishǐ of Emperor Míng,
an ancient bronze bell was found in Wàngcài, Yùzhāng,
one *chǐ* seven *cùn* high,
and two *chǐ* eight *cùn* in circumference.

On the first day of the first month, *wǔmǎo* (戊午), in the fifth year of Dàmíng,

Upon his return, he reported it,
and the Emperor considered it an auspicious sign.
Thereupon, all the *gōngqīng* composed poems about the flower-snow.
The historian remarks, based on the poems:
"That which gathers first is *xiàn* (霰)."
Hán's poem says:
"*Xiàn*,
is *yīng* (英)."
Flower petals are called *yīng*.
The *Lísāo* says:
"The fallen *yīng* of autumn chrysanthemums."
Zuǒ Sī says
"fallen *yīng* flutter and drift,"
which is it.
Thus, *xiàn* is flower-snow.
The flowers of plants mostly have five petals,
but flower-snow uniquely has six points.

Duàn Fóróng, the General of Níngshuò, presented it.
